How is a Bryan County home valued and how is an appeal made?

The assessor sets fair market value, and 40 percent of it, minus any homestead exemption, becomes the taxable value. The commissioner then applies the millage rate. The county has posted the 2026 millage rates on its tax page.

Notices for 2026 went out on June 12, and the final day to appeal was July 27. That window is shut, and the assessor's page says late appeals are refused. Its rules are worth knowing for any later year:

  • Use the county's written appeal form.
  • Get it physically to the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office before 5:00 p.m. on deadline day.
  • Nothing sent by email or fax is accepted, and a postmark proves nothing.

The assessor's staff are also photographing homes to refresh records, so a county vehicle may pause outside yours. After a sale, the new owner sees a value the following year, when the first notice arrives.

Questions about a value belong with the assessor at 912-653-3889, option 1. The assessor's page also offers a guide called Understanding Your Notice of Assessment, which walks through each line of the notice. Read it before you decide whether an appeal is worth filing next year.

Who is billed when a Bryan County house changes hands?

The commissioner's page says the office does not prorate taxes according to the date of sale, the amount of usage or current ownership. Any split between buyer and seller therefore happens at the closing table.

Once you sell, give the tax commissioner the recorded deed and closing papers so the next bill finds the new owner. Leave them at either office, mail them to P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or email propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. Address changes and homestead applications belong with the assessor.

Find out from your closing attorney how this year's bill will be shared and whether the December deadline lands before your closing. For any open bill, get a payoff figure from the commissioner so it can come out of the sale.

How do schools and housing vary across Bryan County?

Bryan County School District covers kindergarten through twelfth grade everywhere except parts of Fort Stewart, where elementary students go to schools run by the Department of Defense Education Activity. Older students from the base attend county public schools.

The numbers describe a young, family-heavy county. In 2020, 28.9 percent of residents were under 18, the median age was 35.5 and 44.8 percent of households had children. QuickFacts adds 16,603 households averaging 2.90 people, 77.7 percent owner occupancy and a median gross rent of $1,618.

  • Pembroke and the north end are mostly rural, and parcels there tend to be larger.
  • Richmond Hill and the south end sit in the Savannah commuter zone, with newer subdivisions.
  • Fort Stewart separates the two ends, so owners in each part usually use the closer tax office.

Go to whichever location is closer, since both handle the same tax matters.

What about homestead, mobile homes and business property in Bryan County?

The county's sample calculation uses a $2,000 homestead reduction from assessed value. Applications go to the assessor, and your status on January 1 decides eligibility, so ask that office which exemptions match your age, income or veteran status.

Mobile homes are billed under their own rules. Without a homestead exemption, the bill arrives in January and is due April 1. With one, the home is taxed along with its land, and that bill is due around November 15. Taxes must be paid, with a receipt in hand, before any mobile home is moved, even out of the county.

A business must file a personal property return with the assessor by April 1 in every year it operates, and state-set values apply if it does not. Timber sales go on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, and heavy-duty equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in its purchase year.

If you own more than one kind of property, ask the commissioner which accounts exist under your name. A forgotten mobile home or business account can hold up a closing just as a missed house bill can.

More questions about Bryan County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the 2026 due date for Bryan County property tax?

The 2026 bills carry a due date of Tuesday, December 15, 2026, and were mailed on October 16. After the due date, interest of 0.875 percent per month applies.

Is it too late to appeal a 2026 Bryan County assessment?

Yes. The 2026 cutoff was 5:00 p.m. on July 27, and the assessor's office refuses late appeals. Watch for the next notice and file in writing within 45 days of its date.

Does Bryan County split property tax by sale date?

No. The commissioner's office says it does not prorate by sale date, so the buyer and seller settle the bill between them at closing.

Where should the deed go after a Bryan County sale?

Send the recorded deed and closing documents to the Bryan County Tax Commissioner, P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or to propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. You can also drop them at the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office.

What happens if I do not pay Bryan County property tax?

Interest and penalties accumulate, and penalties stop at 20 percent. Once a bill is 30 days delinquent the commissioner may start tax sale proceedings, so call early if you cannot pay in full.

Why does Bulloch County, Georgia, work differently from its neighbors?

Bulloch County is a university county in southeast Georgia. Statesboro is the seat, and Georgia Southern University and East Georgia State College's Statesboro campus are both there, with Ogeechee Technical College in an unincorporated part of the county (Wikipedia). The county was created on February 8, 1796, spans roughly 673 square miles and is mostly flat coastal plain.

The 2020 count was 81,099 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 86,949. Half the county's occupied homes, 50.1 percent, were rented in 2020, and the median resident was 28.9 years old. Census QuickFacts adds a median home value of $222,500 for 2020 to 2024, owner occupancy of 53.1 percent and 1,389 building permits in 2025.

The result is a county of student rentals, investor houses and family homes. Many sellers hold a rental or an inherited house, and the tax questions below apply to both.

Where does Bulloch County property tax get handled?

The county's government offices keep weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., according to the county website. Bulloch splits the work in a way that differs from most Georgia counties. The tax assessors, not the tax commissioner, receive tax returns and homestead applications.

Bulloch County property tax contacts, from the county's assessor, tax commissioner and payment pages
OfficeAddressPhoneHandles
Tax Assessors113 North Main Street, Statesboro912-764-2181Values, returns, homestead, appeals
Tax Commissioner113 North Main Street, Suite 101, Statesboro912-764-6285Billing, collection, payments

The commissioner lists propertytax@bullochcounty.net for tax questions. The county's online tax record search and payment portal are linked from the tax commissioner page. Card payments carry a convenience fee charged by the processor, not by the county.

For a quick answer on whether a bill is current, the online tax record search is faster than calling. Use the office phones for payoff letters and for anything that involves an exemption or a correction to the record.

How does Bulloch County value property and take returns?

Fair market value is set as of January 1, and the tax is levied on an assessed value that is 40 percent of it. One mill equals one dollar for each thousand dollars of assessed value. The county commissioners set the county rate, and the school board sets its own, as the assessors' page explains.

Every owner must file an initial return covering real and personal property held on January 1. Bulloch takes returns from January 1 through April 1 at the assessors' office. That first return then carries forward at the last finalized value, and a new one is needed only after you add property, make improvements or want to declare another value.

Email returns are refused. A faxed return has to be in the office by 5:00 p.m. on the closing day of the appeal period, and the board has no power to waive penalties or stretch a deadline.

Millage rate hearings took place in August 2026, and the county home page carries the presentation.

How does an appeal work in Bulloch County?

An appeal must be written and filed within 45 days after the date of the notice of change. Email appeals are turned away, and a fax must land by 5:00 p.m. on the last day.

The path runs through four steps:

  • First you file with the Board of Tax Assessors, which reviews the appeal and answers you.
  • When the board leaves the value alone, the case moves to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • At filing, you can pick arbitration over that hearing.
  • Anyone still dissatisfied can take the matter to Superior Court.

Grounds are taxability, value or how uniform the value is against similar properties. A complaint about the tax amount does not qualify, because that follows the millage rate. The county's How Do I page also has a request link for property tax assessment appeals.

Which Bulloch County exemptions can lower the bill?

The assessors describe several homestead exemptions. Each requires that you own the home and live in it as your legal residence on January 1, and applications run from January 1 to April 1. A granted exemption renews yearly until ownership changes.

  • Standard homestead: a $2,000 deduction from the 40 percent assessed value.
  • Age 65 and up: $4,000 off state and county taxes for households inside the income cap the page lists.
  • Age 62 and up: a school tax exemption capped at $10,000 of assessed value, with its own income cap.
  • Disabled veterans and surviving spouses of military members: bigger exemptions under state law.

A deferral program also exists for homeowners 62 and older who pass an income test. Deferred tax generally comes due when ownership changes or the balance reaches 85 percent of the property's value, so a sale ends the deferral.

Farm owners may apply by April 1 for a conservation use covenant. It runs ten years, costs a $10 recording fee and carries a penalty of twice the taxes saved if broken, so talk to the assessors before selling covenanted land.

How do rentals, schools and highways affect a Bulloch County sale?

Bulloch had 32,983 housing units in 2020, and 9.8 percent sat empty. Rentals stood vacant at a 9.0 percent rate against 1.4 percent for owner homes. Median gross rent for 2020 to 2024 is $995, and a mortgaged owner pays a median $1,462 a month. A landlord selling a Statesboro rental is courting buyers in a county where about half of occupied homes were rented in 2020.

Public schooling comes from one countywide district, Bulloch County School District, plus a charter school, Statesboro STEAM Academy, chartered through another district. Families ask about school zones, and commuters ask about I-16, US 301, US 80 and US 25, all of which cross the county.

  • Student rentals near the university are priced and bought differently than family homes.
  • Rural tracts outside Statesboro often carry farm or timber use, so ask the assessors about covenants first.
  • The county has a separate timber harvest page, worth checking if trees were cut before the sale.

Pull the online tax record for any parcel before listing. It shows what the assessors have on file, which makes a wrong acreage or missing exemption easy to spot.

Does a Bulloch County city send its own tax bill?

Four of them do. Statesboro, Brooklet, Portal and Register each bill and collect real and personal property tax on their own, so a house inside their limits draws one bill from the county and a second from the city.

That matters at closing. Your payoff request should cover both bills, and the title company has to know which city, if any, holds your parcel.

At sale time, get a payoff from the commissioner and ask the person handling your closing how this year's share will be divided; the due date appears on the bill. Landlords should also check that the owner name on each bill matches the deed before closing.

More questions about Bulloch County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which office takes homestead applications in Bulloch County?

The Tax Assessors, at 113 North Main Street in Statesboro. They accept applications from January 1 through April 1, and a granted exemption renews on its own.

What is the appeal window in Bulloch County?

The window is 45 days after the notice date. File in writing, since the assessors do not take appeals by email.

Does a Statesboro homeowner receive one tax bill or two?

Two. Statesboro collects its own real and personal property tax, so the county sends one bill and the city sends another every year.

How do I pay Bulloch County property tax?

Pay the Tax Commissioner in person at Suite 101, 113 North Main Street, Statesboro, or online through the county's payment link. Questions go to 912-764-6285. Cards add a convenience fee from the processor.

Can the Bulloch assessors forgive a late filing penalty?

No. The assessors say they lack authority to relieve penalties or grant filing extensions, so meet each stated deadline.

What is Burke County, Georgia, and who sells homes there?

Burke is among Georgia's original counties, formed on February 5, 1777, and it lies along the state's eastern edge, across from South Carolina. Waynesboro is the seat. Covering 827 square miles of land, it ranks as Georgia's second-biggest county by area and falls inside the Augusta metropolitan area (Wikipedia).

The county's website names seven municipalities: Blythe, Girard, Keysville, Midville, Sardis, Vidette and Waynesboro. It bills Burke as the Bird Dog Capital of the World, with hunting and fishing as a draw.

Mid-2025 population stood at 24,408 per Census QuickFacts, slightly under the 2020 base. The same table shows a median home value of $151,600, owner occupancy of 70 percent and 100 building permits in 2025. Sellers often hold farmland, timber or an older house in town, and in a county this large the parcel can sit a long way from the courthouse.

Schooling comes from the Burke County School District, which Wikipedia lists with a single high school and a single middle school, several lower-grade schools and an alternative school. Wikipedia also gives 11,138 housing units for 2020, of which 11.1 percent were empty.

Where do I go for Burke County property tax business?

Both offices are at 524 Myrick Street in Waynesboro, the Board of Assessors in Suite B and the tax commissioner in Suite A. Assessors set values and, per their page, send no bills and collect nothing. The commissioner collects for the county, the state and the Board of Education, and the commissioner's site says that office has no say in values.

Burke County tax offices, per the county and tax commissioner websites
OfficePhoneHours postedOther detail
Board of Assessors, Suite B706-554-2607Weekdays, 8 to 5Board meets the second Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m.
Tax Commissioner, Suite A706-554-3223Weekdays, 8:30 to 5Saturday hours, 9 to noon, on the first and third of the month

The commissioner's post office box is 671 in Waynesboro, GA 30830, and the assessors use box 46 in that town. Maps and records are online through the assessor's county page and the tax commissioner's site.

Appraisers from the assessor's office may visit your property to update records. They carry a Burke County photo ID badge, drive a marked vehicle and measure the outside of buildings and take exterior photographs. If you are away, they leave a door hanger or a business card. Call 706-554-2607 if you want to confirm a visitor's identity.

How can a Burke County owner contest a value?

An owner has 45 days from the notice date to appeal, and the commissioner's site describes four routes. The assessor's page says assessment notices are sent to taxpayers in July, so watch the mail then.

  • Board of Equalization. The Board of Assessors sees the appeal first and may revise the value with a new notice. If it does, the owner gets 30 more days to challenge that notice; an appeal left unchanged is passed to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Hearing officer. Offered only for non-homestead real property above $500,000, with a state-certified appraiser serving as the officer.
  • Arbitration. Say so in your filing, then hand in a certified appraisal within 45 days of the board's acknowledgement, which it must do within 10 days. A hearing is held within 30 days of authorization.
  • Superior Court. Mail or file a written notice with the Board of Assessors inside 30 days of the earlier ruling.

The arbitrator's fees depend on the result. The page states that the county pays if your value is closest to the arbitrator's figure, and you pay if the board's value is closer.

What homestead exemptions does Burke County offer?

Applications are accepted all year at either the commissioner's office or the Board of Assessors, though to count for the current year one must be postmarked or received by the final day of the appeal period. On January 1 you must hold title, live there and claim it as your residence. The commissioner's FAQ names April 1 as the cutoff for the billing year.

The exemptions listed on the county's homestead page include:

  • S1, the standard exemption: $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school, with no age or income test.
  • S3 and S4, for owners 62 and 65 whose income is under $10,000, which add a $10,000 school exemption.
  • S5, SD, SS and SE, which cover disabled veterans and the unremarried spouses of service members who died in war.
  • SG, for the spouse of a peace officer or firefighter who died on duty.
  • L3 and L4 local school exemptions for owners 65 and older.

A refinance leaves an exemption alone unless the name on the deed changes. Vehicles you own must also be registered in Burke County. The Burke County Board of Commissioners, the Board of Education and the cities of Waynesboro, Sardis, Girard, Midville and Keysville have opted out of the statewide floating exemption.

How does payment work in Burke County?

Accepted forms of payment include cash, checks, money orders and major cards, with a convenience fee on cards. You may also pay on the website or by calling 1-844-898-2374 with your bill number.

Several FAQ answers matter to anyone selling:

  • A part payment is accepted, yet interest and penalty continue on whatever is left.
  • When a parcel faces a tax lien sale, phone the commissioner before sending a part payment.
  • Appealing does not stop billing. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value and corrected after the final ruling.
  • A surviving spouse may petition for a year's support through an attorney or the probate court.

A non-homestead mobile home in the county on January 1 owes tax and must show a current decal. Unpaid taxes draw a 10 percent penalty plus interest, and a missing decal carries a fine of $100 to $300.

What becomes of unpaid Burke County taxes?

Delinquent parcels can be sold at tax sale. The commissioner's site posted October 6, 2026 as a sale date with a parcel list, so the date has passed. The commissioner's home page links to that sale's parcel list.

Before listing, look up the parcel number on the commissioner's site and make sure no earlier year is open. Returns are taken January 1 through April 1, and tangible personal property worth $7,500 or less in fair market value is exempt, though motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes are not. A buyer's attorney will check the real property bill and any personal property or mobile home account tied to the address.

For the figure due at closing, request a written payoff from the commissioner, and have the closing agent explain how this year's bill is shared.

Where does a Burke County resident pay in person?

At the tax commissioner, 524 Myrick Street, Suite A, Waynesboro. The number is 706-554-3223. Weekdays run 8:30 to 5, and two Saturdays a month, the first and third, the office opens 9 to noon.

How soon must a Burke County appeal be filed?

File within 45 days of the notice date. Should the Board of Assessors amend the value, a further 30 days applies to the amended notice.

Must I pay my Burke County tax bill during an appeal?

Yes. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value, and the county corrects the bill after the final decision.

Is a part payment accepted in Burke County?

Yes, though interest and penalty keep running on the remainder. If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, call the commissioner first.

What does the Burke County standard homestead exemption cover?

The S1 exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school taxes, with no age or income test. The owner must be in residence on January 1 and apply by April 1.

Which Jackson offices deal with Butts County property tax?

Value and billing live in two different suites of the same building at 625 W. 3rd Street. Suite 1 is the Board of Tax Assessors, which decides what your house is worth. Suite 2 is the Tax Commissioner, an elected office that mails the bill and takes the payment.

The county's own pages stress that these are separate jobs, and that the tax commissioner answers to voters and the state revenue department rather than to the assessors or the commissioners. For a seller, that means a question about a number on a valuation notice and a question about a payoff go to different counters.

  • Assessors: 770-775-8207, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-775-8206, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, closed on approved holidays.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds recorded deeds and liens, and can give you a copy of your warranty deed.

The assessors' general information page says the tax is figured on 40 percent of fair market value as fixed each January 1. The county government and the school board then pick their own mill rates, with each mill worth a dollar on every thousand of taxable value.

What are the Butts County tax installments?

Butts County splits the bill for houses, land and business equipment into two parts: September 15 and December 7. A date that falls on a weekend slides to the following business day. Mobile and manufactured homes are on a separate April 1 date.

Statements go out to the owner, never to a mortgage servicer. The office does send servicers a data file, yet if your lender pays from escrow you may still need to hand over a paper copy. A buyer who closes mid-year will see the bill in their own name, and the office asks you to call if a statement shows up for a house you already sold.

Part payments are welcome and you may make several, but interest and penalties continue to build on the unpaid part, and an account with any balance can be liened. The FAQ gives two different answers on mailed payments, one saying the postmark is not honored and one saying a USPS postmark is. Settle that with the office before you drop a check in the mail.

What did the 2026 countywide reappraisal change in Butts County?

Butts County hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions to review about 13,000 parcels for 2026, with field crews starting in July 2025. Appraisers measured buildings and took photos from outside, and the assessors say none of them go inside a home.

The new values are as of January 1, 2026, and the annual notices were mailed in April and May 2026. Then on July 8, 2026, the Board of Assessors posted that appeals had passed 3% of total value, which under Code Section 48-5-311(e)(3)(B) gives the board an additional 180 days to answer 2026 appeals.

If you plan to list a house, look up your parcel on the assessors' search page before choosing an asking price, and ask whether an appeal on it is still open. A value that changes late in the process changes the number the tax commissioner bills.

Where does a Butts County assessment appeal start?

It starts with a written appeal on form PT-311-A, filed with the Board of Assessors inside a 45-day window that opens on the notice date. Say which method you want. The grounds the commissioner's FAQ lists are taxability, value, uniformity and denial of an exemption.

The assessors review your evidence first, and the county's explainer says they can change the value if they find a mistake. Your next step is the Board of Equalization, a panel of residents appointed by the Grand Jury, or arbitration if you chose that when you filed.

  • Useful proof: a recent appraisal, comparable sales, or photos of defects.
  • A complaint that the bill is too high is outside the grounds, because the appeal is about value and taxability.
  • The forms page says the board cannot waive a late filing or forgive a penalty.

Which Butts County exemption dates matter when you buy or sell?

The homestead application has an April 1 deadline, and the assessors' forms page lists a second form for owners 62 and older showing $20,000 off county tax and $15,000 off school tax. You must own and live in the house on January 1. A move, or a new name on the deed, means applying again.

Returns for real and personal property are taken at the assessors' office from January 1 to April 1. Farm use valuation on form PT-283A has the same April 1 cutoff, and the office wants a phone call before you submit it.

A relief that belongs to the seller does not follow the house. Whoever buys and plans to live there files their own application ahead of the following April 1.

How does a lien form on a Butts County house?

Before any lien, the tax commissioner sends a 30-day notice of intent. Tax still open more than 90 days after its due date can then be recorded as a FiFa on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. Paying the tax plus the fees, interest and penalties cancels it.

Liens are not sold over the counter in Butts County. Where a levy and tax sale advertisement has started, the FAQ urges paying in person. A recorded FiFa is public and can reach your credit file, and the office says it does not report to the bureaus.

A title company will not close over an open lien. Request a written payoff with a good-through date from the tax commissioner and hand it to whoever runs the settlement.

What kind of place is Butts County to sell in?

Butts is a West Central Georgia county of 184 square miles of land, created on December 24, 1825 as the 64th county from parts of Henry and Monroe. Jackson is both seat and largest city. Flovilla and Jenkinsburg are the other incorporated cities, and Stark and Worthville are unincorporated communities. Interstate 75, U.S. 23 and State Routes 16, 36, 42 and 87 cross it.

Atlanta's metro area includes the county, which touches Henry, Spalding, Lamar, Monroe, Jasper and Newton counties. Jackson Lake took shape in 1910 behind the Lloyd Shoals dam on the Ocmulgee River, and Indian Springs State Park is the oldest state park in the nation, according to the assessors' own site. The county's courthouse of 1898 was used until 2019 and is now a museum and visitor center.

More questions about Butts County, GA Property Tax Guide

Can a Butts County house with back taxes still be sold?

Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalties come out of the proceeds at closing and the lien is released. Get a payoff with a good-through date from the tax commissioner at 770-775-8206, since the amount rises as the months pass.

Which Butts County office answers a bill question?

The Tax Commissioner at 770-775-8206 answers bill, payoff and lien questions. The Board of Assessors at 770-775-8207 answers value, exemption and appeal questions. Both are at 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson.

Does my lender receive the Butts County bill?

No, the statement goes to the owner. The office sends mortgage companies on record a data file, so a lender that escrows may already know the amount. If you have changed lenders, tell the new one and forward the bill yourself.

When must I apply for homestead in Butts County?

By April 1. That deadline is listed for the standard exemption and for the one for owners 62 and older. A form that arrives after April 1 takes effect in the following tax year.

How long is the Butts County appeal window?

Forty-five days, counted from the date on the assessment notice. The appeal must be in writing and filed with the Board of Assessors, and the board cannot extend the period.

What does the Woodbine tax office handle for Camden County owners?

Camden County's tax office takes payments at 200 E 4th Street in Woodbine, and mail goes to PO Box 698. Phone 912-576-3248 between 9 and 5 on weekdays. Appraisal is a different department: the assessors, appointed by the county commissioners, answer valuation questions at 912-576-3241.

One line on the tax commissioner's page deserves attention if you are selling. The office says it has no part in dividing the year's tax between buyer and seller, and that liability for the tax sticks to the owner. Your closing attorney or title company works out the split and asks the office for the figure owed on the parcel.

How is the Camden County bill timed?

Bills leave the county in mid-September, and payment is due 60 days after the mail-out. The recipient is whoever held title on January 1 of that tax year. If you sold afterward, pass the notice to the new owner. Nothing in your mailbox by October 15? Call 912-576-3248.

The Department of Revenue's Camden fact sheet lists December 20 as the standard statewide due date and says a county may shift it or bill in installments. It also gives every taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest begins. Camden's own schedule controls, so read the date printed on your statement.

What does a late Camden County bill cost?

Delinquency begins the day after the due date. Interest is the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent a year, a partial month counts as a whole one, and at least $1 is owed (O.C.G.A. 48-5-148). The county's page quotes a monthly figure of 0.7083% from January 2019 as an illustration only.

A flat 5% penalty lands at 120 days overdue, then again at 240, 360 and 480 (O.C.G.A. 48-2-44). Homestead bills of $500 or less escape it, as do new owners who lived outside Georgia, never got a bill and pay within a year.

  • Week after the due date: 30-day lien warning goes out.
  • About a week after that period ends: lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Filing cost, listed at $28.50 to $33.50, joins the bill.
  • After filing, a tax sale can be scheduled.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Camden County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can I get my Camden County house back after a tax sale?

Yes, for a limited time. The lien reaches back to the January 1 valuation (O.C.G.A. 48-2-56) and outranks every other lien. Each December 31 the tax commissioner must issue an execution against delinquent accounts (O.C.G.A. 48-3-3), which tells the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

Redeeming costs the winning bid, plus any later taxes the buyer covered, plus 20% of that sum for the first year or fraction of a year. Each additional year or fraction adds another 10%. After twelve months the buyer may serve notice to cut off redemption for good (O.C.G.A. 48-4-45 through 48-4-48), and the county notes that the earliest a buyer can take physical control is one year and forty-five days after the deed.

That timeline is why selling before the sale date usually keeps more equity with you than waiting does.

What is the Camden County appeal and refund route?

A Notice of Reassessment starts a 45-day clock. Take the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, and note that the state fact sheet wants it postmarked inside that window. Assessed value is 40% of the January 1 market value, so if market value climbs, assessed value must follow.

Overpayment has its own path. The fact sheet says a written refund request for tax assessed or collected in error can be made within three years of payment.

  • Returns go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Homestead applications are accepted year-round, but April 1 is the cutoff for that year.
  • Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption.

Do Kingsland, St. Marys and Woodbine send their own tax bills?

Possibly, and the answer depends on where the house sits. The Department of Revenue's fact sheet explains that cities levy their own ad valorem tax and that the city clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to put everything on one county statement. Only the county tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax in any Georgia county.

Ask the Woodbine tax office whether your address carries a separate city bill, and ask the city clerk for any city balance, since an unpaid city tax can hold up a closing just as a county one does.

The same sheet adds a few rules that matter around a purchase. A mobile home must get a county location permit within 30 days of placement and every January 1 to April 1 afterward, and a long-term note secured by real estate must be recorded in the county within 90 days, with intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note.

What is the history behind Camden County's county seat?

Camden was created in 1777 from the St. Thomas and St. Marys parishes and named for the Earl Camden. Its seat sat in St. Marys, the old shipping town, until 1923, when it moved to Woodbine as railways overtook water transport. The Florida Central and Peninsular Railroad had crossed the county in 1893, and U.S. Route 17 followed in 1927.

Rice grew along the Satilla River and Sea Island cotton on Cumberland Island in earlier centuries. The original county was much larger, and it gave up land to form parts of Wayne County in 1808 and 1812 and of Charlton County in 1854.

Why does Kings Bay shape the Camden County housing market?

Camden fills Georgia's southeastern corner, with Glynn County to the north, Nassau County in Florida to the south and Charlton and Brantley counties to the west. Of its 782 square miles, about 22% is water. Kingsland is the biggest city, St. Marys and Woodbine are the others, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 run through the county. Cumberland Island National Seashore is part of it.

The Navy chose Kings Bay for a submarine base in 1976, on land the Army had acquired in 1954 for an ocean terminal, and Camden grew fast through the 1980s. Before that, the Gilman paper mill drove the local economy from 1939 until it closed in 2002. More recently, voters overturned the county's option on land for Spaceport Camden in 2022, and the Georgia Supreme Court upheld that result in February 2023.

More questions about Camden County, GA Property Tax Guide

Does the Woodbine tax office divide the bill between buyer and seller?

No. The Tax Commissioner's page says it takes no part in prorating, and liability attaches to the owner. Your closing attorney or title company handles the split, using the balance the office confirms.

I never received a Camden County statement. What now?

Call 912-576-3248. The county asks owners who have nothing by October 15 to get in touch. Interest still builds on a late balance even if the bill never reached you.

How fast does a Camden County lien follow a missed due date?

A 30-day notice is mailed the week after the due date, and the lien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court about a week after that. The $28.50 to $33.50 filing cost is added to your bill.

After a Camden County tax sale, can the owner redeem?

Yes. Pay the buyer's price plus 20% for the first year and 10% for each later year, until the buyer completes the notice steps that bar redemption, which can begin twelve months after the sale.

Is there a late penalty on a small Camden County homestead bill?

The 5% penalty is waived when homestead tax is $500 or less. Interest still applies at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, with a $1 minimum.

Who in Carrollton collects the tax and who values the house?

The Carroll County Tax Commissioner, at 423 College Street, Room 401, collects. Call 770-830-5843 for bill questions or 770-830-5826 for the tag and tax counter. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 to 5, and title transactions end at 4:30.

Valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors at 770-830-5812. In Carroll County the assessors also take property tax returns and homestead applications, which differs from counties where the commissioner does. The commissioner's office states that it does not assess property or set millage, and that the county commissioners and the school board levy the rates.

  • Late interest, returned mail, a bill total: tax commissioner.
  • Value, exemption, return or appeal: assessors.
  • Copy of your warranty deed: Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse.

Card payments, whether at the counter or on the commissioner's site, add a 2.5% fee kept by the payment processor Assurance.

What is the December 1 deadline in Carroll County?

December 1 is the usual due date for real estate and business personal property. The commissioner's FAQ says the date was December 21 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it. Manufactured homes pay by April 1, and vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday.

A mailed check counts on a United States Postal Service postmark, but a postage-meter stamp does not. Statements go to the owner and never to a mortgage company, so an escrow borrower has to hand theirs over.

Interest then accrues each month at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. Any tax unpaid 120 days after the deadline draws a 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days until it totals 20%, with an exemption for homestead accounts under $500.

Why settle a Carroll County lien before listing?

After 120 days past due, the commissioner may record a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court. The office warns that the entry is public and credit bureaus can read it, and that it has no say in how they use it. If the tax stays unpaid, the commissioner can levy on the house, which the office describes as a last resort.

Carroll's tax sale page names the next auction date and says bidders must show up with cash, certified funds or a bank letter. Neither step has to happen to your house. A title company can obtain a payoff from the commissioner, print it on the settlement statement and pay the county out of your proceeds, so the lien never reaches the courthouse steps.

What are the Carroll County appeal rules and choices?

Notices of assessment must be mailed by July 1. The appeal is due in writing within 45 days of the notice date, and the right is gone afterward. The notice shows fair market value, assessed value and a tax estimate built on last year's millage.

At filing you choose one of three tracks: the Board of Equalization with a further appeal to Superior Court; arbitration with no Superior Court appeal; or, for non-homestead parcels worth more than $1 million, a hearing officer with Superior Court appeal rights.

  • Allowed grounds: taxability, value, uniformity with similar parcels.
  • Not allowed: a complaint that the levy itself is too high.
  • Math: tax equals fair market value times 40%, less exemptions, times the millage rate.

Which Carroll County relief programs end when the house sells?

Homestead applications go to the assessors and must be filed before April 1 to cover that year. A first-time filer brings the warranty deed. The exemption renews on its own until the owner moves or title changes.

The commissioner's general information page describes an elderly school tax exemption for owners 62 and older whose net income is at most $10,000, a general exemption for owners 65 and older under the same cap, and a deferral program for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax stays on the property until ownership changes or it hits 85% of fair market value, so a sale makes it payable.

Farmland assessed at 30% of fair market value, and conservation-use land assessed at its current use, both rest on a covenant with the assessors to hold the use for 10 years. Ask the assessors what a sale does to that covenant before you list acreage that carries one.

Does Carroll County offer other special assessments beyond homestead?

Yes, a handful, and each one carries conditions that can matter to a buyer. Historic property listed on the Georgia or National Register of Historic Places may get a preferential assessment covering the building and up to two acres around it, once the Department of Natural Resources certifies it as rehabilitated or landmark historic property.

Brownfield property in the state's Hazardous Site Reuse and Redevelopment Program can have its taxable assessment effectively frozen for ten years while a developer cleans it up. Forest land conservation use has a 15-year covenant and is limited to tracts above 200 acres, and the residence on the land is excluded from the break.

  • Mobile homes: the owner files a return and gets a location permit, and the current year's tax must be paid in full first.
  • Returns for real and personal property are filed January 1 through April 1 with the assessors.
  • A new return can state a different value, which preserves your appeal rights if the board changes the number again.

How did Carroll County grow into a 130,000-resident county?

Carroll lies on the Alabama line in west Georgia, with 499 square miles of land. Lines were drawn on June 9, 1825, and the county was named in 1826 for Charles Carroll of Carrollton. In the 1850s it was nicknamed the Free State of Carroll, and it saw Georgia's first gold rush. The 2020 census counted 119,148 residents and the 2025 estimate is 131,036.

Carrollton is the seat and biggest city. Villa Rica (half of it in Douglas County), Temple, Bowdon, Mount Zion, Whitesburg and Roopville complete the list of municipalities. Interstate 20 crosses the north, joined by U.S. 27, U.S. 78 and State Routes 5, 16, 61, 100, 101, 113, 166 and 274. Carroll has three school districts, and the Carrollton Greenbelt is a local walking and cycling route.

Weather has left a mark: tornadoes hit in February and May 2008, and flooding in September 2009 closed more than 60 roads and wrecked bridges. Buyers of older homes sometimes ask about storm repairs.

When do Carroll County property taxes come due?

December 1 for real estate and business personal property, under a resolution the county commissioners adopted in December 2009. Manufactured homes are due April 1. Read the date on your statement to be sure.

What does lateness add to a Carroll County bill?

Monthly interest at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%, and a 5% penalty that starts at 120 days and repeats every 120 days to a 20% ceiling. Homestead accounts under $500 are spared the penalty.

Is there a fee for card payment in Carroll County?

Yes, 2.5%, collected by the payment processor, whether you pay at the counter or online. The county itself does not receive it. Ask the commissioner's office about other payment methods.

Does the Carroll County Tax Commissioner set my tax?

No. The commissioner bills what the assessors' values and the millage rates produce, and the rates come from the county commissioners and the school board. Value questions go to 770-830-5812.

April 1. File with the Tax Assessor's Office at 423 College Street. A late application waits for the next tax year, and first-time applicants should bring their warranty deed.

Which Ringgold or Fort Oglethorpe counter takes Catoosa County tax payments?

Catoosa County's tax commissioner runs two offices: 796 LaFayette Street in Ringgold and 205 Forrest Road in Fort Oglethorpe. One phone line, (706) 965-2571, serves both.

The Ringgold office keeps uneven hours. It opens at 7:30 on Tuesdays, closes at 6:00 on Thursdays, and keeps an 8:30 to 5:00 schedule the other three weekdays. Fort Oglethorpe is open 8:30 to 5:00 every weekday and stops title work at 4:45 (5:45 on Thursdays).

Appraisal belongs to the Catoosa County Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street, phone 706-965-3772. That office keeps records on over 28,000 real estate parcels and about 6,900 personal property and mobile home accounts, and its field appraisers carry photo identification and drive marked county vehicles when they visit a property.

Is Catoosa County's December 20 bill one payment for the whole county?

Largely, yes. County taxes are generally due by December 20, and the bill folds in the levies of the City of Ringgold and the City of Fort Oglethorpe. A single statement covers all three taxing districts: 01 for the unincorporated county, 02 for Ringgold and 03 for Fort Oglethorpe.

Voting districts do not line up with taxing districts, so the code printed on your bill is the one to trust. The tax commissioner's bill guide defines each column, and a few are worth knowing before you sell.

  • Due date: the last day to pay with no chance of interest or penalty.
  • Sales tax credit: savings tied to the prior year's local option sales tax proceeds.
  • Notice of Assessment: an estimate, not a bill, and it may leave out exemptions you hold.

Mobile and manufactured homes in the county on January 1 are taxed by April 1 with a location permit, and missing it adds a 10% penalty, a FiFa and a possible sale of the home.

What happens if I disagree with a Catoosa County assessment?

You file within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. In 2024 the county gave August 9 as the cutoff, and every later notice runs on the same 45-day clock. Filing works three ways: in person at 798 Lafayette Street, by mail to the Tax Assessor at that address (Ringgold, GA 30736), or through the assessor's page on the qPublic property site.

When you file, you name your path: Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration. The commissioner's site says the dispute may concern taxability, value or uniformity, but not the amount of tax levied. Mobile home owners who want a different value have 45 days to file with the assessors, and 21 days after a changed value to go to the Board of Equalization.

The county's 2024 announcement explains a common surprise: the notice estimates tax at last year's rate, then the county commissioners, the school board and the Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe councils work out a rollback rate that can bring the bill down.

Where is the Catoosa County homestead application filed?

At the tax commissioner's office. Catoosa differs from counties where the assessors take these applications. A Georgia ID is required, and a first-time homeowner should carry the warranty deed. Applications may come in all year but must be received by April 1 to count for that year.

The Board of Assessors rules on eligibility, and an owner who is turned down must be told and can appeal. Once approved, the exemption renews itself until you change residence, ownership or exemption type.

Catoosa has local exemptions that replace state amounts when higher. The commissioner's site sorts them into regular, veteran and senior groups and keeps a separate page on deferral. Check which one applies before you pick a closing date.

How do I clear Catoosa County taxes at a sale?

Ask the tax commissioner for the full amount owed, then have the closing attorney or title company pay it from the proceeds. The commissioner's home page warns that unpaid taxes can lead to a levy and a sale, and it links a Delinquent Tax Sale Information Guide and a list of excess funds from earlier sales.

Georgia attaches the lien to the property as of its January 1 valuation, ahead of other liens, which is why title companies insist on a payoff. If you already hold a tax sale notice, phone the office the same day because timing controls your options.

  • Order the balance from the tax commissioner before you sign a contract.
  • Ask for any excess-funds or tax sale notices tied to the parcel.
  • Keep the payoff letter with your closing papers.

If a bill comes in for a house you sold, send it to the buyer. Statements go to the owner on record, so recording the deed quickly keeps later bills from straying.

Why might a Catoosa County appraiser show up at my door?

The assessor's public notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and lists the reasons: a return being filed, an appeal, new construction or improvements, a review of records for a property division or transfer, and a conservation use application. A field appraiser from the office carries photo identification and drives a marked county vehicle, and the assessors' phone number is 706-965-3772 if you want to confirm a visit.

The annual revaluation matters just as much to a seller. In June 2024 the Board of Assessors finished revaluing every property and mailed notices, stating that Georgia law requires uniform values based on the current Catoosa County sales market. A sale or a division of a lot, both on the assessor's list of reasons to visit, is the kind of change a seller should expect the office to notice, so keep any permits, survey papers and receipts for improvements handy.

What shapes the Catoosa County housing picture around Chattanooga?

Catoosa is a 162-square-mile county on the Tennessee line, created December 5, 1853, with Hamilton County, Tennessee to the north, Whitfield County to the east and Walker County to the west. Ringgold is the seat, Fort Oglethorpe is the largest city, and Tunnel Hill is a town. It belongs to the Chattanooga metropolitan area, and 76.3% of residents live in urban areas.

Interstate 75 and U.S. 27 carry the heavy traffic, with U.S. 41 and 76 and State Routes 2, 146 and 151 spreading it. A fog pileup on I-75 in March 2002 involved about 125 vehicles, and a tornado hit Ringgold on April 27, 2011. All schools are in Catoosa County Public Schools, with Battlefield, Boynton, Ringgold and Tiger Creek among its elementary schools and Heritage, Lakeview and Ringgold middle schools.

More questions about Catoosa County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which day is the Catoosa County property tax deadline?

Generally December 20. One bill carries the county, Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe taxes. The date printed on your own statement controls.

Can I treat a Catoosa County Notice of Assessment as my bill?

No. It lists the fair market value and an estimate built on last year's millage rate, and it may omit exemptions. A rollback of the rate can lower the actual bill.

Where do I apply for homestead in Catoosa County?

At the Tax Commissioner's office, with a Georgia ID and a warranty deed if you are a first-time owner. The application must be received by April 1 to count for that tax year.

When are Catoosa County mobile homes taxed?

By April 1 for homes in the county on January 1, when the location permit is issued. A late payment draws a 10% penalty, a FiFa and possibly a sale of the home.

Which Chatham County offices bill the tax and value the property?

Two separate offices handle a Chatham County property tax bill. The Board of Assessors sets the value and approves exemptions, while the Tax Commissioner bills, collects and passes the money to each taxing body. The Tax Commissioner states that its office plays no part in setting values or millage rates.

According to the county's 2026 property tax brochure, the Tax Commissioner bills for Chatham County, the Special Service District, the school board, transit, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Look at the line items on your own bill to see which of those districts apply to your address.

  • Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100, tax.chathamcountyga.gov, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., 295 Police Memorial Dr. and 1145 Eisenhower Dr., open 8:30am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Board of Assessors: 912-652-7271, boa.chathamcountyga.gov, Suite 113 of the Pete Liakakis Government Building at 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue.
  • Mail: Chatham County Tax Commissioner, P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412.
  • Satellite tax offices on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 see people by appointment only.

What does Chatham County look like from a seller's side?

Chatham County is the northernmost of Georgia's coastal counties. It covers 632 square miles, and 206 of them are water. The Savannah River bounds it on the northeast and the Ogeechee River on the southwest and Tybee Island sits on the Atlantic side. Savannah anchors the county as its seat, with Bloomingdale, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Tybee Island, Thunderbolt and Vernonburg making up the rest of the municipalities.

By mid-2025 the county had an estimated 311,855 residents, compared with 295,291 counted in 2020. On the 2020 to 2024 survey the middle value for a home lived in by its owner is $302,700, typical rent runs $1,471 a month, and 56.8% of households own. Builders took out 4,426 permits during 2025.

Interstates 16, 95 and 516 cross the county along with US 17 and US 80, and the whole county falls inside Savannah-Chatham County Public Schools. Savannah State University and the Savannah College of Art and Design are both located in Savannah, and Live Oak Public Libraries serve Chatham, Effingham and Liberty counties.

What are the Chatham County property tax due dates?

Land and buildings are billed in two pieces. June 1 is the deadline for the first piece and November 15 for the second, while business and other personal property is billed once, also due November 15.

Chatham County billing calendar, from the Tax Commissioner's 2026 property tax brochure
BillMailed byDue
Real property, first installmentApril 1June 1
Real property, second installmentSeptember 15November 15
Personal property, one billNot statedNovember 15

Payment can go by mail to the Chatham County Tax Commissioner at P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412, online, or in person. Online payment by credit card or eCheck carries convenience fees, and the brochure says eChecks are free. A check or eCheck that comes back unpaid costs 5% of the amount with a $30 minimum, under O.C.G.A. 16-9-20.

Taxes not paid by the due date are delinquent. Interest and penalties follow O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 and 48-2-44, and a delinquent parcel can also carry a tax lien that a title company will want cleared before closing.

How does an owner contest a Chatham County value?

A written challenge is due at the Board of Assessors 45 days after the notice date shown on your Annual Notice of Assessment. That notice, rather than any tax bill, starts the clock. An appeal can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and Georgia supplies a uniform appeal form.

On that first written appeal you must name your method. The brochure lists three:

  • Board of Equalization, with a further petition to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within 45 days; the Board of Assessors can accept or reject it, and you may still petition Superior Court.
  • Hearing Officer, open only to non-homestead real property with a fair market value of $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value.

The Board of Assessors says it welcomes recent sales, photographs of similar sold homes, and lease or income figures. It also points out that it measures square footage from the outside perimeter, so a smaller interior living area does not by itself prove an error.

Property returns are filed during the season that opens with the new year and closes April 1, and the forms sit on the Board of Assessors website under Forms. An initial return renews itself every year at the last final value. A taxpayer unhappy with the current figure can file a fresh return declaring a different value, which protects appeal rights if the Board changes the number again. Working farmland can be assessed at 30% of market value instead of the usual 40%, and conservation use land is valued by how it is used today. Each program asks for a covenant to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years.

Which homestead exemptions apply in Chatham County?

The regular homestead exemption removes $12,000 of assessed value from the county levy and $2,000 from the school and state levies. Every homestead exemption requires that you own the house, live in it and claim it as your legal residence as of January 1, which rules out rentals.

  • Stephens-Day and the state floating homestead exemption: the county awards whichever gives the larger saving, then adds other exemptions you qualify for.
  • Special Chatham senior exemption: age 65 by January 1, combined net income of $10,000 or less, $30,000 off county and school assessed value, plus relief from most state assessments.
  • Senior school exemption: age 62, combined net income of $25,000 or less.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: a VA letter showing 100% service-connected disability, with the amount subject to annual change.
  • Year's Support: when a spouse or minor child petitions Probate Court within two years after a death, the court can award tax relief for the year named in the petition.

Bring a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration in your name, with matching mailing and homestead addresses. An application that arrives inside the 45 day notice window counts for that year, and a later one waits for the next year. Buying a different home or changing the deed means filing again.

Who pays the Chatham County bill when a house sells?

The seller is billed because Georgia taxes whoever held title when the year began. A sale in March or August does not shift the bill to the buyer, and state revenue guidance rules out any refund for a partial year.

Any split of the year is therefore a private deal struck at the closing table. If the sale lands between the June and November deadlines, the second installment is still open, so ask the closing attorney whether it is paid at the table or credited to the buyer. A delinquent balance belongs in the payoff so the lien does not follow the title.

Your homestead exemption does not travel with the house, so the new owner files again. If the house came to you by inheritance, look again at the Year's Support option above, and ask the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 for a payoff before choosing a closing day.

More questions about Chatham County, GA Property Tax Guide

Do Chatham County owners pay once or twice a year?

Twice for real property. One half is due June 1 and the other November 15, and personal property comes due in a single November 15 payment.

Which Chatham County office answers valuation questions?

The Board of Assessors, at 912-652-7271. The Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 takes payments but cannot change a value or a millage rate.

Is there any appeal once the 45 days run out?

Generally no. The deadline counts from the notice date, and the Board of Assessors can tell you whether anything applies to a notice that never reached you.

Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?

No. Whoever filed keeps the exemption, so a purchaser has to apply again at the Board of Assessors with a Georgia license and a matching vehicle registration.

Will I owe tax if I sell in the fall?

Yes, for that year, because you held title in January. If the November installment is still open at closing, the payoff or proration appears on the closing statement.

Where do Chattooga County property taxes get paid and who sets the value?

Billing and collection sit with the Chattooga County Tax Commissioner, who has no say over values or millage rates. The Board of Tax Assessors, appointed by the county commissioner, appraises property and approves every exemption claimed. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears appeals. The millage rate itself comes from the county commissioner for county tax and the Board of Education for school tax.

  • Tax Commissioner: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747; postal box: P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. Hours run 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM Monday through Friday, and the office is closed on Wednesdays.
  • Bills can be searched and paid online at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • A mailed payment is accepted with a United States Postal Service postmark, but not with a metered postmark.

Tax bills go to the homeowner and only sometimes to the mortgage company, so forward your bill to the lender if your taxes are escrowed.

What should a seller picture when thinking of Chattooga County?

Chattooga County sits in Georgia's northwest corner. It was created on December 28, 1838 and was named for the Chattooga River. It covers 314 square miles, of which 313 are land. Summerville serves as the seat, with Trion, Lyerly and Menlo as the other incorporated cities. Walker and Floyd counties lie to the north and southeast, and a corner of the Chattahoochee National Forest reaches into the county. The Summerville micropolitan area is part of the Rome-Summerville combined statistical area.

History left landmarks here. The 1863 Battle of Trion Factory was fought along present-day First Street, and the Old Trion Cemetery holds graves of soldiers killed in that fight. Several county properties carry national historic listings, which is worth knowing because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

Two public school systems serve the county: the Chattooga County School System and the Trion City School System. Census QuickFacts estimates 25,300 residents for 2025, close to the 24,965 counted in 2020 and below the 26,015 of 2010. On the 2020 to 2024 survey, a typical owner-held home is worth $115,600, a typical rent is $790, a typical household takes in $50,285, and 66.8% of homes are owned by their occupants. Only 2 building permits were issued in 2025, and workers average a 28.1 minute trip to the job.

What is the Chattooga County payment deadline, and what does paying late cost?

December 1 is the usual deadline for land, buildings and business equipment. Interest runs from the day following that deadline, and a 5% penalty is added once 120 days pass. A homesteaded parcel owing less than $500 escapes the 120-day penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, with interest of 1% added monthly if they are late.

Unpaid taxes can be levied on, though the Tax Commissioner describes that as a last resort. Once a bill is more than 30 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can be entered in the Superior Court clerk's records. Those entries are public, credit bureaus may use them, and the tax office cannot control that.

Listings of excess funds from past tax sales are posted on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

Which homestead exemptions does Chattooga County offer?

The Tax Commissioner lists state exemptions and local ones that replace the state amount when larger. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office. Filing is open all year, but only an application in hand by April 1 takes effect that year.

Homestead exemptions listed by the Chattooga County Tax Commissioner
ExemptionWho qualifiesWhat it does
StandardAny qualifying homeowner$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,000Sliding 20% to 100% share of assessed value, county tax only, for the residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value, school tax only
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

The office cautions that the floating exemption can raise a bill at first, since it replaces other state and county exemptions already in place. Service-connected disabled veterans have their own exemption, and so do unremarried widows of service members killed in armed conflict and of firefighters or peace officers who died on duty.

Can Chattooga County owners defer tax or get a lower assessment?

Owners 62 or older whose gross household income is up to $15,000 can defer, but not escape, tax on a homestead. The deferred amount generally stays due until ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, which means a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Agricultural land used in bona fide farming can be assessed at 30% instead of 40%, and conservation use property is valued at its current use. Both require a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years.
  • Qualifying historic buildings can receive preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it.
  • Manufacturers can claim the Freeport exemption on raw goods, goods in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, by applying with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1.

What is the route for contesting a Chattooga County value?

The deadline to contest is 45 days after the notice date. Your appeal lands first with the assessors, who look at their value again. If you remain unhappy, the next stop is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a final written notice sent or filed with the assessors carries the case to Superior Court.

Grounds for an appeal are taxability, value, or uniformity compared with neighboring properties. A complaint that the tax is too high does not qualify, since the county commissioner and Board of Education set that. Mobile home owners who dispute a revised value have 30 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

Returns are accepted until April 1. After a first return, real property returns carry forward unless something changes, but personal property returns are needed every year.

What tax points matter when selling in Chattooga County?

Whoever holds title on January 1 owes tax for the full year, and state revenue guidance confirms there is no refund for part-year owners. A closing attorney should divide the year on the settlement statement.

Your exemption stays behind with you, and a purchaser moving in must file by April 1. If you need a copy of a deed for the closing file, the Clerk of Superior Court keeps a deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse. Because property in this county is lower priced than the other three Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can matter to a sale, so pull a payoff early.

More questions about Chattooga County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the usual Chattooga County deadline?

December 1 for land, buildings and business equipment. Mobile and manufactured homes run on an April 1 schedule.

Can I visit the Chattooga tax office on a Wednesday?

No. The Tax Commissioner's office is closed on Wednesdays and open 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM the other weekdays.

How costly is a late payment in Chattooga County?

Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5% penalty applies after 120 days, except for homesteaded property with liability under $500.

Does a Chattooga County homestead exemption need yearly renewal?

No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?

Ask the Superior Court clerk, whose deed room is in the Chattooga County Courthouse.

Which Cherokee County office sends the bill, and which one sets the value?

Cherokee County splits the work between two offices on the same stretch of Marietta Highway in Canton. The Tax Commissioner handles real estate, personal property, public utility, timber, motor vehicle and mobile home taxes, then distributes the collections to state, county, school and city governments. The Tax Assessors' Office decides what your property is worth and which exemptions you receive.

  • Tax Commissioner: 678-493-6400, cherokeecountytax.com. Main office at 2780 Marietta Hwy, Canton, and an annex at 155 Towne Lake Pkwy, Woodstock, both open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Assessors' Office: 678-493-6120, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton. Returns are filed here during the season that ends April 1.
  • City tax offices bill separately inside Ball Ground, Canton, Holly Springs, Mountain Park, Nelson, Waleska and Woodstock, so check whether your address is incorporated.

Cherokee County's Assessors Office posts a public notice that appraisal staff may visit a property after an appeal, a new return, new construction or a conservation use application. The visiting appraisers carry county photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and answering their questions is voluntary.

What do sellers in Cherokee County, Georgia need to know about the county?

Cherokee County was created by the General Assembly on December 26, 1831, and Canton became the seat after the early county seat of Etowah was renamed. Growth took off after the first phase of Interstate 575 opened in 1979. The freeway bisects the county from Kennesaw through Woodstock, Holly Springs and Canton to Ball Ground, and the southern end nearest Atlanta is the most densely settled.

The county covers 434 square miles, of which 422 are land. Lake Allatoona fills much of the southwest corner, and the north climbs toward the foothills, with Bear Mountain at 2,297 feet the highest listed summit. Reinhardt University is in Waleska, Chattahoochee Technical College has campuses in Woodstock and Canton, and one school district, the Cherokee County School District, serves every address.

QuickFacts counts 299,273 residents for 2025, which is 12.2% above the 2020 base. Its 2020 to 2024 figures give $435,100 as the middle value of an owner-held house, $108,115 as the middle household income and 77.3% as the owner-occupancy rate. Commutes average 31.3 minutes, and builders pulled 1,524 permits in 2025.

What is the Cherokee County due date for property tax?

Bills go out in September and the payment is due November 15. Whatever remains unpaid after that is delinquent, and the Tax Commissioner reminds owners that a lien then attaches to the property. Mobile home bills are mailed each January with an April 1 deadline.

The county's 2026 rates, as the Tax Commissioner prints them, are in the table. One mill equals a dollar for each thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of market value in Georgia.

The fire levy is the reason bills differ between a Canton address and an unincorporated one such as Hickory Flat or Lake Arrowhead. Your city may add its own levy on top of the county figures above.

How can an owner challenge a Cherokee County value?

Put your appeal in writing and deliver it to the assessors inside the 45 day period that starts when the assessment notice is mailed. The state's uniform form asks you to choose a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration, and the grounds may be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

The county appraisal staff values property with sales comparison, cost and income approaches and tests the results statistically by area, neighborhood and class of property. A good appeal answers those methods with your own evidence.

  • Recent closed sales of similar houses nearby, with dates and prices.
  • Photos and repair estimates that show condition problems the record may not reflect.
  • A copy of your settlement statement or warranty deed if you bought the property recently.

Complaints about the size of the tax are outside an appeal, because assessors do not set millage rates. The governing bodies named on your bill do that.

Where does a Cherokee County owner apply for a homestead exemption?

Apply in person at the Tax Assessors' Office with a valid Georgia driver's license or ID showing the current address of the property. Bring your settlement statement or warranty deed too, since staff print and complete the application when you arrive.

The state's standard homestead exemption applies to an owner-occupied primary residence, and the county can add to it. State revenue guidance adds that an application is taken all year but must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year, and that skipping the application waives the exemption. Ask the Assessors' Office which Cherokee County exemptions for seniors, disabled veterans or surviving spouses fit your situation, since the amounts change.

An exemption follows the person who applied, so a buyer starts over with a new application.

What does selling do to a Cherokee County tax bill?

Georgia taxes whoever holds title on New Year's Day, and the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner says the law gives its office no way to prorate tax for part of a year. The buyer and seller must agree on any split when they close.

A buyer who closes in the fall will not automatically receive a bill. The Tax Commissioner asks to receive the closing statement so the bill can be reissued in the new owner's name, which works for purchases completed before November 15 of that tax year. Should October 1 pass with no bill in hand, phone 678-493-6400 or print one from the website. Even when the bill stays in the seller's name, the lien follows the property if it turns delinquent.

A properly completed PT-61 transfer form on file at the Superior Court clerk's office can stand in for a new real property return in the sale year, as long as nothing was subdivided or built.

What happens when Cherokee County property goes to a tax sale?

A tax sale buyer gets a tax deed but cannot move in, build, or remove tenants right away. The owner, a creditor or any other interested party can buy the property back within 12 months.

The redemption price is the bid, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus special assessments, plus a premium of 20% of the amount for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each year after that, plus sheriff and advertising costs. After 12 months the buyer may serve a notice of foreclosure of the right to redeem by certified mail to the recorded owner and each interest holder, and the notice must also be printed weekly for four straight weeks in the county newspaper.

Should an auction bring in more than is owed, the the surplus is held separately, and O.C.G.A. 48-4-5 lets the owner of record at that time, plus security deed holders, claim it. The county adds that claimants are not required to pay or hire any third party.

More questions about Cherokee County, GA Property Tax Guide

When must a Cherokee County bill be paid?

November 15. Bills are mailed in September, and taxes not paid by that date are considered delinquent.

Will the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner prorate at a sale?

No. The office has no legal provision for prorating partial-year ownership, so any split is settled by the parties at closing.

Where can I file for homestead in Cherokee County?

File in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton, with a Georgia license or ID showing the property address.

How long can an owner redeem after a tax sale?

Twelve months from the sale date. After that the buyer may start the foreclosure of the right to redeem by sending notice.

How can I find my Cherokee County tax bill if I did not receive one?

Call the Tax Commissioner at 678-493-6400 or print a copy from cherokeecountytax.com. The office suggests doing so if a bill has not arrived by October 1.

How is Athens-Clarke County property tax organized?

Clarke County and the City of Athens operate as one government, so the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division handles the bill for the whole county. Its page explains that the money supports the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

Real estate and business personal property taxes are generally due by October 20. If a bill goes unpaid, the property can be levied on and eventually sold. The division describes a 5% penalty added every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a possible total of 20%, on top of interest.

  • Land and buildings are taxed where they are located, per O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Taxable value is set at 40% of market value, with exceptions written into law (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Standing timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

What sets Clarke County apart from the rest of Georgia?

Clarke is Georgia's smallest county by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. It lies in the Piedmont and drains mostly to the Upper Oconee River. The General Assembly carved it out of Jackson County on December 5, 1801 and named it for Elijah Clarke. Watkinsville served as seat until November 1871, when county offices moved to Athens. Athens and Winterville are the cities, and the town of Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County.

Its mills and railroad, which reached Athens in 1841, made it second only to Savannah and Chatham County in manufacturing investment during the 1840s. Today the University of Georgia shapes the housing market. Census QuickFacts counts 129,921 people for 2025, just 1.0% above the 2020 base, and households average 2.19 people with 16.1% of residents under 18.

Just 41.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, the lowest share among the four Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, and typical rent is $1,219. An owner-held home has a middle value of $298,900, the middle household income is $53,625, and 73.5% of people stayed at the same address over the prior year. Many Athens houses are therefore rentals, and investor-owned homes receive the same bill as any other.

What are the steps to contest an Athens-Clarke County value?

Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, with 45 days counted from the mailing of the assessment notice. If the assessors leave the value alone, the file moves to the Board of Equalization on its own. The Athens-Clarke assessors answer questions at 706-613-3140.

Appeal timeline posted by Athens-Clarke County and the Georgia Department of Revenue
StepTiming
Written appeal delivered to the assessors45 days from notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing date15 days after the appeal reaches that board
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that letter
Appeal to Superior CourtWritten, 30 days after the Board of Equalization rules

At the hearing the Board of Assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling is sent to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.
