Which DeKalb County offices value and bill property?

Two separate offices split the job. The Property Appraisal Department sets what your home is worth. The Tax Commissioner's Office then sends the bill and takes payment. The commissioner's office states plainly that it has no say over the assessed amount.

The DeKalb County Board of Commissioners adopts the millage rate each July. The Tax Commissioner's central property tax office is staffed weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. at 404-298-4000. The Property Appraisal Department can be reached at 404-371-0841 about a value or a missing assessment notice.

Cities add their own levies. Atlanta, Brookhaven, Chamblee, Clarkston, Decatur, Doraville, Dunwoody, Lithonia, Pine Lake, Stone Mountain, Stonecrest and Tucker appear on the commissioner's exemption page with local rules, and Avondale does not award local exemptions.

What dates matter on a DeKalb County tax bill?

Bills go out in August, and the county's installment dates are September 30 and November 15. Paying in one lump sum means paying by September 30. If a deadline would be a Saturday or Sunday, the county pushes it to Monday, so the 2026 second installment landed on November 16.

The penalty for a late first or second installment is 5%, and a postmark after the date triggers it. Metered and kiosk postage dates are not accepted as proof, so near a deadline ask the post office to hand-cancel the envelope. Online payments must arrive by midnight on the deadline, Eastern time.

Balances still open 120 days after the deadline pick up a further 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days. Accounts with a balance after December 31 become subject to a lien.

Table source: DeKalb County Tax Commissioner's Office, tax bill, payment and exemption pages.

What are the ways to pay a DeKalb tax bill?

Current-year payments can be mailed to DeKalb County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division, P.O. Box 117545, Atlanta, GA 30368-7545. Prior-year payments go to the Delinquent Collections Division, P.O. Box 100001, Decatur, GA 30031-7001. Checks must be in U.S. funds.

  • Phone: 678-501-7995, with no fee for an e-check
  • Online: the county's GovHub payment portal, searchable by parcel ID, address or owner name
  • Card: a 2.31% fee with a $1.50 minimum per transaction; international and commercial cards add 3.95%
  • A returned payment costs 5% of the check with a $30 minimum

Partial payments are accepted, and the first installment must be paid before the second. The portal handles real estate and business personal property accounts only; mobile home, public utility and heavy equipment accounts go by mail or to a county counter.

What is the route for contesting a DeKalb County assessment?

Read the May assessment notice and count 45 days from the date printed on it. Should the current-year value look wrong, the instructions for filing are included with the notice. State law lets the appeal rest on value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption, filed in writing with the board of assessors.

The Georgia Department of Revenue describes three tracks: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer for non-homestead property valued above $500,000, or arbitration for value. A taxpayer still unhappy can file a notice of appeal for superior court inside 30 days of the decision, once taxes equal to the last year's amount are paid, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-29 requires.

An unresolved appeal does not stop the bill. DeKalb issues a temporary value, normally the lesser of the last final value or 85 percent of the current value. You can ask in your appeal to be billed at 100 percent instead. Interest applies to appeal differences settled after November 15, and the commissioner cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311(e)(6) for the process.

What homestead exemptions can a DeKalb homeowner claim?

To claim the basic homestead exemption you must occupy the house as your main home on January 1 and hold title. It also asks for every vehicle registered at that address, a Georgia ID or license showing the property address, income taxes filed from the home, and no homestead claim anywhere else. Applications are not automatic, and neither a lender nor a closing attorney files one for you.

  • Special exemptions exist for owners 62 and older, disabled residents and disabled veterans, and several depend on income
  • An applicant must already hold a homestead exemption to add a special one
  • Applications are taken in person year-round and online from January 1 to mid-July
  • A county assessment freeze is available when you apply by April 1, and it does not cover school, city or state taxes

City programs differ. Brookhaven lists a $40,000 basic exemption, Chamblee $50,000, and Doraville $10,000 plus a 2.5 mill reduction. Clarkston gives homeowners 65 and older an extra $20,000. Decatur and Stone Mountain take applications at city hall rather than through the county.

Who owes the tax when a DeKalb County house sells mid-year?

Taxes follow the property, and the state sets the year-long liability at January 1. The state's FAQ puts the full year on whoever held the parcel on January 1, however soon after the sale closes. The January 1 owner of record gets the mailed bill, and a buyer whose deed is recorded afterward gets one too.

Who actually pays is a contract matter. The tax commissioner tells new owners to check with the closing attorney, mortgage company or escrow agent, or read the closing statement. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the parcel, and DeKalb does not send bills to mortgage lenders, so an escrow account does not remove your duty to confirm payment.

Before listing, pull your parcel on the payment portal and confirm nothing is open. A parcel with a balance after December 31 can be liened, and the commissioner describes the lien, called a FiFa, as the first step toward a tax sale. Sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month in front of the DeKalb County Courthouse, and buyers pay with cash, a bank-issued cashier's check or a wire. Money left over after taxes and costs is held as excess funds until an entitled party claims it.

What do DeKalb County's Census numbers say about taxpayers?

QuickFacts shows 774,394 people in mid-2025, a 1.3% gain on the April 2020 estimate base. There are 287,239 households of 2.63 people on average, and seniors make up 15.1% of the population. Land area is 267.74 square miles with 2,854.9 people per square mile as of 2020.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,979, those without one $715, and 12.7% of people live in poverty. Owners on fixed incomes should look at the senior and income-based exemptions on the commissioner's page.

More questions about DeKalb County, GA Property Tax Guide

When is the second DeKalb County property tax installment due?

November 15, shifted when it lands on a Saturday or Sunday. In 2026 it fell on a Sunday, so the date became November 16. A late payment carries a 5% penalty if the envelope is not postmarked by the due date.

Which office explains a DeKalb assessed value?

The Property Appraisal Department, at 404-371-0841. The Tax Commissioner's Office, at 404-298-4000, handles billing and has no authority over the value.

Can I pay my DeKalb tax bill in installments?

Yes. The county splits the bill into two installments, due September 30 and November 15, and the first must be paid before the second. Paying everything at once means paying by September 30.

Does the DeKalb homestead exemption apply automatically?

No. You must file an application, and a missed filing waives the exemption for that year under O.C.G.A. 48-5-45(a)(2). You can apply for the following year if you miss the cutoff.

What follows when DeKalb property taxes go unpaid?

Penalties and interest build, a lien can be filed after December 31, and the lien is the first step toward a tax sale. Pay the balance with fees and the lien is marked satisfied.

Where is Dodge County, Georgia, and which towns does it hold?

Dodge County lies in the southern part of Georgia, mostly in the Ocmulgee River watershed, and Eastman is both the seat of government and the biggest city. Wikipedia gives a total area of 503 square miles, of which the Census Bureau counts 495.96 as land.

The legislature organized the county on October 26, 1870, carving it mostly from Laurens County with smaller pieces of Pulaski, Montgomery and Telfair. The Macon and Brunswick Railroad had been built the year before, and towns grew up along the line far from the old county seat at Hawkinsville. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns, and Empire is a census-designated place that crosses into Bleckley County.

Highways include US 23, US 280, US 341 and the US 319 and 441 corridor, plus State Routes 46 and 117 and several others. The Heart of Georgia Regional Airport lies three miles east of Eastman on State Route 46 and houses an aviation campus of Middle Georgia State College. A seller in Dodge County is usually dealing with a rural or small-town parcel, and the county's own offices handle nearly every step.

Who do Dodge County owners call about property tax?

On the county's services page, the Tax Commissioner is 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors are 478-374-8122. County government works out of 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the clerk of courts answers at 478-374-2871.

State guidance divides the roles the same way statewide: the commissioner takes payments and, in most counties, homestead filings, while the assessors own the appraised value and appeal questions. The county website has a Tax Payments link for paying online. The cities and towns inside the county publish these numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

If your house sits inside a city, ask both the county and the city clerk whether city tax comes on a separate bill.

Has the 2026 assessment appeal window in Dodge County closed?

Dodge County mailed its 2026 tax assessment notices on June 19, 2026, and August 3, 2026 was the final day to appeal. For the 2026 digest that window is shut, so a seller who missed it lives with the 2026 value and watches for next year's notice.

The county announcement says appeals could be filed by email, by U.S. mail, or online through the appeal module on the qPublic site. Anyone who did not receive a notice, or who has a question about one, was told to call the assessors at 478-374-8122. The notice arrives every year, and the 45 days run from the day it was mailed, so mark the mailing date when it comes.

The county also raised the processing fee for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels to $30.00 for new, renewal and continuation covenants, effective July 1, 2025. Owners of farm or timber land should ask the assessors whether a covenant is recorded on the parcel before listing.

What are my appeal options once I file in Dodge County?

The state's uniform appeal form makes you pick one of three tracks, and the completed form is sent to the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors. State revenue staff have no power to override a local value.

TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemptionAssessors may revise the notice; if not, a hearing is scheduled and a decision follows
Hearing officerValue or uniformity of non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000Decision, then superior court if still disputed
ArbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer submits a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment; hearing scheduled within 30 days

Table source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Filing a Property Tax Appeal.

  • Going to superior court takes a written notice to the assessors inside 30 days after the ruling
  • The board schedules a settlement conference after your appeal, with notice inside 45 days
  • The court will not hear the case until last year's amount of tax is paid
  • A final value at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure lets the taxpayer recover costs and attorney's fees

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

The state default is December 20, and a county may instead choose December 1, November 15 or installments. Interest also waits until 60 days after the bill was postmarked. Whatever date your Dodge bill prints controls, and the commissioner at 478-374-2154 can replace a lost bill.

Delinquent balances can pick up penalties on top of interest. Ask the tax commissioner what your parcel owes before a closing, request the figure in writing, and give a copy to whoever runs the closing.

A return of value can be filed from January 1 through April 1. An owner who paid last year and files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value, so most homeowners never file one.

Does Dodge County offer homestead exemptions?

State revenue records show no local homestead exemptions in Dodge County beyond the statewide ones. An application can go in any time after the house becomes your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of benefit.

Skipping the application forfeits that year's exemption. The standard state exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value, which is set at 40 percent of fair market value. The county's tax commissioner or assessors take the application, depending on how Dodge handles it, so ask which window applies.

Refunds exist for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim due inside three years of payment. A seller does not get part of a year back, since ownership on January 1 fixes liability for the whole year.

What should a Dodge County seller know about taxes at closing?

The January 1 owner is liable for that year's bill, so a fall sale still carries a full year of tax. The sales contract decides how the year is split, and the closing statement shows who pays what.

Two recorded items matter at closing. A security deed on a long-term loan must be recorded in the county within 90 days, and an intangible tax applies to it, collected by the superior court clerk in most counties. A sale also triggers Georgia's transfer tax, which falls on the seller by law and is figured on the sale price at the clerk's office. A county tax lien is entered on the general execution docket at the clerk's office, which is where a title search finds it.

How big and how priced is the Dodge County housing stock?

QuickFacts lists 19,663 residents for 2025, a 1.7% drop since April 2020, along with 8,643 housing units and just 5 building permits for the year.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 70.6%
  • Middle home value: $118,100
  • Median gross rent: $723
  • Median household income: $51,587
  • Residents 65 and older: 20.8%
  • People per square mile (2020): 40.2

For comparison, the same table gives $357,800 for DeKalb County, so a Dodge County house sits at a much lower price point. Check the parcel's tax status before you list, since a back-tax balance weighs more against a lower sale price.

More questions about Dodge County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which number reaches Dodge County's tax office?

Call the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

Can I still appeal my 2026 Dodge County assessment?

For the 2026 digest, yes. Notices were mailed June 19, 2026, and August 3 was the final day was August 3, 2026. Watch for the next annual notice and count 45 days from its mailing date.

Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?

No. State records list none beyond the statewide exemption, which owners request through the county tax office by April 1 of the first benefit year.

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?

Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.

What kind of county is Dooly County, Georgia?

Dooly County is a rural county in central Georgia with Vienna as its seat. The legislature created it on May 15, 1821, from land ceded by the Creek Nation, and named it for Colonel John Dooly, a Revolutionary War fighter. Crisp County was cut out of its original borders, along with parts of Macon, Pulaski, Turner, Wilcox and Worth counties, so its original borders covered far more ground than the present county.

Wikipedia reports 397 square miles in the upper Atlantic coastal plain. Most of the western two-thirds drains to the Flint River, the northeast and east drain to the Ocmulgee, and the far southeast corner reaches the Alapaha basin. Neighbors are Houston, Pulaski, Wilcox, Crisp, Sumter and Macon counties.

Lilly, Byromville, Pinehurst, Unadilla and Vienna are the cities, and Dooling, Drayton and Findlay are towns. Unadilla is the largest. The 2020 census counted no urban residents at all, so nearly every sale here is a farm, small-town or acreage property, and the county offices in Vienna handle most steps.

Where are the Dooly County tax offices and what are their hours?

Three county offices matter to a seller, and the first two share a building at 105 W. Cotton Street in Vienna.

OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1; mailing address P.O. Box 371229-268-4212Mon to Thu, 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m.; closed Fri
Assessors Office105 W. Cotton Street, Room 2229-268-4719Weekdays, 8 to noon and 1 to 5
Commissioners' Office113 N. Third Street, Room 1229-268-4228Call for hours

Table source: Dooly County, Georgia, official website.

The tax commissioner's page also links an online payment portal and a tag renewal link to the Georgia DRIVES site. Because the commissioner's office closes on Fridays, plan any payoff request or in-person payment for Monday through Thursday.

Did Dooly County raise its millage rate for 2025?

The county posted a notice that its commissioners had tentatively adopted a 2025 millage rate requiring a 2.62% increase in property tax revenue. The proposed rate was 17.45 mills, up 0.445 mills, against a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills.

Three public hearings were set at the commissioners' office on 113 N. Third Street: two on Thursday, September 4, at 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and one on Friday, September 19, at 10:00 a.m. Those hearing dates have passed, so a seller should ask the tax commissioner for the final rate that appears on the current bill. The notice itself worked out two sample increases, about $25.81 for a homestead with a fair market value of $150,000 and about $26.70 for a non-homestead property of the same value.

Georgia sets assessed value at 40 percent of fair market value, and the millage rate applies to that assessed figure. The notice covers the county's own levy; ask the tax commissioner which school and city rates appear on a given parcel's bill.

How does a Dooly County owner contest a value?

Begin by phoning the Assessors Office at 229-268-4719. Each year the board mails a notice of assessment, and an owner who rejects the stated fair market value gets 45 days, counted from the mailing date, to file. The postmark has to fall inside that window.

  • Reasons include taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption
  • On the state's PT-311A form you choose among equalization board, hearing officer and arbitration
  • Email is allowed only if the board has a written policy accepting electronic service
  • The state revenue department does not receive the form

The notice itself carries the filing instructions, so keep the envelope or note the postmark date. A refund for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must be requested in writing within three years of payment.

What returns and exemptions apply to Dooly County property?

The county tax office takes returns of value in the first quarter, January 1 to April 1. Silence counts as a repeat of last year's value for anyone who paid then. For homestead, apply once the house is your primary residence and before April 1 of the first benefit year; a missed application forfeits that year.

The Department of Revenue's Dooly page describes the state exemptions without a local add-on, so ask the commissioner whether the county offers anything beyond them. The commissioner's page links a tax information pamphlet with homestead details. Ask the office for a current copy before you rely on older figures.

Voters can also exempt commercial and industrial inventory under the freeport exemption, which is requested from the board of assessors during the return period. That rule affects owners of a shop or warehouse building, not a typical house.

What do mobile home and vehicle rules mean for a Dooly County sale?

Mobile homes follow their own track. State rules call for a location permit from the tax commissioner within 30 days of placement, renewed every year in the first quarter. A mobile home sitting in the county on January 1 is returned for taxation by April 1, together with the permit.

  • A mobile home on land you are selling needs its permit and return current
  • Vehicle registration renews with the commissioner in the 30 days ending on the owner's birthday
  • A newly bought vehicle needs registration within 30 days
  • Only the tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax

Ask the tax commissioner to confirm the status of any mobile home on the parcel before a buyer's lender does.

What taxes come due when a Dooly County house sells?

Whoever holds title on January 1 carries that whole year's ad valorem tax, even after a spring or summer sale. How the bill is divided is a contract term, and the closing statement should show the proration.

At recording, the seller owes Georgia's real estate transfer tax. The revenue department publishes the schedule and the closing agent calculates it. A long-term note secured by land also triggers an intangible recording tax, with the security instrument recorded locally inside 90 days. Tax liens, whether county or state, are entered on the clerk's general execution docket.

The usual state due date is December 20 unless the county picks another, and interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Request a payoff figure from the commissioner for your closing agent.

What does the Census say about Dooly County homes?

The 2025 estimate is 11,156 people, off 0.5% since April 2020, living among 4,906 housing units. Builders pulled only 22 permits in 2025.

  • Owner-occupied share, 2020 to 2024: 64.7%
  • Typical owned-home value: $107,400
  • Median gross rent: $758
  • Median household income: $60,987
  • Residents living in poverty: 25.6%
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.1%
  • Households with broadband: 76.6%

Wikipedia's reading of the 2020 census shows 4,762 housing units with 15.0% vacant, and county population fell from 14,918 in 2010 to 11,208 in 2020.

More questions about Dooly County, GA Property Tax Guide

When is the Dooly County tax office open?

Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Friday. Find it at 105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1, Vienna, or call 229-268-4212.

What is the deadline to dispute a Dooly County value?

Forty-five days after the notice went in the mail. File in writing with the county board of tax assessors rather than the state, and call 229-268-4719 with questions.

Does Dooly County have a homestead exemption?

The state exemption is available, and the revenue department's Dooly page describes no local add-on, so ask the commissioner about anything more. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since a missed application waives that year.

What was Dooly County's proposed 2025 millage rate?

The county's notice proposed 17.45 mills, an increase of 0.445 mills over a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills. Check your current bill with the tax commissioner for the rate in force.

Who owes the tax if my Dooly County house sells midyear?

The person who owned it January 1 is liable for the full year under Georgia law. A contract can pass part to the buyer, so check the proration on the closing statement.

Who handles property tax in Dougherty County, Georgia?

Dougherty County puts collection and valuation under one roof. The Tax Department answers to an appointed tax director, and no elected tax commissioner sits above it. Returns arrive there, and the office collects ad valorem tax on behalf of the county government, Albany city government, the school system and the state.

Its bills reach real estate, cars, business equipment, mobile homes and timber. The Board of Assessors operates inside the department and assigns each parcel its value. A parcel search runs through qPublic, and the county news page links a short video that walks through it.

  • Value, notice of assessment or appeal: Board of Assessors, 229-431-2130 or DocoAssessor@dougherty.ga.us.
  • County millage rate: voted on by the county commissioners.
  • School millage rate: voted on separately by the school board.
  • Paying a bill, bill dates and a payoff number for a closing: the Tax Department.

What did the 2026 revaluation change for Dougherty County owners?

Albany-area owners opened 2026 notices that came out of the county's first full revaluation in over a decade, and plenty of values moved sharply. A county release from August 31, 2026 repeats one point: the notice is an assessment and carries no payment due. It shows market value, homestead information and appeal steps. Taxes follow once appeals close and the digest and rates are final.

Commissioners explained at that meeting that valuation belongs to the assessors, while the commission handles the county budget and its own rate. They added that a bigger value need not mean a proportionally bigger county bill.

House Bill 581 adds a second layer. It limits annual growth in the taxable value of qualifying homesteads for each participating taxing authority, and counties, cities and school districts each had a choice to opt out. The local school board did opt out after public hearings, and the school system says existing homestead exemptions stay in place. A May 2026 state revenue briefing says SB 33, the HOME Act of 2026, ends the opt-out. The statewide floating exemption then applies from January 1, 2027, with 2026 values as the starting baseline. Ask the Tax Department what that means for your school bill.

The county says it will keep posting explanations of assessments, appeals, homestead exemptions and the millage-setting process on its website and social media pages.

How does a Dougherty County assessment appeal work?

The appeal is a written filing to the Board of Assessors, due 45 days after the notice's mailing date. For 2026 the county published a cutoff of 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026, which is now behind us. Each future notice has its own mailing date, and the clock starts there.

State guidance lets an appeal argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it uses a single statewide form. You declare your preferred route on that form, and the route decides who hears the case.

  • The county Board of Equalization.
  • A hearing officer.
  • An arbitrator.

County leaders encouraged owners whose value doubled or tripled to appeal, and the assessors answer questions at 229-431-2130. Useful evidence includes a recent sale of a comparable Albany house, contractor estimates and photos of damage.

Which exemptions and special assessments apply in Dougherty County?

A homestead exemption goes to people who held title and lived in the house on January 1. The state now allows filing through the 45-day appeal window as well as the old April 1 deadline. The standard state version removes $2,000 from the 40 percent assessed value for county and school tax, and an age 65 version removes $4,000 from county tax where household income stays within $10,000 for the prior year, after the retirement income exclusions the state describes.

Rural land follows separate rules. The Board of Assessors lists three programs, each requiring an application between January 1 and April 1 and a $25 fee:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment: bona fide farmland is assessed at 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment: qualifying farm, timber, sensitive and transitional residential land is valued by current use.
  • Forest Land Protection Act: an exemption for land used in good faith to produce trees, timber or wood fiber.

Eligible owners are individuals, family farm corporations, estates, trusts and non-profits. They commit to the use for 10 years, and a single owner may enroll no more than 2,000 acres statewide. Check with the Tax Department for any local exemptions Dougherty County adds beyond the state list.

What do the Dougherty County numbers look like?

Dougherty County has lost residents since 2010, and renters now outnumber owners. Georgia's legislature created the county from Baker County in 1853. The county lists 326 square miles of land, quail plantations, Flint River recreation and cypress swamps among its draws. Albany State University and Albany Technical College supply higher education, while the Albany Civil Rights Institute and the Flint RiverQuarium bring in visitors.

Albany and Dougherty County housing profile (Census Bureau QuickFacts)
MeasureFigure
Residents counted in 201094,565
Residents estimated for mid-202582,616
Homes and apartments, mid-202540,638
Share of homes lived in by owners (2020 to 2024 survey)45.3%
Middle value of an owned home$134,400
Middle monthly rent$935
Middle household income$49,044
Share of residents below the poverty line23.6%

Owners live in fewer than half of occupied homes here. The Census Bureau recorded 32 building permits in the county for 2025.

What happens to the property tax bill when you sell a Dougherty County house?

Deed and lien searches run through the Clerk of Superior Court. Its real estate records can be searched online, and the office sits in the Judicial Building at 225 Pine Avenue, Suite 126, open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday at 229-431-2198. Pull the record on your own parcel before you list so a forgotten lien does not surprise anyone at closing.

Georgia assigns a year's tax to whoever held the property on January 1 and refunds nothing for a partial year. A seller who closes in March still faces a bill covering twelve months, so the purchase contract and settlement statement decide how the cost is divided. State guidance describes a typical 60-day payment window ending December 20, but the Tax Department supplies Dougherty County's actual dates.

Before you list, gather three things:

  • Your parcel number from qPublic and a copy of the 2026 notice.
  • A written balance from the Tax Department that shows any older unpaid years.
  • Your homestead status, which follows the January 1 owner and resident.

Albany houses with deferred repairs, tenants or an open estate sometimes sell as-is for cash, with the tax balance paid out of the proceeds. Liens are filed with the clerk, so confirm the balance and any recorded lien before you sign.

More questions about Dougherty County, GA Property Tax Guide

Does a Dougherty County assessment notice ask me to pay?

No. It reports market value, homestead details and appeal steps. Tax is calculated later, once appeals end, the digest is final and the county, city and school rates are adopted.

Is the 2026 Dougherty appeal window still open?

No. Appeals on the 2026 notices closed at 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026. Later notices will show their own mailing dates and a fresh 45 days.

Which board votes on the millage rate in Dougherty County?

The commissioners vote on the county rate and the school board votes on the school rate. Assessors only determine value. The county rate comes after appeals end and the digest is complete.

Is the Dougherty school system in the HB 581 exemption?

It opted out after public hearings and says existing homestead exemptions remain. A May 2026 state briefing says SB 33 removes that option from January 1, 2027, so ask the Tax Department how it will reach your bill.

Do I still owe the full year's bill after selling in Albany?

Yes, on paper. Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible and gives no partial-year refund. The settlement statement usually splits the cost with the buyer, so get the balance from the Tax Department first.

Which Douglas County offices touch your tax bill?

Douglas County divides the work between an appraisal team and an elected collector. Appraisal sets values and handles appeals on behalf of the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and takes homestead forms, and the commissioner's website walks through the bill, notices, exemptions and the delinquent list.

  • Appraisal Department: write to 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134 or call 770-920-7228. Walk-in filing is on the annex's second floor at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: ground-level office in the Government Annex, serving the public weekdays except for a lunch closure at noon, with the last line cut off early to allow it.
  • Finance Department: publishes millage rate documents and hearing dates, and its 2026 packet carries a September 4 revision.

Field appraisers also canvass neighborhoods. The county's notice to property owners explains that these visits cover permit follow-up, new construction, additions, remodels, sales, appeals and returns, with measuring and photographing along the way. Each wears a photo badge and drives a marked vehicle.

When were Douglas County's 2026 assessment notices mailed and when did appeals close?

The mailing date for the 2026 annual notices was June 16, 2026. Appeals closed at 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026. The department posts in bold capitals that it cannot extend that date, and it recommends filing ahead of time while keeping your own copy in case the online system misbehaves.

Notices usually land between April 15 and July 1, with the 45 days measured from the date printed on the notice. Owners can post the form, hand it in at the annex, or use the online property search, and the parking lot dropbox covers evenings. Faxed or emailed forms are turned away, and anyone filing for an owner needs a signed authorization letter.

Request your property record card, plus the comparable sales the county holds, before you commit to an appeal. Boats, aircraft and business equipment get a notice only if the value shifts or the county rejects a return filed in the first quarter.

How does a Douglas County appeal move from the assessors to court?

An appeal advances in stages, and you can walk away at whichever stage gives you a fair number. The default track ends before a Board of Equalization seated by the grand jury.

  1. The assessors take a fresh look and mail a written answer, called the 30-day letter, that states whether the value changed.
  2. If the value holds, the file moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. If it drops and you are satisfied, the appeal simply lapses once the 30 days expire.
  3. If it changes and you still disagree, say so in writing before the 30 days end.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails notice of a hearing date, and the county recommends appearing with your own proof of market value.
  5. After the hearing, either party can take the result to Superior Court in the next 30 days after mailing, and the owner pays a $25 filing fee at the court clerk's office.

Other routes open when you file. Arbitration looks at value alone. A hearing officer handles non-homestead parcels valued above $500,000 and rules on value and uniformity. Superior Court directly needs the assessors' agreement and allows every kind of argument. The state's four grounds for appeal are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Which homestead exemptions can Douglas County owners claim?

The Tax Commissioner takes homestead applications online and at the counter year-round, with April 1 as the cutoff for the cycle in progress. To qualify you must be both the owner and a resident as of January 1, and the proof the county asks for is a state ID or driver's license plus a vehicle registration carrying the homestead address. The Revenue Department adds a second window: the 45 days after a notice.

Exemption types listed by the county:

  • The standard homestead exemption.
  • Age 62 and age 65 senior exemptions, plus a 65 fixed-income version with an income requirement.
  • Disability, supported by two kinds of proof or certificates from two doctors, with a Social Security Administration letter.
  • Disabled veteran, shown by a VA statement of service-connected benefits paid at 100 percent on January 1.
  • Surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, and of police officers or firefighters killed on duty.

The Revenue Department's exemption page also names Douglas among counties with a valuation freeze, meaning a base-year figure holds the taxable value while the owner lives there. The Tax Commissioner can give the base year and the conditions.

What do Douglas County's housing numbers show?

About 720 residents share each of Douglas County's 200 land square miles. Growth runs at 6.9 percent over the 2020 base, to an estimated 154,293 people, and the Census Bureau logged 801 building permits in 2025. Workers spend 33.2 minutes getting to work on average.

Because about two of every three occupied homes have an owner living in them, an assessment jump reaches many households together. Set the value on your notice beside these typical figures and beside nearby sales before choosing to appeal. Residents 65 and older make up 13.8 percent of the population, and owners without a mortgage report typical monthly costs of $507.

What happens to the tax bill if you sell in Douglas County?

Under Georgia practice, ownership on January 1 fixes who owes for the year, and a later sale returns nothing to the seller. The state's FAQ describes a 60-day payment window and December 20 as the common due date. Douglas County's bill date and your parcel's balance come from the Tax Commissioner.

Look on the commissioner's site for the delinquent list, upcoming tax sales and excess funds, which will show any unpaid earlier year. Liens from county taxes are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk, and the commissioner can confirm whether your parcel has one.

Dividing a lot before you sell starts with a survey submitted to the Zoning Administrator. After the approved, stamped survey is recorded, new deeds are signed and filed with the clerk, while a deed specialist inside Appraisal updates the tax records. Heirs and delinquent owners sometimes pick a no-repair cash sale, with the tax paid at closing.

Has the Douglas County 2026 appeal period ended?

Yes. Notices were mailed on June 16, 2026, and the period ran out at 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026, without extensions. New notices will start a new 45 days.

Will Douglas County take an appeal by fax or email?

No. Post it, bring it to the annex or use the online property search. If a representative files, include a letter of authorization.

How much is the Superior Court fee for a Douglas County appeal?

A $25 filing fee goes to the Clerk of Superior Court, and the owner tells the assessors in writing. Owner or assessors can appeal a Board of Equalization decision inside 30 days of its mailing.

Where does a Douglas County homestead application go?

To the Tax Commissioner, either online or in person. Bring a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration showing the house address. You need to own and occupy the home on January 1, and April 1 is the usual cutoff.

If I sell in spring, who owes Douglas County's tax for the year?

The person who owned it on January 1 owes for all twelve months, with no partial-year refund from Georgia. Your contract and settlement statement divide the cost with the buyer, so ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance first.

Which Early County office do you call about a tax bill?

The Early County Assessor handles valuation, while the tax commissioner handles the bill itself. The county's forms and applications page carries a Tax Commissioner Forms link. The assessor's number is (229) 723-3088. For anything else, the county administration building at 204 Court Square in Blakely answers at (229) 723-4304 on weekdays, closing for lunch at noon and reopening at 1:00 p.m. until 5:00 p.m.

Parcel records are on qPublic under the Early County listing. State guidance sends payment questions, homestead applications and bill copies to the commissioner, and sends appeals and appraised value questions to the assessor.

  • Appraised value, property record or appeal: the assessor.
  • Bill copy, payment or homestead form: the tax commissioner.
  • Unsure where a form belongs: the administration office in Blakely.

What should a seller know about Early County itself?

Four cities sit inside the county: Blakely, the seat, plus Damascus, Jakin and Arlington, which Early shares with Calhoun County. Georgia formed Early County in 1818 from land obtained from the Creek Indians. Eight later counties, including Dougherty, Grady, Miller, Mitchell and Seminole, were cut from its original territory.

Peanut farming drives local income. The county's history page describes Early as the largest peanut quota holding county in the nation, and a peanut statue went up on the Blakely square in 1954. Kolomoki Mounds State Park, in the north central part, preserves a row of Native American mounds from around the year 800, with a museum covering the area's cultural history since about 5000 B.C. The Early County Museum and the Coheelee Creek Covered Bridge are the other listed attractions.

Census figures show a typical owned home worth $131,300 among 4,993 housing units, and only 12 building permits in 2025. New construction barely registers here.

The county website also lists a code enforcement page, a code of ordinances on Municode, an airport, the Blakely-Early County Recreation Department and a UGA Extension office. Look at the code enforcement page and the ordinances if your house has sat vacant, since a seller who clears any open issues first gives a buyer fewer reasons to hesitate.

What do Early County appraisal visits and notices involve?

Appraisers may turn up at your parcel in any month. The county's standing notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and names the triggers: a return, an appeal, a site improvement permit, a homestead or conservation use application, or a routine review. Keep permit paperwork for any addition you built, since the county's forms page lists building, electrical and manufactured home permits. Staff collect only necessary details and photographs, and they leave a business card at an empty house. A visitor should show photo ID and arrive in a marked vehicle, and a call to the assessor settles any doubt.

It also points out that older owners can claim additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead one, with April 1 as the last day to apply. The full law behind each exemption controls eligibility.

A state revenue briefing from May 2026 outlines a redesigned Notice of Assessment under SB 566. Under that outline the notice lists exemptions and credits, estimates tax savings, names an appeal contact, spells out fair market value and says a homestead application may still be filed inside the 45-day appeal window. It also asks owners who are ineligible for a homestead exemption to say so before the window closes, because the tax and a 50 percent penalty stay with the property.

How do Early County appeals and homestead filings work?

An owner who disputes a value writes to the Early County Assessor within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The statewide appeal form lets you challenge taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and you choose a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on it.

Nobody at the state level can overrule the local decision makers on one parcel's value, whether that is the assessors, a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or Superior Court. The state treats assessed value as 40 percent of fair market value, and the formula deducts the homestead exemption from that assessed figure before the millage rate applies.

That briefing also reports that the 2026 HOME Act ends the local opt-out from the HB 581 floating homestead exemption. The statewide version takes effect January 1, 2027 with 2026 values as its baseline, so a 2026 value carries weight beyond one tax year.

A homestead claim requires title and residence on January 1. File with the tax commissioner, or with the assessor in counties that delegate it, by the April 1 return deadline or during the 45-day appeal window. Before filing, do the following:

  • Save the notice and mark its mailing date.
  • Photograph defects and collect repair bids that support a lower value.
  • Request the property record card from the assessor and compare its square footage and condition notes with the house.
  • Ask which local exemptions Early County adds to the state's $2,000 standard exemption.

What do the Early County numbers look like?

Early is thinly settled: about 21 residents per square mile across 512.6 square miles of land. Its 10,455 estimated residents in mid-2025 are 3.7 percent fewer than the 2020 base, and older adults make up 22.6 percent of the total, which makes the age-based exemptions especially relevant.

Owners with no mortgage report typical monthly costs of $477, and about 14.7 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Rental housing is modest too, at a typical $791 a month. An heir or older owner preparing to sell should look for unpaid tax and budget for repairs.

What does an Early County seller owe in tax at closing?

Georgia charges the full year to whoever owned the parcel on January 1 and, per the state's FAQ, gives nothing back for a later sale. Most counties allow 60 days to pay with a normal due date of December 20, though local dates vary. The Early County tax commissioner can tell you the billing date and your parcel's balance.

Before signing a sale contract, ask the commissioner for a payoff number and whether any earlier years are still open. Liens issued by the commissioner are dealt with through that office. Filed liens appear on the clerk's general execution docket, so the clerk's index is worth a look as well.

The Early County Assessor, reachable at (229) 723-3088, sets values and takes appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects.

May Early County appraisers drop by unannounced?

Yes. A standing county notice allows visits all year for returns, appeals, permits, exemption applications or routine review. Staff show photo ID, use a marked vehicle and leave a card at an empty house.

What is the filing window for an Early County assessment appeal?

Forty-five days from the notice's mailing date. Write to the assessor and name your route: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

What is the deadline for an Early County homestead exemption?

April 1 for the current year, or the 45-day appeal window after a notice. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1.

If I sell in spring, is the Early County tax bill still mine?

Yes. The January 1 owner is responsible for the year, and Georgia gives no partial-year refund. Get the balance from the tax commissioner and settle it at closing.

Where does Effingham County fit in the Savannah area?

Effingham sits on the northwest side of metro Savannah, bordered by Chatham, Bryan and Bulloch counties in Georgia and by Hampton and Jasper counties across the river in South Carolina. Springfield holds the courthouse, while Rincon is the biggest town. Guyton is the third city, and Clyo, Egypt, Meldrim and Shawnee are unincorporated communities (Wikipedia).

Georgia created the county on February 5, 1777, which makes it one of the original ones, and Springfield dates to 1799. Part of the Savannah National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the line. In 2008 the Census Bureau ranked Effingham the sixth-fastest-growing midsize county in the nation for 2000 to 2007, with a 35.1 percent jump.

That growth continues in the QuickFacts figures: 64,769 people at the 2020 count, 74,397 estimated by July 2025, and 212 building permits in 2025. Homes are valued at a median $276,000, households earn a median $88,438, and workers spend 32.3 minutes getting to their jobs. Roughly 78 of every 100 homes are lived in by their owners.

Which two offices decide an Effingham County property tax bill?

The Board of Tax Assessors puts a value on each parcel, and the Tax Commissioner turns that value into a bill and collects it. The commissioner's own page stresses that it sets neither values nor millage. Rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education.

The assessors' board meets the first Monday of the month, according to the assessor page.

What does the 2026 Effingham tax bill look like after the county's relief?

The county advertised a package it calls Project Zero, and the numbers are large. A county news item from September 22, 2026 said bills for tax year 2026 had been mailed and posted online, with homestead property seeing about 30 percent in total savings and other property about 20 percent.

Here is where that relief came from, per the same notice:

  • The county cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The school district cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The county industrial development authority suspended its 2-mill levy.
  • Qualifying homesteads also receive a state grant.

All of that traces to the Project Camellia land sale. A referendum on a Local Homeowners Incentive Adjustment Grant went before voters in November 2026, and if approved it would let the county use available funds to erase county tax on qualifying homesteads in 2027. Read the result on effinghamtax.com before pricing a 2027 sale. Voters also turned down a six-year SPLOST renewal by 140 votes in the same election, per the commissioner's site.

When does Effingham County expect payment, and how fast do penalties build?

The tax FAQ sets out a ladder of consequences:

  • One percent interest per month starts accruing the day after November 20.
  • Every 120 days adds 5 percent, with a cap at 20 percent overall.
  • Once taxes run past 90 days, the commissioner may record a fi. fa. with the court clerk, and credit bureaus can read it.
  • Levy on the property is the last resort, which the office says it would rather avoid.

The FAQ also reminds owners that bills are addressed to them and never to a lender, so anyone with an escrow account should forward theirs. You can pay by e-check online for a $2 processing fee, which the commissioner contrasts with higher card fees.

How do you challenge an Effingham County value?

You contest a value by appealing within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The county FAQ names two routes, the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, with superior court available after either decision.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, taken as of January 1 each year. The commissioner subtracts exemptions, then multiplies what remains by the millage rate, where one mill equals one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

On filing, the assessors accept appeals and waivers only by mail or hand delivery to 802 S. Laurel Street, North Administration Complex. A taxpayer holding a no-change notice who prefers to skip the hearing can submit a waiver until a hearing date is set. A green postcard means an appraiser may visit your area within 60 days under state law, and no response is needed.

What homestead exemptions does Effingham County list?

The county publishes its own schedule, and a local amount overrides the state amount whenever it is larger. Its exemption page breaks the types down this way:

  • Regular (S1): $4,000 for county tax and $2,000 for school tax.
  • Ages 62 to 64, income-tested (S3): $4,000 county and $10,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older (SC): $4,000 county and $12,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older, income-tested (S4): $6,000 county, $20,000 school, and $100 off the sanitation bill.
  • 100 percent disabled veteran (S5) and VA surviving spouse (SS): $101,754.

You qualify by owning and living in the home on January 1, and applications must land by April 1 for that year. The county also takes applications online. It also warns that retitling a home to an LLC, renting out part of it, or claiming a second exemption elsewhere can end the exemption, and a double claim can draw a fine of two times the savings for up to three years.

How should an Effingham County owner handle a sale when tax is behind?

A sale removes the seller's exemption, since the county lists a sold property as grounds for removal, and the buyer applies for a new one. Before you list, get a balance in writing from the commissioner for every open year.

  • Clear old years from the proceeds so no lien rides along with the title.
  • Agree in the contract on who covers the 2026 bill.
  • Stop any lender escrow after payoff.

Unpaid years can end in a public sale. The commissioner advertised a December 2026 tax sale for Tuesday, December 1, at 804 South Laurel Street between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Property goes for cash or certified funds, as is, with rights of redemption, and the buyer pays for title, transfer, advertising and recording. Parcels leave the list when an owner pays, so the advertised list changes up to the sale.

A seller facing a sale date can choose a faster cash closing. Effingham's $276,000 median home value is far above the $94,700 to $142,000 medians for Elbert, Emanuel and Evans counties, so there is often equity to protect.

What is the Effingham County deadline for paying the regular bill?

November 20 is the usual date, per the tax commissioner's FAQ. Interest begins the next day at 1 percent per month. Pay online, by phone at 470-531-3402, or at the office.

Who accepts homestead applications in Effingham County?

The Tax Assessor's office does, and it also takes them online. File by April 1 or the exemption starts the following year. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

Is it too late to dispute a 2026 Effingham County value?

Probably. The window runs 45 days from the date printed on each notice, and for most owners that period has ended. File promptly after the next notice, and call 912-754-2125 for the right form.

Does a new Effingham County owner inherit my homestead exemption?

No. The county removes the exemption after a sale, and the new owner applies. Seniors and veterans must also reapply for the higher categories.

What happens at an Effingham County tax sale?

The ex-officio sheriff sells levied parcels at public outcry for cash or certified funds. Sales are as is and subject to redemption rights, and the buyer pays title, transfer, advertising and recording costs.

How would you describe Elbert County?

Elbert lies in Georgia's northeastern Piedmont, with Anderson, Abbeville and McCormick counties of South Carolina on its far side. Elberton is the courthouse town. Bowman is the second city, with Dewy Rose a census-designated place. The county was formed on December 10, 1790, honors Samuel Elbert, and runs along the shore of Lake Richard B. Russell on the east (Wikipedia).

The QuickFacts table reports 20,072 residents in mid-2025, a 2.2 percent gain over 2020. Half of owned homes sit above $142,000, and gross rent is $844 at the median. Owners live in about 71 percent of the homes, and 23.1 percent of the population is 65 or older, the age group that qualifies for the larger exemptions. Builders took out 129 permits in 2025.

Look further back and the pattern is decline, then slow recovery. Wikipedia's census table shows 24,125 residents in 1910, a slide to 17,262 by 1970, and 19,637 at the 2020 count. Median age at that count was 44.8, rural residents were the majority, and 13.3 percent of the 9,248 housing units stood empty.

Who answers property tax questions in Elbert County?

One office mails and collects the bill. A second office decides what each parcel is worth. Both post weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • Tax Commissioner: 45 Forest Avenue, Elberton; postal box 603; telephone 706-283-2018.
  • Tax Assessors: 706-283-2008, with parcel lookups through the assessors' web portal.
  • Courthouse records room: 12 Oliver Street, Elberton, where a copy of your warranty deed is available.

The commissioner's FAQ routes value questions to the assessors and billing questions to its own staff. A third party handles recovery when a payment check bounces, and the site names the fee rules.

When does the Elbert County bill come due?

Elbert's normal deadline for real estate and business personal property is November 15. The state's baseline is December 20, and Revenue Department guidance lets a county move that earlier, to December 1 or November 15.

Georgia guidance adds a 60-day grace from the postmark before interest runs, and your own bill shows the governing date. The commissioner's FAQ describes what happens once the deadline passes:

  • Interest keeps accruing month by month.
  • A 5 percent charge lands at each 120-day mark, and the total stops at 20 percent of what is owed.
  • Homestead parcels with a bill under $500 are spared the 5 percent.
  • In the end the office can levy, pile on fees and sell the parcel.

Mobile and modular homes are billed separately for May 1, and the location permit waits until that year's tax is paid in full. Vehicles are taxed around the owner's birthday.

The bill starts with fair market value, takes 40 percent of it as assessed value, subtracts any exemption, and multiplies what is left by the millage rate. One mill means one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of taxable value. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rate each year after estimating what other revenue will cover.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1, with real estate returns going to the assessors. An owner who skips a return is treated by state guidance as having filed the same value as the prior year. A challenge to value moves from the Board of Tax Assessors to either the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then to superior court.

You must own and occupy the home on January 1. File before April 1 and the exemption hits that year's bill, while a late filing waits a year.

The exemption stays put while you remain in the same house, and a move needs a new application. Turning 62 or 65 opens an extra exemption, so anyone who recently crossed one of those ages should check the account. Freeport and Conservation Use requests go to the assessors.

When you sell, your exemption ends and the buyer files from scratch. Claiming it on two properties is not allowed.

The county school district operates six schools, including the high school, and Elbert belongs to the Northern Judicial Circuit with Hart, Franklin, Madison and Oglethorpe. Wikipedia lists Richard B. Russell State Park, the dam named for him and the Elberton Granite Museum and Exhibit among local sites.

Acreage can be taxed differently from a town lot. Before you describe the land to a buyer, ask the assessors whether any of it sits in Conservation Use, the Forest Land Protection Act or Preferential Assessment.

Monthly interest runs, and 5 percent is added every 120 days until the penalties reach 20 percent. Homesteaded property owing less than $500 avoids the 5 percent. Call 706-283-2018 for a balance.

How large is Emanuel County, and how many people live in it?

Emanuel covers 681 square miles of east-central Georgia, a lot of ground for 23,147 people, the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate. Density comes to roughly 33.5 per square mile, the thinnest of the four counties in the QuickFacts comparison. Swainsboro serves as seat and largest city.

The 2020 census counted 8,644 households and 9,962 housing units, 13.2 percent of them vacant, and put the median age at 39.5. About 68 percent of residents lived in rural areas.

Where did Emanuel County come from?

Emanuel was created by the General Assembly on December 10, 1812, from parts of Bulloch and Montgomery. Later slices left again to form Johnson in 1858, Jenkins and Toombs in 1905, Candler in 1914 and Treutlen in 1918 (Wikipedia).

Courthouses did badly here. Court first met at a private home, the 1814 courthouse burned in 1841, and fires followed in 1855, 1857, 1919 and 1938. A marble building from 1940 lasted until it was demolished in 2000, and the present single-story courthouse, which folds in the old 1936 post office, opened in 2002. Swainsboro was incorporated on February 18, 1854, and the assessors' site adds that it was briefly renamed Paris before reverting.

The practical lesson for a seller is to keep your own copies of recorded papers and tax receipts.

What roads and parks matter to buyers in Emanuel County?

Swainsboro sits where U.S. 1 meets U.S. 80. I-16, U.S. 221 and state routes such as SR 15, SR 23, SR 46 and SR 56 also cross the county, and nine other counties touch its borders, from Jefferson in the north to Toombs in the south.

George L. Smith State Park, with the Parrish Mill built in 1880 and 11 miles of hiking trails, lies inside the county. Local events listed by the assessors include the Pine Tree Festival, the Garfield Washpot Cookout and Agricultural Appreciation Day. Seven schools make up the county school system, including Swainsboro High School.

The northern end drains toward the Upper Ogeechee River, the east toward the Canoochee, and the west and south toward the Ohoopee.

Mobile and modular homes work on a different calendar. A home standing in Emanuel on January 1 needs its return and location permit by May 1, or the owner pays a 10 percent penalty. The office normally mails those bills on January 2.

What do returns, values and appeals involve in Emanuel County?

Bills print fair market value and, beside it, assessed value, which is 40 percent of that figure. Anyone who bought or altered a parcel should file a real estate return by April 1 with the assessors, while an owner with nothing new may skip it.

State guidance wants appeals postmarked within 45 days of the day the notice went out. A refund for tax paid by mistake needs a written claim inside three years, and the county says it will not refund merely because you disagree with the value.

The person living in the house on January 1 earns it, which means a buyer cannot inherit yours and files fresh the following year. Not sure yours is active? Call the assessors at 478-237-1222 before listing.

What does the Emanuel County economy look like?

In the Census figures, retail is the largest line: $376,121,000 in 2022 sales, or $16,392 for each resident. Health care and social assistance took in $84,006,000, and transportation and warehousing $58,176,000.

Census counted 413 employer establishments in 2023 and 5,792 jobs on their payrolls, a 9.3 percent gain over 2022. The median household earns $52,772, and the poverty rate is 22.1 percent. A typical commute takes 28.5 minutes, and around 56 percent of adults 16 and older are in the labor force.

The commissioner's page gives December 20 as the general due date. Mobile and modular homes are due by May 1. Confirm the exact date printed on your bill by calling 478-237-3351.

What is the Emanuel County Tax Commissioner's street address?

The main office is at 223 W. Moring St., Suite 136, Swainsboro, and mail goes to P.O. Box 763. The tag office is at 101 South Main Street.

Which office handles Emanuel County homestead filings?

The Tax Assessor at 101 South Main Street, 3rd Floor, takes them, and they must arrive before April 1. Anything later starts with the following year's bill. Call 478-237-1222 with questions.

What is the deadline to appeal an Emanuel County value?

Postmark the appeal within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. The Board of Assessors reviews it first, and an unresolved case goes to the Board of Equalization.

Is an Emanuel County sale possible while taxes remain unpaid?

Yes. The unpaid tax is settled from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff beforehand. An open bill left alone can lead to a levy and a public sale.

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia

What sets Evans County apart on the Georgia map?

Of the four counties in the Census table, Evans has the fewest residents, 11,028 in July 2025, and the least land, 183 square miles. Its ground is coastal plain, the Canoochee River drains it, and Statesboro's micropolitan area absorbed it in 2023. Claxton holds the courthouse and the most people, while Bellville, Daisy and Hagan round out the four cities (Wikipedia).

The QuickFacts table shows 2.3 percent growth since 2020. Owned homes are worth $138,200 at the median, rent is $719, and the typical household brings in $53,259. Owners occupy about two of every three homes, and the county issued just 25 building permits in 2025.

Population has barely moved in a decade: 11,000 in 2010 and 10,774 in 2020. Wikipedia describes the soil as red and yellow clays over sedimentary rock, and it notes that local businesses are exempt from property tax on certain inventory classes, which matches the freeport exemption the assessors describe. Manufacturing, education, health and social services make up much of the local economy.

What is the story behind Evans County's creation?

Voters ratified a constitutional amendment on November 3, 1914, that carved Evans out of Bulloch and Tattnall counties. Supporters wanted a nearer courthouse, more office jobs and more hotels and eating places, and some thought a minority in Reidsville controlled Tattnall. The Savannah and Western Railroad created stations that grew into Bellville, Claxton, Daisy and Hagan.

The current neoclassical courthouse in Claxton was finished in 1923. In July 1940 the federal government bought land for Camp Stewart, later Fort Stewart, and an estimated 1,500 people were displaced across the counties involved. Evans Memorial Hospital opened in December 1967, and the Evans County Heart Study ran from 1958 to 1995.

Wikipedia names Claxton Poultry Company, Valmont Newmark, the Georgia Department of Corrections, Camellia Health and Rehabilitation and Pinewood Christian Academy among the larger employers.

Where are the Evans County tax offices?

The commissioner's counter is in Claxton, and the assessor answers on the same county line. Street address and hours come from the commissioner's department page.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 4 at 201 Freeman Street in Claxton, or by mail at P.O. Box 685; call 912-739-1147 between 8:15 and 4:30 on weekdays.
  • Main county line: 912-739-1141, where option 1 reaches both tax offices; the contact page shows a lunch closing from noon to 1.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

With a small staff, the office would rather receive faxed or emailed paperwork and send answers back, though visitors may still look through records at the counter. Start a payoff request early, because the phones stay busy around the deadline.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Evans County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does Evans County charge when taxes are late?

Evans keeps its late-fee schedule short. The deadline is December 20. Every month after it adds 1 percent in interest, and a flat 10 percent penalty arrives with day 91.

Evans County property tax FAQ: due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat the county says
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Interest1 percent added every month after the due date
PenaltyOne-time 10 percent after 90 days
Lien (fi. fa.)Filed on the Execution Docket with the court clerk once taxes are past due

A fi. fa. can follow your credit for as long as seven years, the county cautions. Its escrow position is also spelled out: the bill is addressed to the owner, since the commissioner cannot tell who holds the mortgage or whether an escrow account pays the tax. Mortgage companies ask for the figures every year.

How do Evans County assessments and appeals run?

Values come from the Board of Tax Assessors. A changed value comes with a notice, and the owner has 45 days from that notice to object. If the board holds firm, the assessor's page says the file moves on its own to the County Board of Equalization, which schedules a hearing.

An arbitrator can stand in for that hearing, and superior court sits above both. Only three arguments are accepted:

  • Whether the property is taxable at all.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Whether that value is uniform with similar properties.

Grumbling about the size of the bill does not count, since the bill flows from the millage rate. State guidance wants the appeal postmarked inside the window, so mail it early. Taxable value is 40 percent of market value.

Which exemptions and land programs does Evans County list?

Homestead applications are handled at the commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1, and an approved exemption carries forward each year. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. File again if the deed changes hands, if a name is corrected on the deed, or if you move up to another type.

The assessor's page, which still carries older income figures, describes a standard $2,000 reduction, a $4,000 reduction for those 65 and up who pass an income test, a school-tax reduction of up to $10,000 starting at age 62, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. Ask the assessors what the income limits are now. A deferral program also exists for low-income seniors, and the deferred amount is due when the home changes owners.

Farmland and timber follow separate rules. A Conservation Use filing must reach the assessors by April 1 with a $10 fee, and it commits the land to a qualifying use for ten years. Breaking the covenant can cost double the taxes saved. The deadline for freeport inventory filings is the same April 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Evans County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What should an Evans County seller do before closing?

Get the commissioner's payoff on paper before the closing table. Older years are cleared first, and the sale contract settles who bears the current bill.

  • Clear any fi. fa. before the title search turns it up.
  • Once the deed is recorded, give the commissioner the buyer's mailing address.
  • With an escrow account, notify your lender after payoff.
  • Hold on to your warranty deed copy, and know that the court clerk can supply recorded ones.

Acreage adds one more step. The assessor's page says a buyer who keeps the original use of Conservation Use land can sign the covenant and avoid a penalty, but a change of use inside the ten years triggers all of them.

Why might an Evans County seller choose a cash buyer?

Someone paying cash and accepting the house as is does not argue over repairs, which helps when a tax bill or lien already sits on the parcel. Census shows retail sales of $21,195 per resident in 2022, the top figure of the four counties, alongside a 22.6 percent poverty rate and a 13.4 percent Hispanic or Latino population.

Speed and condition drive the choice. Either way, the commissioner's payoff comes first.

More questions about Evans County, GA Property Tax Guide

When does Evans County expect payment of the annual bill?

The date is December 20, according to the county's property tax FAQ. Interest of 1 percent accrues monthly afterward, and the one-time 10 percent penalty comes after 90 days.

Does the Evans County Tax Commissioner mail my bill to the lender?

No. It goes to the owner, since the office has no record of lienholders or escrow arrangements. Lenders ask the office for amounts each year.

What is the window to contest an Evans County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and an unchanged case moves to the Board of Equalization unless you elect arbitration.

What does a fi. fa. mean on an Evans County parcel?

It is a lien the commissioner records with the court clerk when taxes run past due. The county says it can weigh on your credit for up to seven years, so settle it before selling.

Where do Evans County homeowners file for homestead?

At the commissioner's office in Claxton, from January 1 to April 1. Dial 912-739-1141 and press option 1 for questions. An approved exemption renews itself until ownership changes.

Which Fannin County offices handle my property tax?

Valuation and billing live in different Fannin offices. Assessors decide what each parcel is worth and field exemption forms, and the Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment.

The Tax Commissioner's main office is at 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, Blue Ridge, GA 30513, the same street as the county courthouse. Call (706) 632-2645. The counter opens at 8:30 each weekday, closes at 5:00 Monday through Thursday, and closes at 4:30 on Friday. The county's own directory lists the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954, and the county links to an online parcel search on qPublic.

Fannin County tax offices, as posted on county pages
OfficeWhat it doesContact
Tax CommissionerBills and collects county and school tax400 West Main Street, Suite 103; (706) 632-2645
Tax AssessorsValues property, handles returns and homestead forms(706) 632-5954
Lodging DivisionShort-term rental certificates and lodging tax400 West Main Street, Suite 100; (706) 258-5170
City of Blue RidgeBills its own city taxCity Hall, (706) 632-2091

Sources for the table: the Fannin County Tax Commissioner site, the county home page and the City of Blue Ridge tax page.

What does the Fannin County landscape mean for a house sale?

Fannin is a mountain county with a thin settlement pattern. Census figures show 387.11 land square miles and only 65.4 people per square mile as of 2020, far looser than the metro counties to the south. A parcel here is often a few acres on a slope, so access roads, septic systems and well water show up in a buyer's questions early.

The county government publishes a long list of ordinances that touch a house sale, among them a land development ordinance, a building code enforcement ordinance, a dilapidated building ordinance, a manufactured home and trailer ordinance, a septic installation ordinance and a short-term rental ordinance. Before you list a cabin or a lot, read the ordinances that fit your property on the county's ordinance page, and call the building department at (706) 632-8361 with questions about a past permit.

Blue Ridge holds the county courthouse, and the Chattahoochee forest country around it draws visitors. That visitor traffic is why short-term rental rules matter so much in Fannin, and the next sections cover them.

Who lives in Fannin County and what do homes cost?

Fannin held 26,111 people in the Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, 780 more than its 2020 starting count of 25,331. Seniors make up 32.2 percent of residents, the top share in the three-county comparison the Bureau publishes.

  • Value of a typical owned home (Census survey years 2020 to 2024): $306,600.
  • Median gross rent: $900 a month.
  • Housing units in 2025: 19,655, against 11,890 households.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 78.6 percent.
  • Persons per household: 2.15.
  • Median household income: $57,073.
  • Building permits in 2025: 356.

Notice the gap between 19,655 housing units and 11,890 households. A large share of Fannin's housing stock is not someone's year-round home, which fits the cabin and vacation market and explains why buyers ask about rental history and lodging tax records.

When is Fannin County property tax due?

Check your statement or call the Tax Commissioner for the due date, since Georgia lets each county pick its own. The Department of Revenue calls December 20 the official default, with November 15, December 1 and installment billing as local alternatives.

Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark on the statement, and penalties can follow on balances left open. Mobile homes run on their own track: apply for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew it between January 1 and April 1.

Inside Blue Ridge the city sends a second statement. City Hall says notices usually go out in November with a 60-day payment window counted from the postmark, and its mayor and council set the rate from values the county assessors produce. A Blue Ridge address therefore means two bills.

How do returns and the homestead exemption work in Fannin County?

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1. The state treats silence as agreement: skip a return and last year's value carries forward.

  • Apply whenever you like during the year; the April 1 cutoff decides which tax year the exemption starts.
  • The state treats a missed application as a waiver.
  • The county directory sends property questions to the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954, so call there before you go in.
  • Commercial and industrial inventory can be exempt under freeport if county voters adopted it; apply with the assessors during the return period.

New buyers in Fannin should file for homestead after closing and keep a copy of the recorded deed ready. A seller's exemption does not follow the house, so the buyer files a separate application.

How can I contest a Fannin County valuation?

Mail the appeal to the Fannin County Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no more than 45 days after the notice date. The notice itself carries the filing instructions.

An appeal challenges the fair market value on the notice. The amount of tax is not a ground. Next the assessors reread the file, and unresolved cases can reach the Board of Equalization and then Superior Court. Separately, anyone who paid tax that should never have been charged has three years from payment to ask in writing for a refund, and refunds tied to an appealed value are processed automatically once that value is final.

Owners of boats, aircraft or business equipment get a notice when the board rejects their return, and the same 45 days apply.
