What rules apply to a Fannin County short-term rental when the house is sold?

A short-term rental in unincorporated Fannin needs an annual lodging certificate, and a new owner cannot just keep using the seller's. The county Lodging Division, at 400 West Main Street, Suite 100, lists the steps on its information page.

  • Complete the short-term rental application packet in full.
  • Email it with a PDF of the warranty deed, and wait until closing is done and the deed is in hand.
  • The county then sets up a portal account and emails instructions.
  • Buy the annual lodging certificate, which covers the current calendar year.
  • Report lodging tax each month, due by the 20th for the prior month's rentals.

The county adds that an owner who uses Airbnb or VRBO to remit the monthly tax is still the one who enters the reporting amounts. If you sell a rental, give the buyer your recent monthly reports and ask the Lodging Division how the certificate transfers. Commissioners held public meetings in August 2025 on changes to the short-term vacation rental ordinance, so ask the commissioners' office at 400 West Main Street, Suite 110, for the version now in force before you advertise a house as a rental.

What should a Fannin County seller do about the tax bill?

Get a written payoff from the Fannin County Tax Commissioner before the contract is final, because the closing attorney needs a figure and unpaid balances can pick up interest and penalties.

Spell out in the contract who covers the year's tax: values are set as of January 1, but the statement lands months later. If you hold a mortgage with escrow, tell your servicer about the sale so the escrow refund reaches you. The county also posts five-year tax digest history reports for 2017 through 2026 on its website, which help a buyer see how the levy has moved.

Intangible recording tax on a new mortgage is $1.50 for every $500 of face amount, per the Department of Revenue, and the security instrument is recorded within 90 days. If an inherited house has an estate in process, ask the probate court and the tax offices what papers they need before the deed is signed.

More questions about Fannin County, GA Property Tax Guide

Who sends the property tax bill in Fannin County?

The Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment, while the Tax Assessors set values. Visit 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, in Blue Ridge, or call (706) 632-2645.

What is the appeal deadline for a Fannin County valuation?

Postmark a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the notice, addressed to the Board of Tax Assessors, and dispute the value shown.

Does the City of Blue Ridge send a separate tax bill?

Yes. City Hall reports November mailings and a 60-day window from the postmark, and it relies on county values.

Can I list my Fannin County cabin as a short-term rental after buying it?

Only after you complete the county's application with the warranty deed and buy the annual lodging certificate. The Lodging Division advises applicants to wait until closing is finished and the deed is secured, then pay lodging tax by the 20th of each month.

How do I stop a homestead exemption from lapsing when I buy a Fannin County house?

Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 for the form. File by April 1 of the first tax year you want covered, since a later application slips to the following year.

Who sends and collects property tax in Fayette County?

Billing sits with the Fayette County Tax Commissioner, and valuation belongs to the Assessors' Office. The assessors' page states that the office issues no tax bills and refers billing questions to 770-461-3652.

The Tax Commissioner works from the county administrative complex at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue in Fayetteville. Suite 110 handles property tax and mobile homes, and Suite 109 handles motor vehicles. The mailing address is P.O. Box 70, Fayetteville, GA 30214. The property tax and mobile home counter keeps weekday hours of eight to five, and a pay-by-phone line, (770) 800-6273, is listed for payments.

City tax is not billed separately. The commissioner's FAQ says all city taxes are on the county bill and the county passes the city share to Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks or Woolsey.

What does Fayette County's setting mean for a home sale?

The county sits in Georgia's Piedmont, with rolling hills, elevations between 720 and 1,005 feet, an average annual temperature of 61.4 degrees and 48.61 inches of yearly rainfall, according to the county's own profile. Rainfall of that size is worth remembering when a buyer's inspector looks at gutters, grading and crawl spaces.

Five municipalities share the 199 square miles, and each has its own office for zoning and city questions even though the county bill carries the city tax. The county's list gives these numbers:

  • Town of Brooks: 770.719.7666
  • City of Fayetteville: 770.461.6029
  • City of Peachtree City: 770.487.7657
  • Town of Tyrone: 770.487.4038
  • Town of Woolsey: 770.461.2320

Interstates 75, 85 and 285 are within reach, and the county reports MARTA service from nearby Fulton County. Commuting buyers will ask about those links, and a seller who keeps recent tax bills handy gives them a clear picture of ongoing costs.

What is the Fayette County property tax calendar?

Statements go out in the fall, and the commissioner counts the due date as 60 days after the original mailing. The table lists the dates the office publishes.

Fayette property tax timeline (source: Tax Commissioner FAQ)
ItemDate or rule
Return of property valueJanuary 1 to April 1
Regular homestead applicationYear round, but complete by April 1 for that tax year
Mobile home billsMailed January 1, due on or before April 1, 10 percent penalty after the due date
Real property billsExpected around mid September
DelinquencyAfter November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that is later

Interest accrues once the bill is delinquent. A bill that never arrives does not erase the debt, and the office tells owners to call for the balance before the delinquent date. Bills are not sent to a mortgage company unless the lender requests a copy, so give your servicer the lower portion of your bill and include the loan number.

How does the Fayette County homestead exemption work?

An owner who occupies the home on January 1 can claim the regular exemption. The FAQ lists $2,000 of assessed value off the school portion and $5,000 off the county portion of the bill. Homestead is limited to one property, which must be your primary residence.

  • File any time of year, but get it complete by April 1 for the current tax year.
  • The assessors' page adds that filing can run past the old April 1 date, to the end of the 45-day appeal window on the notice.
  • An approved exemption renews itself at the same address.
  • Someone who qualified for the age 62 exemption must still apply separately when reaching 65.
  • Mobile home residents are not eligible for homestead.

The assessors' page adds that its office also processes homestead applications, so ask which counter takes the form before you go.

What are the floating homestead exemptions in Fayette County?

Fayette voters approved House Bill 1166 in November 2020, an extra homestead exemption that applies to the school board portion of the bill. A similar measure, House Bill 581, was approved by voters in November 2024 and applies to every taxing entity except bonds.

The county's news page says the Fayette County school board opted out of HB 581 in favor of the existing HB 1166 exemption. Both are floating exemptions, so the amount depends on the gap between the current value and a base year value. Ask the Assessors' Office which base year applies to your parcel.

That detail matters when you sell. Buyers who ask what the property tax will be should hear that your bill reflects your own exemption status, and that they need to apply for theirs after closing.

How can I dispute a Fayette County value?

Under state guidance the appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked inside 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. The assessors' page shows how this played out in 2026: commercial and residential notices were mailed June 23, and personal property notices were mailed July 28.

When the assessors hold their value, the case can move to the equalization board, whose records, notices and decision letters are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court. Superior Court is the next level.

Georgia also permits a written refund claim for tax charged in error, started within three years of the payment date. Filing a return between January 1 and April 1 is how an owner declares an opinion of value, and the commissioner says a return is required in the first full year of ownership and afterward only when the property changes.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Fayette County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens to unpaid Fayette County property tax?

The county sells no tax liens or lien certificates, the commissioner says. It runs a single real property sheriff's tax sale a year, with details on the Tax Sales tab of the commissioner's site.

A Fayette house carrying back taxes needs a written payoff from the commissioner before closing. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that delinquent tax can bring penalties as well as interest, and the commissioner reports interest after the delinquent date. Title companies check for open tax at closing, and a clean payoff speeds the closing.

The commissioner adds that boats, aircraft and business personal property are taxable in whichever county holds them. A seller whose boat sits at a dock in another county gets that bill from the other county.

How does Fayette County housing look in Census data?

The July 2025 estimate is 125,156 residents, up 5.0 percent from the 119,193 base set in April 2020 and the fastest climb in the three-county Census comparison. The land area is 194.56 square miles, and the density in 2020 was 612.6 residents per square mile.

  • Housing units in 2025: 47,621.
  • Households: 44,581, at 2.72 persons each.
  • Residents 65 and over: 22.7 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 5.8 percent.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 3,995.
  • Total retail sales in 2022: $2,249,924 thousand.

The county government says Fayette began to grow in the 1970s with the expansion of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and that it adopted building codes and zoning in 1959 and 1960. That early planning shows in a county of five municipalities that still prizes orderly development.

More questions about Fayette County, GA Property Tax Guide

When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?

Past November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that falls later. Bills usually arrive around mid September, and interest starts once a balance is delinquent.

Which number reaches the Fayette property tax office?

Dial (770) 461-3652 for the Tax Commissioner, at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue, Suite 110, Fayetteville. Value questions go to the Assessors' Office, which issues no bills.

What is the Fayette County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1 is the standard cutoff for the current tax year. The assessors' page says applications can also be taken past that date, until the 45-day appeal window on the notice closes.

Are Fayette County mobile home taxes due on a different date?

Yes. Mobile home statements go out January 1 and come due by April 1, and a 10 percent penalty follows a missed date. New owners register the home with the commissioner's office and receive a decal after payment.

Does Fayette County sell tax liens?

No. Fayette sells neither tax liens nor lien certificates, and it holds one real property sheriff's tax sale a year.

Which Rome offices bill and value Floyd County property?

In Floyd County one office sets values and another collects, and both work out of Rome. The Tax Commissioner is in the Floyd County Historic Courthouse at 5 Government Plaza, Suite 109, Rome, GA 30161, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 26, Rome, GA 30162. For property tax, call (706) 291-5146 or (706) 291-5148 on weekdays between eight and five.

The assessors appraise every real and personal property account in the county and in Rome itself. The county notes that the Assessor's Office relocated to the former Law Enforcement Center at 5 Government Plaza, and the tax site lists (706) 291-5143 for the assessor.

Tax for the City of Rome is on the county bill. The three rate-setters are the Floyd County Board of Commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Floyd County Board of Education.

How does Rome's setting shape a Floyd County house sale?

Rome is built among three rivers, the Etowah, the Oostanaula and the Coosa, and the city's own water documents tie them to its early trading history. Floyd spreads across 509.81 land square miles, the biggest of the three counties in the Bureau's side-by-side table with Fayette and Fannin, and its 2020 density worked out to 193.4 residents for each of them.

Retail and services carry the local economy. The Bureau shows 2022 retail sales of $1,651,649 thousand in Floyd, or $16,610 per resident, and accommodation and food sales of $308,299 thousand.

A house in town and a house outside it go through the same assessors but can carry different bills, since the city rate applies only inside Rome. Ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

Who lives in Floyd County and what do homes cost?

The mid-2025 estimate is 101,378 residents, a 2.8 percent rise over the 98,589 counted as the 2020 base. Renters hold a large slice: owners occupy 63.6 percent of homes, the lowest share in the three-county table.

  • Typical owned home, valued at $217,900 (survey years 2020 to 2024).
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $1,014 monthly.
  • Housing units in 2025: 41,737 and 36,856 households.
  • Median household income: $65,565.
  • Persons in poverty: 14.9 percent.
  • Four-year degree holders among adults 25 and up: 25.9 percent.
  • Average trip to work: 23.3 minutes, shortest of the three.
  • Building permits in 2025: 330.

Values near $218,000 and rents just over $1,000 mean the tax questions below matter to landlords and families selling a parent's house as much as to owner-occupants.

When is Floyd County property tax due?

The Tax Commissioner's site puts the usual due date at November 15, with real and personal property statements mailed by September 1.

  • Interest builds monthly once the date passes, and a late penalty reaching 20 percent can be added.
  • Mobile homes get statements by February 1 and owe by April 1; a late payer faces a 10 percent penalty and possibly a citation.
  • For mailed checks the office honors a postmark from the U.S. Postal Service and rejects metered ones.
  • The office mails to the owner and never to the lender, so pass your copy along if a servicer pays your tax.
  • A bill left open more than 90 days can be answered with a tax fifa, a lien recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court where credit bureaus can read it.

The Tax Commissioner's site announced that Floyd County would hold 2026 tax sales tentatively starting May 5, 2026, with listings posted on the website. That date has passed, so ask the office when the next sale schedule is published.

What does a Floyd County assessment notice show, and what if it never arrives?

The notice states the current value of the parcel and the estimated millage rates certified by each taxing jurisdiction. The estimated tax on it cannot be the basis for an appeal, since only the value, taxability or uniformity can be argued.

The notice lists four ways to file, and an owner picks one and must also state a valid opinion of value. A letter should carry the map reference from the notice, your chosen method, your estimate of what the value should be, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

Notices returned as undeliverable are posted on a list under Georgia code section 48-5-306(c). Each listed property gets 30 days from the posting date to appeal, and the assessors say they will not extend that time for an owner who failed to check the list. Anyone who moved, inherited a parcel or changed a mailing address should call the assessors at (706) 291-5143 and confirm the record, so a missed notice does not cost the appeal.

How do I challenge my Floyd County value?

Send a written appeal to the Floyd County Board of Assessors, 5 Government Plaza, Rome, GA 30161, within a 45-day window that starts on the notice date. One that arrives or is postmarked after the stated deadline does not count.

Steps after a Floyd County notice of assessment (source: Board of Assessors)
StepWhat happensTime limit
Written appealFiled with the Board of Assessors along with your own opinion of value45-day window from the notice date
Staff reviewAppraisers raise, lower or keep the value30 days to contest a changed value
Board of EqualizationA three-person panel named by the Grand Jury, serving three-year terms, hears the caseCertified automatically when the value is unchanged
Superior CourtOpen to either side after the board rulesWritten notice to the Board of Assessors

Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization, at the owner's option when the appeal is filed. Grounds are taxability, uniformity, value and denial of homestead. The estimated tax on the notice cannot be the basis. Include the map reference from your notice, the filing method you choose, your estimate of value, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

What homestead and special programs does Floyd County offer?

Local Floyd exemptions replace the state ones wherever the local amount is bigger. The tax site lists regular, veterans and elderly homestead exemptions, with an extra exemption at age 62. Go to the Tax Assessor's Office, and carry the warranty deed if this is your first home.

A form can arrive any month, yet an application received after April 1 starts the benefit a year later. After approval it renews on its own until the residence, owner or exemption type changes.

  • A building listed on the Georgia register of historic places may earn preferential assessment, covering the structure, its land and up to two acres around it.
  • Bona fide farm use qualifies for assessment at 30 percent, and conservation use programs ask for a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Timber still standing escapes tax until cut or sold.
  • Manufacturers may qualify for freeport exemption, with applications taken during the return season that ends April 1.

Before signing a contract on land under such a covenant, ask the assessors what the sale does to it.

What should a Floyd County seller do about the tax bill?

Request the balance from the Tax Commissioner and write the year's split into the contract. Values are fixed as of each January 1 and statements generally follow by September 1, so a spring sale can close before the year's bill exists.

The Floyd County Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax office, collects intangible tax on a long-term mortgage, and warranty deed copies come from its deed room at 3 Government Plaza. A mobile home seller should confirm the April 1 tax and decal are current.

Assessment notices are also tied to site visits. Floyd's assessors must notify owners before inspecting, as Georgia code section 48-5-264.1 directs, and visits follow a sale or purchase, new construction, an active building permit, a return, an appeal or an exemption application. Appraisers drive marked county vehicles and carry identification.

When are Floyd County property taxes due?

Houses, land and business equipment usually come due November 15, while mobile homes come due April 1.

What is the Floyd County appeal window?

Appeals are written and due within the 45-day window, at 5 Government Plaza in Rome. Late ones are rejected.

What penalty applies to late Floyd County property tax?

Interest accrues monthly after November 15 and a penalty that can reach 20 percent may follow. Continued nonpayment can bring a lien and further collection steps.

Does the City of Rome send its own property tax bill?

No. Taxes for the City of Rome are included on the Floyd County tax bill. The county commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Board of Education each set their own rate.

Where do I get a copy of my Floyd County warranty deed?

The Clerk of Superior Court's deed room, in the new Floyd County Courthouse at 3 Government Plaza in Rome, supplies copies of a warranty deed.

Which Forsyth County offices handle my property tax?

Different offices handle valuation and billing. The Board of Assessors sets values and takes exemption and appeal filings, while the Tax Commissioner mails bills and takes payment. The assessors answer to neither the Board of Commissioners nor the Tax Commissioner, and the Tax Commissioner's office is likewise independent.

  • Board of Assessors: 426 Canton Hwy, Cumming, GA 30040, phone (770) 781-2106.
  • Tax Commissioner: main office at 1092 Tribble Gap Road in Cumming, with a second office at 1950 Sharon Road, Cumming, GA 30041. Phone (770) 781-2110 or email tax@forsythco.com.

Taxable value is 40 percent of market value, and the school board and county commissioners set the millage applied to it. The assessors' site posts the rates, so ask which ones cover your parcel.

What does the Forsyth County property tax year look like?

January 1 drives everything: value, owner of record and homestead eligibility are all measured on that date. The calendar below follows the Board of Assessors' own summary.

Forsyth County property tax calendar (Forsyth County Board of Assessors, Key Deadlines)
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value, ownership and use are fixed for the tax year
January 1 to April 1Property returns and exemption filings
Late May to JuneAssessment notices go out to real property owners
45 days after mailingLast day to appeal or to apply for homestead from the notice
SeptemberTax Commissioner mails and posts bills
November 15Payment due

The assessment notice is informational and is not a tax bill. Legislation in 2025 and 2026 removed the estimated taxes and estimated rollback rates from the notice, which now shows the fair market value and the savings from any exemptions you hold.

How do I pay a Forsyth County tax bill, and what if November 15 is a weekend?

Options are forsythcountytax.com (card or e-check), your bank's bill-pay, a check mailed to 1092 Tribble Gap Rd., Cumming, GA 30040, or a visit or drop box at either office. Checks name the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner as payee.

In 2026 the due date of November 15 fell on a Sunday, and the Tax Commissioner announced that payments received Monday, November 16 would be accepted without interest. Check the calendar each fall for the same situation.

Bills go to the January 1 owner, and the FAQ says a bill that never arrives still has to be paid. Escrow accounts usually pay through a tax service, yet the county holds the homeowner responsible for making sure the money arrives on time.

What happens if a Forsyth County property tax payment is late?

Taxes unpaid after November 15 are delinquent. Interest runs monthly at the legal rate. On top of that, 5 percent of the unpaid balance is added every 120 days, capping at 20 percent. At 90 days past due the office adds a Fi.Fa. (tax lien) fee of $22.50 on bills under $100 or $32.50 on bills over $100.

  • Partial payments are accepted, though charges keep building on the unpaid part.
  • A 30-day notice of intent goes out before a Fi.Fa. is issued.
  • The clerk's General Execution Docket carries the lien for seven years, and credit reports may pick it up.
  • A bounced check costs $30 or 5 percent of its face, whichever is larger, and the office then wants cash or certified funds.

Continued nonpayment exposes the property to levy and sale. A sale is an auction on a first Tuesday outside the Cumming courthouse, and proceeds above the amount owed are held for the owners as excess funds.

How do I appeal a Forsyth County assessment?

Counting begins on the day the notice is mailed and runs 45 days. Notices for 2026 were mailed June 26, 2026, which put that year's last day at August 10, 2026, and later notices print their own date.

Appeals can be filed on the county's online property search, by post, or at the assessors' counter at 426 Canton Hwy. The county says email and fax appeals are no longer accepted, and mailed appeals must be postmarked by the last day shown on the notice. Written appeals should say which process you choose.

  • Board of Equalization, with a later appeal to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, limited to valuation, with an appeal to Superior Court. Fees may apply.
  • Hearing officer, for non-homestead real property and certain high-value personal property, on value and uniformity only.
  • Direct to Superior Court, which needs the Board of Assessors' consent. Fees may apply.

How does the Forsyth County homestead exemption work?

Eligibility is set on January 1: you own the house, live there and are a county legal resident, which the county defines through voter or vehicle registration. Nothing happens automatically, so file an application, due April 1 or inside your 45-day appeal window for that year. After approval it carries forward until the deed changes or you stop qualifying.

The standard exemption cuts assessed value by $8,000 for county operations and fire, and by $2,000 for state and school levies. A floating feature freezes your county and fire taxable value at the base year set when you apply, so later increases in value are exempt from those two authorities. School and state taxes still follow current value.

  • Age 65 on or before January 1: full exemption from school general and school bond taxes.
  • Age 62 and up, with income caps: extra school tax relief.
  • Disability and disabled veteran exemptions are listed on the assessors' exemption page.

Standard and 65-plus applications go in online, by notarized mail or in person; the portal is open December through April 1, and notaries at each office are free. Bring a Georgia license or state ID showing the property address, and know the last four digits of your Social Security number.

What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Forsyth County house?

A sale in the middle of the year leaves the seller's name on the bill, because the county bills the January 1 owner. Either side can email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com and the office will reissue the bill to the buyer, as long as the purchase closed before November 15.

A new name on the deed means the occupant must reapply for homestead with the Board of Assessors, the county says. After a death or divorce the new owner applies in person at 426 Canton Hwy.

Past-due tax at closing adds the penalties and fees above to the payoff, so request a figure good through the closing date.

Which other Forsyth County property tax filings could affect a seller?

Owners with more than a house on the parcel should look at the extra filings the county runs on its own calendar.

  • Personal property such as boats, aircraft, equipment and business inventory needs a return filed with the Board of Assessors by April 1. Missing it or filing late brings a 10 percent penalty.
  • A mobile home gets its own early bill: sent in January, due April 1, and open to appeal at the Board of Assessors for 45 days after mailing.
  • Specialized assessments cover preferential, historic, residential transitional, conservation use, brownfield and forest land. The Board of Assessors answers questions about each at (770) 781-2106.

A refund of an overpayment is mailed about 14 business days after the payment posts, and it goes to whoever made the latest payment. An overpayment from a tax service goes back to that service rather than to the mortgage company it was paying for.

What are the numbers behind the Forsyth County housing market?

QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population at 282,805 on 224.62 square miles of land, with 98,879 housing units. Owners occupy 84.4 percent of homes. Median home value for owners is $550,400 (2020 to 2024) and median household income is $143,784.

Owning costs a median $2,525 a month with a mortgage and $674 without. Renters pay a median $2,090 in gross rent, and 4.5 percent of residents live in poverty.

November 15. In 2026 that date landed on a Sunday, and the Tax Commissioner took payments through Monday, November 16 without interest.

What is the appeal window for a Forsyth County assessment?

Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. The 2026 window, for notices mailed June 26, 2026, ended August 10, 2026.

When must I apply for homestead in Forsyth County?

By April 1, or during the 45-day window after an assessment notice. You also had to own and occupy the home on January 1.

What does late payment cost in Forsyth County?

Interest each month at the legal rate, 5 percent of the balance every 120 days up to a 20 percent cap, and a $22.50 or $32.50 Fi.Fa. fee at 90 days depending on bill size.

Should I notify the county after selling?

It is the way to get the bill moved. Email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com, and have the buyer apply for homestead with the Board of Assessors.

Which Franklin County offices do I deal with on a tax bill?

Two Franklin County offices touch your bill. Billing and collecting belong to the Tax Commissioner. Appraisal and exemption approval belong to the Board of Tax Assessors. Neither sets the rate: county commissioners and the school board do.

According to the tax office, the money pays for the following.

  • County government operations and the public schools.
  • Building and repairing public buildings and bridges.
  • Courts, the county jail and law enforcement.
  • County roads and fire protection.
  • Public health and sanitation.

Find the Tax Commissioner at 1221 Hull Avenue in Carnesville, the county seat; mail goes to PO Box 100, Carnesville, GA 30521. Phone the office at 706-384-3455 any weekday during those hours. For value, exemption or return questions, dial the Tax Assessor at 706-384-4896.

How does Franklin County arrive at the amount I owe?

Forty percent of the house's market value becomes the assessed value. Exemptions are taken from it and the millage rate is applied to the rest, a mill being $1 for each $1,000. Your bill lists both figures.

A buyer or an owner who changed the property sends the assessor form PT-50r between January 1 and April 1, and skipping it costs 10 percent of the omitted value plus interest. Owners with no change from the prior year may skip it.

Which Franklin County tax dates and rates should a seller know?

These rows pull together the dates and rates most sellers ask about, all drawn from the tax office and the county site.

Franklin County property tax basics (Franklin County Tax Office and Franklin County government pages)
ItemWhat the county says
Bills dueNormally November 15
Interest after the due date1 percent per month
Added penalty10 percent, if still unpaid at day 90
Assessment appeal window45 days after the notice
Homestead and return filingJanuary 1 to April 1
Mobile home return and permitOn or before May 1
Tax salesA first Tuesday, at the courthouse

Homesteaded property owing under $500 is spared the 10 percent penalty.

What does a late payment trigger in Franklin County?

After November 15 the clock starts: 1 percent monthly interest, then the 10 percent surcharge at 90 days. The fifa, or execution, is then filed with the Clerk of Superior Court. Anyone can read it, and credit bureaus may pull it; the tax office says it has no say over how they use it.

Only full payment of the delinquent taxes releases the lien. Failing that, the tax commissioner, who doubles as ex-officio sheriff, can levy on the property and auction it, a step the office calls its last resort.

If a bill is open when you sell, call 706-384-3455 for the amount owed through your closing date.

Where does a Franklin County value dispute go?

The notice carries a date, and you have 45 days counting from it. The assessors review the value again and send you a decision. Should they stand by their number, the Board of Equalization hears the dispute next, and Superior Court is open after that on written notice to the assessors.

Arbitration can replace the equalization hearing. An appeal can raise taxability, value or uniformity among comparable parcels. The tax rate itself cannot be appealed here, since it is set by other bodies.

Which exemptions can lower a Franklin County bill?

One application with the Tax Assessor starts the exemption, and it continues yearly until the owner changes or a different type is sought. Ownership and occupancy count as of January 1. The county exemptions page and the tax office FAQ name April 1 as the last day to file, but one older page on the tax office site says March 1, so file early and have the assessor confirm.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 subtracted from assessed value (the county page's figure).
  • Age 65 and older, local exemption: $20,000 against all taxes on the homestead.
  • Age 62 and older, floating exemption: tied to natural increases in value, with an income cap of $30,000.
  • Disabled veterans: $100,896, and a surviving spouse who has not remarried or minor children can keep it.
  • Deferral program: for homeowners aged 62 or over earning no more than $15,000 gross, payment can wait until the property changes hands or the deferred balance and interest climb to 85 percent of its value.

Final eligibility rests with the assessors; a denied applicant gets notice and an appeal path.

What is different for farmland and timber in Franklin County?

Land programs carry weight in a county with about 90 people per square mile. Qualifying farm property can be assessed at 30 percent rather than 40. Under conservation use, farm and timber land is valued at its current use rather than market value, but the owner signs a covenant to keep it in that use for ten years. File for conservation use with the assessors by April 1 and pay a $25 recording fee.

A broken covenant costs twice the taxes saved, except after death or condemnation (no penalty) or medically shown illness or foreclosure (one year of savings). A sale does not trigger the penalty when the buyer signs the covenant and keeps the same use.

Timber standing on the land is untaxed until it is cut or sold; then it is valued at 100 percent of market. A mobile or modular home is taxed as personal property each year, with its return and location permit due by May 1 and the year's tax paid first.

What else does the Franklin County tax office handle that a seller may meet?

The Tax Commissioner also runs the county tag office in the Court House Annex at 1221 Hull Avenue, open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. Plan tag renewals for the 30 days leading up to the owner's birthday; a vehicle you just bought must be registered within 30 days. The office warns that some private websites charge a fee on top of the renewal; the official route is the Georgia Department of Revenue site.

Tax paid in error can be refunded on a written claim to the board of commissioners made within three years. The office says refunds rest on errors, and a disagreement over value is handled through the appeal process instead. Personal property owners file a PT-50p return every year by April 1, whether or not anything changed.

You may also see a Homeowner's Tax Relief Grant line mentioned in older materials. The tax office notes the state stopped funding that credit after the 2009 tax year, so do not expect it on a current bill.

How does a Franklin County tax sale work, and can the owner redeem?

Auctions are called for a first Tuesday outside the courthouse and advertised in the Franklin County Citizen every week for a month beforehand. Bidding starts at what the parcel owes in taxes, fees and interest.

Redemption stays open for twelve months, to the owner, creditors or other parties with an interest. The price is the buyer's purchase amount, any taxes the buyer paid since, special assessments, and a premium: 20 percent for the first year or portion, then 10 percent for each added year or portion. The buyer cannot take possession, collect rent or improve the property in that period. The county tells readers to take foreclosure questions to an attorney.

What do the Census figures say about the Franklin County market?

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate for Franklin County is 25,948 people, up 10.8 percent from April 2020, across 261.35 square miles. The county holds 11,475 housing units, and owners occupy 77.2 percent of the lived-in ones. Builders took out 142 permits in 2025. Value of the median owner-occupied home: $179,000 (2020 to 2024). Median household income: $53,046. Share of residents 65 and older: 19.6 percent.

With so many older residents, the senior exemptions above reach a sizable share of owners. Monthly owner costs have a median of $432 without a mortgage and $1,432 with one, and median gross rent is $844. Employers numbered 515 in 2023, with 7,184 employees between them, and 2022 retail sales reached $516,981,000.

More questions about Franklin County, GA Property Tax Guide

When must Franklin County taxes be paid?

By November 15 in the usual case. Late bills add 1 percent interest a month, plus a 10 percent penalty at the 90-day mark.

Who explains my Franklin County property value?

The Tax Assessor, 706-384-4896. The Tax Commissioner, 706-384-3455, handles billing and payment only.

How long do Franklin County owners have to contest a value?

Forty-five days from the notice's date. Start with the assessors; the equalization board or arbitration is next, and Superior Court is last.

Does Franklin County give older homeowners a break?

Yes. Franklin County's exemptions page prints a local $20,000 break for homeowners 65 and older, separate state breaks at ages 62 and 65 that carry income limits, and a deferral option with a $15,000 gross income ceiling.

Can an owner redeem after a Franklin County tax sale?

Yes, for twelve months, if you pay the buyer the redemption amount the county itemizes, with a 20 percent premium in year one. The tax deed holder gets no possession during that year.

Two offices share the job. One office values the land and buildings: the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner then turns that value into a bill and takes the money.

The county covers 526.70 square miles of land. Census Bureau estimates put its population at 1,098,791 in mid-2025. A house in dense Sandy Springs and one in rural Chattahoochee Hills can land in very different tax situations, so read the parcel on your own bill before relying on any county average.

Where can I visit the tax offices, and when are they open?

The Tax Commissioner lists several walk-in centers. Four of them post weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the county page gives 404-613-6100 as the phone line.

  • Government Center downtown: 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, Atlanta 30303.
  • Maxwell Road center: 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta 30022.
  • North Fulton center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Sandy Springs 30350.
  • South Fulton center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, College Park 30349.
  • Greenbriar Mall center: 2841 Greenbriar Parkway, Suite 124, Atlanta 30331.

For valuation or exemption questions, the Board of Assessors takes calls at 404-612-6440 and email at boa@fultoncountyga.gov, with its main office at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018. You can look up and pay a bill at fultoncountytaxes.org, and assessment notices are posted at fultonassessor.org.

How did the 2026 tax year unfold in Fulton County?

It ran on temporary numbers. Notices of assessment appeared online June 19, 2026, and the cutoff to contest a value was Friday, July 31, 2026 for most owners, a date now behind us.

Bills went out August 15, 2026. The state had not yet certified the 2026 digest, so the county asked the Superior Court of Fulton County for a temporary collection order, granted August 4, 2026, and used the 2025 millage rates. The City of Atlanta's share came due September 30, while the county and every other jurisdiction came due October 15. A revised bill or a refund follows only when final rates differ from the temporary ones.

If you plan to sell, find out from the Tax Commissioner whether the parcel carries a temporary or final bill, and have your settlement agent explain how any later adjustment is divided.

What does a Fulton County assessment appeal involve?

Appeal windows run 45 days from the date stamped on the notice you received. Only the assessed value is open to challenge, since the estimated tax amount is off limits.

You can submit online at fultonassessor.org, mail it in, or hand it over at a Board of Assessors office. The filing form asks you to pick among three routes: a Board of Equalization hearing, arbitration that is non-binding and covers valuation alone, or a Hearing Officer. Arbitration and the officer route may involve fees. Plan on several months, and keep paying any temporary bill that arrives meanwhile, because skipped payments add penalties.

The state's property tax FAQ lists the grounds you can raise: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. It also states that the state revenue agency cannot overrule a local board on a single appraisal.

Who qualifies for homestead relief in Fulton County?

A homestead exemption knocks down the taxable value of the house where you live. Georgia's baseline exemption is $2,000 of assessed value, and many counties stack larger ones on top.

In March 2026 the assessors announced fresh school-tax exemptions with no income test:

  • Fulton County School District: 25% of assessed value is exempt once the owner is 65 by January 1, and 50% once the owner is 70.
  • To qualify there, you must have held a homestead exemption in that district for at least 5 of the last 6 years.
  • Atlanta Public Schools district: up to $50,000 comes off assessed value when the owner turned 65 by January 1, and it can be paired with other APS exemptions.

These apply to school levies only. Owners who already have a basic exemption and fit the new criteria get the discount applied without refiling. People who did not own on January 1 apply the next year, and the county confirmed that owners who qualified for 2026 but missed April 1 could apply during the appeal period.

How do I settle the tax bill when selling in Fulton County?

The owner on January 1 carries the whole year's tax. The state revenue agency spells out that Georgia gives no partial refund when someone sells and moves, so any split with the buyer comes from the contract language.

The state's worked formula reads: (assessed value minus $2,000) times the millage rate equals the tax, with assessed value fixed at 40% of fair market value. Fulton's bill breaks the county, school and city rates apart, so check each line.

Before listing, search your parcel on the county tax site and confirm nothing is overdue. County tax liens go on the clerk's general execution docket, and unpaid taxes are best cleared before a sale. If money is owed, ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff amount and hand it to whoever prepares your settlement statement.

What do Census figures show for Fulton County housing?

The 2020 to 2024 QuickFacts table shows $458,800 at the midpoint of owner-occupied values. Owners live in 54.3% of the county's homes. Median gross rent over that span is $1,732, and the housing stock stood at 534,663 units in July 2025.

The median household earns $95,292 per the same table, and builders pulled 9,660 permits in 2025. Renters occupy about 46% of homes, which means tenant-occupied houses and properties needing work are everyday cases in Fulton, and each changes the timing of a sale.

More questions about Fulton County, GA Property Tax Guide

When does Fulton County collect property tax?

The dates change by year and by jurisdiction. In 2026 the City of Atlanta's share was due September 30 and everything else, including county and school levies, was due October 15. Your own bill prints the date, and the Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100 can confirm it.

What happens if I pay Fulton County tax late?

Interest begins the next day and runs until you pay. A 5% penalty lands on day 120, and another 5% every 120 days after, up to 20%. The office takes partial payments, though interest continues on whatever principal remains.

Can the person who bought my house still appeal the value?

Only the owner named on the notice can appeal, and the notice date starts a 45-day clock. For 2026 that clock ran out July 31 for most owners. If you sell before the next notice, ask your settlement agent who files for that year.

Does the seller or buyer pay Fulton County tax at closing?

The contract divides it. The January 1 owner carries the full year, and a seller who leaves mid-year gets no state refund. The settlement statement shows how your deal handled the split.

How do I get a homestead exemption in Fulton County?

Apply with the Board of Assessors. April 1 is the normal cutoff, and the county said a second window opens during the 45-day appeal period. Anyone who bought after January 1 files for the following year. Call 404-612-6440 to confirm your case.

Where do Gilmer County property taxes get paid?

The Gilmer County Tax Commissioner collects the bill. The main office is at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540, reachable at (706) 635-4762, and the doors are open weekdays, 8:30am until 5pm. Anyone processing a vehicle title is asked to arrive by 4:30pm. The office's tax website lets owners search a parcel and pay property tax online.

Per the state revenue department, the tax commissioner collects both county and county school taxes. City taxes are different: a municipal government bills its own tax through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed to send one combined bill. Owners inside Ellijay or East Ellijay should ask both the county office and city hall what they owe.

What is Gilmer County like beyond its tax office?

Gilmer County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia. The legislature organized it on December 3, 1832, and Ellijay was designated seat of the county in 1834. Ellijay and East Ellijay are the incorporated cities, Cherry Log is a recognized community, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls inside the borders. Its neighbors are Fannin, Dawson, Pickens, Gordon and Murray counties. Wikipedia reports 431 square miles in total, most of it cropland or forest, and notes that poultry is the biggest piece of farm output. The Apple Festival fills Ellijay each October.

QuickFacts has 33,894 people living in the county as of mid-2025, 8.1 percent above the 2020 starting count. Housing units total 19,380 and owners occupy 80.7 percent of homes. The survey median for an owner's home is $314,000, above the figure for the other two Georgia counties in the same QuickFacts comparison. Seniors account for 29.3 percent of residents, the average commute runs 28.9 minutes, and builders took out 212 permits in 2025.

With nearly three in ten residents past 65 and a commute near half an hour, Gilmer is a county where buyers weigh distance and terrain. Expect questions about road access and the lot's slope in the Blue Ridge setting.

Which due date will my Gilmer County bill show?

Read the due date on the bill itself, because Georgia lets each county pick one. The state's default for ad valorem tax is December 20, and a local governing authority may move it to December 1 or November 15 or use installment billing. After the bill is postmarked, the taxpayer gets 60 days before interest accrues.

ItemRule

What if I think my Gilmer County valuation is too high?

Start with the yearly notice of assessment and read the appeal instructions printed on it. Under state guidance the notice has to explain how to appeal, and your written appeal must reach the assessors' board and it must carry a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing. The state sets that as the last day, so mark the calendar when the envelope arrives.

Call the Gilmer County assessors' office with questions about comparable sales, property record errors or what happens after a board decision. Gather these items before you call:

  • Your parcel number, found on the bill or notice.
  • Photos or invoices that show damage, a failed septic system or other condition problems.
  • Recent sale prices of similar homes nearby.
  • The postmark date on the notice envelope, if you kept it.

What exemptions can lower a Gilmer County tax bill?

Georgia requires every county to offer certain homestead exemptions, and some counties add larger local ones. Some counties take the application at the tax office and others at the assessors, so confirm with Gilmer's staff where yours is filed. The state's rule is that failure to apply counts as a waiver, so a new occupant should file before the cutoff arrives.

The same state page covers freeport exemptions on commercial and industrial inventory, which exist only where voters adopted them and are filed with the assessors. An owner of farmland or forest should ask the assessors whether a preferential assessment such as conservation use applies and which form to use.

Which other yearly filings affect a Gilmer County owner?

A few chores repeat each year and can matter at sale time. They come from the state's county facts page, so confirm details with the Ellijay office.

  • An owner who returned or paid tax last year and skips the return this year is treated as having returned the same property at last year's final value.
  • A refund request for tax that was assessed or collected wrongly has a three year window, though an appealed assessment is refunded right away once the final value is set.
  • Vehicle owners renew the tag with the tax commissioner during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.
  • A mobile home on the January 1 list must be returned by April 1.

What happens if Gilmer County taxes go unpaid before a sale?

The state's county facts page says unpaid taxes can collect interest after the 60 day window and may also accrue penalties. The tax commissioner is the person to ask about any balance, an execution or older years owed, at (706) 635-4762.

A seller who owes tax should get a payoff number before accepting an offer. Open tax is paid at closing from the proceeds, so a low offer on a house with several years owed may leave less cash than it appears. A mobile home is returned to the tax commissioner by April 1 each year, so a seller of one should ask whether the home and the land sit under separate accounts.

How does closing work on a Gilmer County house that owes tax?

Unpaid tax shows up in the title work, so the closing agent asks the Ellijay office for the balance and settles it at the table. Deeds go on record with the superior court clerk, and long-term notes secured by real estate carry an intangible recording tax that works out to $1.50 per $500 (or part of $500) of face value, collected by the clerk in most counties and by the tax commissioner in others. Ask in Ellijay which office takes it here.

Closing costs and who pays them are set by the contract, so read that section before signing. A written cash offer lets you compare a quick sale against a listing that could sit through a mountain winter.

That can suit an heir who lives out of state, a seller with a deferred roof or well problem, or an owner who needs a firm closing date with no lender conditions. More questions about Gilmer County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where is the Gilmer County Tax Commissioner?

It sits at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540, and answers at (706) 635-4762 on weekdays from 8:30am to 5pm.

What is the state's default due date for Georgia property tax?

December 20 is the statewide default. A county can set it earlier, so look at the date on your own Gilmer County bill.

Do I have 45 days or 60 days?

They measure different things. Forty-five days is the appeal clock that starts when the assessment notice is mailed, and sixty days is the grace period after a tax bill is postmarked.

Is Gilmer County's median home value higher than nearby counties?

In the Census Bureau's comparison, Gilmer's 2020 to 2024 median of $314,000 is above Gordon County's $222,900 and Glynn County's $301,300.

Can I apply for homestead exemption after April 1?

The state rule runs through April 1 of the first year, and not applying counts as a waiver. Ask the Gilmer office what it will accept after that.

Whom do I call about a Glynn County tax bill?

The job is divided between two offices. The Tax Commissioner sends bills and takes payments at 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, phone 912-554-7000, and its counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30. The Property Appraisal Office, Suite 101 in the same building at 912-554-7093, sets values and answers exemption and appeal questions from 8:30 to 5:00 each weekday.

The tax commissioner's page lists the office's duties as billing, collecting and distributing ad valorem and title ad valorem taxes, holding delinquent tax sales and preparing the yearly digest. If you are selling, call the tax side for balances, liens and split bills, and the appraisal side for anything about value or a missing exemption.

What kind of place is Glynn County for a house sale?

Glynn County covers the southeast Georgia coast, and Brunswick is the county seat. The legislature created it on February 5, 1777 as one of the state's original eight counties. Its Sea Islands include Jekyll Island, St. Simons Island and Sea Island, and Wikipedia gives the total area as 585 square miles, with about 28 percent of that water. Interstate 95 and US 17 carry much of the traffic, and the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center occupies part of the former Naval Air Station Glynco.

The Census Bureau's estimate for July 2025 is 87,599 residents, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 census count. The county holds 45,747 housing units. The owner occupancy rate is 66.7 percent, and the survey median for an owner's home is $301,300. Median household income is listed at $69,799, the average commute is 20.0 minutes, and builders pulled 448 permits during 2025.

Brunswick is the one incorporated city on the county's Wikipedia list. A house on St. Simons or on a mainland road outside the city is therefore taxed through the county. Ask the tax commissioner whether your parcel carries any extra district charge.

When do Glynn County property tax bills go out and come due?

Glynn sends one yearly bill covering land, buildings and business personal property. The 2026 bills were mailed September 17, appeared online September 18, and were due November 17, 2026. The county's payment page warns that the schedule can shift depending on when the state accepts the digest.

Which charges apply once a Glynn County bill is overdue?

Waiting costs interest first. The county says it starts on the day following the due date, is figured monthly, and follows a rate set at the federal level. On top of that sits a 5 percent charge on the unpaid principal for each 120 day period, topping out at 20 percent of the bill. Levy fees begin only after the collection process starts.

  • The tax commissioner sends a written notice after the payment deadline passes.
  • Thirty days later, with no payment, a Fi.Fa. (execution) is issued against the owner and the parcel. The issuance fee on the county's page is $13.00.
  • The execution is then recorded on the county's general execution docket kept by the superior court clerk.
  • Money received is applied to the oldest year owed, and partial payments are possible only through the online portal.

If you are behind and plan to list, request a payoff figure first. An execution on record has to be satisfied before a buyer can take clean title.

How do I file for a homestead exemption or appeal a Glynn County value?

File the homestead application by April 1. The state revenue department's guidance lets an owner apply at any point after the house becomes the primary residence, through April 1 of the year the owner first wants the benefit, and treats a missed application as a waiver. The appraisal office can tell you which local exemptions fit your address and which papers it wants to see.

A challenge to value starts with your annual assessment notice. Under the state's description, the appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing and sent to the assessors' board. Glynn's calendar puts that stretch in June and July. Separately, a claim for tax that was assessed or collected in error has to be started within three years after the payment.

Where and how are Glynn County tax payments made?

The office takes payments online, by mail, at the counter and in drop boxes at the front and back of the Harold Pate building. An online card payment adds a service fee of 2.95 percent, never less than $2.50, and an electronic check adds $1.50. Those fees go to the payment vendor and card companies, since the office states that it keeps none of them. Mail checks to Glynn County Tax Commissioner, 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, GA 31520, and write the parcel or bill number, the property address and a phone number on the check.

Items to write on or enclose with a mailed payment, per the county's page:

  • The parcel number or bill number.
  • The property address.
  • A current phone number.
  • The payment coupon or a copy of the bill, and a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

Under state law the bill follows the January 1 owner. A separate bill goes to a new owner around the same time or late in the year, and the obligation stays with whoever owns the parcel at that point. Who reimburses whom comes from the contract. Lenders do not get copies, so a borrower with an escrow account should ask the servicer to confirm it received the bill.

Who settles the tax bill when a Glynn County house sells?

Whoever runs the closing requests the open balance from the tax commissioner, and unpaid tax is deducted from what the seller receives. Because the bill is built on the January 1 owner, a sale partway through the year normally needs a proration written into the contract. Ask whether the bill for your sale year has been issued yet, and keep the receipt from any payment so the closing agent can match it to the parcel.

We buy Glynn County houses as-is, including mainland lots with a delinquent balance or a recorded execution. A cash purchase still runs through a title search, and the tax payoff is cleared in the same way. If you inherited a coastal house that needs repairs, send us the parcel number. For a property passing under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page explains the steps.

More questions about Glynn County, GA Property Tax Guide

What was the 2026 due date for Glynn County property tax?

November 17, 2026. The county mailed bills on September 17 and posted them online on September 18, 2026.

When must a Glynn County assessment appeal be filed?

Count 45 days from the mailing date shown on your assessment notice. The county calendar shows notices going out in May and June, so the window falls in June and July.

Will the lender on my Glynn County home receive the tax bill?

No. The tax commissioner says it does not send bills directly to mortgage companies. A borrower who pays through escrow should confirm with the servicer that the bill arrived.

Are installment payments allowed on Glynn County property tax?

Only partial payments, and only online. The office states that Georgia does not allow increment payments on current year taxes before the digest is accepted and a bill exists.

What does a late Glynn County tax payment cost?

Monthly interest plus a 5 percent penalty on the past due principal every 120 days, capped at 20 percent. Levy fees are added once that process begins.

Who sends and collects Gordon County property tax bills?

The elected Tax Commissioner does both jobs. According to the county's office page, that office mails roughly 28,000 property tax bills a year and collects the county, county Board of Education and state property taxes. It also takes exemption applications, issues executions against delinquent taxpayers and sells vehicle tags.

Walk-in service is on the ground level of Government Plaza at 215 North Wall Street, Calhoun, GA 30701. Call 706-629-9242 on weekdays between 8:30 am and 5 pm. Mailed payments go to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703, and enclosing a stamped return envelope gets you a receipt.

What makes Gordon County different for a house seller?

Gordon County sits in northwest Georgia, and Calhoun is its seat of government. Georgia's legislature formed it on February 13, 1850 from parts of Cass (later Bartow) and Floyd counties, on land that had been Cherokee territory and included New Echota, the last seat of the Cherokee Nation. Cities are Calhoun, Fairmount and Plainville, and Resaca is a town. Wikipedia gives its size as 358 square miles, nearly all dry land.

Baugh Mountain and Horn Mountain rise inside the county, the eastern half drains to the Coosawattee River and most of the western half to the Oostanaula, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest lies within its borders. Neighbors include Murray, Whitfield, Gilmer, Pickens, Cherokee, Bartow, Floyd and Walker counties.

Interstate 75 runs through the middle, and the county has more interstate exits than any other Georgia county. US 41, US 411 and several state routes cross it. Manufacturing anchors the economy: Mohawk Industries, the flooring maker, is headquartered here, and Shaw Industries, Beaulieu, LG Chem and Kobelco Construction Machinery America have a presence too.

QuickFacts lists 61,701 residents for July 2025, growth of 7.2 percent since 2020. The 24,859 housing units include a 73.9 percent owner share, with a survey median value of $222,900 for owned homes. That figure is below the other two counties in the same QuickFacts table. The median household income is $63,650, drivers spend 25.3 minutes on the way to work, and 289 building permits were pulled in 2025.

When are Gordon County property tax bills due?

An administrator's report dated October 20, 2026 said the digest and collection order were expected from the state revenue department that day. The same report said bills would be sent before October 31 and fall due by the end of December. Georgia's default is December 20, and counties may adopt another date, so rely on the one shown on your own bill.

How do Gordon County tax payments and balances work?

For delinquent bills more than seven years old, the page tells owners to contact the tax commissioner's office directly.

Request the payoff from the office and keep a written copy for the closing agent. Staff can say whether a parcel has more than one year outstanding.

  • Card payment online: 2.50 percent convenience fee, set by the processor.
  • Check by mail: P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703, no fee.
  • Questions on older years: the tax commissioner's office, by phone or in person.

The same disclaimer gives closing attorneys and staff an instruction worth following: a property may be under appeal even when the website does not show it, so call 706-629-9242 for the most accurate balance before closing. The county offers no warranty on the website's figures.

What can a Gordon County owner do about the assessed value?

Use the yearly assessment notice. Georgia's guidance requires the notice to explain how to appeal. A challenge to market value is mailed to the assessors' board and must be postmarked inside 45 days of the notice's mailing. The county bills about 28,000 properties, so a high value on your notice is worth checking against neighbors.

  • Keep the notice envelope, because the mailing date starts the clock.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses and any contractor repair estimates.
  • Ask the assessors' office which forms and evidence it prefers.
  • Ask the tax commissioner how an appealed parcel appears on the bill before you pay.

Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Gordon County?

Exemption applications go to the tax commissioner, and the state lets an owner apply once the house is a primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of the benefit. Not applying is treated as a waiver. Returns are due from the first of January to the first of April. An owner who returned or paid last year and then skips the return is deemed to have filed at last year's final value.

Vehicle and mobile home paperwork also runs through this office, since it issues county and city mobile home decals and transfers vehicle titles. A seller who is also moving a mobile home off the lot should ask what must be settled first.

The Georgia revenue department also says municipalities levy their own tax, billed by the city clerk unless the city and county combined billing. Calhoun, Fairmount, Plainville and Resaca residents should ask which bills they will receive. Calhoun also has its own city school system (Calhoun Primary, Elementary, Middle and High Schools), so a home within city limits may sit in a different district than one served by the county system. Ask the tax commissioner which school levy applies to your parcel.

How does Georgia treat unpaid Gordon County tax when I sell?

After the 60 days that follow a bill's postmark, interest can accrue, and penalties may be added to unpaid balances. The tax commissioner issues executions against delinquent taxpayers, and a recorded execution sits on the title until it is paid. A refund for tax wrongly assessed or collected has to be requested inside three years after it was paid.

A seller with a balance should ask for the payoff in writing, give it to the closing attorney, and expect the title company to settle it out of the sale money. We buy Gordon County houses as-is for cash, including homes in Calhoun and the smaller towns along I-75 where an owner has older repairs, tenants or back taxes. A cash buyer still needs a clear title, so the payoff is handled the same way. If an heir received the house under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page lists what must be recorded before a sale.

More questions about Gordon County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Gordon County property tax?

Use the county's online payment site, or mail a check to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. The office is at 215 North Wall Street in Calhoun and takes calls at 706-629-9242.

How much did Gordon County lower its tax rate for 2026?

The county reported a 7.7 mill rate for 2026, down from 9.042 mills in 2024 and 2025. Its report says the last lower rate was in 2002.

Does Gordon County charge extra for card payments?

Yes. The county page lists a 2.50 percent convenience fee on credit card transactions, charged by the processor. A mailed check avoids it.

Who can tell a closing attorney the real balance on a Gordon County parcel?

The tax commissioner's office, at 706-629-9242. The county warns that a parcel may be under appeal without the website showing it.

By when must a Gordon County homeowner file for homestead exemption?

The state's cutoff is April 1 of the first year the owner wants it, and skipping the application is a waiver. In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes the applications.

Where is Grady County and which towns sit inside it?

Grady County lies along Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo is both the county seat and the largest city. The county dates from August 17, 1905, when the General Assembly cut it from parts of Decatur and Thomas; its namesake is Henry W. Grady, an orator and editor of the Atlanta Constitution (Wikipedia).

The county spans 460 square miles, 455 of them land. Water here mostly flows into the Ochlockonee River, with the northwest corner draining toward the Flint, and the Red Hills Region extends into the county. Its neighbors are Mitchell to the north, Thomas to the east and Decatur to the west, with the Florida counties of Leon and Gadsden along the south.

Cairo and Whigham are the only incorporated cities. Calvary is classed by the Census Bureau as a place, and Beachton and Spence are crossroads outside any city limits. Grady County Schools operates six public schools, including Cairo High School. Every parcel appears on one county digest, and cities can add their own levy, which makes each line of the bill worth reading before a price is agreed.

What do the Census figures say about Grady County?

Population moved slowly for decades. Wikipedia's census table shows 18,457 people in 1910, 18,015 in 1960, 23,659 in 2000 and 25,011 in 2010. The county had 26,236 residents at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate of 26,590 is a 1.4% increase. Roughly a fifth of residents (21.2%) are 65 or older, which makes age-based exemptions relevant for many owners planning a move.

Only 55 permits were issued in 2025, so resale houses make up most of the market. QuickFacts reports 19.5% of residents in poverty, and an owner who is behind on tax can ask the commissioner for a payoff number before deciding how to sell (QuickFacts).

Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?

Two offices divide the work. The commissioner's side covers bills for land, buildings, business property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber. The Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser, deals with returns, values and conservation or agricultural applications.

  • Tax commissioner, per the qPublic site: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open Monday to Thursday from half past seven in the morning until six in the evening, shut on Fridays.
  • County service pages for the commissioner and the assessor: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site has a search tool covering each parcel.

Because the two pages show different addresses and hours, call 229-377-3322 before you travel and ask where to pay. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

How does a Grady County assessment appeal work?

Georgia levies tax on 40% of a property's fair market value as of January 1, and a yearly notice lists both numbers. To challenge it, send a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed, choosing among the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on state form PT-311A (Georgia Department of Revenue FAQ).

The 2024 cycle in Grady ran late. A delayed revaluation pushed assessment notices into September, and the county told owners that some appeal windows would end October 28 and others October 31. It added that the digest would reach the tax commissioner behind schedule, that the rate could not be set until December, and that commissioners expected a significant decrease in the mill rate after the revaluation (county notice).

File the notice and any appeal letter with your closing papers; the title company may want to know which value the bill is built on.

What due date will a Grady County bill show?

December 20 is the state's default deadline. According to the Department of Revenue's Grady facts page, local officials may pick December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments, so go by the date on your own bill. No interest runs for 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can be added to balances left unpaid (Grady County property tax facts).

For an overdue parcel, get penalty and interest figures from the commissioner. Three other fixed points apply here:

  • A return for property you held on January 1 is accepted from January 1 until April 1.
  • Mobile homes sitting in the county on January 1 must be returned for tax by April 1, at the same time as the location permit.
  • Anyone seeking a refund of wrongly assessed tax has three years from payment to start the claim.

Which exemptions and special assessments can Grady County owners claim?

A homestead application can go in at any point after you move in; April 1 is the final day for the first year. The assessor's page cites code section 48-5-44, and a missed filing counts as a waiver under state rules. The standard state deduction is $2,000 off assessed value. The Department's Grady facts page lists no local amounts on top of that, though it is dated 2016, so ask the assessor whether newer ones exist.

A county notice from January 2025 said the commissioners intended to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption and scheduled hearings for February 17 and 18, 2025. Check with the assessor on what that means for your home before telling a buyer the value is frozen.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters adopted it, with filing on the return schedule.
  • A buyer files separately, since an exemption does not pass with the deed.

What did the county's 2026 millage notice say?

A county notice dated November 2026 said the Board of Commissioners had tentatively adopted a millage rate that raises property taxes by 4.72 percent. It printed a tentative rate of 12.64 mills, up .57 mill, compared with 12.070 mills at most without the increase, and listed three hearings that month at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo (county notice).

The figure speaks only to the county's own levy. School and city rates come separately, and final numbers show on the bill. For a payoff figure, request the adopted rates from the commissioner's office.

How should a Grady County seller handle tax at closing?

Liability for a year sits with the January 1 owner. By the Department of Revenue's account, selling on January 2 changes nothing, and no portion is refunded. Buyers and sellers therefore divide the bill in the contract and on the settlement statement, which should state who pays what.

  • Find out from the commissioner what the parcel owes for the present year and earlier ones.
  • Alert the closing agent to any open appeal, since a revised bill may follow.
  • Pass the payoff figure and the receiving office to the closing agent.
  • Tell the office once a homestead exemption stops applying because you have left.

A cash buyer taking the house as-is still receives the parcel along with its tax history, so arrears are best listed on the settlement statement.

More questions about Grady County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?

Head to the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. The commissioner's own page gives 114 1st Street NE with Monday to Thursday hours, while the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of eight to five. Call 229-377-3322 first to learn which counter takes payment.

What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?

The limit is 45 days from the mailing date. Postmark your letter inside that period, address it to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?

The state's county facts page, dated 2016, shows only the statewide ones. Because of the county's 2025 opt-out notice, ask the assessor which freeze rules cover your home now.

If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?

The January 1 owner. No part of the year is refunded, so the contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before you close.

Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?

Yes, if the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Ask in writing within three years of paying. When the assessment is under appeal, the refund follows automatically once the final taxable value is fixed.

What towns and landmarks make up Greene County?

Greene County occupies Georgia's east central Lake country, with Greensboro serving as seat and as its largest community. Lawmakers formed it on February 3, 1786 out of Washington County land, and it carries the name of Nathanael Greene, a major general of the Revolution (Wikipedia).

Of 406 square miles in total, 387 are land and 19, or 4.6%, are water. Streams drain three ways: the Oconee River across the west, the Little River flowing toward the Savannah in the north, and the Ogeechee system in the south. Part of Oconee National Forest reaches into the county, and the extinct river town of Scull Shoals recalls the county's earlier years. Interstate 20 runs through, with US 278 and State Routes 12, 15, 44 and 77 as other main roads.

The incorporated places are Greensboro, Union Point, White Plains, Woodville and the town of Siloam, and Bairdstown is an unincorporated community. Oglethorpe, Taliaferro, Hancock, Putnam, Morgan and Oconee counties ring it. Local families can choose among the Greene County School Board, Lake Oconee Academy and Nathanael Greene Academy. A house on the lake and a house in town receive their bills from the same tax commissioner.

How have Greene County's population and housing changed?

The 2020 count found 18,915 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 21,367 is 13.0% higher. People aged 65 and up are 33.5% of the total, about one in three, which is why the senior exemptions further down reach many local owners. Looking back, Wikipedia's table lists 5,405 people in 1790 and 17,547 in 1880, and QuickFacts shows 15,994 in 2010. Wikipedia links recent growth to people moving to Reynolds Lake Oconee.

The 311 permits recorded for 2025 mean new homes keep joining the rolls, and the digest moves each year. A midpoint figure tells you little about one parcel, so rely on the numbers printed on your own assessment notice (QuickFacts).

Which Greene County office takes which tax question?

Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro, and three other bodies shape the bill. The county commissioners and the school board each levy a rate to fund their own budgets, and a Board of Equalization named by the grand jury hears disputes over the assessors' values. The commissioner handles bills and collections for land and buildings, business property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues vehicle tags as the state's agent. Values, returns and exemption approvals sit with the tax assessors.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101 at 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, lobby hours run Monday to Friday, from eight until a quarter to five.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 in the same building, phone 706-453-3355, for values, appeals and homestead filings.

Hours and forms appear on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.
