When does Greene County expect payment?

The county sets December 1 as its payment date and pushes it to the next working day if the 1st is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday. Per the commissioner's page, land whose tax goes unpaid may be levied on and later sold.

Other dates follow a set pattern. A return lists what you held on January 1 and can be filed through April 1. Land and buildings carry forward at their earlier value, whereas business and other personal property need a new return every year. Under the state's county facts sheet, a mobile home must be returned by April 1 and its location permit renewed between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, with millage rates set later.

How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?

Owners get 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. You may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, using the state's PT-311A form sent to the Board of Tax Assessors. That first filing also has to say which route you are taking.

  • Equalization route: the assessors look at it first and may issue a corrected notice, which you can contest within 30 days; an appeal they leave alone is heard by the Board of Equalization, and Superior Court is the final stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser can take value disputes, but only on real property that is not a homestead and is valued at $1,000,000 or above.
  • Arbitration: attach a current certified appraisal. When the assessors turn it down, the case moves to the clerk of Superior Court, a hearing follows inside 30 days, and the arbitrator's ruling is final.

The county page walks through each route and points to the state revenue department for forms.

Which homestead exemptions does Greene County use?

For a given year you must own the home and live in it on January 1, then file by April 1; anything later waits for the next year. Once approved, the exemption carries on yearly until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, described as $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64, net income capped at $10,000: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over, net income capped at $10,000: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. As the county describes it, the freeze covers the house and land up to five acres, and it excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops (county homestead page). The county also describes a deferral program that lets owners aged 62 and older delay, though not cancel, their tax if household income reaches no more than $15,000, and farmland that qualifies is assessed at 30%.

What should a Greene County seller do about tax before closing?

According to the state revenue department, whoever holds title on January 1 stays liable for the whole year, even when the house sells the next day, and there is no refund for a partial year. Contracts usually split the bill, so the number to find is the exact balance on the parcel.

Get a written statement from the commissioner's office showing tax owed now and for earlier years. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should send. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the next owner can apply in their name.

More questions about Greene County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which day does Greene County collect property tax?

December 1, moving to the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. A parcel with unpaid tax can be levied on and in time sold, the commissioner's page says.

How much time do I have to dispute a Greene County value?

Forty-five days from the mailing date on your assessment notice. The Board of Tax Assessors needs a written appeal naming your route, which can be equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?

April 1 for the present tax year. The home must have been yours and your residence on January 1, and later applications count for the year after.

What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?

The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. It applies to the house and land up to five acres, with pools, barns, detached garages and shops left out, according to the county.

Which Greene County office do I phone about a bill or a value?

The tax commissioner, at 706-453-3358, takes bills and payments, and the tax assessors, at 706-453-3355, take values, appeals and exemptions. Both work from 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.

What is Gwinnett County like, and which cities does it include?

Gwinnett County is a core county of metro Atlanta, about nine miles northeast of the Atlanta city limits, with Lawrenceville as the seat and Peachtree Corners as its most populous city. Lawmakers established it on December 15, 1818, and the name comes from Button Gwinnett, who signed the Declaration of Independence (Wikipedia).

Total area is 437 square miles, of which 430 are land, across the upper Piedmont and along the Eastern Continental Divide. Lake Lanier reaches the extreme north, and part of the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area follows the northwest edge. Its northeastern corner was cut away in 1914 to help form Barrow County. Forsyth, Hall, Jackson, Barrow, Walton, Rockdale, DeKalb and Fulton counties share its borders.

Fifteen cities lie wholly or partly within the boundary: Auburn, Berkeley Lake, Buford, Dacula, Duluth, Grayson, Lawrenceville, Lilburn, Loganville, Mulberry, Norcross, Peachtree Corners, Snellville, Sugar Hill and Suwanee. Braselton and Rest Haven are towns, and Mountain Park is a census-designated place. Several of these cross into a neighboring county, so look at the parcel record to see which commissioner sends your bill.

Which roads, schools and employers shape a Gwinnett listing?

Interstate 85 and Interstate 985 are the main freeways, with US 23, US 29, US 78 and State Routes 8, 13 and 20 feeding them. Gwinnett County Airport, formerly Briscoe Field, is the county's own regional airfield, and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International is the closest major one. Workers average a 32.8-minute trip to work, which is worth mentioning to buyers.

The largest school system in the state is Gwinnett County Public Schools, running 143 schools: 21 high, 29 middle, 80 elementary and 13 specialty. Households within Buford city limits belong to the separate Buford City School District. Georgia Gwinnett College and Gwinnett Technical College are both in Lawrenceville.

Employers listed by Wikipedia include AGCO in Duluth, Comcast's Southeast headquarters and ASHRAE in Peachtree Corners, Canon's regional office in Norcross, and Primerica and Waffle House near Duluth and Norcross. Which district and city apply depends on where the parcel sits, and both should appear in your description of the property.

How large is Gwinnett County in the Census figures?

At the 2020 census the county held 957,062 people, second only to Fulton in Georgia. The July 2025 estimate stands at 1,018,099, up 6.3% from the estimates base, and housing units number 356,091. Foreign-born residents are 28.4% of the total. The county had 43,541 people in 1960 and 805,321 in 2010, a long climb that built the county's present digest.

Which Gwinnett County office handles which tax question?

Several offices share the work, and the tax commissioner's brochure names each. The commissioner sends bills and takes in and passes on the money, with no part in deciding the amount. The Board of Assessors sets values, while millage rates come from the commissioners, the school board and each city.

  • Property tax (tax commissioner): 770-822-8800, tax@gwinnettcounty.com, open weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Board of Assessors, real property: 770-822-7200; personal property: 770-822-7220. Values and appeals go through Gwinnett-Assessor.com.
  • Board of Commissioners, county millage rates and fees: 770-822-7000.
  • Board of Education, school millage: 678-301-6200.
  • Clerk of Court, deeds and liens: 770-822-8100.

The commissioner's brochure page is the best single reference, and its mailing address for payments is P.O. Box 372, Lawrenceville, GA 30046.

What does the Gwinnett County yearly tax calendar look like?

The county presents its dates as typical and subject to change, so the bill in your hand outranks any chart. The brochure sets out this order:

  • January: mobile home bills go out, with payment due April 1.
  • April 1: returns on business tangibles, aircraft and watercraft reach the Board of Assessors.
  • May and June: the Annual Notice of Assessment goes out, and appeals must be filed within 45 days of its date.
  • July and August: taxing bodies adopt millage rates through advertised, public processes.
  • August or September: real and personal property bills are mailed and also posted online.
  • October or November: payment comes due.

The page printed November 15, 2025 as the last due date and left the 2026 date to be determined, since the Board of Commissioners can change it yearly. Read your own bill for the date that applies. Personal property worth more than $20,000 combined is taxable, and a late or unreported return may draw a 10% penalty. A late mobile home bill adds a 10% penalty, then 1% interest each month after June 1.

What payment methods does Gwinnett County accept?

Paying online by check costs nothing, and online card payments add a convenience fee. Other options are the drop boxes open around the clock at all five tag offices, a mailed check to the Lawrenceville box, or a visit to any tax commissioner office. Cash must be handed over in person, and the county asks that none be mailed.

A few cities run their own property billing. The commissioner covers mobile home, heavy-duty equipment and timber tax in every city, yet real property inside a city that bills on its own is a question for that city's tax department.

Which exemptions apply in Gwinnett County?

Homestead exemptions cut the tax on a primary residence, and a single application serves every exemption the county offers. It can be filed year-round by mail, at an office or online, provided you lived in the home as your legal primary residence on January 1. Approval continues until ownership or eligibility changes, and mailed forms should go by certified mail.

Gwinnett also has the Value Offset Exemption, a local measure that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of the bill. School and city taxes are not covered. It attaches automatically with a homestead approval and reaches the home plus as many as five acres of land. The Board of Assessors separately reviews conservation use, agricultural, historic and Brownfield preferential assessments and tax-exempt status for property such as places of worship.

What happens to Gwinnett County tax when I sell?

Legal responsibility for the whole year rests with whoever owned on January 1. After a later sale, the earlier owner and the new owner both get a bill, and the commissioner takes no position on how they split it. That is for the two parties to settle, generally at the closing table.

An unpaid bill leads to a lien in the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows proof within 90 days of the due date that liability moved to the buyer. Acceptable proof pairs closing language in which the seller assigns property tax liability to the purchaser and the purchaser accepts it with a deed recorded in the purchaser's name. In the end a delinquent parcel can be sold at a tax auction.

More questions about Gwinnett County, GA Property Tax Guide

When are Gwinnett County property taxes due?

Typically in October or November, following bills mailed in August or September. The county gave November 15, 2025 as the last due date and left 2026 to be determined, so rely on the date printed on your bill.

What is the deadline to contest a Gwinnett County value?

The window is 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in May or June. The Board of Assessors takes the appeal, and the county says it can be filed online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com.

Who pays the tax if my Gwinnett County house sells after January 1?

The January 1 owner carries the full year, and both owners may receive a bill. Buyer and seller decide the split, usually on the closing statement.

What is the Gwinnett Value Offset Exemption?

A local exemption that holds assessed value at its base-year level for the county government share of your bill. School and city taxes are outside it, it reaches the home plus up to five acres, and it attaches automatically when a homestead exemption is granted.

Does Gwinnett County take cash for property tax?

Yes, but only face to face at a tax commissioner office. An online check payment is free and cards add a convenience fee. Never mail cash to the Lawrenceville box.

Where is Habersham County and what lies inside it?

Habersham County fills a corner of northeast Georgia in the Blue Ridge, with Clarkesville as the county seat and Cornelia as its biggest city. It was chartered on December 15, 1818, and takes its name from Colonel Joseph Habersham, who served in the Continental Army. Statistically the whole county forms the Cornelia, GA micropolitan area (Wikipedia).

The county measures 279 square miles, 277 of them land, and a share of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls within it. The top elevation is a knob around 4,400 feet just below the summit of Tray Mountain, which Habersham divides with White and Towns counties, with the Appalachian Trail following the ridge close by. The Chattahoochee River rises in what used to be Habersham County, a point Sidney Lanier's poem about the river makes with its line about the hills of Habersham.

Habersham once spread across much of northeast Georgia. White and Lumpkin counties took land from it in 1857, Banks County in 1859 and Stephens County in 1905. Rabun, Stephens, Banks, Hall, White and Towns counties now touch it, along with Oconee County, South Carolina. Raoul is a census-designated place, while Batesville, Habersham Mills, Hollywood and Turnerville are unincorporated communities. Public schooling comes from one system, the Habersham County School District, and Tallulah Falls School, Piedmont University and North Georgia Technical College are also located here.

What does Census data show for Habersham County?

The 2020 count was 46,031 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 50,416 means growth of 9.5%. About 20.3% of residents are 65 or older, and 9.4% were born abroad.

Over the long run the numbers climb steadily. Habersham had 3,145 residents in 1820, 18,116 in 1960, 35,902 in 2000 and 43,041 in 2010 before the 2020 count of 46,031, according to Wikipedia's table of census results. Owner-occupants hold close to three of every four homes, and 390 permits in 2025 show new building joining a digest of mostly older property. The commissioner's page says the appraisal staff sets values using recent sales and market conditions on January 1, so a house's figure can follow neighborhood sales (QuickFacts).

Who does what in Habersham County property tax?

The tax commissioner holds an elected constitutional office, sending bills, collecting, accounting for and disbursing the money, and takes no part in setting values or rates. Values are the job of the Board of Tax Assessors, which started in 1968 with three members and has had five since January 1, 1990, each serving a three-year term. Rates are set by the county commissioners and the school board, while the state's own levy cannot go beyond one-fourth of a mill.

  • Tax commissioner: 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120, open on weekdays from 8:00 until 4:45, with Saturdays closed until further notice.
  • Tax assessors: phone (706) 839-0100, the number the county gives for mobile home registration questions.
  • Board of Tax Assessors meetings: second and fourth Mondays monthly, beginning at 9 a.m.

The assessors' board has a long to-do list that matters to sellers: it decides which properties are exempt, approves or denies Conservation Use applications and homestead exemptions, reviews tax returns, and levies penalties against property that was never returned. It also meets with taxpayers to talk through concerns, so a seller who doubts a value can ask for that conversation before listing.

Further detail sits on the commissioner's information page and the assessors' board page.

Which dates drive a Habersham County tax bill?

The commissioner's page names August 15 as the mailing target and November 15 as the payment date, both in the same year. That is earlier than the state default of December 20. Mobile and modular homes use a different cycle, since their bills usually go out around February 1 and the tax and location permit are tied to April 1.

Missing the April 1 payment and permit on a mobile home brings a 10% penalty, a citation to appear in the county's Magistrate Court, and in the end possibly a sale of the home. A decal has to be displayed, and registration is done through the assessors' office.

How does a Habersham County assessment appeal proceed?

Spring is when assessment notices normally arrive, and an unhappy owner then has 45 days from the date on the notice. The written appeal may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it goes to the Board of Tax Assessors naming the method you have picked.

Mobile homes carry an extra step on this page: if the owner still disagrees after a changed value, the county says an appeal to the Board of Equalization can follow within 21 days of that notice. That board is appointed by the grand jury and exists to hear administrative appeals from the assessors' values. For a regular parcel, ask the assessors' office for forms and the exact sequence.

Which Habersham County exemptions and special valuations should I know about?

Homestead applications are handled by the Tax Assessor's office, and new buyers should carry in the warranty deed. Filing by April 1 covers your first claimed year, and a late filing slides to the following year. After approval the exemption renews itself until your residence, ownership or qualifying category changes. The county reports local exemptions that take the place of state ones whenever the local amount is greater.

  • Land in genuine agricultural use can be assessed at 30% rather than 40% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use valuation is granted in return for a covenant with the assessors to keep the land in qualifying use for ten years at least.
  • Freeport exemption for manufacturers can reach three categories: raw goods, goods being processed, and finished goods held in a warehouse for out-of-state shipment; applications are filed between January 1 and April 1.
  • A business's equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40% of fair market value.

What should a Habersham County seller do when tax is still due?

Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible for the whole year and refunds nothing for a partial year. The sale contract normally decides who actually pays, so begin by learning the precise balance.

Phone the tax commissioner at (706) 839-0120 and ask what the parcel owes for this year and any before it. When closing lands between the August mailing and the November 15 date, let the closing agent know whether the new bill has gone out and been paid. A mobile home bill follows the April 1 cycle and stands apart from real property. A homestead exemption ends when you move or ownership changes, so tell the assessors after you leave and let the buyer file separately.

More questions about Habersham County, GA Property Tax Guide

What day is Habersham County property tax due?

Bills are mailed by August 15 and payment is expected by November 15. For mobile and modular homes, bills typically go out near February 1 and the tax is tied to April 1.

Where do I find the Habersham County tax commissioner?

The Main Office is at 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120. Weekday hours end at 4:45, starting at 8:00, and Saturdays are closed until further notice.

What is the time limit to appeal a Habersham County value?

You have 45 days from the date on the notice. A written appeal naming your chosen method goes to the Board of Tax Assessors.

By when must a Habersham County homestead application arrive?

April 1 in the first year you claim. Take the application to the Tax Assessor's office, with your warranty deed if the purchase is recent.

Is farmland taxed differently in Habersham County?

Sometimes. Qualifying agricultural property is assessed at 30% of fair market value, not 40%, and Conservation Use valuation applies current-use value in exchange for a covenant of ten years or longer with the assessors.

Which offices handle property tax in Hall County, Georgia?

Two Gainesville offices split the work. Appraisal belongs to the Board of Assessors; the Tax Commissioner mails the statements and takes payment. Neither sets the rate. Mill levies are voted by the county commissioners, the school board and each city that taxes on its own.

Hall County covers 429 square miles, 393 of them land, in the upper Piedmont just below the Blue Ridge foothills. The whole county makes up the Gainesville metro area, Gainesville is the county seat, and the Chattahoochee River gathers strength here on its way to Lake Sidney Lanier. The county was created in 1818, and the incorporated places are Gainesville, Buford, Flowery Branch, Oakwood, Lula, Gillsville, Braselton and Clermont. Most of the county sits in the Hall County School District, while parcels inside the city limits of Buford and Gainesville fall under those cities' own school systems, which changes the millage that applies.

Schools vary by address. High schools in the county include East Hall, North Hall, West Hall, Chestatee, Cherokee Bluff, Flowery Branch and Johnson with Gainesville High on the city side. Brenau University, Lanier Technical College and a University of North Georgia campus are all in Gainesville, and the Crescent train stops at the Amtrak station on Industrial Boulevard.

  • Billing and payment questions: Tax Commissioner, 770.531.6950 option 3, open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • City bills: owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood receive a second statement from that city.

When are Hall County property tax bills due?

Sixty days after mailing is the rule in Hall. A normal season means a September 15 mailing and a November 15 deadline. The 2026 statements went out October 15, a month late because the state approval of the digest came late, so the deadline became December 15, 2026.

The county explains that the 60 day gap stays fixed even when the mailing slips, so a later bill gives you a later deadline. Interest starts building monthly once the deadline passes. Because the mailing date drives the deadline, plan around the date on your own statement.

Paying early is easy. The online portal at HallCountyTax.org shows payment status for every parcel and keeps records and receipts for the past ten years. Hall County lists E-Check as the cheapest route, at a flat $1.50. Expect 2.49% on a credit card and 1.50% on a debit card. You can also mail the pay slip to P.O. Box 1579, Gainesville, GA 30503, use the 24 hour drop box under the breezeway at the Government Center on Browns Bridge Road, or pay by phone with a card.

How do I appeal a Hall County assessment?

Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice is the limit. Hall takes appeals three ways: online in qPublic, by post to P.O. Box 2895, Gainesville, GA 30503, or at the counter at 2875 Browns Bridge Road.

If you do nothing in that window, the value goes to the Tax Commissioner for billing. The notices are mailed to every owner each year, and the 2026 digital copies were posted on qPublic.

Appealing never freezes the bill. Hall County sends an Under Appeal statement for the 2026 cycle, and the amount due by December 15, 2026 is the lower result of 85% of the 2026 value or 100% of the 2025 value. Any unpaid portion still accrues monthly interest from that date. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that a refund after a final appeal decision is processed automatically, and that other refund claims for erroneous or illegal taxes must start within three years of payment.

What exemptions and filing deadlines apply in Hall County?

  • Boats, personal watercraft, aircraft, business personal property and manufacturer personal property returns go under the Personal Property tab. Returns filed after April 1 carry a 10% late filing penalty.
  • Conservation Use covenants are the exception: they are taken in person at the Government Center, where an appointment is advised.

The state revenue department's Hall County fact sheet treats a missed homestead filing as a waiver. You may apply any time once the house is your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of relief. Call 770.531.6720 about real property or 770.531.6749 about personal property.

Who owes the tax when a Hall County house sells?

Hall County holds the January 1 owner of record answerable for that year's tax, even when the house changes hands in spring or summer. Who actually writes the check is a closing-table question, and the closing attorney handles it.

Hall County adds a step that sellers should not skip. If you sold real property during 2026, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the due date, which works out to March 15, 2027. When the documents clearly shift liability to the new owner, the seller is no longer billed. Papers that arrive after March 15, 2027 cannot be considered. Boats, planes and business fixtures work the same way: whoever owned them in January stays on the hook after a sale.

Homeowners with an escrow account should know the county passes tax data to the mortgage servicer, yet the owner still answers for payment. Before listing, ask the Tax Commissioner what your parcel owes and hand that number to the closing attorney.

Of the four counties in this set, Hall is the priciest. Federal survey results for 2020 to 2024 give a typical owned home value of $350,400, household income of $80,901 and monthly rent of $1,341.

Who bills and values property in Hancock County, Georgia?

Two Sparta offices share the work here. One sets what each parcel is worth and approves exemptions. The other prints the bills and banks the payments for the county government and the Hancock schools. Rates come from elsewhere: the county commissioners and the school board settle the mill levy every year.

Hancock sits in east central Georgia and feels like it: open farmland, pine tracts and long county roads. Of its 479 square miles, 472 are land. Sparta is the one incorporated city, and no Interstate runs through the county. Taliaferro, Warren, Glascock, Washington, Baldwin, Putnam and Greene counties surround it. The head count fell from 9,429 in 2010 to 8,735 in 2020, and the latest federal estimate, 8,682, shows the drift continuing.

  • Tax Commissioner: 9031 E. Broad Street, Sparta, phone 706-444-5148. The public counter shuts a quarter hour before five.
  • Tax Assessor: the same street address, phone 706-444-5721.
  • Copies of recorded deeds: the courthouse deed room.

What land and history come with a Hancock County property?

Hancock was created in December 1793 and named for John Hancock. Before the Civil War it was cotton country, and its fertile soil places it in the Black Belt. Enslaved people were 61% of the 1850 population. The Oconee River basin drains most of the county, with the northeastern corner falling in the Ogeechee basin.

Outside Sparta, the settled places are small: Culverton, Devereux, Jewell and Mayfield are unincorporated communities. The Census table shows just 24 building permits in 2025 and a civilian labor force participation rate of 30.1%, with a mean trip to work of 35.4 minutes. Roughly 76% of adults over 25 finished high school and 10.3% hold a bachelor's degree. Few Hancock listings sit in a subdivision. Expect acreage, farmhouses and inherited family places, where the legal description of the land counts as much as the building.

What happens if a Hancock County tax bill goes unpaid?

According to the commissioner's FAQ, houses, land and business equipment fall due November 15, while manufactured homes fall due April 1. Treat the date printed on your own bill as final, since a second county page gives a different November day.

Late real estate bills pick up 1% interest every month. Once three months pass with the balance open, a flat ten percent penalty lands on top. Roughly a month after the deadline, the office can record a tax lien, called a FiFa, in the superior court clerk's docket. These liens are public, credit bureaus can pull them, and the office says it has no hand in how they are reported. Seizure of the property is the final step, and the office describes it as a last resort.

Manufactured housing follows another track. A mobile or modular unit counts as personal property, needs a return and a location permit, and the permit is withheld until that year's tax is settled. Past April 1 the county adds a ten percent filing penalty and a monthly one percent interest charge. A unit that stays unpaid can go to auction.

How can a Hancock County owner contest a value?

Forty-five days is all you get, and the clock starts on the date shown on the notice of assessment, so mail the appeal to the assessors early. When they stand by their number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, then onward to superior court.

In the FAQ's sequence, the assessors look at their own figure again and tell you what they decided. Still unhappy? A hearing follows before the Board of Equalization, whose members the Grand Jury appoints. Arbitration can replace that hearing. After either result, a written notice to the assessors keeps your case alive for superior court.

Hancock taxes forty percent of a parcel's January market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that slice and the mill rate is applied to the remainder. Ask the assessor's staff to show the math on your own parcel.

What exemptions can Hancock County homeowners claim?

Most homeowners begin with homestead. Take the form to the assessor's office. Two conditions apply: you lived in and owned the house when the year began, and the form must be in hand before April. A filing after that point earns nothing until the following year.

  • A granted homestead exemption renews itself as long as you stay put. A move requires a new application for the new address.
  • Owners who reach 62 may apply for an extra exemption, according to the FAQ. The assessor can say which forms are current.
  • Business owners can ask about freeport relief on inventory, and farm and forest owners can ask about the ten-year conservation use and preferential farm programs.

Returns have a spring window that closes April 1. The first real estate return carries forward at last year's value, so you refile only after building or buying more land. A new return with a lower figure is also how a dispute over the current value begins.

How much is a typical Hancock County house worth?

Home prices in Hancock are among the lowest in Georgia. Survey data for 2020 through 2024 value the middle owned house at $88,600 and set the middle monthly rent at $938. About 79% of the homes with residents are owner-occupied.

Notice the distance between 5,088 homes and 2,922 households. Wikipedia's summary of the 2020 census puts the vacant share of housing at 32.6%. A vacant family house or an inherited one still produces a tax bill each year, so call the commissioner before listing to learn what the parcel owes.

How does an unpaid tax bill affect a Hancock County closing?

The bill for a given year lands on the person who owned the parcel when that year opened, which in a sale is normally the seller. The purchase contract and the closing attorney decide how to divide it. Before closing day, request a written payoff from the Sparta commissioner's office.

A buyer's title search will turn up back taxes, and any recorded FiFa must be satisfied at the closing table. With a lien or an unpaid mobile home tax already on file, phone 706-444-5148 early, since the office may levy on property that stays unpaid.

Heirs should also check whose name is on the deed. A warranty deed copy comes from the courthouse deed room, and new homeowners should carry one to the assessor when filing for homestead. The commissioner's office and the assessor's office share the East Broad Street address in Sparta, and the courthouse is in town as well, so one trip can settle the payoff figure, the exemption status and the deed copy.

More questions about Hancock County, GA Property Tax Guide

When do Hancock County property tax bills come due?

November 15 for houses and land, April 1 for mobile homes, per the commissioner's FAQ. Another county page lists a different November day, so call 706-444-5148 and follow the bill.

What does it cost to pay Hancock County property tax late?

Interest of 1% accrues every month on real estate, and the 10% penalty is added when 90 days go by. A FiFa lien becomes possible after a month.

What is the window to dispute a Hancock County value?

Forty-five days, starting at the notice date. The written appeal goes to the assessors first.

What is the last day to file for homestead in Hancock County?

Get the form to the assessor's office before April arrives; the home must also have been yours, and lived in by you, on New Year's Day. A late form counts toward the next year.

Are mobile homes taxed differently in Hancock County?

Yes. They count as personal property with an April 1 deadline, and no location permit is issued until the year's tax has been paid.

Where is Haralson County and who runs its property tax?

Haralson County sits in northwest Georgia on the Alabama line. It covers 282 square miles and was carved out of Carroll and Polk counties in 1856 as Georgia's 113th county. Buchanan holds the courthouse, and the county's own website says nearly 30,000 people live here. The newest federal estimate, 33,066, is 10.5% above the April 2020 base.

Property tax splits across two desks. The assessors appraise each parcel and take exemption filings. The Tax Commissioner builds the digest, issues bills and collects. The commissioner has no say over value or millage; those come from the assessors and from the county commissioners and the other taxing bodies such as cities and schools.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: 4266 GA Highway 120, Buchanan, 770-646-2022, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-646-2020 for payment and billing questions.
  • Towns inside the county: Bremen, Buchanan, Tallapoosa and Waco. Ask the clerk in the town where the house sits whether it sends its own bill.

What towns and neighborhoods affect a Haralson County sale?

Haralson County has four incorporated places and three small unincorporated communities. Bremen is the largest city, at about 6,500 residents, followed by Tallapoosa at roughly 3,155, Buchanan at 1,159 and Waco at 522. Budapest, Draketown and Felton are unincorporated.

Each town has its own story, and that shapes the houses you find there. Bremen grew around the railroad and became known as a clothing capital of the Southeast, with men's suits shipped nationwide. Tallapoosa, the Dogwood City, began as a gold mining town and opened Georgia's first free school in 1889. Buchanan's 1891 courthouse still stands on the square, and Waco is home to West Georgia Technical College. The county also lists a major hospital and two public school systems, so the school district a house falls in is worth checking during a sale.

State revenue guidance says a city may levy its own tax and have its clerk bill it, unless city and county agreed to one combined bill. A Bremen or Tallapoosa address can therefore mean two statements, while a house in an unincorporated community like Felton or Draketown sees only the county bill.

When are Haralson County property taxes due?

December 1 is the payment deadline for land and houses; mobile homes are billed for April 1. Late balances add interest every month at a rate pegged to prime, plus a 5% penalty at each 120 day mark until the penalties reach 20%.

Under the state's guidance, interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark. The county's tax calculation page spells out how the bill is built: the assessors' value times 40 percent gives the assessed value, and the millage rate from the commissioners and other levying bodies is applied to that figure.

The Tax Commissioner's office also handles tag renewals, titles, mobile home decals, timber tax and handicap placards. The title desk stops processing at 4 p.m., so plan a closing-day errand with that in mind. The county posts a notice each year with the current digest and the five year history of the levy, as Georgia law requires.

How do I appeal a Haralson County valuation?

Appeals go in writing to the assessors before the cutoff on the yearly notice. In 2025 the notices were mailed June 6 and the cutoff was Monday, July 21, long past.

The assessors define market value as the price an informed buyer and a willing seller would agree to in an arm's length deal. The notice also shows estimated taxes based on the prior year's millage, so the real bill can differ once the commissioners and the Board of Education set rates, usually between July and August.

Haralson County's appeals volume has been heavy. The assessors' page states that appeals passed the 3 percent threshold in O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, which gives the board an extra 180 days to decide and notify owners. Anyone with an open appeal can call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for status. Field appraisers may visit a property under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and carry photo identification in a marked county vehicle.

Which Haralson County exemptions and programs matter to sellers and owners?

The homestead exemption is the common one, and the Haralson County page tells owners to file with the Tax Commissioner's office. Ownership on New Year's Day plus an April 1 filing earns the current year's benefit. A late application waits until the next calendar year.

  • Homestead: applies to the house and its land when you live there as your legal residence. A person away for health reasons is not denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office for them.
  • Conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment: both use a 10 year covenant, and apply between January 2 and April 1. The county says preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage, and conservation use can save more than 50 percent in some cases.
  • Residential transitional assessment: a 10 year covenant for land moving from residential to commercial use.

Covenants matter in a sale. A farm or timber tract under a 10 year covenant carries obligations the buyer has to continue, so ask the Specialized Assessment department at the assessors' office what a transfer does to the covenant before you sign a contract.

What should a Haralson County seller do about the tax bill?

Phone the Tax Commissioner at 770-646-2020 to learn the parcel's balance and whether this year's bill exists yet. Bills fall due December 1, so a closing earlier in the year often happens before the statement exists, and the contract has to say who covers that gap.

Interest and penalties stack up after the due date. Interest is added monthly, a penalty of 5% attaches at each 120 day mark, and the total penalty stops at 20%. A buyer's title search will pick up unpaid taxes, so a written payoff figure from the commissioner helps the closing attorney.

  • Confirm whether you filed for homestead by April 1 and whether it applies to the buyer's first year.
  • For a mobile home, remember the April 1 due date, which is separate from the December 1 bill on land.
  • If the land is under a conservation or preferential agricultural covenant, ask the assessors what a transfer does to it.

How does Haralson County's housing market compare?

Haralson County is mid-priced for rural west Georgia. For 2020 to 2024 the survey gives $227,500 as the middle value of an owned home, $72,127 as the middle household income and $923 as the middle rent.

The average trip to work takes 33.8 minutes, second only to Hancock among these four counties. Land area is 282.17 square miles with about 106 people per square mile, so the county is far less crowded than Hall County to the northeast and far busier than Hancock County to the east.

When is Haralson County property tax due?

December 1 for land and houses, April 1 for mobile homes. Interest builds monthly at a prime-linked rate. A 5% penalty hits at each 120 day mark, and penalties stop at 20%.

Which number do I call about a Haralson County tax bill?

Call the Tax Commissioner's office at 770-646-2020 for billing and payment. Questions about value or appeals belong with the assessors at 770-646-2022.

What is the Haralson County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1. Ownership on January 1 and a filing by the return deadline are required. A later filing is held until the following calendar year.

Does Haralson County offer a break for farmland?

Yes. Both conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment ask for a ten year covenant, with applications taken January 2 through April 1. The county says preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage over fair market value.

Why is my Haralson County appeal taking so long?

Appeals passed 3 percent of parcels or digest value, so O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 gives the assessors an extra 180 days to rule. Call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for the status of your appeal.

What is Hart County, Georgia, and who handles its property tax?

Hart County is lake country in the northeast corner of Georgia, right beside I-85. Hartwell is the county seat, Lake Hartwell supplies 222 miles of shoreline, and Exit 177 on I-85 is about an hour and a half from Atlanta. Federal figures list 232 square miles of land and 28,639 residents as of 2025.

Hart County was formed in 1853 from parts of Elbert and Franklin counties and is the only Georgia county named for a woman, the Revolutionary War figure Nancy Hart. Gateway Industrial Park sits at the I-85 exit, and the county shares an airport and an animal shelter with Franklin County. The county's own profile cites about 49 inches of rain a year, with summer averages near 89 degrees and winter averages near 57, which is the climate any buyer's inspector will be reading a house against.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: P.O. Box 810, Hartwell, GA 30643, 706-376-3997. Values property, takes homestead applications and handles appeals.
  • Tax Commissioner: in the courthouse in Hartwell. Collects property tax, auto tags, timber payments, mobile home tax and the intangible recording tax.
  • Records: the county website links to a property tax record search and to an online payment site.

When are Hart County property taxes due?

Hart's assessment page describes a December 20 deadline in a normal year, with state law holding off interest for 60 days after mailing. Whatever your bill prints is the date that counts.

Georgia's revenue department puts it the same way: December 20 is the official statewide due date, a county can move it to December 1 or November 15, and a bill carries a 60 day grace from the postmark. Penalties can attach to delinquent taxes on top of interest. Hart County's tax commissioner has added a drop box outside the courthouse for property and auto payments, and an online payment option is linked from the county website.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. A mobile home standing in Hart on January 1 must be returned to the Tax Commissioner by May 1, and the yearly location permit window is January 1 to May 1 as well. A newly placed home needs a permit within 30 days. Ask the Tax Commissioner when the tax on a mobile home account falls due.

How do I challenge a Hart County assessment?

Hart wants the appeal postmarked inside 45 days of the date on the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. That notice goes out when they disagree with the value you returned.

Hart County states that every parcel is reevaluated each year, and a tax notice is sent out each year by April 15. Owners in Hartwell and on the lake shore should read that notice as soon as it arrives, because the 45 day appeal clock starts from the notice date. The assessors' office will explain the filing procedure by phone.

Another route runs through the return. A return can be filed with the assessors from January 1 through April 1. The tax commissioner's page tells owners who think their value is too high to file a return reducing it by April 1 in order to have a chance at a lower value for the next year's taxes. The state revenue fact sheet gives three years from payment to claim back tax that was wrongly or illegally collected, with a written claim to the county governing authority.

What homestead and exemption rules apply in Hart County?

Hart expects the homestead filer to live in the house as a legal residence, and the paperwork goes to the assessors' office. A person away for health reasons will not be denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office on their behalf.

  • Owning the property on January 1 and filing by the April 1 return date secures the exemption for that tax year.
  • Certain elderly owners qualify for additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead. The Tax Commissioner's page urges eligible owners to apply by April 1 so the benefit carries into later years.
  • Call the assessors at 706-376-3997 to ask whether a local homestead exemption sits on top of the state ones for your parcel.

Timing matters in the sale year. A buyer who moves in after New Year's files for a personal exemption later, and the seller's old filing does not follow the seller to a new address. The state revenue sheet treats skipping the application as a waiver.

What do the Census numbers show for Hart County housing?

Population rose 10.9% from the April 2020 base to the 2025 estimate, and about one resident in four is a senior. With 13,800 housing units against 11,034 households, the county has more homes than households. Owners of a house that sits empty part of the year should ask both offices whether an exemption they hold still applies.

What local features shape a Hart County sale?

Lake Hartwell drives much of the local market. The county profile highlights its parks, camp sites, marinas and boat ramps, and annual events such as the Antique Boat Festival and a dam run. Hartwell itself has historic homes near a downtown shopping district, and the county reports a 74 bed hospital with a 24 hour emergency room, which counts for a county where 24.6% of residents are 65 or older.

Daily travel runs on the roads and I-85. Hart Transit offers local rides on weekdays at 706-376-3975, and the county profile lists Clemson and Athens as within commuting distance. A shoreline lot, a farmhouse and a Hartwell bungalow can each raise different tax questions, from acreage covenants to homestead, so gather the parcel number before calling either office.

What should a Hart County seller know about recording and closing costs?

Hart County's Tax Commissioner collects the intangible recording tax. A lender holding a long-term note on real estate has 90 days to record the security instrument locally. The charge is $1.50 per $500 of the note, rounded up for any fraction.

A seller mostly needs the property tax payoff and a clean title. The county homepage lists 185 West Franklin Street in Hartwell as the overnight and physical address for the Clerk of Superior Court, who handles recording, and it notes that mail to the office had been coming back from the post office.

Before listing a Hart County house, gather your latest assessment notice, the most recent tax bill, any mobile home permit records and any covenant paperwork. Get the unpaid balance from the Tax Commissioner, then settle with the closing attorney who carries this year's bill.

When are Hart County property taxes due?

Hart describes December 20 as the normal deadline, and state law holds off interest for 60 days after mailing. Go by the date on your bill.

How soon must a Hart County appeal be filed?

Postmark it within 45 days of the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. Phone 706-376-3997 for the steps.

When is the Hart County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1. You need to have owned and lived in the house on January 1, with the form at the assessors' office by the return deadline.

Where do I pay a Hart County mobile home tax?

Pay the Tax Commissioner. The return and the yearly location permit both fall between January 1 and May 1, and whoever owned the home there on January 1 files.

Does Hart County reassess every year?

Yes. The county says it reevaluates every parcel each year and sends notices by April 15, with 45 days to appeal a value you dispute.

Which Heard County tax office should I call first?

Two rooms in the Administration Building in Franklin split the work. Room 300 takes payments. Room 400 sets parcel values and approves exemptions. Walking into the wrong one costs an afternoon.

Heard County tax offices at the Franklin administration building
OfficeAddress and mailPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner201 Park Avenue, Room 300, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 519(706) 675-3391Weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM
Board of Tax Assessors201 Park Avenue, Room 400, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 476(706) 675-3786Weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, shut for lunch at noon until 1:00 PM

The Tax Commissioner's counter began staying open through lunch on September 1, 2026. The assessors did not announce the same change, so schedule an assessor visit outside the noon hour. The commissioner's email is heardtc@heardcountyga.com and the assessors answer at heardtax@heardcountyga.com.

How did Heard County, Georgia, take shape?

Georgia carved Heard County out of Carroll, Coweta and Troup counties in 1830, giving it 301 square miles. Its history page calls it the state's seventy-seventh county, and it says Creek holdings were lost under the 1825 Treaty of Indian Springs. State land lotteries then placed settlers on the parcels, mostly families moving within Georgia in search of better ground.

Franklin, named for Benjamin Franklin, existed as a village by 1770 and gained a charter in 1831. Fire destroyed the first courthouse in 1893, a replacement opened in 1894, and the building in use now replaced that one in 1964. Centralhatchee incorporated in 1903 and Ephesus in 1964. Stony ground discouraged big farms, so households lived by subsistence farming until cotton brought a period of relative prosperity once the war ended. The boll weevil, a falling cotton market and the Great Depression pushed many families out, and the people who stayed turned to timber.

That history still shows on the map. Today a large share of acreage is held for lumber, beside a few beef and poultry producers and some factory work. A seller with a wooded tract is dealing with land-use questions that a seller with a Franklin city lot never meets.

What do Heard County housing numbers look like?

Census QuickFacts lists 12,149 residents for Heard in July 2025, a 6.5% gain on the 2020 base of 11,410. Land area is 295.97 square miles, which worked out to 38.6 residents per square mile at the 2020 count. Owner-occupied homes carried a median value of $186,800, and renters paid a median of $917 a month.

  • 4,979 housing units and 4,309 households.
  • Homeowners occupy 72.3% of homes.
  • Permits issued during 2025: 54.
  • Persons aged 65 and over: 17.8%.
  • Persons in poverty: 12.5%.
  • Share who stayed in the same house for a full year: 93.2%.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 120.

Few households move in a given year, and only 54 permits were issued countywide in 2025. A listing here usually competes with older resale houses and country properties. Workers spend 34.9 minutes getting to work on average, a fairly long commute.

Why does a Heard County field visit matter before I list?

The assessors' office exists to settle taxability, value and equalization, to mail owners a notice when a value moves, and to approve the exemptions people claim. A county press release dated March 12, 2026 told owners that field staff would be visiting each parcel to update the digest. They take a front photo and a rear photo of every structure and log changes since the previous countywide update. Heard says the state requires this cycle every three years.

Crews carry county identification and vehicle markings. A door hanger is left when nobody answers, so the owner can confirm the interior description. Before you list, phone (706) 675-3786 and ask what the card on your parcel says about bedrooms, baths, outbuildings and finished space. A garage that was converted years ago but still appears as a garage on the record can pull the value in the wrong direction, and a correction before the notice goes out costs you nothing.

  • The valuation date is January 1, and the taxable share is 40% of fair market value.
  • The assessors point owners to a qpublic portal for parcel records.
  • Returns of value are accepted from January 1 until April 1.

What can I do if my Heard County value seems too high?

Put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You get 45 days counted from the mailing date on the notice, and the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or an exemption the county denied. State revenue officials cannot override the county on one parcel, so the form should not go to Atlanta.

The uniform PT-311A form asks you to pick a route up front.

  • Board of Equalization: the common choice. The assessors can change the number and mail a fresh notice, which you may contest for another 30 days.
  • Hearing officer: reserved for non-homestead property above $500,000.
  • Arbitration: disputes over value alone, with a certified appraisal due 45 days after the board acknowledges your filing.

A dispute that survives can go on to superior court after written notice within 30 days of the ruling, and the previous year's tax has to be paid first. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside an appeal because elected bodies set the millage rate on their own.

Which 2025 homestead and millage changes affected Heard County owners?

Two items on the county site are worth knowing. First, House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, lets owners file a homestead application while the 45-day appeal window is open after assessment notices go out. The Assessor's Office takes it, and you should bring photo ID showing your current address. Second, the Board of Commissioners advertised in 2025 that its tentative millage meant an 18.29 percent rise in collections: 6.467 mills against a rollback figure of 5.467.

Public hearings were held September 15 and September 23, 2025. The Tax Commissioner page posts a History of Tax Levy document for the year, which helps when you price a listing. Skip the homestead filing on a house you live in and the state treats the exemption as waived. April 1 is the usual deadline for a first-time filer.

Who owes Heard County tax when a house sells?

Whoever holds title on January 1 owes that year, and Georgia refunds nothing to someone who sells early in the year. Heard's commissioner page prints no due date, so read your bill or call (706) 675-3391. The statewide default is December 20, though a county may pick December 1, November 15 or installment billing. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill.

Unpaid tax can lead to a recorded lien and then a public auction. The county page carries a 2025 tax sale list revised October 17, 2025, plus older lists. After an auction, Georgia's consumer office says the owner has twelve months to redeem by paying the winning bid, later taxes and assessments, and a 20% premium. Anyone who inherits a house in that position should phone the commissioner early and get the payoff confirmed in writing.

More questions about Heard County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where can I pay a Heard County tax bill?

Pay at Room 300, 201 Park Avenue, Franklin, or send a check to P.O. Box 519, Franklin, GA 30217. The phone is (706) 675-3391. Weekday hours run 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, with no lunch closure since September 1, 2026.

Who decides what my Heard County house is worth?

The Board of Tax Assessors, in Room 400 at the same address, phone (706) 675-3786. The commissioner's office only bills, so value disputes go to the assessors.

How much time do I have to contest a Heard County assessment?

You have 45 days beginning on the date the notice was mailed. A new notice opens a new window. File with the county assessors, not the state revenue department.

Can I add a Heard County homestead exemption after April 1?

Sometimes. House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, opened the 45-day appeal period after notices are mailed to homestead filings. Bring photo ID with your current address to the Assessor's Office.

Can I sell a Heard County house that has back taxes?

Yes, as long as the lien is paid off at the sale. Request a payoff figure from the closing agent before signing day. If an auction has already happened, Georgia allows twelve months to redeem at the bid plus a 20% premium and other charges.

What is Henry County like, and what do its housing numbers show?

Georgia formed Henry County in 1821 from Creek lands, and its annual financial report places it about 25 miles southeast of downtown Atlanta. Its neighbors are DeKalb (north), Rockdale and Newton (east), Spalding and Butts (south) and Clayton (west). The county seat is McDonough, joined by the cities of Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove. The same report counts seven Interstate 75 interchanges inside the county and mentions a planned eighth at Bethlehem Road.

QuickFacts shows 264,922 residents in July 2025 across 318.71 square miles of land, about 755 people per square mile when the 2020 count was taken, many times Heard County's density. Permit offices issued 1,666 permits in 2025, so unsold new homes and resales share the market.

  • Typical owner-occupied home: $313,900 (2020 to 2024 median).
  • Homeowners hold 74.9% of occupied housing.
  • Rent at the median: $1,674 per month.
  • Median household income: $83,146.
  • Typical one-way commute: 33.1 minutes.

At those values, a small error in the square footage on file moves the bill, so check your digest record before setting a price.

What is the Henry County property tax deadline?

The commissioner's bill page says statements go to the January 1 owner and are payable on or before November 16, and the FAQ says mailing happens by mid-September. Counties may move the statewide December 20 default earlier, which is what this date reflects. For the 2022 digest, the fiscal 2023 financial report records a levy on August 11, billing on September 10 and a payment deadline of November 16. Whatever the calendar says, follow the date on the bill you receive.

Late payment gets costly. The commissioner says interest builds monthly and a further 5% penalty attaches every 120 days after the deadline, up to a ceiling of 20%. Mailed checks need a USPS postmark before the deadline. Since December 2025 the county reads that mark as the first automated processing date at a regional center, which can be later than the day you dropped the envelope off. A transfer from your bank's own bill-pay service has no postmark, so the money must be in hand by the deadline.

  • The online portal charges 2.5% on cards or $1.50 for an e-check, a fee set by its outside processor.
  • Daily ceilings are $20,000 on cards and $60,000 on e-checks.
  • Paying at a counter does not waive the card fee.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the lender is the contact for the bill.

Will Henry County bill the buyer after closing?

Not automatically. Statements go to the person who owned on January 1, and Henry's page explains the risk: a lien is filed against that owner unless the office receives a settlement statement inside 90 days of the due date, per Georgia Code 48-3-3. Send page one, where county taxes appear as collected, to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov with the address or a copy of the bill.

State revenue officials add that the owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year with no partial refund. Look at the Henry County line on your closing statement before signing, and as the seller, send the paper yourself instead of assuming someone else did.

Other charges can share the bill. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation fees appear on it, and a county water charge called the 2 mill tax pays for storage and pipes whether or not a home has a well. The Water Authority at 770-957-6659 explains that line.

How does a Henry County homestead application work?

File in person at either commissioner office, through the online option, or by mail postmarked on or before April 1, since only a USPS postmark counts. One filing covers you for as long as you stay put. Bring these items.

  • Driver's licenses for you and your spouse that show the property address.
  • Registrations for every vehicle at that address.
  • The warranty deed.
  • A letter from any other county or state where you own a house, confirming no homestead is claimed there.
  • The divorce decree, if one applies.

Turning 62 by January 1 opens an added reduction on the school portion of assessed value, and approved exemptions step up again at ages 65, 68 and 70. The disability version asks for two doctors' letters, or one doctor's letter with a Social Security award letter, describing 100% disability. A married couple gets only one homestead.

What if I think my Henry County value is wrong?

Count 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Tax Assessor menu on the county site includes Notice of Assessment, Property Appeals, an appeal FAQ and conservation use rules, and the state's uniform PT-311A form asks you to commit to a route.

  • Board of Equalization: the route for value, uniformity, taxability or exemption fights. Henry lists this board under the Clerk of Superior Court, with its own members, forms, calendar, FAQ and appeal process pages.
  • Hearing officer: available only when non-homestead real estate exceeds $500,000.
  • Arbitration: restricted to value, and it needs a certified appraisal 45 days after the county acknowledges the appeal.

A superior court appeal follows written notice given within 30 days of the decision, after last year's tax is paid. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, as the state revenue department summarizes it, a final value of 85 percent or less of the board's figure entitles the owner to litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

What happens if a Henry County bill goes unpaid?

The commissioner runs judicial in rem tax sales at 140 Henry Parkway on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM. Once a sale happens, a twelve-month redemption period opens for interested parties, who repay the buyer's bid plus later taxes, assessments and a 20% premium, as Georgia's consumer office explains. Before a sale, paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest releases the lien.

If you are selling with a lien open, ask the closing agent for a payoff figure well ahead of time. For background on the rate, the fiscal 2023 report lists the county general fund at 12.733 mills, level since fiscal 2017. Other levies are separate, so ask the commissioner what else appears on yours.

More questions about Henry County, GA Property Tax Guide

When are Henry County property taxes due?

The commissioner's page prints November 16, and bills mail by mid-September to the January 1 owner. The state default is December 20, so trust the date on your own bill.

How do I keep a Henry County lien off my name after selling?

Email page one of the settlement statement to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov inside the 90-day window. Without it the office records a lien against the January 1 owner.

How steep are Henry County late penalties?

Interest builds monthly, and 5% more is added every 120 days until penalties hit 20%. Make sure a mailed check has a USPS postmark before the deadline.

Where can I check a Henry County parcel's value?

Use the records search in the Tax Assessor section of the county website, or call (770) 288-7999, option 1. Billing questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 288-8180.

Can I appeal in Henry County while my house is listed?

Yes. Listing does not pause or cancel the 45-day window. A lower final value also shrinks the bill that is divided at closing.

Which Houston County office handles my property tax question?

Three groups share the job here: the Tax Commissioner, the Tax Assessors and the three city offices. Collections happen at a Warner Robins office and a Perry office. Valuation and homestead filings happen in Perry. The assessors' own FAQ says they never send out bills.

Who answers what in Houston County
QuestionOfficePhone
County bill and paymentsTax Commissioner, 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088(478) 542-2110
County bill and payments, PerryTax Commissioner, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry, GA 31069(478) 218-4940

Personal property returnsTax Assessors, Personal Property Department(478) 218-4760
City taxes: Warner Robins, Perry, CentervilleEach city's own office(478) 929-1148; (478) 988-2740; (478) 953-4734

Both commissioner offices open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. The county's pay-and-search portal lets you look up taxes online and adds a convenience fee to each payment.

How did Houston County grow into the Robins Air Force Base area?

The county dates to May 15, 1821 and carries the name of Governor John Houstoun, minus the letter u. Wattsville became the seat because it lay in the middle of the new county. It was incorporated as Perry by 1824, and the county's statistics page calls Perry the geographic center of Georgia. Two national highways later crossed in town, which earned it the name Crossroads of Georgia. Peach orchards made the county famous by 1870.

Warner Robins began as a depot the Army Corps of Engineers built on cotton fields near Wellston during World War II, and it incorporated on March 5, 1943. Centerville incorporated in 1958 and takes its name from lying between Macon and Perry. Interstate 75 and the first hospital arrived in the 1960s. The county history now calls Robins Air Force Base Houston County's biggest employer and the fourth biggest in Georgia.

  • Area: 375.54 square miles, 67th largest among Georgia's 159 counties.
  • Roads: 1,088.2 miles, 94.5% of them paved.
  • Cities: Centerville, Perry and Warner Robins.
  • Fairgrounds: the Georgia National Fairgrounds & Agricenter opened in 1990.

What do Houston County housing numbers look like?

QuickFacts puts Houston at 178,214 people in July 2025, an 8.9% rise over the April 2020 base. The county holds 74,635 housing units and permitted 1,218 more in 2025. Workers travel 22.8 minutes on average, a shorter trip than Heard's 34.9 or Henry's 33.1.

  • Typical owner-occupied house: $219,800.
  • Homeowners occupy 66.9% of housing, so roughly a third of households rent.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,208.
  • Typical household income: $80,698.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or more: 32.5%.

Sellers who rented a house out before listing it should check whether the homestead exemption still applies, because the county describes the exemption as applying to property the taxpayer owns and occupies as a legal residence.

Who is buying and selling homes in Houston County?

Employment data points to a steady local job base. QuickFacts lists 2,832 employer establishments in 2023 with 44,134 jobs, a 5.1% rise from 2022, and annual payroll near $1.86 billion. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $879 million in 2022, and retail sales ran $18,898 per resident. The county also counts 19,366 veterans for 2020 to 2024.

The county's statistics page says the county had 105,808 residents in 1998, and that twenty-three public schools have earned the Georgia School of Excellence label and four have been named National Blue Ribbon Schools. Sellers in Perry, Warner Robins and Centerville can expect buyers to weigh school and base-commute information alongside price.

How does Houston County set the value my tax is based on?

On the Tax Commissioner's page, fair market value is pinned to January 1 and the taxable amount is assessed value, set by law at 40% of it. A mill is $1.00 for every $1,000 of assessed value. Whenever the Board of Tax Assessors alters a value from last year, or from the figure an owner returned, it must mail a notice.

Real property returns on form PT-50R, plus applications for conservation use, exempt status and similar programs, must be mailed with a US postmark on or before April 1. Personal property returns share that date and are taken by mail only, with forms sent in January to anyone who owns a boat, an aircraft or a business. Call (478) 218-4750 about real estate. Parcel records are searchable on the county's qpublic site.

A seller wondering whether a city levy was paid must call Warner Robins, Perry or Centerville directly, since the assessors do not bill. Confirmation of county and school tax comes from the commissioner.

How do I claim a Houston County homestead exemption?

Submit your first application to the Tax Assessor's Office before April 1 of the year the benefit should start. Approved exemptions roll over annually. You file again only when ownership changes or you want a different exemption.

The statewide standard exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value, per the state revenue department, and some counties layer larger local exemptions on top. Ask the assessors at (478) 218-4750 which amounts apply to your parcel, and have a mid-year buyer ask how the closing date affects first-year eligibility.

How do I appeal a Houston County valuation?

Your clock is 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first, re-examines its number and writes back. Unresolved appeals continue to the County Board of Equalization for a scheduled hearing and a ruling at its close. Superior court comes after that, and the county says arbitration can replace the Board of Equalization step.

  • Permitted grounds: whether the property is taxable, the value assigned, or uniformity against similar properties.
  • Excluded: any gripe about the tax rate or amount levied.
  • Hearing officer option: limited to non-homestead real estate over $500,000.
  • Arbitration option: value only, with a certified appraisal.

If a board rules against you, a written notice of superior court appeal is due in 30 days under the state's summary, and unpaid prior-year tax blocks the hearing. Email property tax questions to taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.

What are the Houston County tax due dates, and who pays at closing?

Houston's commissioner pages list no fixed due date, so go by your bill or phone (478) 542-2110. The statewide default is December 20, which a county may shift to December 1 or November 15 or replace with installments. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked.

Title on January 1 decides who owes, and a seller leaving partway through the year gets no refund under state rules. For a Perry or Warner Robins sale, have the closing agent list county, school and city taxes on separate lines, because the cities send their own bills.

An unpaid bill can lead to a recorded lien and a later auction. Afterward, Georgia's Consumer Ed office says, a twelve-month window lets interested parties redeem by paying the bid, subsequent taxes, special assessments and a 20% premium.

More questions about Houston County, GA Property Tax Guide

Does the Houston County Tax Assessor mail my bill?

No, because the assessors' FAQ says the office does not handle billing. Phone the commissioner at (478) 542-2110 (Warner Robins) or (478) 218-4940 (Perry) for county bills, and call your city for a city levy.

By when must I file a Houston County homestead exemption?

The cutoff is April 1 of the first year you want the benefit, and the paperwork goes to the assessors. Once approved it carries forward without a new form, until the home changes hands or you ask for a different exemption.

How many days do I get to appeal in Houston County?

The window is 45 days from the day the notice was mailed, and the assessors receive the filing first. Arguing that the tax is simply too high is off the table, while taxability, value and uniformity are fair game.

Where can I visit the Houston County Tax Commissioner?

The Warner Robins office is on Carl Vinson Parkway (number 202), and the Perry office is on Perry Parkway (number 201). Counters stay open every weekday from half past eight until five.

Who pays Houston County tax when a house sells mid-year?

The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and no partial-year refund exists. Ask the closing agent to break out county, school and city lines.

How did Jackson County, Georgia take its present shape?

The legislature split Jackson County off Franklin County in February 1796, when it held roughly 1,800 square miles and Clarksboro was the first seat. Land kept leaving it: 40,000 acres went to the state college in 1801, which grew into the university campus and the city of Athens, and Madison, Walton, Gwinnett, Hall, Banks and Barrow counties were all later carved away, per Wikipedia.

What remains is about 343 square miles, 340 of them land, centered on Jefferson. The seat took that name in 1804 and now sits at the heart of a county with Banks to the north, Madison to the east, Clarke to the southeast, Barrow to the west and Hall to the northwest. Nearly all the land drains through the Upper Oconee sub-basin; a thin northern band from Maysville to just east of Commerce feeds the Broad River instead.

Braselton, Hoschton, Commerce, Pendergrass, Nicholson, Talmo and Maysville fill out the list of towns, and two of them, Braselton and Maysville, extend into neighboring counties. The countywide school district serves most addresses, while Commerce and Jefferson operate city districts of their own. Which one governs your house shows up on the tax bill.

How big and how costly is Jackson County's housing market?

Growth defines this county. QuickFacts shows 99,265 residents in mid-2025, a 30.7% jump over the 2020 starting count, and 79.3% of homes are lived in by their owners.

The 2020 count was 75,907 people, against 60,485 in 2010 and 41,589 in 2000. With 1,827 permits in a single year, new subdivisions keep arriving, and an older house is often compared with builder-new ones down the road. A 31.3-minute average trip to work suggests many residents are employed in other counties.

Who bills, who values and who records in Jackson County?

Value and payment sit in separate offices, and neither sets the rate. Property Appraisal decides worth; the Tax Commissioner mails the bill and receives the money.

  • Tax Commissioner: 4965 Jackson Pkwy, Jefferson, weekdays from 8 until 4:30; the county page gives 706-367-6320 for the office.
  • Property Appraisal (Board of Assessors): 67 Athens Street, Jefferson; phone 706-367-6330. Returns, homestead filings and appeals begin here.
  • Real estate records: deeds, plats and liens back to 1796, mailing address PO Box 7, Jefferson, GA 30549, phone 706-387-6251.

Parcel details are also searchable on qPublic through the county's links, with the caveat that the county says it is not refreshed daily. When you need a payoff or bill history, phone the Tax Commissioner.

What due date appears on a Jackson County tax bill?

December 20 is the normal date for real and personal property. The county mails in October and lets the bill be paid for 60 days after the postmark.

Late mailings do occur. In that case the Tax Commissioner treats the day after the date printed on your own bill as the delinquent date. Part-payments are welcome until that due date and are refused afterward.

Billing waits on the state. Around July 1 the county submits its digest to the Department of Revenue, approval typically returns within a week, and only then can the Tax Commissioner bill and collect.

What else does the Jackson County Tax Commissioner's office handle?

The Jefferson office is the county's only counter for several different jobs. Beyond real and personal property, it bills and collects mobile home and timber tax, and it is the single place in the county for motor vehicle transactions.

Real property covers land and the improvements on it. Personal property means furniture, fixtures, tools, inventory and equipment used to run a business. If you are selling a house that also holds a home business, ask which of those items were returned for tax, so the file reflects what you actually owned on January 1.

  • Returns for real estate and business personal property are accepted from January 1 through April 1
  • Georgia tags are renewed within the 30 days before the owner's birthday
  • A person who cannot come in during office hours can send someone with a limited power of attorney for motor vehicle business

What are the key dates in the Jackson County tax year?

January 1 anchors the calendar, because use, condition and ownership on that day drive value and exemptions.

  • January 1: Returns and exemption applications open.
  • April 1: Last day for returns and for applications such as conservation use or historic rehabilitation. It doubles as the homestead cutoff for that tax year, for owners who lived in the home on January 1.
  • Mid-April: Assessment change notices are mailed.
  • Late May: Appeals of the notice are due; the 45 days run from the mailing date shown on it.
  • July 1: Digest goes to the state.
  • October: Bills are mailed.

The office takes homestead forms at any time, but a late one takes effect a year later.
