What is the appeal route for a Jackson County value?

Begin by mailing the Board of Assessors a written notice of appeal, no later than 45 days after your assessment notice was dated.

When the assessors revise the value, a notice of the revision arrives, and a written appeal on that revision reaches the Board of Equalization; the notice prints its own deadline. When they revise nothing, they report that to you and to the board, and your appeal proceeds without further action. The board schedules a hearing within 15 days of receipt, held 20 to 30 days after you hear from it.

Three members vote on every question raised, and the ruling is sent by registered or certified mail; Superior Court is the next step. A bill printed before the ruling is a temporary one, based on your return value or 85% of the assessors' figure, whichever is higher, with any difference settled afterward.

What happens to unpaid tax when a Jackson County house sells?

Request a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner before signing, then have the closing office pay it out of your proceeds. An open bill can turn into a recorded FiFa, which costs $25 to issue and record at the county's records office.

Sales that close in autumn can leave the seller named on a bill the buyer will pay, so spell out who covers it in the contract and the settlement statement. For a former rental, an inherited house or an empty one, ask about each earlier year separately.

What are the recording fees at Jackson County's records office?

The posted schedule charges $25 for each deed. Plats run $10 a page, liens $25, and UCC filings $25, or $50 when an assignment is attached.

  • Plain copies cost $0.50 a page; a certified copy costs $2.50 for page one and $0.50 for each page after
  • Cards carry a 4% fee; the office also takes cash, money orders and business checks
  • Any deed that changes ownership needs a PT-61, even when only a name is added or dropped or the property is given away

Real estate filing rules changed on January 1, 2025, and the office recommends the FANS alert site at fans.gsccca.org. Staff will explain where to file; legal advice and title searches are outside what they do.

More questions about Jackson County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which Jackson County number reaches the tax office?

Dial 706-367-6320 or 706-367-6325 for the Tax Commissioner, whose office is at 4965 Jackson Pkwy in Jefferson and keeps weekday hours from 8 to 4:30.

Can I pay part of a Jackson County bill?

Yes, until the due date, normally December 20. Once that day has passed the office no longer takes partial amounts.

When can a Jackson County owner file for homestead?

Any time of year. A form filed after April 1 counts for the next tax year, and the home must have been your residence on January 1.

How many days do I have to contest a Jackson County value?

Forty-five days after the notice date, which usually lands in late May. Mail the written appeal to the Board of Assessors.

Does the Jackson County Tax Commissioner set the rate?

No. Local governing bodies set rates, and the Tax Commissioner collects. Questions about value belong with Property Appraisal, while questions about a payment belong with the Tax Commissioner.

Why does Jasper County, Georgia feel so rural?

Scale is small in every direction. Only one city exists, Monticello, which doubles as the county seat; the one town is Shady Dale; and the 2020 count listed the whole population as rural. Area comes to 373 square miles, with roughly 5 of that water.

Legislators created the county on December 10, 1807 out of Baldwin County territory under the name Randolph; the switch to Sergeant William Jasper's name came in 1812, per Wikipedia. Newton County later took a piece of its land, in 1821.

Runoff west of State Route 11 reaches the Upper Ocmulgee, and the eastern half feeds the Upper Oconee. Public education is a four-school system that includes Jasper County High School.

High school graduates make up 89.6% of adults, and 19.5% went on to a bachelor's degree. Monthly owner costs are $1,461 with a mortgage and $480 without. Employers numbered 225 in 2023, with 1,911 employees, and 13.2% of residents fall below the poverty line.

Which office answers which Jasper County tax question?

A bill passes through several hands, and the Tax Commissioner's are the last. Millage comes from the commission and school board, value from the assessors, dispute rulings from a board the Grand Jury appoints, and mailing and collecting from the commissioner.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; (706) 468-4902; counter open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4:30
  • Tax Assessor: signs off on exemptions and notifies owners when it changes a value
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room provides warranty deed copies

One mill is a dollar per thousand of assessed value, and 40% of market value is the assessed figure.

When does a Jasper County bill come due?

On the standing schedule, land, buildings and business personal property are paid in two halves, September 20 and December 20. The state's county facts sheet names December 20 as the default statewide due date and gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark before interest begins.

The 2026 notice departed from that schedule: mailing on October 16, a first installment dated November 20, and the balance dated December 20. Dates have shifted from year to year, so trust the ones on your own bill.

  • Manufactured housing: payment and a location permit by April 1 each year
  • Missing it brings a 10% penalty and possibly a citation to Magistrate Court or sale of the unit
  • Vehicles renew during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday

How can unpaid Jasper County tax affect a sale?

Liens tend to appear when a sale is about to close. Taxes left unpaid past 90 days are recorded as a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the county warns that property can be levied on and sold.

Anyone can read a FiFa entry, bureaus included, and the tax office says it cannot dictate how they use it. Clear a recorded lien before closing.

The balance is available at (706) 468-4902. If your closing falls between the two installment dates, settle who pays each half and put that in the settlement papers.

What exemptions does Jasper County list?

The base exemption is two thousand dollars off assessed value. It reduces the county, school and State levies, but the share of the rate that retires bonds is excluded.

  • Owners 62 and over (school tax): as much as ten thousand dollars off, for net income not above that same figure, and bond levies are covered
  • Owners 65 and over (general): as much as four thousand dollars for an applicant and spouse earning ten thousand or less, with Social Security and certain retirement income set aside
  • Veterans with service-connected disabilities: $63,780 at most; a surviving spouse who has not remarried gets the same if the service member died in armed conflict
  • Owners 65 and over (State levy): the whole value of the house and as many as 10 acres, if you qualify under another homestead category

Bring a driver's license showing your Jasper County address when you apply at the Tax Commissioner. A form received by April 1 counts for that year. Approval carries over each year until you move, change owners or switch type, and a bigger local exemption replaces the State figure.

How do I dispute a Jasper County value?

The clock is 45 days from the notice date. Your choices are the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors sends either result up to Superior Court.

Preparation helps. During the January 1 to April 1 return period an owner can state a personal view of market value, which creates solid ground if the assessors alter it. Mobile home owners have 45 days to file with the assessors and 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Can Jasper County tax be refunded, and who bills city tax?

Yes, within limits. A written request can recover tax assessed or collected in error or illegally, started within three years of paying. When the claim comes from an appealed value, the refund is processed once the final taxable value is fixed.

City tax is a separate levy. Municipalities tax on their own, and the city clerk sends and collects that bill unless city and county have agreed on one combined bill. Vehicle tax is always collected by the county Tax Commissioner.

Holders of long-term notes secured by real estate must record them within 90 days, at the state's intangible recording rate of $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of it.

What do returns and special programs involve in Jasper County?

Returns for taxable property are accepted January 1 through April 1. An owner who files none is treated as repeating last year's value and last year's real property exemptions.

Mail goes to the last address the county has, so report any move. Three programs change how land or buildings are valued.

  • Historic property: a building on the Georgia register, with up to two acres around it, may be assessed preferentially
  • Brownfield sites: land approved for cleanup can keep a frozen value for a decade
  • Public safety survivors: the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or officer killed on duty may be fully exempt once the agency's papers are filed

If your property is in a program, the Board of Tax Assessors can say what a buyer must do to keep the status.

More questions about Jasper County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the street address for the Jasper County tax counter?

126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064, telephone (706) 468-4902. Weekday hours run 8 to 4:30.

Deadline for a first Jasper County homestead claim?

April 1 of the first year. Anything later counts toward the next tax year, and the home must have been yours and lived in on January 1.

Does a Jasper County tax lien reach my credit file?

Possibly. Ninety days past due puts a FiFa lien on record with the Clerk of Superior Court, and those entries are public.

How do I get a Jasper County deed copy?

Visit the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the Jasper County Courthouse.

What is the Jasper County appeal deadline?

Forty-five days from the date printed on the assessment notice. A later written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors carries a ruling to Superior Court.

What sort of place is Jeff Davis County, Georgia?

Farming and timber define Jeff Davis County, down in Georgia's southeast. The seat is Hazlehurst, the largest community; Denton is the lone other city; and lawmakers established the county on August 18, 1905, per Wikipedia.

The area is 335 square miles, 331 of it land. Cotton and peanuts lead the crops, tobacco once counted for more, and timber stays a steady product. Wheeler, Montgomery, Toombs, Appling, Bacon, Coffee and Telfair counties touch its borders. Water leaves in several directions: toward the Lower Ocmulgee along the north and part of the west, into the Altamaha in the east, and to the Little Satilla and Satilla in the south.

Satilla is a census-designated place, while Roper, Snipesville and Tallahassee are unincorporated crossroads. A house in Hazlehurst, a country place near a crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each attract different buyers.

How affordable is housing in Jeff Davis County?

Very. For 2020-2024, QuickFacts gives $118,300 as the middle value of an owned home, and owners occupy 71.3% of homes.

Who lives in Jeff Davis County, and why should a seller care?

Households are numerous and settled. QuickFacts lists 5,484 of them at 2.70 people apiece, and 89.3% of residents had not moved in the past year, so many buyers already know the neighborhood.

Children are 24.4% of residents and seniors 17.0%. A bachelor's degree is held by 13.2% of adults, and 77.3% completed high school. Households with broadband total 76.6%, a detail worth stating in a rural listing. In 2023 the county had 260 employer establishments and 3,834 jobs, and 2022 retail sales reached $201,004,000.

Those numbers describe a buyer pool that leans local, which is why paid tax receipts and a clear title help in a market this size.

Where do Jeff Davis County taxpayers go with questions?

Begin at the Tax Commissioner, 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Letters go to PO Box 558, and weekday service ends at 4:30.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends and collects bills, hands out mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: sets values and receives appeals
  • Board of Equalization: the Grand Jury names its members to rule on value disputes
  • Commission and school board: choose the millage rates

An online payment portal also exists. Check with the office on the best method before you mail a check near a deadline.

How fast do penalties grow on a late Jeff Davis County bill?

They stack up. The normal mailing date is October 20 and the due date December 20; part payments are fine until then, and afterward interest builds monthly at the bank prime rate.

Every 120 days brings another 5% penalty, ending at 20%. A balance left for a year grows noticeably, and any payoff quote goes stale fast.

  • Mobile homes: January mailing, April 1 due date, and a decal displayed after payment
  • Past April 1: a 10% filing penalty plus 1% monthly, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • A mobile home on land the owner holds can be homesteaded and is then taxed like real property

Another county page lists May 1 for mobile homes, so check with the office before relying on either.

What does the Jeff Davis County homestead exemption cover?

The base exemption deducts two thousand dollars from assessed value. It applies to county and school taxes but leaves out municipal school levies and bond debt.

File at the Tax Commissioner's counter from January 1 to April 1, between 8 and 5 on weekdays. The county says state law grants no extension, so a missed date gives up the exemption for that year. Once approved it renews until your circumstances change, and it never exceeds the tax owed.

  • Conservation use and residential transitional property
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

Each of those three programs asks the owner to covenant with the Tax Assessor to maintain qualifying use for ten years or more. If you plan to sell enrolled land, phone (912) 375-6624 and ask what the covenant demands of a new owner.

What can I do if I think my Jeff Davis County value is too high?

Write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice and name the appeal method you prefer. Spring is when notices for real and personal property usually go out.

The county accepts four grounds: whether the property is taxable, its value, its uniformity with similar parcels, or a denied exemption. Objecting to the rate or the bill's size does not qualify. A return filed between January 1 and April 1 can state your own January 1 opinion of market value and protects your appeal rights if the figure changes. Mobile home owners have 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days after a change notice to go before the Board of Equalization.

How should I prepare to sell a Jeff Davis County property with tax outstanding?

Obtain a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner and have the closing office settle it out of your proceeds. Interest runs every month and penalties step up each 120 days, so an old quote may fall short.

Timber land may owe timber tax, billed by the same office. If your mobile home sits on rented ground, confirm the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is public record, so a title search will turn it up.

Does Jeff Davis County tax ever get refunded, and who bills city tax?

A refund is possible when tax was assessed or collected in error or illegally. Put the request in writing and start it within three years of payment; a refund that results from an appeal is handled as soon as the final taxable value is fixed.

Hazlehurst and Denton can levy their own ad valorem tax, and the city clerk normally bills it unless the city and county agreed to one combined bill. The county Tax Commissioner alone collects vehicle tax. State freeport rules let voters exempt commercial and industrial inventory, with applications due in the same window as returns.

When you buy or finance land, a long-term note secured by real estate has to be recorded within 90 days, and the state's recording tax is printed as $1.50 for each $500 of face amount or fraction of it.

What do returns and spring notices involve in Jeff Davis County?

Owners return taxable property to the Tax Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1. When nothing is filed, last year's value and last year's real property exemptions carry over.

Appraisers use recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice states each parcel's value. A return of your own with a January 1 opinion keeps your appeal right alive if the figure is revised.

  • Tell the county about a new mailing address quickly, since notices follow the last one on file
  • Approved exemptions renew yearly until eligibility changes

What is the payment date for Jeff Davis County property tax?

December 20. The usual mailing date is October 20, and partial payments are accepted up to the deadline.

How do I reach the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?

Dial (912) 375-6622 or visit 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. For valuation, phone the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

What does lateness cost on a Jeff Davis County bill?

Monthly interest at the bank prime rate, plus 5% every 120 days up to a 20% cap. A mobile home paid after April 1 owes 10% plus 1% a month.

When can Jeff Davis County owners claim homestead?

From January 1 through April 1 for that tax year; the county says Georgia law offers no extension.

What is the appeal deadline in Jeff Davis County?

Forty-five days from the notice date. Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors and state your method.

How big is Jefferson County, Georgia, and who lives there?

Wide open describes Jefferson County: 530 square miles, 526 of them land, and fewer than 30 residents per square mile in 2020. Louisville serves as seat and biggest city, joined by Avera, Stapleton, Wadley and Wrens. The legislature established the county on February 20, 1796, per Wikipedia.

Its neighbors are McDuffie, Richmond, Burke, Emanuel, Johnson, Glascock, Washington and Warren. Streams south of a line running southeast from Stapleton, just below State Route 80, empty into the Upper Ogeechee; the small area north of it belongs to Brier Creek and the Savannah system. A single school district follows the county line. The 2020 census found no urban population at all, and residents' median age stood at 43.4.

People 65 and over make up 22.4% of the county and children 21.3%. QuickFacts lists 5,751 households of 2.58 people, a 21.5% poverty rate, and a bachelor's degree for 13.5% of adults. Employers numbered 326 in 2023, with 4,046 jobs.

What is a Jefferson County house worth, and is the market growing?

Prices are low and the headcount is shrinking. An owned home has a midpoint value of $105,400 for 2020-2024, while 15,011 residents in the mid-2025 estimate is 4.5% below the 2020 base.

How has Jefferson County's population changed since 1900?

Jefferson County reached its largest count in 1920, with 22,602 residents, after growing from 6,111 in 1810 and 18,212 in 1900. Numbers slid to 17,174 by 1970, edged up to 18,403 in 1980, and have declined at every count since: 17,408 in 1990, 17,266 in 2000, 16,930 in 2010 and 15,709 in 2020.

The mid-2025 estimate of 15,011 extends the pattern. QuickFacts also reports that 18.7% of people under 65 have no health insurance, 93.4% of households own a computer and 83.7% subscribe to broadband. Retail sales in 2022 averaged $10,893 a person, and 1,631 nonemployer businesses operated in 2024.

With a shrinking market, base your asking price on recent local sales, since figures from ten years back may mislead. Where buyers are few, tidy paperwork counts for more.

Where do I take Jefferson County tax questions?

Payments and bill questions go to the Tax Commissioner, 736 Peachtree Street, Louisville, GA 30434, telephone (478) 625-7736; the counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 5:00 on weekdays. For the worth of a parcel, call the Tax Assessor at (478) 625-8209.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills for land, business equipment, vehicles, mobile homes and timber
  • Board of Tax Assessors: receives returns, homestead forms and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: its record center supplies warranty deed copies and runs the FANS alerts; the tax site lists the clerk at (478) 625-7922

The county commissioners and the school board decide millage; the Tax Commissioner has no vote.

What happens if I miss the Jefferson County deadline?

Land, buildings and business personal property are generally due on November 15, and a 10% penalty follows after another 90 days. Small homesteaded bills, those under $500, escape it.

After that, levying on the parcel is possible. The office calls it a last resort and would rather collect another way.

  • Mobile and modular homes show April 1 on one county page and May 1 on another, so ask which one governs you
  • The year's mobile home tax must be fully paid before a location permit is issued
  • Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday

The tax site also mentions a one-time state homestead relief grant shown as a line on bills for owners with an approved exemption. Rentals and homes without an exemption were left out.

How do returns and homestead applications work in Jefferson County?

If you hold taxable property on January 1, file at least one return between January 1 and April 1. Real property returns afterward roll over at last year's value until you acquire more land or build.

Business personal property follows its own rule: form PT-50P is filed annually, and items you have sold must be reported or the tax continues. If you file a return that states a lower value and the assessors decline it, that is where your appeal begins.

  • First-time owners take a copy of the warranty deed along to the Tax Assessor's Office
  • Forms are taken any time, though one arriving after April 1 takes effect a year later
  • An approved exemption lasts until you move, sell or request another kind
  • A denial comes to you in writing, with the right to appeal

When a local exemption is bigger than the State's, the local one prevails. The assessor's office can quote the amounts in force.

How can I appeal a Jefferson County value?

Once a notice of changed value reaches you, mail the Board of Tax Assessors a written appeal. One county page counts 45 days from mailing and another says 30, so follow the notice you hold and file early.

Three arguments are open to you: the property should not be taxed, the value is wrong, or it is out of line with comparable parcels. A complaint about how much tax was levied is not accepted. The assessors review, then answer; a remaining dispute goes to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing, and Superior Court follows. Arbitration substitutes for the board, and the assessors' office explains how to choose it.

Which farm, timber and historic programs apply in Jefferson County?

Active farmland may be assessed at 30% of market value rather than the standard 40%. Conservation use is a second route and values farm, timber, sensitive or transitional land by its present use.

  • Covenant: the owner commits to the Board of Tax Assessors to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years, and applications are due in April
  • Standing timber: untaxed until sold or cut, then taxed at full market value times the millage rate
  • Historic buildings: a register-listed structure and up to two surrounding acres can get preferential treatment

If you own acreage, talk to the assessor before listing so you know what the covenant requires of a new owner.

How do I clear tax before a Jefferson County closing?

Obtain the payoff figure from the Tax Commissioner in writing, then have it paid at the table. A bill older than 90 days already carries the 10% penalty.

The Clerk of Superior Court runs FANS, a free service you join voluntarily that alerts you when records are filed for your property. Sign up before you list, so a lien cannot appear mid-contract. For an inherited or former rental house, ask for each earlier year's balance by itself.

(478) 625-7736. The office is at 736 Peachtree Street in Louisville and keeps counter hours from 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays.

Is there a penalty on a small homesteaded Jefferson County bill?

No. The 90-day penalty skips homesteaded property whose bill is under $500.

April 1. The office takes applications through the year, though a later one starts a year after.

What should a Wrightsville-area seller know about Johnson County?

Wrightsville is the seat of Johnson County, which a bill dated December 11, 1858 carved from Washington, Laurens and Emanuel land. Johnson County's history page pictures a rural place: tree-lined streets, historic structures, and easy driving to Macon, Savannah, Augusta and Milledgeville. Court first met in the Cedar Creek Primitive Baptist Church, then in a rectangular brick building, until the present courthouse opened. That 1895 courthouse, renovated in 1938 and again in 1995, is a listed National Register property and anchors an older downtown that appraises differently from the farmhouses outside town.

Two smaller places add wrinkles. Kite dates to the 1890s and keeps a museum in a former Masonic lodge. Adrian straddles a line with Emanuel County that zigzags through town like a Z, so one street can hold neighbors who owe tax to different counties. Match an Adrian-area parcel to its county before you phone a tax office.

Land area is 303.02 square miles, with 30.3 residents per square mile in 2020 against 32.9 in 2010. Expect listings to be acreage, wooded tracts or a farmhouse past the pavement.

How do Johnson County's housing figures look next to its neighbors?

Johnson County's middle home value is under half of Jones County's, and its 33.4% poverty rate is the highest of the four counties in the Census comparison.

What does it cost to carry a Johnson County house each month?

Census owner-cost medians give a sense of the monthly picture. Owners who still have a mortgage report median costs of $1,193 a month, while owners with the house paid off report $440, a difference of $753 that reflects the loan payment. With a median gross rent of $647, a buyer comparing renting and owning will notice that a paid-off home costs less per month than a rental.

A tax surprise stands out more against a $440 monthly budget than a larger one. Households average 2.41 people, and 89.4% have a computer, which is relevant because the county's tax commissioner site accepts payment online. A seller who lets a delinquent balance sit risks adding interest at a pace that is hard to absorb on a fixed income, so asking for a payoff early gives you a number to plan around before a buyer appears.

How strong is the local economy behind Johnson County home prices?

Payroll data for 2023 show 123 employer establishments, 888 jobs and $29,673 thousand in annual pay. Retail sales in 2022 reached $69,176 thousand, or $7,510 per resident, and health care and social assistance took in $17,999 thousand against $10,333 thousand for transportation and warehousing.

Just 43.4% of people 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, the typical commute is 28.1 minutes, and 8.4% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband reaches 83.0% of households, and 18.6% of residents under 65 have no health insurance. Self-employment fills the gap: 662 nonemployer businesses were counted in 2024, more than five times the number of employers, and accommodation and food service sales were only $3,835 thousand in 2022. Veterans number 490, and 13.2% of residents under 65 report a disability. Most buyers are therefore local and many are retired, so a house priced near $94,900 draws more calls than one priced like a Macon listing, and financing often hinges on small loans or cash.

Which Johnson County desks answer which tax question?

Two tax offices share the building at 2484 West Elm Street, Wrightsville, ZIP 31096.

  • Tax Commissioner, (478) 864-2565 ext. 1: sends bills, takes payments, supplies payoff numbers and renews tags. Counter hours are weekdays, 8 until 4:30, and the commissioner's website accepts online payment.
  • Tax Assessors, (478) 864-3325 ext. 2: set value, take returns and exemption forms, and receive appeals. Search parcels through the assessors' qPublic page.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 2557 East Elm Street, (478) 864-3484: holds recorded deeds.
  • Probate Court, (478) 864-3316: opens an estate when the person named on the deed has died.

The commissioner's page on the county site carries one unusual notice. Owners whose timber was damaged and then cut after Hurricane Helene can seek relief with a form from the Georgia Forestry Commission, attaching the documents it lists and delivering the packet to the commissioner. Anyone selling woodland should ask whether a claim exists for the parcel.

How does an assessment dispute work in Johnson County?

A Johnson County notice shows two numbers: the fair market value set for January 1, and the 40% slice of it that is actually taxed. An owner who buys or improves a parcel files a return during the first quarter, through April 1, and the county warns that value left off a required return draws a 10% surcharge plus interest.

A challenge begins with a letter to the assessing board, postmarked within 45 days after the notice went out. The letter has to pick a path. State guidance names an equalization board, a hearing officer or an arbitrator, and the county's tax page adds superior court. The assessors can supply the state form.

Tax paid by mistake can be reclaimed through a written request filed inside three years. A refund that follows a won appeal is issued automatically.

Do Johnson County owners get a local homestead break?

Not a local one. The Revenue Department's page for this county says none were adopted, so the state's own exemptions are the only choice.

  • Eligibility rests on owning the house and living in it as your legal residence, with the assessors deciding.
  • A form arriving after April 1 waits for the following year.
  • Once approved, the exemption continues until you move, sell or switch types.
  • Business personal property is returned every April 1, changed or not.
  • Mobile homes need a location permit within 30 days of being set, then a yearly renewal from January 1 through April 1.

Business inventory can qualify for a freeport exemption where voters approved one, requested at the assessors' desk during the return window.

When does Johnson County want its tax money?

The state's fallback deadline is December 20, but counties may substitute December 1, November 15 or installment billing. No date appears on the Johnson County information page, so phone (478) 864-2565 ext. 1 and ask.

Interest waits until 60 days after the postmark, and penalties may follow on late balances. Because the bill is addressed to the owner, a lender holding escrow may not get a copy, and heirs should update the mailing address in writing.

Sellers ask whether a spring closing shifts the bill. It does not: the owner on January 1 carries that year's tax, and the state refunds nothing for a mid-year move, so the purchase contract has to divide it.

What if the Johnson County house I want to sell has unpaid tax?

Ask the commissioner for a written payoff figure, then have the Clerk of Superior Court's records searched for any lien on the parcel. Parcels that stay delinquent can reach the sales listed on the commissioner's tax sales page.

At the table, the closing agent pays the commissioner from what the seller would otherwise receive, and the lien clears as the deed records. A house passing through an estate has to go through Probate Court first. A buyer paying cash and taking the home as-is can absorb repairs, but the payoff, the recorded deed and any estate paperwork still happen.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

More questions about Johnson County, GA Property Tax Guide

Who sends the Johnson County tax bill?

The commissioner's office at 2484 West Elm Street in Wrightsville mails it, and (478) 864-2565 ext. 1 reaches that desk. One bill carries the county, school and state levies. A question about the value itself goes to the assessors at (478) 864-3325 ext. 2.

Does Johnson County add a local homestead exemption?

None, per the state's county sheet. Only the statewide exemptions are available, and the form has to reach the county by April 1 of the first year.

What is the Johnson County appeal window?

Owners get 45 days, counted from the day the notice went in the mail. The challenge is a letter to the assessing board naming the path you want.

What is a typical home worth in Johnson County?

About $94,900 at the median, based on 2020-2024 Census estimates for homes their owners live in. Renters pay a median of $647 monthly.

Does a January closing move the year's tax to the buyer?

Only if the contract says so. Whoever held title on January 1 owes the year, and the closing statement is where the parties divide it.

Why do so many Jones County residents work in Macon or Milledgeville?

Jones County sits in the middle of the state astride the fall line, and the New Georgia Encyclopedia says many residents live here and commute to jobs in Macon or Milledgeville. The county dates to 1807, when it became Georgia's thirty-second. Cotton, then peaches and peppers, paid the bills early on, and the encyclopedia now points to two gravel quarries as the main industry.

Gray has been the seat since 1905, replacing Clinton, whose early houses still form a historic district. Two fights took place in 1864, at Sunshine Church that summer and at Griswoldville in November. Jarrell Plantation State Historic Site draws history buyers, and during the 1930s more than 30,000 worn-out cotton acres, partly in neighboring Jasper County, became a federal wildlife refuge in the Piedmont.

Jones was Georgia's most densely settled county in 1820, at 43.5 people per square mile, and did not regain that population until the 1980 census. Today it has 393.94 square miles of land and a 2020 density of 72.0 per square mile, versus 30.3 in Johnson County.

Older layers show in the land. The Garrison Road across southern Jones followed an old Lower Creek trading path and was eventually folded into the Federal Road running from the national capital to New Orleans. In 1849 Griswoldville started as an industrial hamlet on the Central of Georgia Railway, where a cotton gin maker later turned out pistols for the Confederacy. Clinton was the fourth-largest town in Georgia in 1820, with almost 850 people. Central Georgia Technical College now keeps a learning center in Gray.

What do Jones County's numbers say about its housing stock?

Jones County's 83.6% ownership rate and $75,500 household income are both well above the matching figures for Johnson County.

Jones County in Census QuickFacts, housing and household snapshot
IndicatorJones County figure

Jones has 10,786 households of about 2.63 people each, and 92.4% of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Growth since 2020 is 3.0%. A seller here competes mainly with resale houses in Gray and the unincorporated parts, and with whatever the Macon side of the county line offers.

What does a Jones County owner spend to keep a house?

Census medians for owner costs are $1,483 a month with a mortgage and $470 without, against $964 for rent. The $1,013 difference between the two owner figures is the typical loan payment.

Some 60.6% of residents 16 and over are in the labor force. Jones employers numbered 354 in 2023, with 3,165 jobs (up 11.4% from 2022) and $124,135 thousand in payroll, and another 2,614 nonemployer businesses existed in 2024. Retail sales reached $167,806 thousand in 2022, or $5,885 per person, while health care and social assistance billed $44,237 thousand. Adults 25 and older are 92.0% high school graduates and 19.9% bachelor's degree holders. The poverty rate is 11.7%, broadband reaches 89.5% of households, and 1,837 residents are veterans, which matters because the county's disabled veteran exemption is among the largest breaks on the books.

Which Jones County and Gray offices should I call about taxes?

The commissioner's counter is at 166 Industrial Blvd. in Gray, open 8 to 4:45, and mail goes to P.O. Box 417, Gray, GA 31030.

  • Tax Commissioner, 478-986-6538: bills, payments, mobile home decals, plus timber and heavy-equipment tax. Look up a parcel or pay on jonescountytaxes.com.
  • Board of Tax Assessors, (478) 986-6300: value, returns and exemption forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, courthouse deed room: copies of a recorded warranty deed.
  • Gray City Hall, 478-986-5433: a city bill kept separate from the county's, paid at 109 James Street or mailed to P.O. Box 443.

The Clerk, not the commissioner, collects the intangible tax due when a buyer's lender records a security deed. For a sense of how the city bill works, Gray mailed its 2024 bills on October 29, 2024, due December 29, 2024, and set 14.45 mills with a 4.95 rollback, leaving 9.50 mills net.

When does a Jones County owner pay, and what do late payments cost?

Bills for land, houses and business personal property are usually mailed by October 1 and fall due December 1. The 2025 round was mailed September 25, 2025, due December 1, 2025. Once the deadline passes, interest of 1% a month builds, tallied at the close of business on the first of each month.

A penalty follows 90 days after the deadline. The commissioner's property page puts it at 5% and the FAQ at 10%, so get the figure in person before you set a payoff. A homesteaded house with a bill under $500 skips that penalty. Beyond 90 days the office can record a fifa lien with the Clerk and in the end levy on the property.

  • Mobile homes: billed around January, due April 1, with a 10% penalty, Magistrate Court citation or sale as the risks. The 2026 bills left January 29 with an April 1, 2026 deadline.
  • Partial payments are taken, and interest keeps running on what remains.

Which exemptions can a Jones County homeowner claim?

Local legislation here stacks on the state exemptions. The amounts below come from the county's own tax pages.

  • A $2,000 standard homestead off assessed value, which reaches county and school operating levies and the state levy but not bond debt.
  • A $15,000 local school break for anyone who turned 62 by January 1, with no income test.
  • Two income-tested elderly breaks, up to $10,000 for school tax at 62 and up to $4,000 for all levies at 65, each capped at $10,000 of net income.
  • The disabled veterans exemption, up to $63,780, which also reaches an unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in an armed conflict.
  • A floating exemption for owners 62 and older whose gross household income is $30,000 or less; it replaces other state and county exemptions, so the county warns it can raise a bill at first.

First-time owners should carry in a warranty deed, and the form has to arrive by April 1. Owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until ownership changes or the deferred sum and interest reach 85% of fair market value. Farmland may be assessed at 30% rather than 40%, and each preferential program calls for a 10-year covenant.

How do I challenge a Jones County valuation?

Forty-five days from the notice date is all you get to start. Route the case to the county equalization board or an arbitrator, then to superior court by notice to the assessors if you lose. Grounds include taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption.

Between January 1 and April 1 you can file a return stating your own opinion of value, which can protect appeal rights if the assessors then change it. Skip the return and the county treats you as returning last year's property at last year's final value. Mobile home owners get 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days from a revised notice to reach the equalization board.

What should a Jones County seller settle before closing?

Phone the commissioner for today's payoff and, if the house is in Gray, the city's bill too. A spring sale still carries the full year because the January 1 owner is liable, so spell out the reimbursement in the contract. Remember that bills reach the homeowner and not the mortgage company.

A cash buyer can move quickly, but the title search has to come back clean first.

More questions about Jones County, GA Property Tax Guide

When must Jones County owners pay their real estate tax?

December 1, with bills mailed around October 1. The 2025 round went out September 25, 2025, and 1% monthly interest starts once the date passes.

Which owners qualify for the $15,000 Jones County school exemption?

Anyone 62 or older as of January 1. The amount reduces school operating and school bond tax, and no income ceiling is stated.

Where is my Jones County deed on file?

Recorded deeds sit in the courthouse deed room in Gray, and the tax commissioner's FAQ points owners to that office for copies.

How big is the late penalty on Jones County taxes?

The county's pages differ, naming 5% on one and 10% on another. Call 478-986-6538 for the number on your bill. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused.

How much is a typical Jones County house worth?

Census estimates for 2020-2024 center on $194,500 for houses their owners live in. Tenants pay a median of $964, and the median household brings in $75,500.

What is Lamar County, Georgia known for?

Lamar County lies between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is its seat. Barnesville was settled in 1826, and its leaders petitioned the legislature in 1869, 1906, 1912 and 1916 before the county finally came into being in 1920, cut from Monroe and Pike counties. The result is about 185 square miles of rolling land whose streams run to the Flint and Ocmulgee rivers.

The town earned the title Buggy Capital of the South. One factory predicted in 1897 that it would ship at least 1,200 buggies, and a September Buggy Days parade still shows off original Barnesville buggies. Gordon State College, founded in 1872 as Gordon Institute and a four-year school since 2007, fills out the town's profile, and the Barnesville Expo Center joins a wetlands trail to a livestock arena. Pecan and peach groves cover the farmland.

The population stood at 9,745 in 1930, reached 18,317 in 2010 and 18,500 in 2020. Land area is 183.50 square miles, and the 2020 density of 100.8 residents per square mile is the highest of the four counties in the Census comparison.

Settlement came after the 1821 treaty with the Lower Muscogee (Creek), which ceded the land of Monroe, Pike and Crawford counties and brought English settlers from Virginia, the Carolinas and older Georgia counties. Gordon Military College (1927 to 1972) trained men who served in World War II, Korea and Vietnam, and the Expo Center bills itself as the first in the nation to join wetlands to an exhibition hall.

How fast is Lamar County growing, and what does it mean for prices?

Lamar County added 13.2% to its head count after April 2020, according to the Census estimate through July 2025, far ahead of Johnson, Jones or Lanier.

The $216,500 median owner-home value tops the four counties, and the 31.8-minute commute is the longest. With 136 permits pulled in 2025, an older Lamar County house will be shopped against new construction.

What does the Lamar County economy add to the housing picture?

A homeowner with a mortgage pays a median of $1,469 a month and one without pays $526, while renters pay $878. The county has 7,133 households of 2.60 people on average, and 92.5% of residents did not move in the past year.

Employers numbered 275 in 2023, supporting 3,775 jobs (up 10.1% over 2022) and $174,423 thousand in payroll, and 1,922 nonemployer businesses were counted in 2024. Retail sales were $150,591 thousand in 2022, which works out to $7,733 per resident, and transportation and warehousing took in $20,621 thousand, almost as much as health care and social assistance at $22,229 thousand. Another $23,100 thousand came from accommodation and food service. Labor-force participation is 56.7%. Among adults 25 and over, 89.6% finished high school and 19.2% hold a bachelor's degree. Poverty is 12.6%, 1,320 residents are veterans, 21.7% of residents are under 18, and 13.5% of people under 65 lack health insurance. Foreign-born residents make up 2.7% of the county, and 93.2% of households have a computer.

Where do I go for Lamar County property tax questions?

Barnesville hosts every office a seller needs.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204; mail to P.O. Box 850; phone (770) 358-5162. Walk-in hours are Monday through Thursday, 8 to 4:30, and Friday, 8 to 4:15, with a drive-thru that closes 15 minutes earlier.
  • Tax Assessor, (770) 358-5161: values, appeals and homestead forms, Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to 4.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. The site also stresses that the commissioner neither sets values nor chooses millage, so a complaint about a high figure goes to the assessors.

When are Lamar County taxes due, and what happens after?

The county mails bills by mid-September and wants payment by November 15, a schedule that began with the 2018 tax year. It beats Georgia's December 20 default by five weeks, which surprises owners new to the county.

  • Late real estate and business personal property bills collect 1% interest per month.
  • Amounts still open 90 days after the deadline take a 10% penalty.
  • The FAQ says a lien (fifa) goes on file once taxes are over 30 days late, and credit bureaus may see it.
  • Mobile homes are due April 1; late ones pick up a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly, and can be auctioned.

State guidance also says interest should wait 60 days after the bill's postmark, so keep the envelope. A refund request for tax paid in error must begin inside three years.

Which Lamar County homestead exemptions can I file for?

The assessors take forms from January 1 to April 1 and cannot extend the window, so a late filer loses that year. Once approved, an exemption renews itself. Carry a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • State types carry codes: S1 regular homestead, S3 elderly at 62, L4 elderly at 65, S5 disabled veteran and SS surviving spouse of a veteran, the last two requiring VA proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Over 65: Lamar takes $20,000 off the county operating levy, nothing else.
  • Over 70: $7,000 comes off school operating tax and school bond tax.
  • Disabled owners: $15,000 off school operating tax when combined household income is under $20,000, documented by two physicians or a Social Security letter that declares 100% disability.

The county says you must satisfy the state rules before any local break applies. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 may also defer tax. For a mobile home to count as a homestead, the home and the land under it must have the same owner.

How does a Lamar County owner appeal a value?

County appraisers lean on recent sales, measured at January 1, and the spring notice shows the result. An owner who objects has 45 days from the notice date and may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. The letter goes to the assessing board and picks a route, and cases that go to the Board of Equalization are heard by a panel the Grand Jury appoints.

Landowners have preferential programs. Lamar cites section 48-5-7.4 for conservation use and residential transitional land, 48-5-7.4.1 for agricultural land and 48-5-7.2 for rehabilitated historic property, and every one asks for a covenant of 10 years or more. Enrolled acreage needs a call to the assessors before the deed changes hands.

How do I sell a Lamar County house with taxes still owed?

Request a payoff that folds in interest and penalty, and check with the Clerk for a recorded fifa. The closing agent pays out of the seller's share and secures the release. January 1 ownership decides who owes the year, so most contracts prorate.

When the owner has died, the county Probate Court can explain how to open the estate before a listing goes up. Cash buyers in Barnesville or the rural parts of the county will still expect the payoff settled at closing.

What is the due date for Lamar County property tax?

November 15. Bills normally go out by September 15, and mobile homes are due April 1.

What do late Lamar County payments cost?

1% per month interest after the due date plus a 10% penalty at 90 days. The FAQ adds that a lien can be recorded after 30 days.

Do older Lamar County owners get extra relief?

Yes. Past 65, $20,000 comes off the county operating levy, and past 70, $7,000 comes off school operating and bond tax, once the state rules are satisfied.

What does a typical Lamar County house cost?

About $216,500, the 2020-2024 Census median for owner-occupied homes. The county had an estimated 20,941 residents in July 2025.

Who accepts Lamar County homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor's office, from January 1 through April 1. Bring a driver license and a 1040 or signed income affidavit.

What shapes the housing market in Lanier County?

Lanier County was the state's 157th, formed in 1920 from pieces of Berrien, Clinch and Lowndes counties. Lakeland is the seat. It began as a mill village on a stagecoach route between Thomasville and Waycross, took the name Milltown in 1832, and became Lakeland when it incorporated in 1925. Banks Lake, Grand Bay Lake and Lake Irma anchor the county's fishing reputation, and Banks Lake National Wildlife Refuge, set up in 1985, protects more than 4,000 acres of water, marsh and swamp.

The encyclopedia lists Moody Air Force Base (shared with Lowndes County), the hospital, the lakes and a large state correctional facility among the forces behind jobs here. The first courthouse dates to 1921 and the current one replaced it in 1973. Stockton, once called Registerville, is the other named community, and downtown Lakeland carries the Murals of Milltown, which show community life in the 1920s.

Census land area rose from 185.26 square miles in 2010 to 196.54 in 2020, a density of 50.3 residents per square mile.

Visitors and buyers alike notice the outdoors. The refuge draws about 20,000 visitors a year, a 75-acre nature trail in Lakeland's city limits opened in August 2001, and Fender Cemetery east of Lakeland, at the junction of U.S. 221 and Georgia 37, holds many early settlers. A former governor's house was moved to West Main Street in the early 1980s, and Union Baptist Church stands near Georgia Highway 135.

Who handles property tax in Lanier County?

The Magistrate Court number is (229) 482-2207, the Extension Office is at (229) 482-3895 for questions about farm and woodland, and the Sheriff's Office is at (229) 482-3545.

The county's website also has planning and zoning, code enforcement and business license pages, useful if a property needs repairs or has a commercial use. Parcel maps run through qPublic, which lets you confirm acreage and the owner of record before quoting a price.

When does Lanier County expect payment on a house?

December 20 is the baseline in Georgia. Counties may move it to December 1 or November 15 or divide the bill, and because Lanier's website posts no date, the tax commissioner's number, (229) 482-3795, is the place to confirm.

Interest is held back for 60 days after the postmark, and penalties can attach to what stays open. A sale in February does not move the burden: whoever held title January 1 owes the year, and Georgia refunds nothing for partial-year ownership. Liens for unpaid county tax are recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which is where a title examiner will look.

Mobile homes keep a separate schedule. A location permit is due within 30 days of placement and renews between January 1 and April 1, and the January 1 owner returns the home to the commissioner by April 1.

Does Lanier County offer homestead exemptions?

Just the statewide set. The state's county sheet lists no local exemptions for Lanier, leaving the standard exemptions and the disabled veterans exemption, which reaches both city and county tax.

  • Apply at the county tax office once the house is your primary residence.
  • A form that lands after April 1 misses that tax year.
  • Commercial and industrial inventory can be exempt where voters approved a freeport exemption, which the assessors process.

An exemption renews itself only until ownership or residence changes, so a buyer moving in files a fresh application by April 1. As the seller, ask the commissioner whether your exemption was active so the closing figures reflect it.

What can I do if a Lanier County value looks too high?

A real property notice goes out every year, and you have 45 days from its mailing to dispute the fair market value. The first step is a letter to the board of tax assessors. Email counts only if the county adopted a written policy consenting to electronic service.

The letter must name a route: the county's equalization board, a hearing officer or an arbitrator. A uniform state form exists, and Revenue Department staff cannot overrule the local decision on one parcel.

What happens to back taxes when a Lanier County house sells?

Request a payoff from the commissioner and ask whether a lien is on file. If the buyer finances, the lender's security instrument is recorded within 90 days, and the state prints the recording tax at $1.50 per $500 (or fraction) of the note.

Heirs should talk to Lanier County Probate about opening the estate before listing. Out-of-town cash buyers can generally accept a payoff deducted at the closing table.

Where can I pay in person in Lanier County?

At the Tax Commissioner, 56 W Main St, Suite 1, Lakeland, GA 31635. The phone is (229) 482-3795, and the office is open weekdays 8 to noon and 1 to 5.

Which date does Lanier County use for real estate tax?

Georgia's baseline of December 20 applies unless the county picked December 1, November 15 or installments, so call (229) 482-3795 to confirm. Interest starts 60 days after the postmark.

Does Lanier County add its own homestead exemption?

No, per the Revenue Department. State exemptions and the disabled veterans exemption are available if the application arrives by April 1.

How much is a house worth in Lanier County at the median?

$162,300, the 2020-2024 Census median for owner-occupied homes. Rent runs $913 a month at the median, and 73.2% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Is an emailed Lanier County appeal accepted?

Only when the assessors have a written policy allowing electronic service. If not, mail it within 45 days of the notice. The assessor's number is (229) 482-2090.

Why does the Laurens County tax picture matter before I list a Dublin-area house?

Dublin hosts the offices that set and collect your bill, and Laurens County is geographically the biggest of the four Georgia counties in this research set, with 807.34 square miles of land. Its headcount was 48,434 in 2010. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 51,041.

Per the QuickFacts comparison, Laurens owners live in 64.3 percent of the county's 22,277 housing units, and a typical owned home is worth $154,500. Middle household income is $55,010. Builders here took out just 102 permits in 2025, which leaves resale houses doing most of the work for newcomers.

Spending numbers set Laurens apart. Shops rang up roughly $1.06 billion in 2022, about $21,379 for every resident, where Lee County shows $9,592. Clinics, hospitals and social services booked $598.6 million. A Dublin payroll of about $768.5 million across 1,106 employers backs it up.

What does a Laurens County household pay to own or rent?

Ownership is cheap by Georgia standards. For 2020 to 2024 the Census lists $1,347 a month for Laurens owners carrying a mortgage, $418 for owners with none, and $863 for renters.

Here is more local color that a buyer may ask about:

  • 18,592 Laurens households average 2.63 people.
  • Broadband reaches 86.2 percent of them, a point for remote workers.
  • The commute from home to job averages 24.6 minutes.
  • Roughly 19.1 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree.

Put a copy of your latest Laurens bill beside your listing sheet. A buyer comparing the $154,500 median with a $863 rent will want the yearly tax shown up front.

Which Laurens County office answers a question about my bill, and which about my value?

Billing goes to the commissioner. Values go to the assessors. The county tax site says the commissioner's side covers real property, personal property, motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber.

What happens to a Laurens County bill left unpaid?

Trouble starts about a month after the bill falls due. Laurens says a tax fifa can then be filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, and because the filing is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

  • The Laurens pages name no fixed date, so rely on the bill you receive.
  • A recorded fifa can stall a title search, which is why a payoff request belongs before your listing agreement.
  • A mobile or modular home owner faces April 1, and the Laurens location permit waits for full payment.
  • A dishonored check goes to a collection partner and may bring a service fee.

Request your account history before listing photos are taken. A complete file helps a buyer's lender.

How does a Laurens County owner dispute a value?

Put it in writing to the Laurens assessors, inside 45 days of the notice date, and pick a route. Choices: the Board of Equalization with Superior Court behind it; a hearing officer, open only to non-homestead real property over $750,000; or arbitration on your own certified appraisal, which ends the matter.

Call 478-272-6443 for the form. If you file a return between January 2 and April 1, you can state your own number, and that return keeps your appeal rights alive when the assessors change the figure again. The reasons that count are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. A high tax total does not count.

Which exemptions and land programs apply to Laurens owners?

The homestead exemption comes first. File by April 1 if you owned the house and lived there on January 1. It continues until you relocate or the deed changes.

Laurens also posts a longer list for older owners and landowners:

  • An extra exemption at age 62, then relief from the state share at 65 on the house plus up to 10 acres.
  • Tax deferral for qualified owners 62 and up. The commissioner has the current income cap.
  • Farm assessment at 30 percent in place of 40, plus Conservation Use, each tied to a 10 year covenant.
  • Forest Land Protection, a 15 year covenant covering tracts past 200 acres.

Land applications go to the assessors by April 1. The commissioner's page and the FAQ name different offices for homestead filing, so phone first. One in five Laurens residents is 65 or older, and 2,430 are veterans, so many sellers hold breaks that the buyer must request again.

Who pays the Laurens County tax in the year of a sale?

Whoever held title on January 1. Georgia pays no part-year refunds, so the Laurens contract and closing statement must handle the split.

  1. Ask the commissioner if the current bill is out and paid.
  2. Have your closing attorney credit the buyer for the months after the sale.
  3. Expect your exemption to lapse when title transfers.
  4. Tell the buyer to file a fresh application by April 1.

Warranty deeds sit in the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court at the Laurens courthouse. Some 90.4 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so a clean paper trail reassures buyers in a stable market.

Who is likely to buy a house in Laurens County?

Census numbers sketch the pool. Children under 18 make up 24.0 percent of residents and children under 5 another 6.4 percent, so family buyers are common. Workers 16 and older in the civilian labor force are 57.1 percent of that age group, and 4,670 residents run businesses with no employees. Total county employment slipped 1.1 percent between 2022 and 2023.

Those figures point to a buyer who wants a modest monthly payment and may be self-employed. Price the house with that monthly budget in mind. A seller who attaches the tax history and the exemption status answers the question these buyers ask before they tour.

Do I have to file a Laurens County property tax return?

Everyone who owns taxable property on January 1 files at least once. In Laurens the return window runs January 2 through April 1, and one county page says the forms are available at the Tax Commissioner's office in Dublin.

After the first filing the return renews on its own. You file again only when you add property, improve an existing parcel or want to declare a different value. If you are listing a house, a return on file shows buyers you have kept up with the county, and it is one less thing the buyer's attorney will chase.

Who sets values in Laurens County?

The assessors, at 478-272-6443. The tax commissioner, at 478-272-6994, bills and collects. Use the first number for any question about what your Laurens house is worth.

What share of market value gets taxed in Laurens County?

Forty percent. The exemption is subtracted from that amount and the millage rate is applied to the rest.

Is April 1 the cutoff for a Dublin homestead application?

Yes. A form that arrives later starts the exemption the following year.

What if I miss the 45 day appeal window on a Laurens notice?

The ordinary appeal is gone. Note the date on each notice and call the assessors in the first week.

Can a Laurens mobile home get a location permit before the tax is paid?

No. That year's tax must be paid in full first, and April 1 is the due date.

A recent episode matters to anyone who bought in 2025. Lee issued refund checks for tax year 2025 solely to the owner of record on January 1, 2025, with none sent to mortgage or escrow companies:

What should a seller know about Liberty County, Georgia property tax?

Hinesville anchors Liberty County, which packs in more people per square mile than any other of the four Georgia counties researched here and grew fastest since 2020. Seven taxing areas share the county, each carrying its own proposed rate, so pin down which one your house falls in.

The Census QuickFacts page shows 70,313 residents for July 2025, which is 7.7 percent above the April 2020 base, spread across 516.47 square miles and 126.3 people per square mile at the 2020 count. Owners occupy only 50.9 percent of the housing units, the smallest share in the group. Renters pay a median $1,246, and the typical owned home is valued at $201,500. Builders took out 355 permits in 2025, and 8,042 residents are veterans.

Just 80.7 percent of residents stayed at one address for a year, the lowest figure of the four counties, so moves are common. A house that has been a rental raises questions about its tax history and homestead status, so settle both with the offices below before you list.

The rest of the profile is useful context for pricing. The Census lists 23,998 households averaging 2.70 people, a median household income of $60,456 and a per capita income of $28,215. The civilian labor force takes in 51.8 percent of residents 16 and up, the average commute is 23.9 minutes, and 2022 retail sales reached roughly $873.3 million. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,500 a month.

Which Liberty County office handles my bill, and which my value?

Bills go to the tax commissioner and values to the assessors, and both work out of 100 Main Street in Hinesville. The commissioner's site takes online payments, and the office still accepts them in person or by mail at Suite 1545 (ZIP 31313). Call 912-876-3389.

Assessors work from Suite 1550 at the same address and answer at 912-876-3568. Their handout splits the phone menu this way:

  • Option 1: administration, which covers homesteads and general information.
  • Option 2: mapping, GIS and specialized assessment.
  • Option 3: personal property, including prebill mobile homes, vehicles, boats, business inventory, aircraft and commercial property.
  • Option 4: real property appraisers.

The county's Official Assessment Documents page lets you pull a property record card or a real property assessment notice by typing a parcel number, with a separate search if you do not know yours. The assessors also take email at Tax.Assessors@libertycountyga.gov.

What are the proposed 2026 millage rates in Liberty County?

The county commissioners proposed 19.4000 mills for the unincorporated area and lower rates inside most cities. The figures below come from the county's press release on the proposed 2026 increase, so your bill is the final word on the rate that applies.

The release puts the proposed levy change at 1.32 percent for the unincorporated area and 6.15 percent for Hinesville. Midway and Riceboro show 100 percent only because both set a city rate for the first time in 2026. FLOST, the Floating Local Option Sales Tax, collected from January to June, trims the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills. Hearings were set for November 3 (noon and 6 p.m.) and November 12, 2026, in the annex board room on North Main Street, and all three dates are behind us.

The release also prints rollback rates, the levels that would raise last year's revenue from the new digest: 19.1460 mills for the unincorporated area, 16.3300 for Hinesville, 17.6830 for Flemington and 18.9030 for Walthourville. Hearings are required wherever a proposal tops its rollback rate. Ask the commissioner for the adopted rate, because your bill will use that figure.

When do Liberty County notices arrive, and what are the appeal rules?

Most notices are mailed in May, and the appeal clock is 45 days from the notice date. The county handout stresses that the notice is no bill, and the exact deadline is printed on it.

The calendar the assessors publish looks like this:

  • Homestead applications and real property returns: January 1 to April 1.
  • Prebill mobile home bills: mailed around February 1, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Annual notices of assessment: mailed in May, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Personal property returns: mailed around December 22 and returned between January 1 and April 1.

Taxes themselves are not qualifying grounds for an appeal. Owners with 10 acres or more of agricultural, forestry or environmentally sensitive land may qualify for a specialized assessment, and the mapping option on the phone menu handles that and any splitting or combining of parcels.

Expect a visit. Staff inspect a property after a homestead application, a return, an appeal, a purchase or a permit, and when it has not been seen in more than three years. They measure, photograph and note features. State code 48-5-264.1 lets appraisers go onto land outside the buildings, and they are expected to carry visible identification.

How does the homestead exemption work for a Liberty County home?

You qualify if you own the land and the home and live in it, and the application deadline is April 1 of each year. Call 912-876-3568 and press 1 to ask what documents to bring.

The state formula takes 40 percent of market value as the assessed figure and subtracts the $2,000 standard exemption before millage applies. Some counties add bigger local amounts, so ask the administration desk about Liberty. Millage differs by area, so the same exemption is worth a different sum in Hinesville than in the unincorporated area.

Your exemption follows you, and the house loses it when you sell. A buyer who will live in the property should file soon after closing, and by April 1 of the first tax year.

What should I do about taxes when I sell in Liberty County?

Find out if the year's bill is issued and paid, then settle the split at closing. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year under state rules, and a part-year owner gets nothing back.

The commissioner's online system lets you search records and pay, and a printout can serve as proof of payment for a buyer's lender. With about half of Liberty's units owner-occupied, a tenant may live in the home you are selling. If so, hand the buyer the lease and the tax status together. Call 912-876-3389 about any open balance, and have your closing attorney account for it.

Who lives in Liberty County, and what does that mean for a sale?

Liberty is young. Children under 18 are 27.3 percent of residents, children under 5 are 9.2 percent, and only 11.2 percent are 65 or older. Of adults 25 and up, 92.6 percent finished high school and 20.5 percent hold a bachelor's degree. A share of 6.3 percent were born abroad, and 12.8 percent of residents speak another language at home.

The employer base is sizable: 921 establishments in 2023, total employment of 14,880 with a payroll near $802.6 million, and a 4.5 percent jump in jobs over 2022. With 8,042 veterans in the county, buyers from the military community are part of the market, and an organized tax file helps the paperwork move.

Who values property in Liberty County?

The Liberty County Assessors Office values it, at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550 in Hinesville. Call 912-876-3568 and press 4 to reach the real property appraisers.

When must I file a Liberty County homestead application?

By April 1 each year. Real property returns use the same January 1 to April 1 window.

Why is Lincoln County, Georgia a small-county tax story for a seller?

With 8,112 residents, Lincoln County has the fewest people of the four Georgia counties researched for this guide, and the county seat, Lincolnton, hosts both tax offices on Humphrey Street. Expect short phone queues.

Headcounts tell of a dip and recovery in the Census QuickFacts figures: 7,996 in 2010, 7,690 at the 2020 count, and a July 2025 estimate that sits 5.5 percent over the 2020 base. Land area is 210.38 square miles, so each square mile holds about 36.6 people. Of 4,779 housing units, 76.6 percent are lived in by their owners, the top share among the four, and a typical owned home is valued at $165,900.

Age shapes the market here. Residents past 65 make up 28.1 percent of the county, and 93.9 percent of people kept the same address for a year. Builders took only 55 permits in 2025. A house that a parent or grandparent held for decades comes with a long record, and the buyer will ask for the exemption and tax history in writing.

What do Lincoln County households earn and spend?

Money is tight for many. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $56,907 and per capita income $29,291, with 14.1 percent of residents under the poverty line. A mortgage holder's monthly cost is $1,597 at the median, a paid-off owner's is $500 and a renter's is $786.

  • 2,997 households live in the county, at 2.60 people each.
  • Broadband reaches 64.5 percent of households and 81.5 percent own a computer.
  • A one-way drive to work averages 31.2 minutes, the longest in the group.
  • Retail sales totaled about $54.2 million in 2022, or $6,899 per resident.

Long commutes and thin broadband narrow the buyer pool. A seller who prices with those facts in mind and hands over a clear tax record will see fewer stalled deals.

Where do I find the Lincolnton tax commissioner and the board of assessors?

Humphrey Street holds both. The commissioner works from the courthouse address and the assessors from the county government office.

Lincoln County property tax offices as printed on the county website

The assessors' page says the board's mission is to value every Lincoln County parcel fairly and see that staff hold the training Georgia requires. It links to the qPublic property search. The 2026 board meetings were set for the third Tuesday of each month, at 5:30 p.m. in the courthouse conference room, with any change posted on the courthouse bulletin board and the assessors' front door.

How can I pay a Lincoln County property tax bill?

You may pay at the window, by post or online. Accepted: cash, personal and cashier's checks, money orders and the four major card brands. Make paper instruments out to the Lincoln County Tax Commissioner, the county page says.

  • The county adds 3 percent to each card or online payment.
  • The page names no fee for cash, checks or money orders.
  • The mailing address is P.O. Box 946, Lincolnton, GA 30817.

Georgia's default due date is December 20, and a county may choose an earlier date or installments. Interest begins 60 days after the bill's postmark. Lincoln's pages print no date of their own, so your bill decides.

How do I fight a Lincoln County valuation?

Your written appeal has to reach the assessors' mail with a postmark inside 45 days of the notice's mailing date. Three paths exist under state law: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer and an arbitrator, and the Department of Revenue cannot overrule any of them on one parcel.

If the Lincoln assessors have adopted a written policy on electronic service, an appeal may be emailed. Ask at 706-359-5502. Returns of property go to the county tax office from January 1 to April 1. Skip a year and you are treated as having filed last year's figure again. Keep the notice itself, because it states how to file.

What exemptions, refunds and permits matter in Lincoln County?

Homestead filing closes April 1 of the first year you want relief, and a missed filing counts as a waiver. Ask the commissioner whether Lincoln has any local amount above the state's.

  • Refunds: a written claim for tax assessed in error must begin within three years of payment, and an appeal win triggers a refund automatically.
  • Mobile homes: the commissioner issues the location permit, requested within 30 days of placement.

City tax is separate. A city clerk bills it unless the city and county have agreed to one combined bill, so ask which applies.

What should I handle about tax when I sell a Lincoln County house?

Confirm the year's bill is paid and share it at closing. Under the state's rule, the January 1 owner owes the whole year, with nothing back for a part-year sale.

  • Call 706-359-5536 for any open balance.
  • Tell the buyer your exemption does not carry over.
  • Ask the closing attorney whether a city bill exists beside the county bill.

With over a quarter of residents past 65, many Lincoln sellers hold an age-based exemption, and the buyer applies separately.

What does the Lincoln County economy look like?

Work is small-scale. In 2023 the Census listed 162 employer sites with 884 jobs and a $33.2 million payroll, plus 764 one-person businesses. Jobs grew 2.9 percent over 2022.

Receipts for 2022 show how modest the base is: about $6.5 million in lodging and food sales and $1.9 million in health care and social services. Against that backdrop, the 31.2 minute average commute stands out.

Schooling and youth round out the picture. High school graduates are 87.9 percent of adults, college graduates 15.5 percent. Minors are 18.9 percent of residents, and 492 residents are veterans. Buyers will ask what the yearly bill runs. Have the answer ready, and add the last bill to your listing packet.

How do I look up a Lincoln County parcel before listing?

The assessors' page carries a qPublic link for online property records, and the office at 182 Humphrey Street takes calls at 706-359-5502 if you prefer to ask. Look over the record before you list so you know what the assessors have on file.

Check three things on the card: the acreage, the building description and the owner of record. If any looks wrong, call the same number. The board of assessors meets monthly at the courthouse on Humphrey Street.

What should I gather before listing a Lincolnton house?

Pull together the papers a buyer's attorney will request. Having them in one folder shortens the closing.

  • The latest tax bill and proof it was paid, from the commissioner on Humphrey Street.
  • Your last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork.
  • Proof of your exemption, if you hold one, so the buyer knows what ends at closing.
  • The deed for the parcel.
  • Any mobile home location permit, if a manufactured home sits on the land.

Builders took out only 55 permits in 2025, so a ready file can set your listing apart from other homes on the market.

Weekdays from 8 to 4:45 at 210 Humphrey Street.

Is there a surcharge on Lincoln card payments?

Yes, 3 percent on card and online payments.

Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice, judged by postmark.

December 20 by default, unless the county sets another date. Your bill states it.

Can I get back tax I overpaid in Lincoln County?

Possibly. A written claim has to begin within three years of paying.
