Who bills, values and sets the rate in Long County?

Three offices share the job in Ludowici, and all three sit on McDonald Street. One sets values, one sends and collects bills, and one votes the county rate.

  • Long County Tax Assessor's Office: 285 S McDonald St, Ludowici, GA 31316. Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Phone (912) 545-9111. Its page links to the qPublic parcel search and a digest archive that goes back to 2016.
  • Long County Tax Commissioner: P.O. Box 628, 285 South McDonald Street, Ludowici, GA 31316. Phone 912-545-2127. Payments now run through a newer site, and the older taxpayer search tab no longer takes them.
  • Long County Board of Commissioners: 468 S. McDonald Street, Ludowici. It adopts the county millage rate at a called meeting, and the office works Monday through Thursday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, closed on Fridays since January 26, 2026.

State guidance from the Department of Revenue sorts the questions this way: bills and payments go to the commissioner, while value, exemption and appeal questions go to the assessors. If you call the wrong desk, expect a quick referral.

Why does growth matter to a Long County seller?

Long County is rural and mostly farm and forest, roughly 400 square miles with Ludowici as its single city and county seat. The county's history page traces the farm economy from cotton to tobacco, corn, soybeans and cattle, with pine timber and nearby paper mills supplying steady work.

Fort Stewart, the largest military installation east of the Mississippi River, occupies the northern tip and provides civil service jobs for residents. Altamaha Technical College keeps a satellite campus in Ludowici. Long County School System covers the public schools, apart from the base, where the Department of Defense Education Activity runs the elementary level.

The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 21,557 residents, against 16,168 in the 2020 count. QuickFacts lists 7,798 housing units, and about two of every three homes are lived in by their owners (65.2%). Homes that owners occupy have a middle value of $218,300, and the average commute takes 29.8 minutes.

Aimar, Beards Creek, Donald and Tibet are unincorporated, so owners there go to the county rather than a city hall for permits and tax questions. Liberty, McIntosh, Wayne and Tattnall counties border Long County.

How has the Long County tax digest changed since 2021?

The county's published five-year history shows a taxable base that keeps growing and a county rate that moves in steps. The net digest rose from about $328.8 million in 2021 to about $546.0 million in the 2026 figures, with a net maintenance and operation millage of 17.802 mills in the 2026 presentation.

Long County net digest and net M&O millage, 2021 to 2026 (county levy only)

Source: the 2026 Tax Digest and 5 Year History published by the Long County Board of Commissioners. The notice says the levy reflects reductions from Property Tax Relief Local Option Sales Tax proceeds, also called FLOST, applied against property tax. County voters authorized FLOST in 2025, and the combined sales tax rate in Long County became 9% on January 1, 2026.

For the 2025 rate, the assessors' page carried a notice of a tentative increase of 20.72 percent: 18.707 mills against 15.496 mills without the increase, with hearings on February 12 and February 19, 2026. A called meeting on September 24, 2026 was scheduled to adopt the 2026 millage. School and state levies sit on top of the county figure, so use the rate shown on your own bill.

The same publication splits the 2026 digest into a gross figure of $791,914,814 and exemptions of $245,871,061, which leaves the net value in the table. Exemptions stood at $104,458,820 in 2024 and $234,837,877 in 2025, so the jump in the net base in 2025 came with a much larger exempt share. Real and personal property made up $774,693,757 of the 2026 gross, while motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber were small slices.

When are Long County property taxes due?

Recent Long County due dates have followed the digest rather than a fixed calendar date. For the 2025 bills, the tax commissioner's page listed real estate taxes due May 12, 2026, and mobile home taxes due June 1, 2026 in place of the usual April 1, because the digest came out late.

The state default is December 20 with 60 days from billing, and a county may choose another date. Check the due date shown on each bill, and ask the commissioner's office when the next mailing goes out.

  • Property returns are due in the window that opens January 1 and closes April 1.
  • Mobile home tax is normally due April 1.
  • Payment runs through the newer payment site linked from the commissioner's page.

How do you appeal a Long County assessment?

You get 45 days after the notice goes out in the mail. Put the appeal on paper for the Long County assessors, using the uniform form the state provides.

That first filing is where you pick a route: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue officials have no power to overrule any of those bodies, or Superior Court, on one property's appraisal. Where a county has adopted a written policy accepting electronic service, the appeal may be emailed, and the assessors can say if Long County has done so. Their page lists longcoappr@longcountyga.gov.

Valid grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, equal treatment with similar parcels, or a turned-down exemption. Before filing, pull your parcel on qPublic and compare it with recent sales nearby.

Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Long County?

The standard state homestead exemption knocks $2,000 off the assessed value, which Georgia sets at 40% of market value. The home must be your main residence.

  • Some counties take homestead filings at the commissioner's desk and others at the assessors. Ask Long County which one applies.
  • Local exemptions can exceed the state one. The assessors can list them with their age and income limits.
  • Farm, timber and conservation assessments rest on a covenant signed with the assessors, so confirm eligibility before assuming acreage qualifies.

Census data show 275 building permits in Long County for 2025. New construction and added improvements feed the digest, so compare your January 1 value with the parcel record.

What happens to unpaid Long County tax when you sell?

The January 1 title holder owes the full year, and a sale on January 2 changes nothing with the state. No refund goes to partial-year owners, so buyer and seller divide the bill in the contract.

Ask the commissioner for a payoff amount that includes interest or penalty, and hand the closing attorney the current bill. If the county has recorded a tax lien (a fi fa) against the parcel, payoff or release is needed before a buyer can take clean title.

An inherited, behind-on-tax or tenant-occupied house in Long County follows the same steps. Call early, since a figure quoted weeks ahead can grow as interest adds up.

Which Long County office answers questions about my bill?

Billing and payment questions go to the Tax Commissioner at 912-545-2127, or by mail to P.O. Box 628 in Ludowici. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office at (912) 545-9111.

How long is the Long County assessment appeal window?

Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. File on paper with the county assessors and name your chosen route in that first filing.

Has the Long County millage rate gone up?

The published history shows net M&O millage of 14.738 in 2023, 18.707 in 2024 and 2025, and 17.802 in the 2026 presentation. Sales tax relief proceeds were applied against the levy, so use the rate on your bill.

Is any tax refunded when a Long County home sells mid-year?

No. The January 1 owner owes the whole year, so the buyer and seller settle the split in the sales contract.

Use the qPublic property search linked from the Tax Assessor's page. It shows parcel records, and the assessors' office can explain any value you find.

Where do you pay and question property tax in Lowndes County?

Lowndes County runs its property tax out of Valdosta, with the commissioner and the assessors answering different questions. Bills, payments and liens go through the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs go through the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. Counter service starts at 8:00 AM on weekdays and ends at 4:45 PM. Drivers have a separate lane that opens half an hour later and closes at 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County tax assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Deed room run by the Superior Court clerk, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, ground-level 1st Floor: copies of your warranty deed.

A payment box for drivers stands on the right side of the Government Building's front lot. Mailing a check? Put the bill number on it, and slip in a return envelope if you would like a receipt.

How does Lowndes County compare with nearby Georgia counties?

Lowndes sits in south Georgia and has roughly 497 square miles of land area. Census estimators put the county at 122,867 people in mid-2025, which is 3.9% above the 118,259 starting count they use for 2020. That pace is slower than Lumpkin County's 8.0% and far slower than Long County's 33.5%.

QuickFacts lists 54,425 housing units and a 2020 density of 237.8 people per square mile. Owners occupy 56.9% of homes, and the middle price tag on those homes is $215,600 in the Bureau's 2020 through 2024 figures. The midpoint household income is $58,541, and the poverty rate is 18.1%. Workers average 19.5 minutes to get to work, shorter than in Lumpkin, Long or Macon-Bibb counties.

Builders pulled 804 permits in 2025. Retail sales reached about $2.64 billion in 2022, and medical and social service receipts were near $1.07 billion that year.

Which date counts in Lowndes County, and what does lateness add?

Tax on land, buildings and business equipment is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails each bill two months or more before that date, and the county's tax information page says bills reach mailboxes in early October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges, as the tax commissioner publishes them
ItemWhat the commissioner's site says
Property returnsFiled from New Year's Day through April 1
Homestead applicationMust reach the office by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessmentForty-five days after the notice date
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15, with weekends and holidays pushing it to the next day the office is open
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of the tax once 120 days pass, added again every 120 days until 20% is reached
Penalty exceptionA homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00

Source: Lowndes County Tax Commissioner FAQ and tax bill information pages.

A mailed check avoids interest only if the postmark falls on or before that day. The commissioner also lets owners pay in two installments, though interest and penalty attach to whatever remains open after the due date. The office warns that the date may change, so use the one on your bill.

How are Lowndes County values set and challenged?

Georgia taxes only 40% of market value, called assessed value, and the Lowndes assessors set that figure every year. From New Year's Day through April 1, an owner may file a return declaring a proposed value. If the Board of Assessors disagrees, it mails a notice with its own number, and the county's tax information page puts those notices in May.

Disagree with the figure? The clock is 45 days, starting on the notice date. An equalization board or an arbitrator hears the dispute first. If you still disagree after the ruling, send written notice to the assessors to go on to Superior Court.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • One mill raises a dollar on every thousand dollars of assessed value. Two bodies vote a rate each year, the county and the school board.

With value settled, exemptions come off the assessed figure and the millage rate multiplies the remainder. Your current bill shows the Lowndes rate in force.

How does a Lowndes deed turn into a bill?

The county's own tax information page walks through the path. The cycle opens when a sale closes and its deed is recorded in Valdosta. The assessors then give the parcel a value, and they mail a notice the following May. When the appeal period closes, the assessors compile the tax digest: an official listing of every owner, street address, legal address, property location, exemption, assessment and tax due. State revenue officials approve that digest before the commissioner prints bills.

Personal property follows a separate track. Boats and motors, tractors, farm equipment and machinery count, and so do furniture, fixtures, equipment, inventory and supplies for a business. Who owns it is settled as of New Year's Day, appraisers mail their values every year, and owners get the same 45 day appeal window.

Sellers should know that the commissioner hears about a transfer through the recorded deed. If your closing statement prorated the tax, hand that statement to the commissioner yourself.

Which ways of paying does the Lowndes commissioner accept?

Options include the counter, the mail, the drive-up box and a credit card. The card company, not the county, adds a convenience fee. The printed rates are 2.57% on Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% on American Express, each with a minimum of $1.50.

The office does not mail past-due bills every month, only at certain intervals, so confirm the amount due before you send money. Interest accrues monthly until the balance clears. The commissioner's page adds that a lien stays on a credit record for at least seven years.

If taxes stay unpaid beyond 90 days after the due date, the county's tax information page says the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before that point about the exact balance and your options.

Who owes the bill when a Lowndes County house changes hands?

Bills follow whoever held title when the year began. A lien is recorded in that person's name unless the commissioner has a contract or closing statement in hand, no more than 90 days after the due date, showing the new owner took on the tax. If tax was prorated at closing, take the signed statement to the Patterson Street office.

The Department of Revenue puts it bluntly: the January 1 owner is liable for the year, and a sale the next day earns no refund. The office may bill the buyer as well once a deed transfer reaches it.

If a bill still reaches you after the sale, send it along to the new owner. A house inherited from a relative or occupied by tenants follows the same path. Get the payoff figure first, then have the closing attorney settle it at the table.

Which exemptions and special programs reduce Lowndes County tax?

Residences usually get the homestead break, and business inventory usually gets the freeport break. Ownership and occupancy as of January 1 decide eligibility, and the assessors take the filing.

  • Applications are taken year-round, though one arriving after April 1 applies to the following year.
  • Approval carries forward each year at the same address, and a move requires a fresh filing.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption, according to the commissioner's FAQ.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

Mobile and modular homes count as personal property, and the commissioner's FAQ says the owner of any such home located in the county must file a return.

More questions about Lowndes County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the usual Lowndes County due date?

Generally November 15 each year for land, buildings and business equipment. The commissioner cautions that it can change, so check your bill.

What does a late Lowndes County payment add?

Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty begins at the 120-day mark, recurring on that cycle until it totals 20%. A homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00 escapes the penalty.

Does the Lowndes County commissioner take cards?

Yes. The card company adds its own fee, printed as 2.57% for Discover, Mastercard and Visa and 3% for American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each. A drive-up box is also available.

How large is the Lowndes County housing market?

QuickFacts lists 54,425 housing units in Lowndes County for mid-2025 and 46,106 households in the 2020 through 2024 period, averaging 2.50 people each. Builders pulled 804 permits in 2025.

How long does a Lowndes County owner have to contest a value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. An equalization board or arbitrator hears the case first, and written notice to the assessors keeps it alive for Superior Court.

Which Lumpkin County offices do what?

Two offices sit at 99 Courthouse Hill in Dahlonega, a few suite numbers apart. One handles value and exemptions. The other handles billing and collection.

Lumpkin County property tax offices
OfficeHandlesLocationPhone and hours
Tax CommissionerBilling, collection, payment questions99 Courthouse Hill, Suite E, Dahlonega, GA 30533706-864-2666; weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm, closed 1:00pm to 1:30pm; fax 706-867-6010
Board of Tax AssessorsValues, returns, exemptions, appeals99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, Dahlonega, GA 30533706-864-2433; weekdays 8am to 5pm; fax 706-864-9806

Source: Lumpkin County Tax Commissioner FAQ page and the county's Assessor's Office page.

Owners can search, view and pay property tax on the commissioner's site. The commissioner sends bills to homeowners only. Lenders do not receive them, so an owner with escrow should pass the bill along.

What should a Lumpkin County seller know about the local population and homes?

Dahlonega is the address for Lumpkin County's tax offices. In its mid-2025 estimate the Census Bureau gives the county 36,178 residents, 8.0% more than its 2020 starting figure of 33,486. The county has about 283 square miles of land, and in 2020 it held 118.4 people to the square mile.

The housing numbers set Lumpkin apart from its three neighbors in the QuickFacts comparison. Owners occupy 76.3% of homes, the top rate among the four places compared, and the middle price of those homes is $307,900 in the 2020 through 2024 data, far above the $174,500 shown for Macon-Bibb County. The household income midpoint is $77,448, with 13.0% of people below the poverty line.

Lumpkin skews older, with 20.6% of its people past 65 against 9.7% in Long County. Age matters for tax relief here, because several exemptions in the county's flyer begin at 62 or 65. QuickFacts shows 14,302 housing units and 270 permits issued in 2025. A commute averages 28.3 minutes.

What does Lumpkin County bill, and what does lateness cost?

December 1 is the due date for houses, land and business equipment. The commissioner's FAQ explains that the date was December 20 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it up.

  • After the due date, a 5% penalty arrives at the 120 day mark and returns every 120 days until the total reaches 20%.
  • Past 90 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can go on record at the courthouse.
  • Levy on the property is possible, though the FAQ calls it a last resort.
  • Credit bureaus can see the lien, and the tax office says it cannot control their use of it.

Mobile homes run on their own calendar, so an owner of one should phone 706-864-2666 for that date. A location permit is issued only after the current year's mobile home tax has been paid in full.

Which appeal routes exist for a Lumpkin County value?

Three routes appear in the county's flyer, and each begins with a written appeal filed 45 days or sooner after the notice date. Grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, uniformity, or a refused exemption.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors look first and may revise the value in a new notice, which the owner has 30 days to contest. Otherwise it goes automatically to a hearing, and Superior Court is the next stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser takes value or uniformity disputes on non-homestead real property above $500,000, or on certain wireless property above that same level.
  • Arbitration: the owner submits a certified appraisal, and the assessors either accept it or certify the appeal to the Clerk of Superior Court for arbitration.

The state provides a uniform appeal form, and you name your chosen route in that first written filing. Unsure which fits your case? Call the assessors at 706-864-2433 before filing.

Which exemptions and special assessments does Lumpkin County list?

The standard state homestead exemption subtracts $2,000 from assessed value, set by law at 40% of market value. You qualify by owning the home and living in it on January 1. Applications can go in all year, but one received after April 1 starts with the following year. Owners who reach 62 can apply for an additional exemption.

The county's tax information flyer, last dated 2021, also describes local and special programs. Ask the assessors to confirm the current amounts, since those figures may have changed.

  • School tax break for owners 62 and over whose federal adjusted gross income is at most $20,000: $30,000 off assessed value.
  • Owners 65 and up, or permanently disabled: as much as $120,000 off for school tax and $60,000 off for county tax, covering the home and at most 5 adjoining acres.
  • Agricultural preferential assessment: qualifying land is assessed at 30% instead of the usual 40%, under a 10-year covenant that carries penalties if broken.
  • Forest land conservation use: 200 acres or more in total, with parcels of 100 acres or more inside the county.
  • Tax deferral: owners 62 or older with household income under the flyer's $15,000 line can postpone the tax, which is different from an exemption.

A conservation use application (PT-283A) needs a notary's signature and must go in by April 1 with a $25.00 recording fee, because the original is recorded at the courthouse. A senior application should enclose a state ID showing birth date and address, and a disabled veteran application needs the VA letter showing a 100% combined rating.

What are Lumpkin County's assessors doing on the ground?

A posted notice from the Assessor's Office says field inspections are under way countywide, and it cites state law as the authority. Appraisers carry identification, drive marked vehicles, measure exteriors, take photographs and note improvements. Entering a home is generally unnecessary, and owners need not be present.

A second notice on the page says McCormick Solutions, a division of LMC, Inc, will do commercial and industrial appraisals for the board. Its staff wear county-issued badges, and owners may ask to see them.

Forms can be downloaded from the state revenue department's site and mailed in, and the assessors ask for a USPS postmark no later than April 1. These include the state homestead form, the business personal property return (PT-50P), the freeport application (PT-50F), the marine (PT-50M) and airplane (PT-50A) returns, and PT-50R, the taxpayer return of value used to ask for a review.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lumpkin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who pays the Lumpkin County bill if you sell?

State law puts the full year on whoever owned the parcel January 1, and the revenue department says a mid-year sale earns no refund.

Before listing, phone the commissioner at 706-864-2666 and ask what is still owed on the parcel, interest or lien included. Hand that number to the closing attorney. An unpaid fifa has to be cleared first. A bill that still reaches you after closing should go to the buyer.

An inherited, tax-delinquent or rented house goes through the same sequence.Ask the assessors early whether a senior exemption or deferral is attached to the account, since it can change what is owed at the closing table.

More questions about Lumpkin County, GA Property Tax Guide

On what date is Lumpkin County property tax due?

December 1, per the commissioner's FAQ. Before a December 2009 resolution by the county commissioners, the usual date had been December 20.

How long is the Lumpkin County dispute window?

Forty-five days after the notice date. Send a written filing to the assessors at 99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, and say which route you pick.

Does Lumpkin County send my bill to my mortgage company?

No. Bills go to the homeowner, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account should send a copy to the mortgage company.

When must a Lumpkin County homestead application arrive?

The assessors need it ahead of April 1 for it to count this tax year. A later one starts with the following year.

Which office should a Lumpkin County seller call first?

Start with the commissioner at 706-864-2666 to learn what is owed. Use the assessors at 706-864-2433 for value or exemption questions.

Which door in Danielsville do I knock on for a Madison County tax problem?

Everything runs out of the Government Complex at 91 Albany Avenue, the former Danielsville Elementary School building that the county renovated and moved into in June 1997. Property Valuation sits upstairs in Suite 404 and speaks for the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner is in Suite 14.

The split is simple. Disputes over worth, acreage on the record or a missing exemption go to Property Valuation. Questions about the amount owed or a cleared check go to the commissioner. The county's home page also links a public parcel lookup run through qPublic.

Madison County tax desks at the Government Complex (source: county government pages)
OfficeSuitePhoneOpen
Property Valuation404706-795-6355Mon to Fri, 8 to 5
Tax Commissioner14706-795-6385Mon to Fri, 8 to 4:30

After hours, a drop box behind the complex takes checks. The county describes the commissioner's counter as the only place in Madison County that bills land, mobile homes and timber.

Is Madison County a good fit for a rural sale?

The county calls itself a comfortable suburb of Athens, Commerce and Elberton. Its calendar leans on a Fourth of July parade in Colbert, a fall festival in Danielsville and a Christmas parade in Comer. Carlton, Colbert, Comer, Danielsville, Hull and Ila are the six towns.

Georgia formed it in 1811, the 38th county, and honored President James Madison with the name. Danielsville was named for General Allen Daniel and made the seat in 1812. Crawford W. Long, the first doctor to use ether in surgery, was born there in 1815, and the house he grew up in carries a National Register listing. Cotton wore out much of the soil before the 1930s, and the county now counts about 23 percent of its acreage as prime farmland, with chickens and eggs leading agribusiness.

  • People: an estimated 32,919 by July 2025, which is 9.3 percent more than in April 2020.
  • Elbow room: 282.32 land square miles, about 107 residents for each one in 2020.
  • Ownership: 76.9 percent of 11,242 households live in a home they own.
  • Money: a typical owned home is valued at $219,700 and a typical rent is $972.
  • Paychecks: the middle household earns $61,963, and a trip to work averages 29.5 minutes.
  • Building: 130 permits were written in 2025.

Every figure above is from Census Bureau QuickFacts.

How do Madison County appraisers settle on a house value?

The starting point is market value on January 1, and the taxed slice is 40 percent. County appraisers lean on comparable sales, on rebuilding cost with depreciation subtracted and land added, and on rent-based math for income property.

Notices arrive between April and May. Read it as a preview of the later bill. If you plan to list in spring, open it the day it lands, because the objection clock starts on the notice date.

Returns go to Property Valuation during the first three months of the year. One return keeps working until a garage goes up, acreage is added or the owner wants a different value on record.

  • Field appraisers measure buildings and photograph them, wearing photo ID and driving marked county vehicles.
  • Conservation use and similar specialized assessments need an application on file by April 1.
  • Madison County counts only the Postal Service postmark when judging whether a return, homestead form or appeal was on time.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Madison County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What are the Madison County billing dates?

A September mailing is typical, and December 20 is the usual deadline. The counter takes partial payments, so a seller can chip away at a balance before closing.

Mobile home statements go out in late January with an April 1 deadline. A mobile home that has a homestead exemption skips that early statement, and its tax rides on the year-end property bill.

The Department of Revenue's county facts page allows 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts, and lets local government shift the official date. Timber is a one-time event, taxed at full market value when cut or sold, with payment going to the commissioner in the county where the trees grew.

Ask the commissioner's staff for a written payoff on your parcel before signing a contract. A closing attorney will want that number.

What is the appeal route if a Madison County value looks too high?

Mail a written appeal so it is postmarked within 45 days of the date on the notice. Property Valuation refuses faxes, emails and any other electronic delivery, because it cannot confirm who sent them or what value was under appeal.

The county describes four steps. First, a letter with the parcel number, the reason and a phone number. Second, a staff review and possibly an appointment. Third, notice of a change, or an automatic move to the Board of Equalization (or arbitration, if you asked for it up front). Fourth, Superior Court for whoever is still unhappy.

  • Grounds that count: value, taxability and equalization. Complaints about the size of the bill do not.
  • The Board of Equalization is drawn from people eligible for grand jury service and charges nothing.
  • Arbitration costs each side its own arbitrator plus half of a third.
  • The court filing fee quoted by the county is $25.
  • A recent state law bars the assessors from altering a board or court result for two years unless they inspect the property or a return is filed.

The county invites recent sale information and photos of comparable homes. Skip the window and that year's appeal rights are gone.

What are the S and L codes on Madison County exemptions?

The county sorts homestead relief into letter codes. S1 means an owner-occupied principal residence, with the owner holding title to both home and land. S3 and L3 apply from age 62 with income under $10,000 for the applicant and spouse, leaving out Social Security and retirement pay. L4 starts at 65 and L5 at 70, with no income test at all.

S5 is for a veteran rated 100 percent disabled or the unremarried surviving spouse. SG is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed on duty, and SS is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in action.

File between January 1 and April 1 after owning and occupying the home on January 1. The three-member Board of Assessors meets monthly to act on homestead, conservation and preferential status requests, so a late application waits for the next cycle. Colbert has its own city exemption that you request from the town. For the other five towns, ask the city clerk whether a separate city levy exists.

Someone who buys your house has to apply in their own name, so do not count the exemption as part of what you are selling.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Madison County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who pays what when a Madison County house sells?

The county taxes whoever held title on January 1. A June closing can still leave the seller holding a December bill, which is why the contract language and the closing statement matter.

The state adds a transfer tax at recording. Georgia's revenue department sets it at $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents per further $100, charges it to the seller by default, and refers questions to the Clerk of Superior Court.

Properties once sold at a Madison County tax sale may have money waiting. The Tax Commissioner posts an excess funds list and takes claims on an application form.

  • Get the payoff figure on paper ahead of closing.
  • Make sure your exemption ends once the deed records.
  • Mail your forwarding address so later notices reach you.

More questions about Madison County, GA Property Tax Guide

What day do Madison County property taxes come due?

Expect a September mailing and a normal deadline of December 20 for land, houses and business property. A mobile home has its own April 1 deadline. If the printed date on your bill differs, believe the bill.

Is an emailed appeal accepted in Madison County?

No. Madison County wants paper, mailed so the postmark lands within 45 days of the notice date. Fax and electronic submissions are turned away.

Which office decides what my Madison County house is worth?

The Board of Assessors does, with Property Valuation staff doing the fieldwork. Value is outside the Tax Commissioner's role.

Does a new owner keep my homestead exemption?

No. A buyer has to apply personally, with January 1 to April 1 as the window. Anything filed after April 1 first helps in the next tax year.

Can I pay part of a Madison County tax bill?

Yes. The commissioner's office takes installments of any size on a property bill. Request the balance in writing so you know the exact remainder at closing.

Which McDuffie County body does what with my house?

Three separate bodies touch a McDuffie County tax bill. The Board of Assessors, working out of the Tax Assessor's Office, judges taxability, value and equalization. Billing, collecting and passing money to other governments belong to the Tax Commissioner. When the assessors will not budge, the Board of Equalization, a citizen panel appointed by the Grand Jury, hears the dispute.

Reach the assessors at 706-595-2128, in person weekdays 8 am to 5 pm. The county describes that office as one that sets values only, so a question about a statement goes to the commissioner. Returns are also filed with the assessors under a delegation described on the county's general info page.

  • Value, returns, exemptions and homestead filings: the Tax Assessor's Office.
  • Statements, payments, liens and excess funds: the Tax Commissioner.
  • Millage: voted each year by the county commissioners and the school board, so neither tax office controls it.
  • A rejected appeal: Board of Equalization or arbitration, then Superior Court.

Budget and millage hearings meet at the McDuffie County Government Center, 210 Railroad Street, Thomson.

What makes McDuffie County different from its Augusta-area neighbors?

McDuffie County is a small, steady county in the Augusta metro area, west of Columbia and Richmond counties. The state created it on October 18, 1870, and named it for South Carolina governor and senator George McDuffie. Thomson, incorporated in 1854 while it still sat in Columbia County, became the seat, and Dearing is the lone town beside it. The old Wrightsborough settlement, occupied from 1768 to 1920, is kept alive by a local historic foundation.

Every creek here ends in the Savannah River, with Brier Creek serving much of the south and the Little River basin the north. Interstate 20 crosses the county along with US 78, US 221 and US 278. Census business data for 2022 list $68.8 million of transportation and warehousing revenue and $89.9 million in health care and social assistance.

  • Headcount: 21,640 in July 2025, almost the same as the 2020 base of 21,628.
  • Space: 257.37 land square miles, with 84 residents to each in 2020.
  • Homes: 9,725 units, 65.0 percent owner-occupied, valued at $170,200 in the middle, with rents around $792.
  • Residents: 22.3 percent are 65 or older, 19.6 percent live in poverty, and a typical household takes in $56,733.
  • Workers spend 22.7 minutes getting to a job.
  • Builders pulled 86 permits during 2025.

When does a McDuffie County bill arrive and what do late fees look like?

McDuffie runs one of the earlier schedules in Georgia, with a mailing by September 15 and a November 15 deadline, five weeks ahead of the December 20 default used in other counties. The county's wording is laid out below.

Dates and charges on a McDuffie bill, as the county words them (source: thomson-mcduffie.gov tax pages)
EventCounty wording
MailingBy September 15
DeadlineNovember 15
InterestCharged monthly from the 16th, prime rate plus 3 divided by 12
Penalty5 percent each 120 days, topping out at 20 percent
FIFA tax lienFiled with the Clerk of Court 30 days after the bill is delinquent
Mobile homesMailed in January, due April 1

For a seller the lien is the problem. It shows on your credit report and in the public record, so clear the bill before the 30 days are up and the title search stays simple.

Installments are possible. The Tax Commissioner must approve a signed agreement set up before the bill goes delinquent.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McDuffie County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What changed on McDuffie County bills in 2026?

The county's 2026 tax page reported that the separate fire fee ends, with FLOST sales tax revenue taking its place. It proposed a county rate of 7.998 mills, compared with 7.809 mills in 2025, to absorb the fire cost. The final vote was slated for the evening hearing on October 13, 2026, so ask the Tax Commissioner what was adopted.

The page also explains why a Notice of Property Tax Increase may arrive even when the typical homestead bill drops: the comparison is to the rollback rate, shown as 6.085 mills for 2026, and it ignores the fire fee. City and school taxes, 15.124 mills in the estimator, are billed separately.

Homesteads also get a one-time state credit. The Tax Commissioner describes it as $18,000 off assessed value, applied automatically when the homestead was filed on time.

How does a McDuffie County owner fight a new value?

Count 45 days from the date on the notice of assessment. An appeal that arrives later is invalid, and it has to be in writing, delivered to the Board of Assessors.

The assessors look again and either adjust the value or send the file to the Board of Equalization, where each side states its position. The loser may go to McDuffie County Superior Court. Arbitration is available in place of the Board of Equalization if you choose it when you file.

  • Accepted grounds: taxability, uniformity and value.
  • Uniformity compares your value with similar properties.
  • Objecting to the size of the tax itself is not a ground.
  • Either the owner or the assessors can take a Board of Equalization ruling to court.

A denied homestead has its own path. The assessors decide eligibility, and a turned-down applicant must be told how to appeal.

What homestead and land programs does McDuffie County list?

File at the Board of Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1, having owned and lived in the house on January 1. Per the county, the ordinary homestead exemption is $4,000. At 62 and older with net income under $15,000 it is $15,000, and at 65 and older there is $30,000 off assessed value for schools. Owners rated 100 percent disabled may use a local exemption with a doctor's documentation and the same income limit. After approval it continues without reapplying until ownership changes.

Land programs carry a ten-year covenant with the county:

  • Preferential agricultural property is taxed on 30 percent of market value in place of the usual 40.
  • Conservation use values land by what it produces now.
  • Environmentally sensitive property stays in its natural state under state rules.
  • Residential transitional property sits in an area changing to another use.

Timber is taxed one time, at 100 percent of fair market value, when cut or sold. The county also describes a deferral for homestead owners 62 and older with income of $15,000 or less, usually lasting until ownership changes.

What can a seller do about an unpaid McDuffie County bill?

Phone the Tax Commissioner for the full balance, including interest and any lien charge, and ask how the payoff reaches your closing attorney. A bill a few days late looks nothing like one stacked with penalty layers and a recorded lien.

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, with fees on cards and no American Express. If land once sold at a delinquent tax sale left money over, claim it in writing with proper ID. The county publishes a list and an application.

For a mobile home, deal with the April 1 bill first, because it is an account separate from the land.

More questions about McDuffie County, GA Property Tax Guide

What day are McDuffie County property taxes due?

Plan on November 15, with bills out by September 15, which is earlier than the December 20 default in other counties. Mobile homes follow an April 1 deadline.

How long can I appeal a McDuffie County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. The appeal must be written, and a late filing is treated as invalid.

What does it cost to pay a McDuffie County bill late?

Interest builds monthly from the 16th and a 5 percent penalty lands every 120 days up to 20 percent. A tax lien follows once the bill has been delinquent for 30 days.

Is the McDuffie County fire fee gone?

Per the county's 2026 page, yes. FLOST revenue replaces it, and the county rate was proposed at 7.998 mills. Ask the Tax Commissioner what was adopted.

Where does a McDuffie County homeowner apply for homestead?

At the Board of Assessors Office, between January 1 and April 1. The county says the assessors handle and approve every exemption application.

Which McIntosh County office answers a tax question?

Darien's North Way holds both tax offices. The assessors at number 601 appraise property and approve exemptions. At number 1200, in the county annex, the Tax Commissioner prints and mails statements and takes in what owners pay. The commissioner's own page states that it sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone (source: county website and Tax Commissioner site)

A house inside Darien may carry a city levy as well. State guidance gives billing of city tax to the city clerk, unless city and county agreed to merge the statements, so City Hall can tell you which applies.

What should a seller know about McIntosh County itself?

Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county. The Census Bureau measures 574 square miles, and 150 of them are water. Darien started life as New Inverness in 1736, settled by Scottish Highlanders whom Oglethorpe had recruited, and the county separated from Liberty County in 1793. A British fort, Fort King George, went up in 1721. Federal troops burned Darien in June 1863. Following the Civil War, and until Georgia's disenfranchisement laws of 1907, McIntosh was a center of Black political strength, sending three Black representatives to the legislature between 1875 and 1907.

Besides Darien, the named places are Crescent and Eulonia, both census-designated places, with Townsend and Valona unincorporated. Sapelo Island is the most familiar of the islands. Liberty, Glynn, Wayne and Long counties are the neighbors, and Brunswick's metro area takes in the county.

  • Headcount: 11,989 in July 2025, a climb of 9.3 percent from 10,970 in 2020, though 2010 had counted 14,333.
  • Owners: 80.0 percent of households, living in homes worth $182,700 in the middle.
  • Tenants: $800 a month for the typical rental.
  • Older residents: 28.2 percent are 65 and over.
  • Pay and travel: households earn a median $50,273 and commute 37.5 minutes on average.
  • Room: 431.35 square miles of dry land, roughly 25 people on each in 2020.
  • Construction: 106 permits issued in 2025.

How does flood zoning change a McIntosh County sale?

Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding, and the county names St. Catherine's, Sapelo, Doboy and Altamaha Sounds as contributors. Lenders ask about flood zones, so look yours up before listing.

Both the county and Darien participate in the federal flood insurance program. Regular homeowners coverage typically excludes flood, and a structure in a mapped high-hazard area with a federally backed mortgage must carry its own flood policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • In the AE and VE zones the underside of the lowest horizontal beam has to clear base flood elevation by one foot.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Marshes and low ground along the Darien, Altamaha and Butler rivers and Blackbeard Creek work as natural floodplains, per the county, that spread and absorb water, and that barrier islands such as Sapelo, St. Catherine's and Wolf blunt hurricane waves.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

What payment dates and penalties does McIntosh County use?

The commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing, as the usual deadline and says that unpaid property can be levied upon and sold. State guidance counts the 60 days from the postmark and allows each county to choose its own official date.

Returns go in between January 1 and April 1. Without one, last year's return and value stand. An owner who thinks the value is wrong can file a return with their own estimate of market value, which protects appeal rights if the assessors raise it again.

Mobile homes follow a different clock. A home sitting in McIntosh County on January 1 needs tax and location permit settled by April 1, or the owner faces a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale. To contest a mobile home value you have 45 days to reach the Board of Tax Assessors, and then 21 days from the notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Send new mailing addresses to the assessor or commissioner quickly, since notices only go to the address on file.

How did the McIntosh County millage conversation go in 2024?

In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate. The press release cited pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs, inflation and the fact that millage had stayed flat for more than 15 years.

Because the rate exceeded rollback, state law called for three hearings, which the county held at Darien City Hall on September 26 and October 7, 2024.

For any later year, ask the County Commission Office for the adopted millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

Which McIntosh County exemptions and appeal rights matter before a sale?

The Tax Assessor's Office takes homestead applications, and new homeowners bring the warranty deed. A filing earns the current year's benefit only if it arrives by April 1, even though Georgia takes applications all year. Approval stays on the account until you move, sell or switch types, and a larger local exemption beats the state figure.

The commissioner's page describes a $2,000 standard exemption and elderly relief for incomes of $10,000 or less: up to $10,000 on school tax from age 62 and up to $4,000 on general tax from age 65. A floating exemption suits owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less and replaces other state and county exemptions. A deferral for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less delays tax until ownership changes or the debt hits 85 percent of value.

  • Qualifying farmland may be taxed on 30 percent of market value rather than 40.
  • Conservation use taxes eligible land on its actual use value.
  • Both programs bind the owner to a 10-year covenant.

Appeals of a real property value go to the Board of Tax Assessors, with a postmark inside 45 days of the notice's mailing.

What should a McIntosh County seller line up before closing?

Request each parcel's exact balance from the Tax Commissioner and ask the Assessor's Office whether a change in value or exemption is pending. Gather the flood zone and permit history before the sign goes up.

Deed recording triggers the state transfer tax: $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on every additional $100, which the seller owes unless the contract assigns it to the buyer. The Clerk of Superior Court can speak to exemptions.

At the closing table, settle who covers the current-year bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption ends.

What is the McIntosh County property tax deadline?

The commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing. A mobile home is due April 1. Treat the date on your own statement as final.

Which McIntosh County office handles a disagreement over value?

The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner, 912-437-6627, sends bills and cannot change a value.

Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?

They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require raising the floor after major renovation.

What if a McIntosh County mobile home tax misses April 1?

Expect a 10 percent penalty, with a possible citation to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or sale of the home.

How does a McIntosh County owner apply for homestead exemption?

Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office, with the filing in by April 1 for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.

What kind of place is Meriwether County for a seller?

Meriwether County is a rural county in west central Georgia, counted inside the Atlanta metro area, with Greenville as the county seat and Manchester as its largest city. The General Assembly formed it on December 14, 1827, as the 73rd county in the state and named it for David Meriwether, a Revolutionary War general who later sat in Congress, according to Wikipedia.

Only about four of its 505 square miles are water. The land lies in the Piedmont, and the Pine Mountain range rises in the south near Warm Springs and Manchester. The eastern two thirds drains into the Upper Flint River basin, while the western third runs toward Lake Harding on the Chattahoochee. Coweta, Spalding, Pike, Upson, Talbot, Harris and Troup counties all touch its borders.

Greenville, Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs and Woodbury are cities. Gay, Lone Oak and Pine Mountain are towns, and Pine Mountain sits mostly in Harris County. Alvaton is unincorporated. The Meriwether County School District runs six campuses: Mountain View Elementary, Unity Elementary, Greenville Middle, Manchester Middle, Greenville High and Manchester High. A lot inside Manchester and a farm on a county road land on one county bill, while a lot in the Town of Gay adds a separate city bill.

What is a typical Meriwether County home worth?

Of occupied homes, 73.0% belong to their owners in the 2020 to 2024 figures from QuickFacts, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,800.

The head count slipped from 21,992 in 2010 to 20,613 in 2020 and then climbed 4.4% by mid 2025. About 23.8% of residents are 65 or older and 17.8% are in poverty. With a 34.3 minute average drive to work and a median household income of $57,340, buyers here watch carrying costs closely, and a parcel with a clean tax record is easier to sell.

Who sends and collects the Meriwether County tax bill?

Billing and collection happen at the tax commissioner's counter, 17234 Roosevelt Highway, Building A, Greenville. The county tax site gives (706) 672-4219, says the doors are open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30, and lists PO Box 729, Greenville, GA 30222 for letters.

The Board of Tax Assessors (706 672-4222) appraises; disputes over its numbers reach a Board of Equalization staffed by grand jury appointees. The county commission and the school board vote on separate millage rates, where a mill means $1 of tax on every $1,000 assessed.

Residents of Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs, Woodbury, Greenville and Lone Oak pay city and county tax together to the county commissioner. The Town of Gay collects its own city tax, so a Gay owner pays the county here and the town separately. The tax site also has tabs for tax sales and excess funds.

When are Meriwether County property taxes due?

Land, houses and business personal property owe their tax to Meriwether County by December 20. The commissioner's site says bills normally go in the mail by October 1 and asks anyone without one by October 15 to call the office.

  • Land, houses and business equipment: December 20.
  • Mobile homes: April 1, with the decal posted by that date.
  • Boats: November 15, after May assessment notices and a 45 day appeal window.
  • Boat, equipment and other personal property bills: mailed at least 60 days ahead, usually in mid November.
  • Cars and trucks: renewal follows the owner's birth date.

State rules let a county shift its official date to December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments, and interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked. The county's own site lists December 20, yet the printed bill is what you answer to.

What does a late Meriwether County bill cost?

Late real estate bills in Meriwether County collect interest starting the day after December 20, then a penalty that builds in steps. The tax site says the interest rate on real and personal property is reset yearly, so ask the counter for the rate in force.

  • Real and personal property: 5% lands on the 120th day past due, and again every 120 days, with a ceiling of 20%.
  • Mobile homes: one flat 10% penalty, with 1% interest.
  • Lien: a FiFa is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court once a bill is 90 days overdue, and credit bureaus can read it.

The counter takes partial payments while interest keeps running. Paying off a recorded lien before listing keeps it out of the buyer's title search.

How can I pay a Meriwether County tax bill?

Payments can arrive at the counter, on the website, by mail or in the drop box out front. Inside, the staff take checks, cash and cards (Visa, MasterCard and Discover), and the website takes cards or PayPal.

  • Website card payments add a fee of 2.57%, with a $1.50 floor.
  • Cards run at the counter or by phone add 3.00%, again with a $1.50 floor.
  • Mail a check to the Meriwether County Tax Commissioner at the PO Box above and write the parcel number on it.

Homeowners with an escrow account can ask the office to share tax data with the lender, and the site suggests mailing your coupons to the lender with a short note.

How do I contest a Meriwether County value?

The county tax site says notices usually mail in the spring, and the written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors first, naming the route you pick.

You may argue taxability, worth, fairness against similar parcels, or a refused exemption. The Board of Equalization and an arbitrator are the two routes the county site names, and the state also lists a hearing officer. Either route can end in superior court.

Which exemptions can lower a Meriwether County bill?

Homestead is the big one. Live in the house on January 1, file before April 1, and it applies that year.

First-time owners should bring a warranty deed, and the driver's license must show the Meriwether County street address, because a post office box is not accepted. The county FAQ notes an additional exemption at age 62. Business owners can ask about the freeport exemption on inventory, and the county tax site says the assessors make the final call on eligibility. Ask the Tax Assessor's office about conservation use or other special programs.

What else does the Meriwether County tax office collect on rural property?

Manufactured homes, boats and heavy equipment each follow their own rules at the Greenville counter. Every mobile home must show a current decal by April 1, and decals are issued once tax is paid: on the spot for walk-in payers, by mail for everyone else.

The office says anyone placing a mobile home in the county should visit the Building and Zoning office next door to the commissioner, which takes appointments at 706-672-1283. A buyer or new owner has 30 days to apply for a title and must bring a paid tax receipt and proof of ownership.

Boats need Department of Natural Resources registration and are taxed on value. Tractors, farm equipment and machinery also count as personal property. Heavy equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in the purchase year, with a return due at the commissioner's office 30 days after that month ends. Timber harvests are reported on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, available from the assessors at (706) 672-4222. Deeds sit in the courthouse deed room run by the Clerk of Superior Court, so ask there for a copy of yours.

Who owes the tax if my Meriwether County house sells mid-year?

The Department of Revenue says the January 1 titleholder owes the whole year, with no refund for part of it. Put any buyer and seller split in the contract.

A few days before closing, request a written balance from the tax commissioner that shows penalties and any lien. Back taxes can be cleared out of your payoff. If the sale closes before the fall bills mail, ask the closing attorney how that year's bill is being handled.

Which number reaches the Meriwether County tax office?

Dial (706) 672-4219 for billing and payments. Value questions go to (706) 672-4222.

When does Meriwether County want its real estate tax?

December 20. The commissioner's site says bills normally mail by October 1 and asks anyone still waiting on October 15 to call.

Can I pay a Meriwether County bill online?

Yes, by card or PayPal on meriwethertax.com, with a 2.57% fee that has a $1.50 floor. The counter, the mail and the front drop box also work.

If I sell in Meriwether County, is that year's tax erased?

No. The January 1 owner stays liable for the year and Georgia gives no refund for part of one, so put the split in the sales contract.

What is the deadline to fight a Meriwether County value?

Counting from the notice date, you get 45 days. The written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

Where does Monroe County sit in central Georgia?

Monroe County lies on the fall line, where the Piedmont gives way to the coastal plain, and it belongs to the Macon metro area. The legislature created it on May 15, 1821, and named it for James Monroe, per Wikipedia. The courthouse stands in Forsyth, the largest city.

The county measures 398 square miles, of which 396 are land. Nearly all of it drains to the Upper Ocmulgee River, with one small southwestern corner, west of a line between Yatesville and Culloden, draining to the Flint. Interstate 75 and Interstate 475 cross it, along with U.S. 23, U.S. 41 and U.S. 341 and state routes 18, 19, 42, 74 and 83. Butts, Jasper, Jones, Bibb, Crawford, Upson and Lamar counties surround it.

Forsyth and Culloden are the two incorporated cities. Bolingbroke, Juliette and Smarr are census-designated places. One school system, the Monroe County School District, covers every address in the county, which keeps school questions simple for a seller and a buyer alike.

How fast has Monroe County grown, and what are homes worth?

Monroe County has grown quickly, adding about 14.5% to its population between the April 2020 base and July 2025, and the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $271,200 for 2020 to 2024, according to QuickFacts.

What does the Monroe County economy look like to a buyer?

Monroe County had 604 employer establishments and 6,750 jobs in 2023, with annual payroll of $315,090,000, according to QuickFacts, and employment rose 1.6% from 2022. Another 2,928 businesses had no employees in 2024.

Retail sales reached $433,618,000 in 2022, about $14,714 per resident, and accommodation and food service sales were $58,733,000. The civilian labor force takes in 59.1% of residents 16 and older. Households are well connected: 95.1% have a computer and 90.4% have broadband. About 10.8% of people under 65 lack health insurance, and 9.1% have a disability. These figures help a seller describe the local buyer pool, where owner households are the large majority.

Where do I pay and ask questions about Monroe County property tax?

The Monroe County Tax Commissioner works from 38 W. Main Street in Forsyth and answers at (478) 994-7020. The commissioner's site says the doors open at 7:30 and close at 5:00 on weekdays, with a drive-through lane out front and P.O. Box 357, Forsyth, GA 31029 for letters.

The office calls itself the collector for the county. Its desk handles real property, personal property, mobile homes, timber and vehicles, yet it answers to voters and has no control over a parcel's value or the rate applied to it. Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 about value. Rates are voted on by the county's elected commissioners and the school board.

The statement is addressed to the owner of record on January 1, so anyone who bought or sold after that date should phone the tax office.

What payment options does the Monroe County tax office offer?

Monroe County takes checks, cash and cards at the counter, in the drive-through lane, by mail, in a drop box and through the county's online search and pay page. The office notice asks mailed payments to carry a postmark dated 12/20, the date the real estate bill is due.

  • Visa, MasterCard and Discover carry a 2.5% fee on the total.
  • American Express carries a 3% fee.
  • The drop box takes car tag, property tax and mobile home payments after hours, on weekends and on holidays.
  • Tag renewals can also be done on the Department of Revenue site or at a kiosk.

For current-year tax, only a postmark from the U.S. Postal Service proves an on-time mailing. Meter-dated postmarks are not honored. For overdue bills, the office urges walking the payment in, especially after a levy or tax sale advertisement has begun. Mobile home owners pay by April 1 instead.

What happens if a Monroe County property tax bill goes unpaid?

An unpaid Monroe County bill leads to interest, penalties and eventually a lien called a FiFa. The office's FAQ says interest and a penalty are added to late balances, so ask the counter for the current amounts.

  • A 30 day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before a FiFa is issued, and payment in full within those 30 days stops it.
  • Nonpayment past 90 days lets the office record a FiFa on the General Execution Docket, which the Clerk of Superior Court keeps.
  • Paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest wipes out the FiFa.
  • Liens are not sold over the counter.

As many partial payments as needed are accepted, yet penalties and interest keep growing on the remainder, and any open balance can be liened. Lien filings are open to anyone, including credit bureaus, though the tax office says it sends them nothing. A seller with a lien should plan on a payoff letter before closing.

How do I question a Monroe County property value?

Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 first, and if the answer falls short, put an appeal on paper within 45 days of the notice date. The county's FAQ lists four grounds (taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption) and requires you to name the appeal method.

Owners may declare a proposed value by filing a return with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. If the board disagrees, a notice with its own figure arrives by mail. Fair market value is the full figure the board sets, and the assessed value that gets taxed is 40% of it, less any exemptions. Each mill adds $1 for every $1,000 of that assessed figure.

Does Monroe County offer a homestead exemption?

Yes. Homestead requests are approved by the Tax Assessors' Office, and the test is ownership plus residence on January 1. Approved owners skip the annual refiling unless they move or change the deed.

The tax office points owners to the assessors, at (478) 994-7038, for other exemptions and special assessment programs. Ask which of them fit your situation rather than assuming a neighbor's savings apply to you. The state also lets counties raise homestead amounts above the statewide minimum, so the local figure may differ.

Which Monroe County departments should a seller check before listing?

A seller should check planning and zoning, building inspections and code enforcement, all of which have pages on the county site, monroecoga.org. Clearing an open permit or a code notice first removes a snag from the buyer's inspection period.

The county also lists a water department, recycling centers and a landfill, and it invited residents to a town hall on its 20 year comprehensive plan at the Monroe County Conference Center on October 27, 2026. Ask planning and zoning how the plan may affect a particular parcel. For deeds and liens on file, the Clerk of Superior Court is the office to contact; the tax office points owners there for warranty deed copies.

Who pays Monroe County tax if my house closes in spring?

Because bills follow the January 1 owner, the seller usually receives the full-year bill even if the sale closes in spring. State revenue officials confirm there is no partial-year refund, so the contract and the settlement statement decide who ultimately carries which share.

The mailed statement reaches the homeowner, not the lender, although lenders on file receive a data file from the office. If you have an escrow account, confirm with your lender that it plans to pay, and forward the bill if necessary. A call to the tax office before closing will turn up the current balance and any FiFa.

What phone number reaches the Monroe County tax commissioner?

(478) 994-7020 reaches the commissioner's office in Forsyth. For value, ring (478) 994-7038 and ask for the assessors.

Can I mail my Monroe County property tax payment?

Yes, provided a Postal Service postmark dated by the due date is on the envelope. Metered mail does not qualify.

Where can I leave a Monroe County payment after hours?

Yes, a box outside the office handles tag, property and mobile home payments when the counter is closed.

Who gets the Monroe County tax bill after I sell?

The January 1 owner of record receives it. If the sale came later, call the tax office.

How long can I appeal a Monroe County value?

Within 45 days of the notice date, using a written appeal that goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names your method.

What sets Morgan County apart in north central Georgia?

Morgan County pairs a historic seat in Madison with a share of the lake country, and its housing boom since the early 2000s comes from easy reach of Lake Oconee and four employment centers: Atlanta, Athens, Augusta and Macon. Lawmakers carved the county out on December 10, 1807, as Wikipedia recounts.

Oconee, Greene, Putnam, Jasper, Newton and Walton counties are the neighbors.

Madison, Bostwick and Rutledge are cities, Buckhead is a town, and Godfrey is a census-designated place. Apalachee and Pennington are unincorporated communities. Madison levies its own city tax on top of the county's, so an owner inside the city limits has two sets of charges to keep in view when selling.

How have Morgan County home values and population changed?

Morgan County homes are priced high for the region: the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $342,300 for 2020 to 2024, and population up 10.0% from the April 2020 base to July 2025, according to Census QuickFacts.

Which two Morgan County offices split the tax work?

Collecting and valuing sit in separate county offices, the Tax Commissioner and the Tax Assessor. The commissioner's county page lists these services:

Anyone doing business there needs a Georgia driver's license or ID showing a Morgan County address.

The Tax Assessor's office takes returns and homestead applications at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, Madison, GA 30650. The filing window for returns runs January 2 to April 1. Challenges start at that desk and can go on to the grand jury's appointees on the Board of Equalization. The county's Board of Commissioners sets the county budget and the county mill rate, and the Board of Education recommends a school rate that, with very few exceptions, the commissioners must levy.

The state limits its own levy to one fourth of a mill. Ask the commissioner's office whether the Madison city bill arrives separately from the county bill.

What property tax deadline does Morgan County print?

The commissioner's page gives November 15 as the official deadline, after which penalties and interest begin. State guidance names December 20 as the default and lets a county move to December 1 or November 15, which is the route Morgan took.

The same page says you may pay online through the county's online tax payment system. The state adds a 60 day grace period counted from the bill's postmark, so read the bill itself before assuming a day. The office also collects mobile home and timber tax, so ask the counter for those dates.

A buyer who closes after January 1 should confirm who carries that year's bill, because under state guidance the January 1 owner is the one liable.

Which homestead and senior exemptions does Morgan County list?

Morgan County's assessor page lists a ladder of exemptions that stack on the state basics. The county page spells out each one, and the assessors decide eligibility.

  • Standard homestead: as much as $2,000 comes off the assessed value, which is 40% of market value, for county, school and state operating levies.
  • Age 65 and up: a further $10,000 comes off the county and school operating portion, with no income test.
  • Madison residents over 65: another $10,000 off for city maintenance and operations tax.
  • Standard elderly: up to $4,000 off for owners 65 and older whose net income with a spouse stays at or below $10,000, with Social Security and some retirement income excluded.
  • Age 65 and older, state portion: the home and up to 10 acres are exempt from the state's levy in full.
  • Disabled veterans rated 100% service connected: a larger deduction that changes every year, with a DD214 and Veterans Affairs letter required.
  • Surviving spouses: up to $50,000 for an unremarried spouse of a service member who died in war or armed conflict, and a full exemption for the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or peace officer who died in the line of duty.

How do I file or keep a Morgan County homestead exemption?

Take the application to the Tax Assessor. Drop it off at any time, but April 1 ends the window for the current year, and the house must have been your residence on New Year's Day.

Once approved, the exemption rolls forward by itself. A new filing is needed only after a change of ownership, a move, a switch to a different kind of exemption, or when the exemption depends on income. If the Board of Assessors denies an application, the county must tell the applicant, and an appeal path is available. The page also points to conservation use and personal property information under the assessor menu for farmland owners and business owners.

How does a Morgan County value appeal work?

After the Board of Tax Assessors mails a notice that a value has changed, the owner gets 45 days to respond. The board looks again and sends back its decision. Still unhappy? The next stage is a Board of Equalization hearing, unless you chose arbitration when you first filed.

The county page allows three grounds: taxability, value, and how the value compares with similar properties. Complaints about the size of the bill do not count, and a late filing is barred. Superior court remains open after the administrative step. A new return filed during the January 2 to April 1 window can set a different value and protect your appeal rights if the board raises it again.

What else in Morgan County government affects a house sale?

Morgan County lists a Planning and Development department with zoning information, flood plain management information, a fee schedule and a comprehensive plan, plus a Roads and Bridges department that publishes a mowing schedule and a road resurfacing list. Check the zoning page and the flood plain page if the lot is near water.

Court Services covers Magistrate Court, Probate Court and Superior Court, which matters for an inherited house. The county's Solid Waste and Sanitation page includes recycling. QuickFacts counts 573 employer businesses with 6,763 jobs in 2023, and 87.1% of households have a broadband subscription. It also counts 963 veterans, of whom only those rated 100% service connected qualify for the disabled veteran exemption listed above.

What should a Morgan County seller settle on tax before closing?

Request a payoff figure from the commissioner's office, and have the closing attorney say who covers the November 15 bill when a sale closes earlier. The Department of Revenue says no refund exists for part of a year, so proration lives in the contract.

A Madison address adds a city bill, so ask which office collects it. Sellers over 65 should check that the exemptions above are on the account before the buyer's lender reviews the tax figures. Buyers who will occupy the home file their own application, again by April 1.

What is Morgan County's official property tax deadline?

November 15, according to the commissioner's page, after which penalties and interest build.

Who takes Morgan County homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor, at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, in Madison. Aim for April 1 if you want the savings this year.

Can I pay Morgan County property tax online?

Yes, through the online tax payment system that the commissioner's page links to.

Does Morgan County give seniors an extra exemption?

Yes. Residents 65 and older can take an additional $10,000 off assessed value for county and school maintenance and operations, with no income limit, and Madison residents can add the same amount for city tax.

How many days do I have to appeal in Morgan County?

Forty-five, counted from the notice of changed value. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first.

How did Murray County and its county seat come to be?

Murray County began in December 1832, when the Georgia General Assembly set aside the extreme northwestern corner of the state, land that had been part of Cherokee County, and named it for Thomas W. Murray, a former speaker of the Georgia House. Wikipedia notes that the original county was far larger and later shed territory to form Dade, Walker, Catoosa, Whitfield, Gordon and parts of other counties.

Spring Place served as the seat until the railroad skipped it. A Moravian mission opened there in 1801, and the Chief Vann House, built in 1805 for a Cherokee chief, still stands as a historic site. Cherokee removal in 1838 and 1839 opened the land to settlers. In 1906 the Louisville and Nashville line was built through the county's length, and Chatsworth grew up along it as timber and talc, discovered in the 1870s, moved out by rail. A countywide referendum in 1912 made Chatsworth the seat.

What natural landmarks mark Murray County?

Murray County covers 347 square miles in the mountains and valleys of northwest Georgia, and it is part of the Dalton metro area. Most of it drains to the Conasauga River, with the southeastern corner draining to the Coosawattee.

Fort Mountain State Park occupies 3,712 acres in the Cohutta Mountains, and the Chattahoochee National Forest covers much of the northeast, including the Cohutta Wilderness. Carters Lake, on the Coosawattee, spans 3,200 acres behind the largest earth-rock dam east of the Mississippi. Lake Conasauga, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1940 and sitting at 3,150 feet, is the highest lake in Georgia.

Chatsworth is the only city, and Eton is a town. Spring Place, Carters, Tennga, Cisco and Crandall are unincorporated communities. Fannin, Gilmer, Gordon and Whitfield counties border it, along with Polk and Bradley counties in Tennessee. Ask the commissioner's office which taxing districts cover your parcel, since an address inside Chatsworth or Eton may carry city tax.

What do Murray County's Census numbers show for housing and income?

An estimated 41,607 people lived in Murray County in July 2025, and owners valued their homes at a median of $180,700 across 2020 to 2024, per QuickFacts.

How do Murray County jobs and shops show up in Census data?

QuickFacts shows 430 employer establishments in Murray County for 2023 and 62.7% of people 16 and older in the civilian labor force. Retail sales were $281,579,000 in 2022, health care and social assistance receipts were $66,857,000, and accommodation and food service sales were $37,928,000.

The average commute takes 28.4 minutes. Foreign-born residents are 7.0% of the population, and 13.4% of those 5 and older speak another language at home. Of residents 25 and older, 78.9% finished high school. About 1,732 veterans live in the county.

Where do Murray County residents pay and ask about property tax?

The Murray County Tax Commissioner is at 101 S 3rd Ave in Chatsworth, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 336, Chatsworth, GA 30705. Phone payments go through 470-289-4681, according to the county's online payment page, which a third-party company runs for card and e-check payments.

The county's FAQ lists (706) 517-1400, extension 1, for the tax commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors. The Clerk of Superior Court sits in the courthouse at 114 N. Third Ave, across the street from the commissioner's office, and holds warranty deeds. Murray County also offers digital statements and automated reminders through the online payment site.

The assessors' office is separate from collections. As the county puts it, the assessors do not take part in collecting property tax.

Which date does Murray County use, and what does lateness cost?

Real estate and business personal property tax are normally due December 1 in Murray County, which is earlier than the statewide default. Manufactured homes come due May 1, while vehicle renewals track the owner's birthday.

  • Interest runs at 1% a month once December 1 passes.
  • Balances still open 90 days later add a 10% penalty.
  • A homesteaded parcel owing under $500 is spared that 90 day penalty.
  • Past 90 days, the clerk's office can record a FiFa that credit bureaus may pick up.
  • The commissioner may levy on the property, which the office describes as a last resort.

Your printed bill controls. Murray's FAQ adds that a former owner who still receives a bill or notice may forward it to the new owner.
