Which exemptions and special programs does Murray County offer?

Murray County homestead exemptions are filed in the assessor's office rather than the commissioner's, at (706) 517-1400, extension 2. Documentation of ownership is required, and elderly exemptions require income verification.

  • Regular homestead: ownership and residence on January 1, with no income test, and filing online is allowed.
  • Elderly exemptions: several versions with different ages, filed in the office or by mail because of income checks.
  • Homestead freeze: available after one year of homestead, applied for in the office.
  • Veterans: the taxpayer must be 100% disabled during war, with Department of Veterans Affairs documentation.
  • Low income: household income below $15,000 a year, with documents.
  • Special assessments: Conservation Use, Preferential Assessment and Forest Land Protection, applied for January 1 through April 1.

Manufactured home owners who also own the land can claim homestead, get a free decal between January 1 and May 1, and pay the home's tax with the land tax. Other manufactured homes, such as rentals, buy a decal.

How do I appeal a Murray County property value?

Mail or deliver a letter to the assessors inside 45 days of the Notice of Property Value Change. The county suggests certified mail or hand delivery, and the letter should explain as fully as possible why the value looks wrong.

The Board of Assessors studies it and replies in writing. The tax commissioner's FAQ describes the challenge as going to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator within 45 days of the notice, with superior court available afterward by written notice to the assessors. A state-certified five-member board updates county values every year at 40% of market value, and notices and bills follow the owner of record on January 1.

What happens to Murray County tax when I sell?

Murray's assessor lists January 1 as the date of liability for ownership, so a seller who closes later in the year still answers for the full bill. No partial-year refund exists, the Department of Revenue says, so the contract decides how the bill is split.

Ask the tax commissioner at extension 1 for the balance on your parcel and any FiFa before closing. If the bill goes to a mortgage escrow account, ask your lender whether it has paid, because the assessor's office says collection questions belong to the tax commissioner. Need a warranty deed copy? The Clerk of Superior Court is across the street.

When are Murray County real estate taxes due?

Normally December 1, after which interest builds at 1% a month. Manufactured homes pay by May 1.

Which phone line serves Murray County property tax?

The county's FAQ gives (706) 517-1400, with extension 1 for the commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors.

Is there a penalty for paying Murray County tax late?

Yes. Interest of 1% accrues monthly after December 1, and 90 days later a 10% penalty arrives, except on homesteaded parcels owing under $500.

Can I file a Murray County homestead exemption online?

Yes for the regular one. Elderly exemptions need income proof, so those go in person or by mail.

What is the cutoff to appeal a Murray County assessment?

Within 45 days of the notice date, by letter to the assessors. The county suggests certified mail or hand delivery.

Why does Muscogee County share one government with Columbus?

The two merged at the start of 1971, so Columbus is at once the lone city and the seat of Muscogee County, per Wikipedia. The county hugs the Alabama border, where the Chattahoochee marks the boundary, and the legislature drew its lines on June 9, 1826 before giving it a name that December 14. Bibb City, a mill company town, dissolved its charter in December 2000, two years after the mill shut down for good.

Fort Benning occupies roughly a quarter of the land and spills over into Chattahoochee County. Total area comes to 221 square miles, with the fall line running through: hillier ground in the north, flatter ground to the south. The newer Fall Line Freeway follows JR Allen Parkway across the north end. Russell and Lee counties lie over the river in Alabama, while on the Georgia side the neighbors are Harris, Talbot and Chattahoochee.

In its first years the county reached east to the Flint River. Harris (1827) and Chattahoochee (1854) were later carved out of that territory.

How many people live in Muscogee County, and what do homes cost?

The July 2025 estimate puts Muscogee County at 202,171 people, below the 206,922 counted in 2020. Owners live in 50.8% of homes, which leaves about half of the housing to renters.

The headcount slid 2.3% from the 2020 base. QuickFacts reports 81,415 households, 20,438 veterans and a drive to work that averages 20.9 minutes. The 2020 census found 90,348 housing units, 8.8% of them empty, and 96.2% of residents in urban territory. The median resident was 35.8 years old, 24.1% were under 18 and 14.8% were 65 or older. Of 82,360 households, 31.9% were one person living alone, 11.5% were someone 65 or older living alone, and 31.7% had children under 18 at home.

Which Muscogee County office handles what?

Three separate bodies touch a Muscogee County bill: one mails and collects it, one sets the value and rules on exemptions, and one hears disputes.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills, takes payments, tracks delinquent accounts and posts tax sale lists on columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner
  • Board of Tax Assessors: fair market value, exemption approvals and the yearly assessment notice
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury, it rules on disputes over value, a denied homestead, freeport and taxability

The assessors sit on Wednesday mornings at 9:00 in the City Services Building, 3111 Citizens Way, according to the assessor's page. Call the Tax Commissioner for counter hours and a written payoff figure before you list the house. The commissioner's home page also links to a parcel search, homestead and forms pages, a delinquent tax section and the tax sale registration class.

What is the Muscogee County property tax calendar?

Bills for real and personal property reach owners in late summer, and payment is due in two steps: 40% or the full amount in October, then the balance of 60% in December. The county's Important Dates page sets out the full year.

  • April 1: mobile home bills come due, the current-year homestead window closes, and returns on business equipment, aircraft and watercraft are due at the assessor
  • May: assessment notices go out, and the appeal period begins
  • July: millage rates are set after advertised public input
  • August: bills are mailed
  • October: first payment, 40% or everything
  • December: the remaining 60%

The county's 2026 billing update, on its tax commissioner site, shows bills mailed September 1 and a final balance due December 1, payable online with the parcel number. Pages differ on month details, so follow the dates printed on your bill.

How can a Muscogee County owner challenge an assessment?

Send a written appeal within 45 days after the date printed on the assessment notice. Because the notices go out in May, the clock runs through early summer, and a homestead application filed in that stretch can stand in for an appeal.

Name your ground in the letter, such as value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption, and keep a copy. The Board of Equalization decides the matter. Ask the assessors whether another route applies to your parcel type.

Overpayment has its own path. State guidance on the Department of Revenue county facts page lets a taxpayer request a refund in writing for tax assessed in error, with the claim starting inside three years of payment.

Which homestead exemptions does Muscogee County list?

The basic exemption knocks $2,000 off the state portion and $13,500 off the local assessed value for an owner who lives in the house, according to the assessor's exemption page. It freezes the assessment but skips the slice of millage used to retire bonds.

  • Elderly school-tax exemption: owner 62 or older, net income at or under $10,000 the prior year, school tax only
  • Elderly general exemption: owner 65 or older with the same $10,000 test, up to $4,000 off the state portion and $21,500 off local value
  • Floating exemption: 62 or older, household gross income $30,000 or less, covers state and county tax but not schools
  • Disabled veterans: up to $117,014 off both the state portion and the local assessed value, with Veterans Administration proof

The page cautions that the floating exemption replaces any other state and county exemption and may raise the first year's tax, so ask the assessors before choosing it. A buyer should confirm whether a new application is needed after closing.

Who covers a Muscogee County tax bill when the house sells?

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's whole bill in the eyes of the law. The Tax Commissioner does not divide it between buyer and seller; the closing paperwork does that.

If nobody pays, a lien goes under the January 1 owner's name. A seller can shift it to the buyer by delivering evidence within 90 days of the due date: a recorded deed in the buyer's name and wording in the closing papers that hands the tax to the buyer. The buying and selling page explains the process.

On liens, the delinquent tax page says the office never sells tax liens or lien certificates, and a parcel that finds no bidder at a tax sale rejoins the queue for later sales. Staff cannot offer legal advice, so see an attorney if a lien is already recorded.

More questions about Muscogee County, GA Property Tax Guide

If I close in the middle of a year, who is billed for that year in Muscogee County?

The owner on January 1 is liable for the full year. The county leaves the buyer and seller split to the closing documents, and a lien can move to the buyer if the proof described above arrives within 90 days of the due date.

Where do I find a Muscogee County parcel record or balance?

Use the search and pay links on columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner and enter the parcel number printed on your bill. Assessor records are on the city-county public access site.

Does a homestead filing replace an appeal in Muscogee County?

Yes, during the 45-day period after the assessment notice a homestead application can be made in place of an appeal. For the current year, the general homestead cutoff is April 1.

Will the Muscogee County Tax Commissioner sell my lien to an investor?

No. The office states it does not sell tax liens or lien certificates. An unsold property returns to the rotation for future tax sales.

Which public schools cover Muscogee County addresses?

Muscogee County School District serves everything except Fort Benning for kindergarten through grade 12. Fort Benning children are zoned to Department of Defense Education Activity schools for grades K-8, then attend county high schools.

Where does Newton County fit in the Atlanta region?

East of Atlanta, Newton County counts Covington as both seat and biggest city. Georgia's General Assembly set it up on December 24, 1821, and the name honors a sergeant who fought under Gen. Francis Marion in the Revolutionary War, per Wikipedia. Terrain is Piedmont, and most of the county drains toward the Upper Ocmulgee River; a sliver in the east runs to the Upper Oconee.

Covington shares the map with four more cities: Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle. Newborn is a town, and Starrsville is unincorporated. Interstate 20 and US 278 cut through, joined by state routes 11, 20, 36, 81, 138, 142, 162 and 212. The adjoining counties are Walton, Morgan, Jasper, Butts, Henry and Rockdale.

Hollywood found the courthouse square. Crews shot the first five Dukes of Hazzard episodes around Covington in late 1978, and In the Heat of the Night filmed there from 1988 to 1995. Schools come mostly from the Newton County School System, with some Social Circle addresses served by that city's own district. The county also claims to be where Georgia 4-H began: canning and corn clubs started in 1904 took the 4-H name in 1906.

How quickly has Newton County grown, and what do homes cost?

Newton County had 41,808 residents in 1990 and 112,483 at the 2020 count; the July 2025 estimate stands at 125,583. The 2000 count was 62,001 and the 2010 count 99,958, so the sharpest jump came in the 2000s.

Newton County by the numbers (Census QuickFacts, 2020-2024 unless noted)

Where do I pay or ask questions about Newton County property tax?

Pay in person at the Tax Commissioner's Admin Building at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101 in Covington, or to the Westside office at 3612 Salem Rd. Each opens at 8:00 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, and 770-784-2020 reaches both, according to the office's locations page.

  • Tax Assessors, 770-784-2030: returns, exemptions, appeals and value questions
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and balances; an elected office, separate from the assessors and the county commission
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the millage rates
  • Deed room at the Newton County Courthouse: copies of recorded deeds

Self-service kiosks stand inside Kroger on Highway 20 South and on Highway 278 NE. The commissioner's home page also publishes a delinquent tax list, refreshed every quarter, and a page on excess funds. A written balance request can be mailed to the Admin Building.

What is the Newton County tax due date, and what happens if it is missed?

Newton County bills come due each November 15, an earlier date than the old December 20 that applied before the 2026 tax year. Commissioners adopted the change in 2025, as the office's FAQ explains.

That 2026 deadline landed on a Sunday, so the office gave until Monday, November 16 with no interest. Real estate and personal property statements are mailed by September 15, while non-homesteaded mobile homes get a statement by February 1 and pay by April 1.

  • Late interest is figured monthly at prime plus 3% a year, and the page listed .0875% per month
  • After 120 days a penalty of 5% of the original tax is added, and it repeats every 120 days up to a combined 20%
  • Mail counts only with a U.S. Postal Service postmark; meter postmarks are rejected
  • The office takes partial payments, but charges keep building on the unpaid remainder

Cards add 2.35% (Visa, MasterCard, Discover) or 3% (American Express), each with a $1.50 floor. An online eCheck costs a flat $1.50. Subdivisions that opted in to pay for street lights see a separate street light fee on the statement, and the revenue the bill raises goes to county government, schools, roads and bridges, courts and the jail, fire protection, public health, parks and libraries.

How does the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant show up on a Newton County bill?

The credit prints on its own line marked HTRG Credit and comes off the current taxes due before the total. For 2026, eligible homesteaded properties get an $18,000 cut in assessed value for purposes of the credit, and the dollar result varies by tax district.

Owners file nothing extra with the Tax Commissioner. The credit rides on an existing homestead exemption, and it sits alongside that exemption rather than replacing it. The office describes it as good for the 2026 tax year alone.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, call the lender: the tax office has no say over escrow amounts, and a smaller bill may leave the mortgage payment unchanged.

Which Newton County homestead exemptions exist, and how do appeals work?

Apply by April 1, or inside the 45-day window that follows assessment notices. One filing lasts until ownership or your primary residence changes, and exemptions never transfer to a buyer.

  • Standard: $4,000 off taxable value on county and school levies, one homestead per owner
  • Age 62: $20,000 off county and school levies, with a $15,000 cap on net earned income
  • Age 65: $30,000 off county levies and $50,000 off Newton Schools, with a $25,000 earned income cap
  • Disabled veteran: up to $126,526 off the 40% taxable value, backed by a Veterans Administration letter

The two senior exemptions also limit household social security and retirement income to $99,648, per the homestead page. To contest a value, write to the Board of Assessors inside 45 days of the notice and say which appeal route you pick; Board of Equalization is one option.

What should a Newton County seller know about liens before closing?

A FiFa is the lien Newton County records for unpaid tax, entered on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. A 30-day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before one is filed.

Once recorded, a FiFa lasts seven years and can be renewed again and again. Because the filing is public, credit bureaus can see it; settling the tax, fees, penalties and interest clears it. The office does not sell liens over the counter and posts a list when a tax sale is set.

Ask for a written balance dated near closing, then have the closing agent settle it out of proceeds. Because statements go to the owner, not to the lender, pass your bill along if a servicer needs it.

More questions about Newton County, GA Property Tax Guide

When is Newton County property tax due each year?

On November 15, a date that replaced December 20 beginning with the 2026 tax year. In 2026 the no-interest window ran through Monday, November 16 because November 15 was a Sunday.

What is the appeal deadline for a Newton County valuation?

Forty-five days, counted from the assessment notice date. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors, pick your method, and rest it on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

Will my Newton County homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. Exemptions do not move with the house, a point the office makes plainly. The buyer files a new application, due April 1 or during the 45-day appeal window.

What are the Newton County tax office hours and addresses?

The Admin Building is at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, and the Westside office is at 3612 Salem Rd, both in Covington. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the phone is 770-784-2020.

Which cities and towns sit inside Newton County?

Covington is the seat, joined by Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn. A city address may also carry a city levy, so read the whole bill.

Why was Oconee County split off from Clarke County?

Residents of southwestern Clarke County wanted their own government after the Clarke seat moved from Watkinsville to Athens in 1872, and the General Assembly answered in 1875 by creating Oconee County, per Wikipedia. Watkinsville became the new seat. The name comes from a Muskogean people of central Georgia and from the river on part of the eastern border.

The county is compact: 186 square miles, 184 of them dry land, all inside the Upper Oconee River sub-basin and all in the Piedmont. Clarke lies north, Oglethorpe east, Greene southeast, Morgan south, and Walton and Barrow to the west. A piece of the Oconee National Forest falls within its lines.

Four towns appear on the local map: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville. Elder, Farmington and Salem are unincorporated. Progressive Farmer magazine ranked Oconee the third-best rural county to live in during 2006. Outside Watkinsville, the sheriff's office handles policing, while the town runs its own police department, and the courts belong to the Western Circuit of the 10th Judicial District.

How big has Oconee County grown, and what does a home cost there?

The county went from 32,808 people in 2010 to 41,799 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate reads 44,893. Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $461,600 for 2020-2024, and 81.3% of homes are lived in by their owners.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,221, and the drive to work averages 24.7 minutes. Density is 226.7 people per square mile across 184.34 square miles of land. At the 2020 census, 14,360 households lived in 14,998 housing units, 4.3% of them vacant, and 43.2% of those households had children under 18. Median age was 39.7, and 54.1% of residents lived in rural territory. QuickFacts also lists 2,128 veterans, 94.5% of households with broadband and a 96.4% high school graduation rate among adults 25 and over.

How is Oconee County governed, and what is daily life like?

Four commissioners and a separately elected chairman, all picked countywide for staggered four-year terms, hold the budget, taxing and ordinance powers. The chairman is the chief executive and appoints staff with the commissioners' input.

The weekly Oconee Enterprise covers local news, and a radio facility on Tower Place in the northeast corner broadcasts four stations. Walkability is limited, and a multi-use trail network has been under discussion since 2017, so most errands mean a drive.

Which schools and colleges serve Oconee County?

Public school students attend one of eleven district buildings: six elementary, three middle and two high schools, enrolling about 5,615 children with 361 full-time teachers. Three private schools sit inside the county line as well.

The University of North Georgia keeps a satellite campus near Watkinsville, and the College of Athens, a private Christian college, opened there in 2012. Oconee County belongs to the Athens-Clarke County metropolitan area, and Clarke County adjoins it on the north.

School zoning is a district decision, so ask the district which school an address feeds before you describe it to buyers.

Who bills and who values property in Oconee County?

A bill and a valuation come from two different desks here. The Tax Commissioner is at 7635 Macon Highway in Watkinsville, mails go to Suite 300, and the doors open at 8:00 and shut at 4:30, Monday through Friday. Phone (706) 769-3917 or text (706) 765-7790, according to the tax office FAQ.

  • Courthouse record center, 23 North Main Street, (706) 769-3940: copies of warranty deeds

The appraisal staff say nearly 70% of a tax bill funds schools and the rest funds county government. They also note that they handle value only; the tax amount follows from the millage the two boards set.

What are the Oconee County due date and late charges?

Real estate and business personal property tax normally falls due November 15 in Oconee County, and mobile home tax on April 1.

  • Interest: bank prime rate plus 3 points a year, divided by 12 and applied monthly, with the state announcing the year's rate on or after January 1
  • Penalty: 5% of principal every 120 days past due, topping out at 20%
  • Enforcement: an unpaid account lets the Tax Commissioner levy on the property
  • Payment plans: set up by phone once bills are mailed, with interest and penalties still running until the balance is paid

Interest moves every month, so an old figure may fall short by closing day; ask for the payoff in writing before the sale.

How does an Oconee County appeal or homestead filing work?

Look in the upper right corner of your assessment notice for the phrase last date to file a written appeal. That date sits 45 days past the notice date, and a letter or the county's appeal form will do, but an emailed or online filing will not.

Owners may go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After that ruling, a written notice sent to the assessors carries the case to superior court. Remember that appraisal staff rule on value only, never on the size of the bill. They calculate real estate, marine, aircraft and business personal property values in a computer-assisted mass appraisal system, and four certification levels govern the appraisers.

Homestead rests on owning and living in the house on January 1, with the application in hand before April 1. Valuation is frozen as of January 1, so a renovation or demolition during the year counts from the next January 1. Exemption amounts are available at (706) 769-3921.

What should an Oconee County seller sort out before closing?

January 1 fixes both ownership and condition, which means a house sold later in the year still has a tax bill to divide at closing. Settle that split in the contract.

  • Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and hand a copy to the closing agent
  • Pull a copy of the warranty deed at the courthouse when the legal description is needed
  • Check whether the parcel is in unincorporated Oconee County or inside Watkinsville, Bishop, Bogart or North High Shoals, since a town may bill its own tax
  • Wrap up any open appeal before closing so a pending value cannot stall a refund

State refund claims for tax assessed in error have a three-year clock from payment, per the Department of Revenue's county tax facts page.

More questions about Oconee County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which date does Oconee County use as the normal property tax due date?

Real estate and business personal property are due November 15 and mobile homes April 1. Charges begin to accrue after the date.

What is the last day to appeal an Oconee County value?

It is printed on the notice itself, 45 days after the notice date. The appraisal office will not accept an appeal filed electronically.

Which boards set the millage rate in Oconee County?

Two bodies: the Board of Commissioners for county government and the Board of Education for schools. A mill means a dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, with assessed value set at 40% of market value.

How much does Oconee County charge for late property tax?

Monthly interest at prime plus 3% a year, and then a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20% of principal.

Which towns are in Oconee County?

Four: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville, the seat. Elder, Farmington and Salem have no town government.

What is Oglethorpe County like to live in and sell in?

Lexington is the seat of Oglethorpe County, a rural stretch of northeast Georgia that Wikipedia describes as the biggest county in that corner of the state. Lawmakers created it on December 19, 1793, honoring the colony's founder, Gen. James Oglethorpe. Its land came from a tract the Creek and Cherokee gave up to the Colony of Georgia in the treaty of 1773, per Wikipedia.

The county measures 442 square miles, 439 of them land. Most runoff reaches the Broad River on its way to the Savannah, and a thin western strip near Woodville, Crawford and Winterville sends its water to the Upper Oconee. Elbert, Wilkes, Taliaferro, Greene, Oconee, Clarke and Madison counties all touch its edges.

Arnoldsville, Crawford and Lexington are the cities, and Maxeys is a town. Philomath, Point Peter, Sandy Cross, Stephens and Vesta are unincorporated. Visitors come for whitewater rafting on the Broad and South Fork Broad rivers, hunting for deer, turkey and rabbit, an ATV and motorbike park, and antique shopping in historic Lexington, with slices of the Oconee National Forest and Watson Mill Bridge State Park inside the line. Statistically, the county sits in the Athens-Clarke area.

How many people and homes does Oglethorpe County have?

Roughly 16,415 people share Oglethorpe County's 439 land square miles, a density of 33.8 per square mile by the 2020 count. Owners occupy 83.8% of the homes.

One district, Oglethorpe County School District, runs every public school.

What does the Oglethorpe County economy and housing market look like?

Business here is small: QuickFacts lists 182 employer establishments with 1,104 jobs for 2023, set against 1,453 businesses with no employees. The labor force takes in 60.4% of people 16 and up, and a bachelor's degree is held by 25.3% of adults.

A typical household has 2.84 people, and 93.1% of residents were in the same house a year earlier. The county has 1,138 veterans, and 12.2% of residents live below the poverty line. Builders pulled 80 permits in 2025.

Who handles Oglethorpe County tax questions?

  • Board of Equalization: Grand Jury appointees who rule on challenges to assessor values
  • County commissioners and school board: each adopts its own mill rate
  • Deed room, Oglethorpe County Courthouse: copies of warranty deeds

The same office registers motor vehicles as the state's agent. It has no say over value or millage, so a complaint about either belongs with the assessors or the boards that set rates.

When is Oglethorpe County tax due, and what do late payers owe?

The county's tax FAQ sets December 20 as the usual deadline for land, buildings and business personal property. Manufactured homes run on an April 1 cycle, and vehicles follow the owner's birth month.

  • Interest accrues at 1% per month once December 20 passes
  • A 10% penalty applies to tax still open after 90 days; a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 is exempt from it
  • After 90 days a FiFa lien may be filed with the Superior Court clerk
  • A mobile home unpaid after April 1 owes a 10% filing penalty plus 1% monthly, and the home can be auctioned

The bill is mailed to the owner of the house, never to the lender, and an owner with escrow should forward it to the servicer. A recorded lien is an open record, the FAQ adds, and credit bureaus may use it.

Does Oglethorpe County really assess city property at 100%?

That is what the county tax FAQ states: 40% of fair market value at the county level and 100% at the city level. Before assuming a number, ask the tax office or the city clerk which base and which levies cover your parcel.

The tax site walks through the arithmetic: market value as of January 1, then 40% of it, then exemptions off the top, then millage on what remains.

The state revenue commissioner reviews county digests so assessments stay even between counties, and the state's own ad valorem levy cannot exceed one quarter of a mill.

How do I challenge a value or claim homestead in Oglethorpe County?

A written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors, with the 45-day clock starting on the date of the assessment notice, and it has to state your chosen appeal method. Value is the common ground, and taxability, uniformity and a refused exemption also qualify.

Manufactured homes run on separate deadlines. An owner has 45 days after the bill is mailed to propose another value, and 21 days after the resulting notice to take the dispute to the Board of Equalization. The assessors' office is at (706) 743-5166.

  • Applications are accepted all year, yet one that arrives after April 1 only starts the next tax year

Total area is 442 square miles with 439 of them land, and the 2020 count gave 33.8 people per square mile. Wikipedia names it the largest county in Northeast Georgia.

Which river carries most of the water out of Oglethorpe County?

The Broad River. Most of the county sits in the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin, with a narrow western strip draining to the Upper Oconee and a small southern part to the Little River.

When was Oglethorpe County founded, and for whom is it named?

It was founded on December 19, 1793 and is named for Georgia's founder, Gen. James Oglethorpe. The land was part of a tract the Creek and Cherokee surrendered to the Colony of Georgia in 1773.

What is the penalty for late tax in Oglethorpe County?

Interest runs 1% a month after December 20, and a 10% penalty follows if the tax is still open 90 days later. A homesteaded bill under $500 avoids the penalty.

Ask the Clerk of Superior Court's deed room at the Oglethorpe County Courthouse, which holds the recorded copies.

What should a seller know about Paulding County, Georgia?

Paulding is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta. Dallas is the county seat, and the government offices sit together on Constitution Boulevard. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 190,996 people, a 13.3 percent gain on the 168,630 in its 2020 base. That is the largest population of the four Georgia counties in this comparison, packed into 312.35 square miles of land.

The housing numbers explain why sales here move at a different pace than in rural south Georgia. Half of owner-occupied Paulding homes are worth more than $326,300 (a 2020 to 2024 estimate), and 80.8 percent of households own where they live. Permits issued in 2025 totaled 1,326, and the median gross rent was $1,772 a month. A seller in the newer subdivisions competes with new construction, which sets buyer expectations for finishes and age of systems. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, a sign that many residents commute toward Atlanta.

For a seller, the tax side is simple in outline. Value is fixed on January 1, taxed at 40 percent of that figure, and the commissioner multiplies by the millage. The commissioner's general information page explains the sequence. What follows concentrates on points that come up when a Paulding County house is sold.

Which Paulding County offices handle property tax?

The assessors and the tax commissioner divide the job between them, and deeds sit with a third office. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Where to reach Paulding's tax commissioner and assessors, from the county's own pages
OfficeLocationPhoneHours listed
Tax Commissioner240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3006, Dallas, GA 30132(770) 443-7581Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Board of Assessors240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3082, Dallas, GA 30132770-443-7606Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The commissioner's page warns that the phone line may be cut off early so the office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email at the address printed on the county's homestead page, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

What is the Paulding County property tax deadline, and what does missing it cost?

On the commissioner's general information page, the deadline is November 15 every year. The site's FAQ still shows December 4 for tax year 2024, which differs from the general page, so let the bill itself guide your payoff and closing plans.

The general information page spells out what happens after the deadline:

  • Interest posts to the account on the 16th of every month, calculated as prime plus 3 percent spread over twelve months.
  • A FIFA, which is the county's lien filing, is recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court's office thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and credit bureaus can read it there.
  • Penalties of 5 percent land at the 120-day mark and recur on that cycle until they reach 20 percent in total.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. Mobile home bills normally mail near January 2, fall due April 1 and pick up a 10 percent penalty the next day.

How do I appeal a Paulding County assessment?

Paulding gives owners six and a half weeks, measured from the mailing of the notice. The county says a late filing cannot be accepted, so mark the envelope date when the notice arrives. Grounds are limited to whether the parcel is taxable, what it is worth and whether that value is fair next to similar homes. Anger about the millage or the total on the bill will not carry an appeal.

The path through the system runs in a fixed order:

  • Send the appeal to the Board of Assessors first, which re-checks its number and replies with a decision.
  • No deal at that stage means a hearing before the Board of Equalization.
  • Arbitration is the alternative to that board, and the assessors' staff can walk you through it.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form, a 2026 guide to reading the notice, and a list of 2025 sales used for comparison. Someone serving abroad can have a relative or friend file for them, with 90 days instead of 45. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

What homestead exemptions can a Paulding County owner claim?

A Paulding County homeowner must apply with the Board of Assessors, because exemptions are never granted automatically. Expect to show residency and citizenship papers, for example a Georgia license or ID card, and your name has to be on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

The county's homestead page names several categories beyond the standard exemption:

  • Lower school tax for owners aged 65 or more.
  • Relief for owners with a total and permanent disability.
  • A break for veterans rated fully disabled from service.
  • A full homestead break for the unmarried survivor of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. The assessors say applications must arrive by April 1, while the homestead page ties the current-year deadline to the appeal deadline on that year's assessment notice, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Farmland and timber programs come with a covenant that runs at least 10 years, so a seller of acreage should read the agreement before listing.

What happens to Paulding County property tax when a house sells?

Your purchase agreement spells out how the year's bill is shared with the buyer, and the settlement statement shows the result.

Request a balance figure from the commissioner before the sign goes up, including any interest, penalty or lien recorded against the parcel. A balance still open comes out of your proceeds, which hands the buyer a parcel with nothing owing. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. The courthouse deed room can supply a copy of your recorded deed, which the buyer's title work will want.

What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?

The commissioner's general information page says November 15 each year. The site's FAQ still names a December date for the 2024 tax year, so go by the bill in your hands.

Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?

Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?

Forty-five days from the notice mailing. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

Does Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?

Yes. After approval it carries over from year to year until the owner moves, the title changes or a different exemption is sought. A buyer starts a new application after closing.

What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?

Interest is charged monthly, and a penalty layer stacks on after four months. Its ceiling is one fifth of the tax, so a long-ignored Dallas-area bill grows quickly.

What is Peach County, Georgia, like for someone selling a house?

Peach County is a small central Georgia county with Fort Valley as its seat and Byron as the second city. Its own website describes a place about 90 minutes south of Atlanta where big industry, small business and agriculture meet. Peach counted 29,877 people in the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, 6.7 percent more than its 2020 base. The land area is 150.28 square miles, which gave 186.2 people per square mile in 2020.

Homes here cost far less than in the Atlanta suburbs. Peach's median owner-occupied value is $207,800 (2020 to 2024), well under the Paulding and Pickens figures. Owner-occupancy of 69.6 percent is the lowest among the four counties compared, which makes rental houses a real part of the local market. Median gross rent was $940 and the median household income was $71,293. Builders pulled just 139 permits in 2025. Seniors make up 18.8 percent of the population, and workers spend a mean of 24.5 minutes getting to work, against 39.6 in Paulding County.

That mix of renters, older owners and modest values shapes the tax questions sellers ask. Many Peach County sellers have inherited a house, rented one out, or fallen behind on a bill. Poverty runs at 17.7 percent, and total employment was 7,571 in 2023, up 3.0 percent from the year before, so household budgets here can be tight. The tax offices described below can give a payoff figure in any of those situations.

Where do I go for Peach County property tax questions?

The Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors values property, takes exemption applications and handles appeals. Peach County's own assessor pages say the commissioner has no role in appraisal or in setting the millage rate, and that the county commissioners only appoint and fund the assessors.

Peach County tax contacts listed on the county websites
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Commissioner902 Campus Drive, Fort Valley, GA 31030 (mail: PO Box 931)478-825-3161
Board of Tax Assessors902 Campus Drive, Fort Valley, GA 31030478-825-5924

The commissioner's office keeps Monday to Friday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Its site covers county tax only. The city tax page lists separate district codes for Byron, Fort Valley, Perry and Warner Robins, a reminder that parts of this county's tax base fall inside several city limits. If your house is inside one of those cities, ask that city's finance office about its separate bill.

When is Peach County property tax due?

December 20 is the customary deadline for real estate and business personal property, says the commissioner's FAQ. Mobile homes run on an April 1 schedule, and vehicle tax follows the primary owner's birthday. Dates can shift, so go by the one on your bill.

Late charges on real estate follow a simple schedule:

  • One percent interest accrues for each month the bill stays open.
  • Taxes still open 90 days after the deadline carry a one-time 10 percent penalty.
  • Owners with a homestead and a bill under $500 are exempt from that penalty.
  • An unpaid bill gives the commissioner both the authority and the responsibility to levy on the property.

The commissioner's home page has announced delinquent tax sales at the Peach County Courthouse at 205 W Church Street in Fort Valley, including one scheduled for March 3, 2026 at 10 a.m. The office posts a tax sale list for download. A seller who is behind should phone the Fort Valley office for a written balance before choosing a listing date.

How does a Peach County assessment appeal work?

A new value you dispute can be challenged for 45 days after the notice date. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator takes the case. An owner who loses can go on to Superior Court by giving the assessors a written notice. The assessors' page cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 as the authority for the appeal.

Some facts about how Peach County measures value:

  • Assessed value runs at 40 percent of market value unless a statute sets another ratio (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Both the notice and the bill print the market value next to the assessed value.
  • The county's definition of market value is a price between an informed buyer and a willing seller who deal at arm's length.
  • Peach County says its assessors review property annually and may enter a parcel during business hours, with identification, to check data after a permit, a sale or an appeal.

Think about how a recent contract price compares with the notice before you contest a value on a house you plan to sell.

Which homestead exemptions apply in Peach County?

For the standard exemption, you must be living in the house as owner on January 1. Peach lists it as $2,000 subtracted from assessed value for state, county and school levies. Applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. The county describes a filing period running from April 2 of the prior year to April 1 of the year the benefit is wanted.

The county's exemption page lists these programs:

  • A $4,000 reduction at age 65, for a household whose income the year before was $10,000 or less. Retirement, pension and disability payments are left out of that figure up to the Social Security cap.
  • Owners at 62 can add a school-tax reduction capped at $10,000 of assessed value, using the same $10,000 income ceiling.
  • A floating, inflation-proof option for households with income up to $30,000 and an owner of 62 or more. The county itself cautions that it may increase what you pay.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, which the page lists at $109,986 for the 2023 tax year.

Bring proof of age, a warranty deed and income statements as the facts require. Refinancing, or any other deed change, requires a new application. A buyer files separately for the new home. Freeport exemptions for manufacturing and warehouse inventory are filed with the assessors by April 1.

How should a seller handle Peach County property tax at closing?

Call 478-825-3161 and ask what the parcel owes, including this year's tax, interest and anything left from earlier years. How the year's tax is split comes from your sale contract, and the settlement statement shows it.

If the buyer pays off a bill that includes city tax, remember that Fort Valley and Byron levy their own. Ask the commissioner whether the parcel is billed through the county alone or has a city component. Mobile homes are billed separately and are due April 1, so a manufactured home on the lot may carry its own balance.

The buyer needs to file a new homestead application after closing. After the sale, tell the assessors your exemption has ended. Peach asks owners to report any loss of eligibility.

More questions about Peach County, GA Property Tax Guide

When are Peach County real estate taxes due?

According to the FAQ, December 20 is the standard due date for real estate. Mobile homes are due April 1, so confirm the exact date on your bill.

What is the late penalty in Peach County?

Interest of 1 percent monthly begins once the date passes, with a single 10 percent penalty at the 90-day point. A homesteaded home owing less than $500 escapes that penalty.

How do I appeal a Peach County property value?

Counting starts on the notice date and stops at day 45. The hearing body is the Board of Equalization, or an arbitrator if chosen, with Superior Court above.

Who takes homestead applications in Peach County?

Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office in Fort Valley, with a warranty deed and any proof the exemption requires. The deadline to receive the benefit for the same year is April 1.

Does Peach County tax mobile homes?

Yes. Peach classes a mobile home as personal property, and the permit for its location waits on full payment of the April 1 bill.

What makes Pickens County, Georgia, different for a home seller?

Pickens County sits in the north Georgia mountains with Jasper as its seat, and it skews older and pricier than its neighbors in this comparison. Pickens County grew to an estimated 37,167 residents by mid-2025, and seniors are 26.8 percent of residents. The county covers 232.06 square miles of land at 143.1 people per square mile.

Pickens has the priciest typical home of the four counties compared, at $332,700, and 81.2 percent of its housing is lived in by the owner. Median gross rent was $1,136. Builders took out 277 permits in 2025. Health care and social assistance receipts reached $222,994 thousand in 2022, second only to Paulding among the four counties. Retail sales per capita came to $20,835.

A senior-heavy owner base matters for tax questions, because Pickens County has local exemptions that older owners may already hold. A buyer who loses those exemptions at closing may see a different bill than the seller paid, and sellers who understand that can explain it before the contract is signed.

Who bills and who values property in Pickens County?

The Pickens County Tax Commissioner bills, collects and distributes, and also processes motor vehicle registration. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property, approves exemptions and reviews appeals. Grand jurors appoint the Board of Equalization that hears the administrative appeal.

Pickens County tax contacts, per the commissioner's website
ItemDetail
Tax Commissioner address1266 E. Church Street, Jasper, GA 30143
Tax Commissioner phone(706) 253-8882
Tax Assessor phone(706) 253-8700
Commissioner office hoursMonday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The commissioner's news box also mentions a drop box that is open around the clock in front of the Administration Building. Using a card costs a 2.60 percent convenience fee at the counter, on the web or by phone. An e-check adds a flat $3.00. Partial payments are welcome, though interest keeps running on whatever stays unpaid. The same site lets owners ask online for a mailing address change, and it keeps forms, an excess funds page and a tax sale page for bidder registration.

What are the Pickens County tax deadlines and late costs?

November 15 is the commissioner's date for real estate and business personal property. Manufactured homes get a January bill and an April 1 deadline. A US Postal Service postmark counts as timely, but a metered postmark does not.

The FAQ page describes the consequences of paying late:

  • Interest of 0.8750 percent was added for 2025 bills, and from January 2026 the rate is prime plus 3 percent divided across 12 months.
  • The commissioner's news box says a 5 percent penalty comes at day 120, recurs every 120 days and stops at 20 percent.
  • Taxes more than 90 days late can lead to a recorded FIFA lien at the courthouse.
  • The office can levy on the property but calls that a last resort.

Mail goes to the homeowner only, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account has to pass the bill along. If you sell near the due date, ask whether the lender already paid.

How do I appeal a Pickens County assessment?

Day 45 after the notice date is the last day. The Board of Tax Assessors looks again at its value first and responds with a decision. Where the board holds firm, the Board of Equalization takes the appeal up at a hearing. Superior Court is the final stop.

Some details from the commissioner's general information page:

  • You can appeal on taxability, value, uniformity compared with similar property, or the denial of an exemption.
  • You can request arbitration at the time of filing instead of going to the Board of Equalization.
  • Filing a return happens at the assessors' office in the first three months. Filing one that declares your own value can preserve appeal rights if the board later changes the number.
  • Taxable value begins at 40 percent of market value. County commissioners and the school board each pick a millage rate.

Ask the assessors for the exact mailing date on your notice, since the 45 days count from that date and not from the day it reaches you.

What exemptions can a Pickens County homeowner use?

The standard homestead subtracts $2,000 from assessed value before the county, school and State operating rates are applied. The Board of Tax Assessors accepts applications, and the books close April 1. Anything received later counts toward the following year. New owners should carry in a copy of their warranty deed.

The commissioner's page lists several age and service exemptions:

  • One Pickens-only exemption erases the school levy for owners aged 62 or older with a gross household income of $25,000 or under.
  • A standard elderly school exemption of up to $10,000 for owners 62 or older whose net income does not exceed $10,000.
  • A general elderly exemption of up to $4,000 for owners 65 or older under the same income limit.
  • A disabled veteran exemption of up to $50,000 of assessed value.
  • A deferral that postpones the bill without erasing it, open to owners 62 or older with household income at or below $15,000.

A floating exemption is open to owners 62 or older whose income is $30,000 or lower. It stands in for other state and county exemptions, and the commissioner warns that the first bill may rise. Ask the assessors before applying for it.

How should I handle property tax when selling a Pickens County house?

Dial (706) 253-8882 to learn what the parcel owes, and ask if earlier years, interest or a lien are involved. The commissioner's site has a tax sale page with procedures and a bidder registration form, which tells you how the office handles properties that stay delinquent.

The sale contract, applied by the closing attorney, sets the split of the year's tax. If the seller held an elderly or local school exemption, the buyer starts without it and must apply for a homestead on the new home. Deed copies are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.

Mobile homes on the lot are billed in January with an April 1 due date and need a current decal, which is issued when the tax is paid. If a mobile home sits on the lot, ask the commissioner whether it carries a separate bill before you set a closing date.

What will a buyer moving into a Pickens County home need from the tax office?

A buyer who relocates from another state will deal with the same Jasper office that bills the house. The commissioner also registers vehicles, and its new-resident page names what a person needs to tag a car in Pickens County. Mention this to buyers early, because it saves a second trip.

  • For a car with no loan: the out-of-state title, the registration from the previous state, proof of Georgia insurance, a Georgia driver's license showing a Pickens County address, and the current mileage.
  • For a car with a loan: the loan agreement with the lender's full name and address, the T-17 affidavit of the lienholder, and the same insurance, license and mileage items.

The license requirement means a buyer should update the address on the license after closing. The commissioner's site posts a link for searching property and mobile home taxes online, so a buyer can check the parcel's bill history before signing.

More questions about Pickens County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the Pickens County property tax due date?

The commissioner's site gives November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

How can I pay a Pickens County tax bill?

Walk-in payments take check, cash or card. Online payment takes cards and e-checks. A drop box outside the Administration Building stays open day and night. Cards add a 2.60 percent fee and e-checks add $3.00.

How many days do I have to appeal in Pickens County?

Forty-five days, starting on the date of the assessment notice. Step one is the Board of Tax Assessors. Step two is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

Does a Pickens County homeowner need to reapply for homestead after buying?

Yes. A new owner or new residence must apply again, and the assessors need it by April 1 for it to count that year.

Does late Pickens County property tax hurt my credit?

It can. Lien filings at the courthouse are public, and the commissioner notes that credit bureaus may pick them up.

What should a seller know about Pierce County, Georgia?

Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat. According to the county, the land came from Appling and Ware counties when Pierce was organized in 1857, and the name honors President Franklin Pierce. The Alabaha River winds through it, and its website points visitors toward fishing and the history of the Okefenokee.

It is the most spread-out county in the four-county Census comparison. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 count is 20,764 people, up 5.3 percent on 2020, over 340.46 square miles of land. That works out to 57.9 people per square mile in 2020. The county issued only 68 building permits in 2025, the fewest of the four compared, so a resale competes with little new housing.

Prices reflect that. The median owner-occupied value is $153,300 in the 2020 to 2024 estimates. Roughly three homes in four (76.5 percent) are owner-occupied, and rent is a median $799. Median household income was $60,517, and 82.9 percent of households have broadband. With prices like these, unpaid tax can swallow a large part of the proceeds, so learn the balance early.

Storm damage can also affect a sale. The county's home page carries a notice that Hurricane Debby damaged personal and business property and that the emergency management agency collected damage reports from residents and business owners for a federal disaster relief application. A seller with a damaged roof or outbuilding should keep photographs and repair estimates, since a buyer's inspection will ask about them.

Which Pierce County offices handle property tax?

Duties divide between the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, whose addresses are both on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's page describes an office independent of the assessors and of the county commissioners, who control only its budget. The commissioner's main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

Pierce County tax offices, from the county and commissioner websites
OfficeAddressPhoneHours listed
Tax Commissioner312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, Blackshear, GA 31516 (mail: PO Box 192)912.449.2026Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
Board of Assessors312 Nichols Street, Blackshear, GA 31516 (mail: PO Box 589)912.449.2025Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and the site says online payments post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

What did the 2025 Pierce County millage notice say?

A notice on the county's millage page says commissioners tentatively set a 2025 rate that raises property tax by 19.98 percent in unincorporated areas and 20.20 percent in incorporated ones. The hearings were held at the NFC Building at 705 College Avenue in Blackshear on November 6 and November 13, 2025, and those dates have passed.

  • Tentative millage rate: 11.241 mills.
  • Increase over the prior rate: 1.872 mills.
  • Rate without the increase: no more than 9.369 mills.
  • Increase printed for unincorporated areas: 19.98 percent; for incorporated areas: 20.20 percent.

That page also links the 2025 digest with its five-year levy history, plus the prior year's digest. Three authorities set millage: the commissioners, the school board and the State. A tentative rate may change before it is final, so ask the commissioner which millage is on your bill and whether the parcel lies in Blackshear, Patterson or unincorporated land.

When is Pierce County property tax due?

Your bill carries the due date, and the commissioner's office can confirm it by phone. The state revenue department's county facts page explains the range. December 20 is the official date, yet a county can pass a resolution for December 1 or November 15, or can split billing into installments.

State rules give you some breathing room, and a few other facts help sellers:

  • Per the state's county facts page, interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can follow if the balance goes delinquent.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • The return window at the county tax office runs January 1 to April 1.
  • A manufactured home parked in Pierce on January 1 gets its return and its location permit on the same visit, before April 1.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

How does a Pierce County assessment appeal work?

After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. The assessor's FAQ says late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If the value stands, the Pierce County Grand Jury's appointees on the three-person Board of Equalization hear the dispute next.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers work from three methods (cost, comparable sales and income). Field staff may stop at a parcel to look into an appeal, a return, a new addition or a conservation application. Visitors from the office show photo identification and arrive in a marked county vehicle. To meet with the Board of Assessors, book by the Friday before its 9:00 a.m. session; the board sits at least twice monthly.

What exemptions and special assessments apply in Pierce County?

The Pierce County homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. A purchase made after New Year's Day misses that year's exemption, since the January 1 test looks at who owned and lived there. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The Georgia Department of Revenue's county page says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so state exemptions are what applies; ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

The assessor's FAQ lists special programs that can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential farmland is assessed at 30 percent instead of 40, and the owner commits to ten years of farm use.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Trees on the stump escape tax until they are sold or cut, then count at full market value.

Land held under a covenant deserves a question to the assessors, before the contract is signed, about how a sale or a new use changes things. The county has 57.9 people per square mile, so farm and timber parcels are a real part of its sales, and the covenant terms are worth requesting in writing.

It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

Ask the commissioner or check your bill. December 20 is the state's default, which a county can replace with an earlier date or installments.

Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?

Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

April 1 of the year you want it. Ownership and residence on January 1 of that year are both required.

Pike's buyers tend to be working households with commutes. The labor force takes in 60.3% of residents over 16, and 55.3% of women over 16 are in it. Employment at county employers rose 9.5% between 2022 and 2023, on a 2023 payroll of $93,756,000.

Connectivity helps a remote worker consider the county. In 2020-2024, 94.4% of households had a computer and 84.6% had a broadband subscription. High school completion for adults 25 and over is 89.2%.

Land is not scarce, yet density is rising. The county counted 82.7 people per square mile in 2010 and 87.4 in 2020, across 216.09 square miles. Health coverage is a weak spot: 12.4% of residents under 65 lack insurance, and 7.4% have a disability.

A seller can use these numbers when pricing. Buyers with higher incomes and long drives expect a well kept house, and a listing with an open tax lien or unfinished repairs gives them a reason to wait.

Which Pike County office should I call?

Call the tax commissioner about a bill and the assessors about a value. The two numbers are one digit apart.

  • Tax commissioner: (770) 567-2001, weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00. Online payments run through pikecountypay.com.
  • Tax assessors: (770) 567-2002 for returns, homestead forms, valuation and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room at the county courthouse, and the place where a tax lien is recorded.
  • City of Zebulon: its website says Pike County bills city property tax for it, so there is no second counter for city residents.

The office states that bills are addressed to the owner. A lender holding an escrow account will not receive one, so pass your copy along.

What does a late Pike County bill cost?

Real estate and business personal property bills fall due December 1. A mobile home bill is due April 1. Postmarks from the United States Postal Service count, and a metered mark does not.

The county writes its penalty schedule in four steps:

  1. Interest posts on the 2nd of every month at prime plus 3%, divided by 12.
  2. A 5% penalty is added at 120 days, then again every 120 days, capped at 20%.
  3. Thirty days past the delinquent notice date, a FIFA is filed in the Clerk of Courts office.
  4. The account then moves to a contractor, and fees of $215 plus can be added for certified mail and a title search before the sale.

A mobile home takes a 10% penalty starting April 2. In the weeks before an auction the parcel is posted, photographed and advertised in the local paper for four weeks.

How do I dispute a Pike County valuation?

Write to the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date. The county says an appeal sent after that cutoff cannot be accepted.

Argue one of three things: the property is not taxable, the value is wrong, or the value is out of line with similar parcels. A complaint that the tax amount is too high will not work, because millage is a separate decision. Should the assessors stand by their number, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, or arbitration if you prefer. Superior Court is the last stop.

Mobile home owners follow a shorter chain: 45 days with the assessors, then 21 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

What lowers a Pike County tax bill?

A homestead exemption is the first thing to check. You need to own and occupy the house on January 1, and the assessors must receive your form before April 1.

  • The assessors ask first-time filers to show their deed.
  • Pike adds its own county exemption amounts, and the bigger of the local and state figures applies.
  • Age 62 opens an extra exemption.
  • Working farmland may be taxed on 30% of market value, and conservation land on its use value. Both need a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption in the January 1 to April 1 window.

The exemption continues from year to year until the home, its owner or the kind of exemption changes.

How is a Pike County bill built?

Taxable value is 40% of market value as of January 1, less exemptions. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board separately. Each mill levies $1 on $1,000 of taxable value.

Returns follow a pattern. A real estate return is needed only after a purchase or an improvement, and it is filed January 1 through April 1. A required return that never gets filed draws a 10% charge on whatever value was left off. Equipment and other personal property goes on a fresh return every year.

How should I sell a Pike County house that has unpaid tax?

Collect a written payoff and have the closing attorney deduct it at the table. Interest keeps growing monthly, so the number changes with the calendar.

  1. Phone (770) 567-2001 for the amount owed and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA exists and what clears it.
  3. If the account is at the contractor stage, request the extra fees as a separate line.
  4. Check which year's bill falls on you under the contract.

Closing before the tax sale stage avoids newspaper and levy costs. When repairs or an inherited deed are the holdup, an as-is purchase lets you pick a closing date around them.

Which date should I use for the Pike County bill?

December 1 for real estate. The county tax site gives that date, even though the state default is December 20.

How fast does Pike County add penalties?

Interest posts monthly, the first 5% penalty comes at 120 days, and the cap is 20%. Mobile homes get 10% on April 2.

Which Pike County office takes a homestead form?

The tax assessors, and it must be in hand before April 1. First-time homeowners should carry the deed.

Will a recorded FIFA stop a Pike County sale?

No. It is a lien that gets paid out of the proceeds. Ask the tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 what the payoff is.

Who answers questions about my Pike County value?

The assessors at (770) 567-2002. Billing and payment go to the commissioner at (770) 567-2001.

What does a Polk County seller need to know about the county?

The county's 2023 payroll reached $479,368,000 across 670 employer establishments, and those employers counted 10,640 jobs. Medical and social service providers took in $101,139,000 in 2022, and hotels and restaurants sold $80,215,000.

Retail sales of $538,472,000 in 2022 work out to $12,331 per resident. Another 3,187 businesses have no employees at all, so a share of Polk sellers are self-employed owners who may also hold commercial space or equipment on the tax rolls.

Employment at Polk employers grew 2.0% between 2022 and 2023, a slower pace than the other three counties managed. Transportation and warehousing receipts reached $51,678,000 in 2022. The labor force takes in 58.1% of residents over 16.

Who are Polk County's residents?

Education runs below the other three counties: 84.5% of adults hold a high school diploma and 15.4% hold a bachelor's degree. A 12.5% disability rate under age 65 and a 16.3% uninsured rate round out the picture. Broadband reaches 87.4% of households, and 1,810 residents are veterans.

When does a Polk County bill become late?

That depends on which county page you read, so confirm the date on your bill. The tax commissioner FAQ says December 20 is normal, while the county's own commissioner page puts payment at sixty days after mailing.

The FAQ lays out the cost of lateness this way: interest of 1% a month starts after the date, and a 10% penalty hits anything still open at 90 days. A homestead parcel owing under $500 skips that penalty. Once 90 days pass, the tax office may record a FIFA at the Clerk of Superior Court. The record is open to the public, which the FAQ warns can show up in credit reports.

A bill is mailed to the owner and not to a lender. If a mortgage company escrows your tax, forward the bill to the servicer and include your loan number.

The Board of Assessors mailed them on July 17, 2026. Each notice starts a 45-day appeal clock, so owners who did not respond within that time have passed the deadline for the 2026 values.

The county directs owners to qpublic.net/ga/polk to see property characteristics, ownership, assessed values, parcel maps and sales history. Its tax estimator asks you to choose the right tax district, choose Not Exempt, key in the market value on the notice, and then subtract the estimated tax savings printed on the notice. The county describes the result as an estimate only, because final millage rates may differ.

An appeal goes to the assessors first. A dispute that stays open can move on to the Grand Jury's appointed Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, with a superior court filing available after that.

Which exemptions can a Polk County owner claim?

Four conditions apply: you held title on January 1, it is your legal residence, you live in it, and you claim no other homestead anywhere. Filing is open all year, but the paperwork has to arrive before April 1 to affect that year's bill.

  • First $2,000 of assessed value off county, state and school tax for a homestead.
  • Age 65: $20,000 off school tax and $4,000 off county tax.
  • Age 62 with owner and spouse income under $10,000: extra relief.
  • Age 70 with household income under $10,000: extra relief.
  • Veterans who are 100% permanently disabled: an added exemption.

Only your primary home can be homesteaded, and a move means a fresh application.

How do I close a Polk County sale when tax is owed?

Get the numbers first and pay them from the sale proceeds. Polk's commissioner says tax liens are not sold, but a recorded FIFA still clouds the title until it is satisfied.

How would you describe Putnam County to a home seller?

Putnam County had 21,218 residents in 2010, 22,047 at the 2020 census and an estimated 23,722 in July 2025. Eatonton levies its own city tax, and the tax commissioner runs the county's billing from putnamgatax.com.

Older people shape the market. Residents 65 and over make up 27.1% of the population, children under 18 make up 17.9%, and households average just 2.17 people. Per person income is $48,458, the highest of the four counties compared, and 31.1% of adults have finished a four-year degree.

The county spans 344.68 square miles of land with 64.0 people per square mile. Shoppers spent $321,128,000 at Putnam retailers in 2022, or $14,003 per resident, and medical and social service providers took in $55,842,000. Employers numbered 546 in 2023, with 5,509 jobs and a payroll of $264,921,000, up 5.6% in jobs from a year earlier.

What do Putnam County's household and work numbers add?

The county has 10,435 households and 1,590 veterans. The Census table puts Black residents at 24.7%, higher than in any other county of the four, and Hispanic or Latino residents at 8.6%. People born abroad are 7.6% of the total, and 11.2% of residents over 5 use another language at home.

Disability affects 13.8% of residents under 65, and 16.6% in that age group lack health insurance. For an owner on a fixed income, an unpaid tax bill and a deferred repair list are the two problems most likely to push a sale.

Which Putnam County office does what?

The tax commissioner collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors values.

  • Tax Assessors: (706) 485-6376, with parcel records at qpublic.net/ga/putnam.

The commissioner publishes a Taxpayer Brochure that walks through returns, exemptions and appeals, and the Department of Revenue's county sheet points to putnamgatax.com for the commissioner and putnamcountyga.us for the county.

What are the Putnam County payment dates and penalties?

December 1 is the date for real and personal property. The commissioner mails those bills by October 1. Mobile homes follow a separate calendar: bills by February 1, payment by April 1, and a decal is no longer required after a resolution dated July 2, 2021.

Interest starts accruing one day late, then posts again each month on the 1st. The rate is the prime rate in force at the start of the year plus 3%. At 120 days a 5% penalty arrives, with another 5% for each further 120-day period, to a ceiling of 20%. A mobile home pays a flat 10% beginning the day after its due date.

Homesteaded property owing less than $500 skips the 90-day penalty described on the office's page. The commissioner mails each bill to the owner, never to the lender.

If I sell mid-year, who gets the Putnam County bill?

The seller of record on January 1 gets the first bill. Once a new deed is recorded, the commissioner sends the buyer a copy as well.

The office's advice is to read your closing papers or ask the closing attorney who owes the money. For a seller, that means checking that the contract and the settlement statement spell out the year's tax, regardless of whether closing lands before or after December 1.

Boats follow the same January 1 logic. Sell one and the fall bill still comes unless the assessors' marine specialist is told. Only accounts totaling $20,000 or more in marine equipment get a bill.

How can Putnam County owners appeal or reduce a bill?

Your first appeal goes to the assessors, who may revise the value and mail a second notice. If they hold at the same number, the file is forwarded for a hearing. An arbitrator is another option, and the county's FAQ sets 45 days from the notice date for it.

  • Homestead: own and occupy on January 1, file at the assessors, and get the paper in before April 1.
  • Age 70: owners who reach it can request an extra homestead exemption.
  • Relief grant: the 2023 state grant cut assessed value by $18,000 on homesteaded property, and the commissioner says it returns for tax year 2026. Rentals and non-homesteaded property were not eligible.
  • Refund: a claim for tax wrongly collected has to begin within three years of the payment date.

The final step in a dispute is Superior Court, started by written notice to the assessors.

How are Putnam County bills calculated and spent?

The formula starts at 40% of fair market value, subtracts exemptions, then applies the millage rate. The county commissioners, the school board, the City of Eatonton and the State of Georgia each adopt a rate, with one mill worth $1 per $1,000 of taxable value.

The county lists what the money buys: schools and county government, public buildings, bridges and roads, courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation. The assessors take real estate returns during the first three months of the year.

What happens in Putnam County if tax goes unpaid?

A FiFa can be recorded 30 days after the commissioner sends a 30-day notice. Because it is a public lien record, the FAQ warns it can reach credit bureaus once a bill is more than 90 days late.

The tax sale is generally annual, held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of July. Registration opens at 9 am, and bidders must show photo ID, pay in certified funds and settle the same day by 4 pm. No electronic bidding exists, and owners with delinquent county accounts cannot register. The list is published in The Eatonton Messenger and on Georgia Public Notice.

Paying the commissioner's payoff at closing keeps your property off that list.

December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home taxes are due April 1.

Yes. It generally holds one sale a year, on the first Tuesday in July at the courthouse, with in-person bidding only.

The January 1 owner is billed first, and the buyer later receives a copy. Your closing attorney and contract decide who pays.

Interest runs at the January prime rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty follows at day 120 and repeats every 120 days until 20%.

Past that date, prime plus 3% accrues monthly, and 120 days later a 5% penalty joins it. Once a bill is over 90 days late, a FIFA lien can be recorded, and the commissioner may levy on the parcel. The FAQ points out that the lien becomes a public record that credit bureaus may read.

The county accepts a United States Postal Service postmark, not a metered one. Mobile homes are billed in January, and the two county pages disagree on their due date, April 1 on one and May 1 on the other, so call (706) 782-3613 before paying one.
