How can I contest a Rabun County value?

File the appeal in writing, and file it early. The county's assessor FAQ says an appeal filed late is invalid.

It names three grounds: whether the property is taxable or exempt, whether it is valued in line with comparable property, and whether the dollar value is too high or too low. The assessors review it, and if nothing changes, the Board of Equalization hears the case. Rabun County Superior Court is the next level for either side.

The assessors remind owners that they follow the market and do not create it, using cost, market and income approaches. A recent sale price of a similar nearby house gives the strongest backing.

Which Rabun County assessment programs matter for land?

Land owners have more choices here than house owners. Every program below ties the land to its use for 10 years by covenant. Apply between January 2 and April 1.

  • Preferential agricultural: taxed on 30% of fair market value where other property uses 40%.
  • Conservation use: current use value replaces market value.
  • Environmentally sensitive: land left in its natural state, valued by use if it meets Department of Natural Resources standards.
  • Residential transitional: current use value where an area is moving away from residential use.

Standing timber is taxed once it is sold or harvested. Anyone selling land under a covenant should tell buyers, since the 10-year commitment affects what they can do with it.

How does Rabun County handle homestead and bill math?

The test is ownership plus residence on January 1, and the form goes to the assessors. The tax commissioner's site says the form must arrive before April 1 for that year, while the assessor's page lists a different in-person window, so call (706) 782-3613 to confirm which one governs you.

Owners aged 62 can ask for an additional exemption. Arithmetic is simple: take 40% of market value, subtract exemptions, and apply the rate set by the county commissioners and the school board. The county says the money pays for police, fire, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

Can I sell a Rabun County house with tax still owed?

Yes, with a payoff from the commissioner and the closing attorney handling it.

  1. Ask for the exact balance with interest and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. If the land is in a covenant program, share that with the buyer.
  4. List each payoff on the settlement statement.

A house stalled by repairs or long vacancy can sell as-is, on a closing day you choose, with the tax paid out of the proceeds.

Where is the Rabun County tax commissioner?

At 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, in Clayton. Call (706) 782-3613. Counter hours end at 4:30 pm.

Can I pay Rabun County tax by card?

Preferential agricultural, conservation use, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional assessments. Apply from January 2 to April 1.

Which Richmond County offices handle my tax bill?

Valuation and collection sit in different hands here. Appraisers working for the Board of Assessors value each parcel, and the elected Tax Commissioner, whose site is arctax.com, prints the bills and accepts payment. Because the commissioner has no hand in the size of any levy, a dispute over rates belongs with the commission and school board, and a dispute over worth belongs with the appraisers.

  • Assessors: 706-821-2310, plus an online property search.
  • Tax Commissioner: 706-821-2391, counter at 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta.
  • Mail to the commissioner: P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903.

Richmond County is consolidated with Augusta, so county notices appear on the Augusta government website and a single government sits behind the county and city side of the bill.

What do Richmond County's numbers say about its housing?

Census QuickFacts, linked here, shows 206,559 residents in July 2025 on 324.34 square miles of land, level with 206,607 counted in 2020. The county has 76,694 households and an estimated 94,651 housing units. Authorities issued 534 building permits in 2025.

Owners hold only 51.2 percent of households, so renters are nearly half. A typical owned home is valued at $178,500 and a typical rent is $1,141. The middle household earns $55,637, 19.0 percent of people live below the poverty line, and 17,087 are veterans. The drive to work averages 21.4 minutes.

With so many rentals, buyers here include landlords as well as first-time owners. A parcel with deferred repairs or an old tax balance sells at a discount, since the buyer subtracts what the county is owed.

What are the 2026 millage rates in Richmond County?

Whatever remains unpaid is charged .875 percent interest monthly (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40), and a single 10 percent penalty follows. If the account keeps sitting, a lien and levy can follow. Settle an old balance ahead of any sale. The commissioner's page stresses that the owner remains responsible for payment, whoever was supposed to remit it.

Escrow does not transfer the legal duty. Lenders do not get paper bills from the office, only the data. After a change of servicer, phone the new company and ask whether the county account was paid.

How can I challenge a Richmond County valuation?

The clock is 45 days and starts on the date the notice was mailed. The batch mailed June 29, 2026 had an August 13, 2026 cutoff, which has passed. The next notice states its own date.

You can file through the assessor's website, by post, by email or in person. Since 2011 every owner receives a yearly notice, even when nothing changed. A change in 2026 is the layout: Senate Bill 566 replaced the old tax estimate grid with an estimated savings section plus appeal and exemption directions.

  • Pull sale prices of comparable houses close to yours.
  • Photograph defects that lower value.

What homestead relief does Richmond County offer?

You qualify by living in the house on January 1 and filing by April 1. The commissioner takes the form and sends it to the assessors for a ruling, and an owner who is turned down may go to the Board of Equalization.

After approval the benefit rolls forward by itself. Owners refile only after a deed change in name or spelling, an ownership change, or when they want a different exemption. Refinancing leaves it alone. A couple gets one homestead between them, and each vehicle either spouse owns has to be registered here. Solid waste and street light fees stay payable.

Augusta adds a local floating homestead exemption, aimed at holding back growth in the assessed value of a primary home. The form is accepted from January 1 through the end of the 45 day appeal window that follows the mailing of assessment notices, and it can accompany an appeal or replace one. Each applicant states citizenship or immigration status under O.C.G.A. 50-36-1, and qualified aliens attach their federal documents. Senior and other special exemptions need an in-person or mailed application with full documentation. For mailed forms the office recommends certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are refused.

Who owes the tax in a Richmond County sale?

Georgia puts each year's tax on whoever holds title January 1. A contract can pass that burden to the buyer, which the closing table normally handles. The commissioner will not divide the year between the parties.

  • A bill goes to the January 1 owner and to any buyer who took title later that year.
  • If nobody pays, the lien carries the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows the deed plus closing papers inside 90 days of the due date.
  • The office calls its proof an acknowledgment and receipt of settlement statement.

If a fall closing runs on an estimated tax figure, ask the attorney who absorbs any gap when the real bill arrives, and keep your signed settlement statement.

How can I check whether a Richmond County parcel is current?

The tax commissioner publishes a mass tax bill file listing outstanding real estate balances, normally refreshed on Mondays. Its warning is worth repeating: some accounts are coded bankruptcy, under appeal or awaiting an assessment change, and those are not yet due, so a balance in the file does not by itself mean a delinquency.

For an exact status, call 706-821-2391 and have the bill number or map and parcel number ready. Bad checks go to a recovery partner, Envision Payment Solutions, and a service fee applies under state law.

Can I sell a Richmond County house with taxes behind?

Yes. A payoff request goes from the title company to the commissioner, and the amount is deducted from your proceeds the way a mortgage payoff is.

Forty-five days, counted from the notice. The 2026 batch ran out on August 13.

April 1, for a home you occupied on January 1. After approval, the benefit continues until the deed or the owner changes.

No. Buyer and seller settle that between themselves at closing, and their papers can later show who took on the tax.

Who does what on a Rockdale County tax bill?

Three bodies shape a Rockdale bill. Appraisers under the Board of Assessors value the parcel, the Tax Commissioner collects, and the county commissioners, school board and city council choose the rates. The county's tax facts page adds that the commissioners control only the assessors' budget, and the Tax Commissioner is elected and answers to voters rather than to the assessors.

  • Assessors: 770-278-7676, P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012. Phone first to confirm where the counter is now.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-278-7600, text line 678-964-4712, and an account portal at rockdaletaxoffice.org.

Real estate returns are filed with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. Anyone who thinks the value is too high may file one. It is mandatory after a lot split or after new construction in the prior year, and a late filing triggers a 10 percent non-return penalty.

What do Rockdale County's numbers show about local homes?

The county packs 98,416 people (July 2025 estimate) into 129.82 square miles of land, about 721 per square mile, and the estimate is 5.3 percent over the 2020 base of 93,487. The QuickFacts comparison records 34,437 households and 37,611 housing units, plus 339 building permits in 2025.

Two of every three households own, 69.6 percent. A typical owned home is valued at $292,900, a typical rent is $1,525, and the typical household earns $77,247. Residents born abroad are 10.7 percent, and 11.8 percent speak another language at home. Workers spend 33.7 minutes on the road each way.

Those values make a missed tax year costly. Before listing, ask the Tax Commissioner whether the parcel shows anything unpaid.

How is a Rockdale County bill worked out?

Market value is multiplied by 40 percent, exemptions are taken off, and the rate is applied to the remainder. Appraisers lean on three methods: comparable sales, replacement cost and income capitalization. The facts page points out that a bill can climb with an unchanged rate if value rises or an exemption is lost.

How do I file a value appeal in Rockdale County?

The quickest path is the assessors' real property page: search your parcel on qPublic, press the Appeal to Board of Assessors button and send the form. Georgia gives 45 days from the notice date, and the notice states the exact deadline.

Four grounds are open: value, taxability, uniformity and denial of an exemption. Complaints about the rate itself have no route here.

  • Gather recent sold prices and photos for comparable houses.
  • Name board or arbitration in the first filing.
  • Once the Board of Equalization or the court decides, the assessors need an on-site inspection before changing that value for two years.

What homestead rules apply in Rockdale County?

The final day is April 1, and the county says the law gives it no authority to extend. You need to have owned the house and lived in it on January 1.

The 2026 exemption chart lists the regular exemption at 15,000 off county maintenance and operations and 15,000 off school maintenance and operations, with a state component at 100 percent. Further lines serve age 62 and up, total permanent disability, and disabled veterans at 126,526, and variable exemptions apply where household income is $30,000 or less. A floating statewide exemption appears too. The HOST credit covers up to five acres and the main residence, while the state portion covers up to ten acres.

Take a current license, the recorded deed and a utility statement to the assessors. Income-based forms need the latest federal and state returns. One homestead per family unit is the limit.

When is Rockdale County property tax due?

The date is November 15. The Tax Commissioner's tax sale page says taxes still open after it become eligible for levy and sale.

Send payment in the pink return envelope, leave it in the drop box beside the front door, pay at the window or log into an online account. Cards cost 2.35 percent with a $1.00 minimum. How does a Rockdale County tax sale work?

Sales are public auctions at the J.P. Carr Community Center in Conyers, starting at 10 a.m. The office lists the next one for March 2027. Properties are advertised in the Rockdale Citizen for four weeks beforehand, and buyers pay by cash or certified check for a tax deed. Liens are not sold.

  • Bidding opens at the tax due plus penalties and costs.
  • The winner cannot move in, improve the land or evict anyone yet.
  • The owner or any party with an interest may redeem, and the buyer waits a year and a day before moving to cut off that right.
  • Money left after costs may be sent to superior court through an interpleader.

The Tax Commissioner's real estate resources page posts downloads of the sale list, excess funds and delinquent tax file. If you sell first, the overdue amount is paid at the closing table, so request a payoff before you accept an offer.

What does a buyer at a Rockdale County tax sale actually get?

Less than a normal purchaser. The tax deed is not a warranty deed, so the bidder carries the risk that the title has defects, and the sale is advertised as buyer beware with no guarantees. The winning bidder must pay within one hour, pays the clerk's recording fee, and takes on later taxes, including any owed to a city if the parcel lies inside one.

A mobile home passes with the land only if a certificate of permanent location was issued. A sale can be set aside for irregularities such as a bankruptcy filing or an assessment error, and the money is then refunded in full. Unbid parcels may be re-auctioned at 3 p.m. that day, or knocked off to the county.

For an owner, the practical point is the redemption window of at least twelve months. Redeeming means paying the deed holder what is owed, so the better move is to deal with the balance well before any auction date is set, whether by paying it or by selling.

Can I sell a Rockdale County house if tax is owed?

Yes. The closer pays the county from your proceeds and the buyer receives title free of that debt. A cash buyer removes the appraisal, lender repair demands and loan timing that slow an ordinary sale.

Heirs, landlords and owners who have fallen behind should get a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and a price opinion from an agent, and compare both with a cash offer.

November 15, according to the Tax Commissioner. After that date unpaid taxes are open to levy and a tax sale.

April 1 of the tax year, with no grace period under the county's reading of the law. Call the assessors at 770-278-7676, and mail goes to P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012.

Who sets a Rockdale parcel's value?

The Board of Assessors, run day to day by its Chief Appraiser. County commissioners appoint the board and hold only the purse strings.

Does the Rockdale Tax Commissioner auction tax liens?

No. Only tax deeds are auctioned, and the original owner keeps a right to redeem.

Forty percent of market value, as set by state law. Exemptions come off that figure before the rate is applied.

Those bills typically mail around January 2. The state sheet gives a newly placed home 30 days to get its permit.

Which Spalding County offices touch a tax bill?

Spalding County divides the work among five bodies. The Tax Commissioner owns the bill and the payment window. The assessors value property and approve exemptions, and a Grand Jury appointed board of equalization settles disputes. Millage rates come from the commissioners and the school board.

The Tax Commissioner's office moved to 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, three blocks from the courthouse. The phone is (770) 467-4360 and the mailbox is PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. Call (770) 467-4240 for the Tax Assessor. County administration works from 119 E. Solomon Street.

What is the November deadline in Spalding County, and what do late payers owe?

Bills for land, buildings and business equipment normally fall due on November 15. The Tax Commissioner says late fees do not start until 60 days after the bills go out. After the due date the county adds interest monthly at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty accrues every 120 days up to 20%.

Homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty. Mobile homes sit on an April 1 schedule with a location permit, and the office can levy on unpaid property as a last resort.

What are the key Spalding County tax rules at a glance?

Spalding County property tax rules, from the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's website

A mill is one thousandth of a dollar per dollar of assessed value. The county's order of operations is to subtract exemptions from the 40% assessed value first and apply the millage rate to what remains.

What is the route for contesting a Spalding County value?

Owners in Spalding County have forty-five days after the assessment notice goes out. The county's FAQ says to argue taxability, value or uniformity, and to leave the size of the bill out of it. For tax year 2026, the county Tax Commissioner stretched the homestead filing window to match the appeal period, June 5 through July 23, 2026, and that period has ended. Exemptions based on income had to be requested in person with proof of 2025 income.

Which homestead exemptions does Spalding County offer?

The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly: age 65 before January 1, net income capped at $15,000, with bigger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption: age 62 or older, or totally disabled at any age, with household gross income capped at $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating school exemption for owners 65 and up, which freezes the value used for school tax.

An approved exemption carries forward until the owner moves, so a buyer applies fresh for the new address. Owners 62 and up with household income below $15,000 may have a deferral on file; the Tax Commissioner can confirm for your parcel.

Roughly one resident in five (20.6%) is 65 or older, which puts the senior exemptions above in play for many sellers.

The county covers 195.97 square miles of land with 343.5 people per square mile, and Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk all sit. The county's own news page notes a comprehensive plan update that looks toward 2050 and the county commissioners' adoption of a full rollback rate for 2025, which can come up in buyer conversations.

The county reports it moved up to a Tier 2 ranking in Georgia's 2026 Job Tax Credit rankings, which it ties to better employment and income measures.

The Georgia Department of Transportation held a public open house in Griffin on May 7, 2026 about replacing the State Route 16 bridge over the Norfolk Southern Railroad, with comments accepted through May 21, 2026. A house near that corridor may draw questions from buyers. Heirs selling an inherited house can reach the county Probate Court at (770) 467-4341.

How are delinquent taxes and tax sales handled in Spalding County?

The Tax Commissioner's FAQ explains that Georgia law puts delinquent tax sales on a month's first Tuesday, within a 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. window. The sale takes place at 411 E. Solomon Street. Bidder rules on the Tax Commissioner's site:

  • Register on sale morning between 8:00 and 9:30.
  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Show a driver's license or other official ID.

Bidding usually starts around 10:00 or 10:30.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

Where do I record the deed or get a copy in Spalding County?

The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds, at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin. Call 770-467-4309 to reach the clerk, whose staff includes a deputy for real estate. The Tax Commissioner's FAQ sends owners to this office for a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. The Planning Commission gathers on the last Tuesday evening of each month, and the Board of Appeals follows on the second Thursday, both at 6:00 p.m. in the Courthouse Annex. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. Its contact list also names a business and alcohol license technician and a permit technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

November 15, for bills on land, buildings and business personal property. Late fees wait until 60 days after the bills are mailed.

Forty-five days after the notice is mailed. Assessors review first, then the equalization board or an arbitrator, and finally Superior Court.

Once November 15 passes, interest accrues each month, and penalties climb in 5% steps every 120 days to 20%. Homesteaded parcels with less than $500 due skip the penalty.

411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, phone (770) 467-4360. It opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

Which offices handle property tax in Stephens County?

Two offices carry most of the work, and they sit in different buildings. The Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bills from Room 103 at 70 North Alexander Street in Toccoa, in the same government building as the county tag office. Weekday hours end at 4:45 in the afternoon. Call (706) 886-4753 or write to PO Box 187, Toccoa, GA 30577. The county site notes that the Tax Commissioner's website is maintained separately from the county's.

For values and homestead forms, call the Tax Assessor at (706) 886-7435. Returns also go there, because the county's funding page says the assessors, not the Tax Commissioner, were delegated that job in Stephens County. Appraisers who visit a parcel identify themselves with photo ID and a marked county vehicle, says the assessor page, usually after an appeal, a return or new construction.

Who pays which millage rates in Stephens County?

Three rates apply to every parcel: Georgia's, Stephens County's and the Stephens County School System's. A fourth, the Toccoa city rate, is added for homes inside Toccoa city limits, so an in-town house carries one more layer than a rural parcel that only uses a Toccoa mailing address.

Stephens County taxes 40 percent of a property's market value, and each mill of tax equals $1 per $1,000 of that taxed amount. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education pick the rates. A seller unsure whether the address is in city or county should ask the Tax Assessor which digest holds the parcel.

What are the Stephens County deadlines for returns, homestead and appeals?

Stephens County property tax dates and rules, from the county's Tax Assessor and Tax Commissioner pages
ItemRule

The Tax Commissioner's website says refunds cover errors of fault, not valuation disputes. Business personal property needs a yearly return by April 1, and real estate owners with no changes can skip one.

Which homestead exemptions can Stephens County owners claim?

The county lists these exemptions on its homestead page, with the state code section for each:

  • Standard: $2,000 taken from the assessed value of the owner's primary residence, covering state, county and school tax, though municipal school levies are excepted.
  • Seniors 65 and up: an added local exemption, and another one if the owner's and spouse's net income did not top $10,000 the year before.
  • Age 62 school exemption: same $10,000 income ceiling, and it cannot exceed $10,000 of assessed value.
  • Floating inflation-proof exemption: owners 62 and up, with total household income under $30,000.
  • Disabled veterans: $50,000, passing to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.

Ownership and residence both have to be in place on January 1. The county says an exemption renews itself unless ownership changes, which means a buyer files fresh. A tax deferral is a further option for owners 62 and older at $15,000 of gross income or below. A state Homeowners Tax Relief Grant that once showed up as a bill credit was withdrawn in 2008.

What do Census numbers show for Stephens County?

Census numbers for Stephens County: 27,854 people in mid-2025, up 4.0% from 26,780 at the 2020 base, spread over 12,461 housing units. Owners live in 73.6% of those units. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $175,300 and a typical rent is $820. Median household income is $54,754, and 23.3% of residents have passed 65.

The county covers 178.86 square miles of land at about 150 people per square mile, so most parcels are not in a compact city grid. The Census Bureau counts 36 building permits for 2025 against the 12,461 units already standing. Toccoa holds the Historic Courthouse at 37 West Tugalo Street, where the board of elections also works.

What else does the Stephens County Tax Commissioner collect that a seller should know about?

The Tax Commissioner's website says property is taxable in the county where it sits, and it lists categories beyond the house itself. Business equipment is assessed at 40 percent. Timber on the lot is treated differently, since it is taxed only when sold or harvested, and then at full market value. A seller with timber on the lot or business equipment in an outbuilding should ask the Tax Assessor how each is carried on the digest.

Vehicle owners renew their registration and pay ad valorem tax every year in the 30 day period that ends on their birthday, and a newly bought vehicle must be registered within 30 days. The tag office is in the Stephens County Government Building at 70 N. Alexander Street, Room 103, with weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00. This registration is separate from the real estate bill.

Other deed related services listed on the county site include recording a plat, trade name registration and power of attorney filings, which can matter if an heir or an agent signs for the owner.

What does recording a deed cost in Stephens County?

The county's deeds page prints these numbers:

  • Transfer tax of $1 per $1,000 of money paid.
  • A $25 filing fee.
  • A $5 blank deed form.
  • 50 cents a page for copies.

Per recorded deed, fifty cents of that tax is kept by the county and the rest goes to the state. The grantor's signature must be witnessed and notarized, and the clerk can help calculate what is due.

Warranty deeds must carry a transfer tax form whether or not money changes hands, and the forms can be completed online at the state clerks' authority site. Filing a deed is not required for it to be legal, but the county says filing protects the owner. A closing attorney usually prepares the deed.

How do I pay or find a Stephens County tax bill?

Start at the county's Online Payments page, then use the Tax Assessor's online record search or tax estimator to look up a parcel.

A seller closing late in the year should agree with the buyer on who covers a bill charged to the January 1 owner. Call the Tax Commissioner for your parcel's balance ahead of any contract signing, and expect the payoff to come out of your sale proceeds. The Tax Commissioner's website warns that unpaid tax can lead to a levy and sale.

What is the usual payment date for a Stephens County tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner's website says real estate and business personal property bills are generally due November 15. Check the date on your own bill, or call (706) 886-4753.

When must a Stephens County homestead application be filed?

April 1. A later filing takes effect the year after. Applications go to the Tax Assessor, and you must have lived in the home on January 1.

What is the appeal window for a Stephens County assessment notice?

Forty-five days from the notice date, counted by when the appeal is received. The Tax Commissioner's website adds that an appeal the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

Do Toccoa residents pay extra property tax?

Yes. Residents inside Toccoa city limits pay the Toccoa city millage in addition to the Georgia, Stephens County and Stephens County School System millage.

What does the county charge in transfer tax on a sale?

The county's deeds page prints $1 per $1,000 of money paid, with fifty cents per deed staying in the county. Ask the Clerk of Court to confirm the figure for your sale.

Why should a Sumter County seller care about the lay of the land?

It tells you what a parcel sits near and who might want it. Sumter spreads across 493 square miles, 483 of them land, and Americus is both courthouse town and largest city. Wikipedia dates its creation to December 26, 1831 and lists Andersonville, De Soto, Leslie and Plains as the other cities, with Cobb and Flintside left unincorporated.

Muckalee Creek winds through, Kinchafoonee Creek and Lake Blackshear lie inside the lines, and the western part of the county drains toward the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee system while the east feeds the Middle Flint. The county holds the Jimmy Carter National Historical Park and part of the Andersonville National Historic Site, and thirteen state and federal routes cross it, among them U.S. 19, U.S. 280 and State Route 49.

Population has slid from 32,819 in 2010 to 29,616 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 28,801. Fewer local buyers per listing means a house with a clouded tax record loses ground fast.

What do housing and income figures show for Sumter County?

Owner-held homes have a midpoint value of $120,200 over 2020-2024, and the owners occupy 56.6% of occupied homes. Renters face a midpoint of $857 a month. Below are the housing rows of the Census profile next to its income and turnover rows.

Thirty-six permits against nearly 14,000 housing units means resale drives the market. With owners in barely more than half the occupied homes, plenty of sellable properties are rentals or inherited houses, and some carry a tenant with a lease.

Owner costs run $1,211 a month with a mortgage and $470 without, and the commute averages 19.9 minutes. The county counts 10,986 households averaging 2.49 people.

Who bills, and who values, in Sumter County?

Two offices split the work, and a house inside Americus draws a third bill from the city. The tax commissioner's page places it at 500 W. Lamar St., Americus. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1044, the phone is (229) 928-4530, and the counter is staffed weekdays from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m.

  • Commissioner: collects money, posts payments, takes homestead filings, handles mobile home and vehicle accounts.
  • Assessors: set fair market value and taxability, and receive returns in the winter filing window.
  • Americus finance office: sends city tax bills for parcels inside Americus.

The Department of Revenue's sheet for Sumter lists no local homestead breaks beyond the state's. Use that as a starting point and verify with the commissioner. Contact details for the appraisal side are on the county's Tax Assessor page.

When must Sumter County bills be paid, and what happens after?

The county FAQ calls December 1 the normal due date for land, buildings and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes fall due April 1, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday. The revenue department's sheet describes December 20 as the statewide default that a county may move to December 1 or November 15, so the date on your notice settles it.

Past that date, the FAQ cites 1 percent interest each month and a 10 percent penalty after 90 days. A homesteaded house billed under $500 avoids the penalty. Unpaid property can be levied on, though the office says it prefers other collection methods.

Americus uses its own calendar for the city portion:

  • Two installments, September 1 and December 20.
  • Installment one is based on half the prior year's total, and installment two true-ups to the current value and millage.
  • Interest of .542% per month, built from the federal prime rate plus 3%.
  • Penalty of 5% after 120 days, plus 5% more for each further 120 days, capped at 20%.

The city and county pages describe late charges differently, so ask for a written payoff with an expiration date before choosing a closing day.

Who decides the Sumter County millage rate?

The Sumter County commissioners and the county Board of Education set it each year, according to the county FAQ. A mill means one dollar of tax for each thousand dollars assessed, and each body takes its budget needs, subtracts revenue from other sources, and picks the rate that raises the remainder.

That is why two neighbors with the same value can see different bills if one lives inside Americus. The city adds its own rate on top of the county and school levies. The rate does not appear in your value appeal, because an appeal covers taxability, value and uniformity only.

How do I dispute a Sumter County valuation?

Put it in writing no later than 45 days after the notice date. The county FAQ says a late appeal is invalid, so mail it promptly and keep proof.

Owners may declare a value each winter on a return filed between the first of January and the first of April. If the board rejects your number, a notice with its own follows. Appeals can argue taxability, value, or fairness against similar properties. Disliking the final bill is no ground, since the county commissioners and school board set the rate.

The state fact sheet adds a refund rule. A written request for money collected in error or illegally must begin within three years of payment, and an appealed assessment brings an automatic refund when the final value is set.

What discounts can Sumter County owners claim?

Homestead is the main one. The state lets you apply at any point once the house is your main residence, provided the form arrives by April 1 of the first year you want relief. Not applying counts as waiving it.

  • Homestead: one application, then it carries forward.
  • Freeport: business inventory, if voters in the county approved it.
  • Mobile home permit: required 30 days after permanent placement, then renewed each year from January 1 to April 1.

Dollar amounts come from the state constitution and the General Assembly, so ask the commissioner for the current numbers rather than trusting an old figure.

How should a Sumter County sale be handled when tax is owed?

Gather payoffs first, one from the county for each open year and another from Americus if the house lies within the city. A delinquent account can turn into a FIFA, a lien entered in the superior court clerk's records, and a title search will show it.

Georgia county pages describe the year's bill as belonging to the January 1 owner, the same date used to measure fair market value. For a June sale, your settlement statement splits the cost with the buyer, and the closing agent covers any balance out of your proceeds. A manufactured home adds an April 1 permit tax and decal to the list.

Inherited houses and former rentals often hold the heaviest balances, especially where nobody opened the mail for a few years. A cash purchase can settle those in one closing.

500 W. Lamar St. in Americus, and mail goes to P.O. Box 1044. The county page lists (229) 928-4530 and weekday hours from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m.

Is Sumter County's due date December 1 or December 20?

The county FAQ says December 1 for real estate. Georgia's default is December 20 and a county may pull it earlier, so go by your notice.

How long can I wait to dispute a Sumter County value?

No more than 45 days after the date printed on your assessment notice. It must be written, and the FAQ calls a late one invalid.

Does living in Americus mean a second bill?

Yes. The city finance page lists city installments due September 1 and December 20, separate from the county's bill.

Can I sell a Sumter County house that owes back taxes?

You can. Get a payoff from the commissioner, then have the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds so the lien is released when the deed records.

  • Commissioners' office, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: mobile home location permits.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax on recorded loan documents.

Accepted forms of payment are cash, checks, money orders and Visa, MasterCard or Discover cards, and card payments carry an added fee. Look up a parcel through qPublic.

What is the Talbot County billing calendar?

Real and personal property statements typically arrive in October and fall due December 20. Part-payments are welcome. After the deadline, interest accrues at prime plus 3%, and every 120 days a further 5% penalty is added until the total hits 20%.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow a January-to-April rhythm. Statements usually go out early in the year with an April 1 deadline, a decal is handed over once the tax is paid, and the return for a home in the county on January 1 is also due April 1. Filing late costs a 10% penalty.

The tax office's site also carries a note about trash service: beginning January 1, 2026, the garbage collection fee is $225.00 per year, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that charge rides on your parcel's account so the closing agent includes it.

How is timber taxed in Talbot County?

Standing trees escape tax until sold or cut, and then 100 percent of fair market value is multiplied by the millage rate. The commissioner's page sorts these events into three kinds.

  • Lump sum sale: the purchaser fills out form PT-283T and delivers form and tax to the commissioner inside five business days, and is personally liable if the seller fails to pay.
  • Unit price sale: a quarterly report goes to the seller and the assessors 45 days after each quarter closes.
  • Owner harvest: the landowner reports to the assessors 45 days after the quarter and pays the tax.

If you have cut or plan to cut trees, ask the office whether a timber account is open before you list.

How does Talbot County auction property for unpaid tax?

The commissioner runs levy sales under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. A parcel is advertised in the Talbotton New Era for four straight weeks, then auctioned on the first Tuesday of the month after the notices end.

  • Location and time: the courthouse on South Washington Avenue, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • The county gives no title guarantee, and the bidder gets no access to the property and no rent for at least a year.
  • The high bidder pays in cash or certified funds as soon as the sale ends.
  • Money left after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request to 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

The commissioner's site posts a guide to the right of redemption. An owner in arrears has time before the auction, and settling the account in a private sale may leave more equity with the seller.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Talbot County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How do I dispute a value or claim an exemption in Talbot County?

Both go through the tax assessors. A disputed value starts with a written filing to the Board of Assessors that names the route you want: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration, or hearing officer. The revenue department's county sheet sets the cutoff as a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed.

A real estate return is due between January 1 and April 1 whenever something changed, and omitting a required one costs 10% of the unreported value. Personal property returns, form PT-50P, are filed yearly by April 1.

For exemptions, April 1 is the cutoff the commissioner's site gives for the current year, and later filings roll to the next. The state sheet lists no local homestead exemption for Talbot, which leaves the statewide ones. An approved exemption renews itself until the owner moves or ownership changes.

What should a Talbot County seller do about unpaid tax?

Request a written payoff for each year still open, adding mobile home and timber accounts where they exist. With an inherited house, learn which years went unpaid before you list, since a recorded lien has to be paid at the table.

Refunds are narrow. A written request for tax paid in error goes to the Board of Commissioners within three years, and the commissioner's page ties refunds to errors of fault, not to a quarrel over value. Dividing the year's bill between buyer and seller happens on the settlement statement.

With so little building and a small buyer pool, a house with a tax cloud is harder to place. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can pay the balance out of your proceeds at closing.

More questions about Talbot County, GA Property Tax Guide

What is the Talbot County tax commissioner's address?

38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with P.O. Box 147 for mail. Weekday service runs 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with a closure from noon to 1:00.

When are Talbot County property tax bills due?

December 20 for real and personal property, with statements typically mailed in October. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

Does Talbot County accept partial tax payments?

Yes, the commissioner's property tax page says so. Interest and penalties still build on the remainder after the due date.

When do Talbot County tax levy sales happen?

They take place on a first Tuesday, once four weeks of Talbotton New Era notices have run, at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

What is the Talbot County homestead exemption cutoff?

April 1 for the current billing year. Per the commissioner's FAQ, forms are accepted all year, and a later one applies to the following year.

How is Tattnall County laid out for a home seller?

Tattnall is a farm-and-river county in southeast Georgia. Reidsville holds the courthouse and Glennville is the biggest town. Wikipedia gives December 5, 1801 as the founding date, credits Josiah Tattnall as namesake, and measures 488 square miles with 479 of land.

Three river basins split the land. The Ohoopee drains the west, the Canoochee takes the northeast strip between Cobbtown and east of Reidsville, and the Altamaha collects the southeast and southwest corners. Municipalities are Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas and Reidsville, and Mendes is a census-designated place. U.S. 25 shares a roadway with U.S. 301, U.S. 280 runs with State Route 30, and eight counties touch the boundary: Candler, Evans, Liberty, Long, Wayne, Appling, Toombs and Emanuel.

The county's own website devotes pages to agriculture and the Vidalia onion. Census counts fell 10.5%, from 25,520 residents in 2010 to 22,842 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate of 24,376 shows a rebound.

What do Census figures show for Tattnall County housing?

Owner-held homes have a midpoint value of $140,000 for 2020-2024, and owners fill 71.0% of occupied housing. That tops the $117,100 to $120,200 range for Talbot, Terrell and Sumter counties, while middle gross rent is a lower $699.

Who does what in Tattnall County tax administration?

Billing and collection happen at 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, with P.O. Box 920 for mail. The county's payment portal lists the phone as 912-557-6736 and the hours as 8 to 5 on weekdays.

  • Tax commissioner: ad valorem tax, mobile homes, public utilities, timber, and vehicle tags.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: five members chosen by the county commissioners, with a chief appraiser directing the staff.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury to hear disputed values.

The county's general information page says Tattnall's assessors, rather than the commissioner, receive returns. It adds that a state levy cannot exceed one fourth of a mill.

The commissioner is elected every four years, and the county notes that this is one of the four elected positions created by the original Georgia Constitution. How do returns, homestead and use-based assessments work in Tattnall County?

A taxpayer holding property on January 1 files a return between then and April 1. The first one renews itself at last year's final value, so a new filing is needed only for added property, improvements or a different value you want on record.

Homestead covers the house you own and live in, with paperwork going to the assessors' office. The assessors' own page sets April 1 as the deadline and says Tattnall offers no local homestead exemptions beyond the statewide ones. The FAQ asks for applications before March 1, so filing early avoids a miss.

Programs described in the county FAQ:

  • Preferential agricultural property: assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40, with a ten year commitment.
  • Conservation use: valued by current use for bona fide farm or forest land, also ten years.
  • Environmentally sensitive and residential transitional land: current-use value, with applications taken January 2 through April 1.
  • Standing timber: no tax until it is sold or cut, then 100 percent of fair market value.

Before listing enrolled land, ask the assessors what the covenant means for the next owner.

How do Tattnall County assessors arrive at a value?

The county defines fair market value as the price a knowledgeable buyer and a willing seller would agree on in an arm's length sale, fixed as of January 1. Assessed value is 40 percent of that, and each mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Three methods appear in the FAQ. Cost starts from replacement cost less depreciation and adds land, market compares nearby sales, and income capitalizes net rent on commercial or rental property. Business equipment and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent too. If you have a recent arm's length sale, hold on to the contract and settlement statement as your best market evidence.

What is Tattnall County's due date?

Read your statement. The state fact sheet for Tattnall treats December 20 as the official date, lets a county switch to December 1, November 15 or installments, and gives each taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts.

The online portal offers a property tax option, and the office line is 912-557-6736. Mobile homes follow their own state schedule: a location permit within 30 days of permanent placement, then a return and permit renewal each year from January 1 to April 1.

One credit is not guaranteed. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant shows up only in years the General Assembly funds it, and the county warns that bills climb when the money is absent. Ask what credit, if any, is on your statement.

How do I contest a Tattnall County valuation?

Once the assessors change a value, a written answer is due within 45 days of the notice date, and the county treats a late one as invalid.

Your reason has to be taxability, uniformity or value, and a gripe about the tax itself does not count. The assessors review first. If the number stands, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, and either side may continue to Tattnall County Superior Court. Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization if you choose it at filing.

The county stresses that assessors read the market and do not invent prices. If a recent contract differs from the county's number, attach it to the appeal.

What happens when Tattnall County tax goes unpaid?

Delinquent parcels go to a courthouse sale. One was held Tuesday, June 7, 2022, at 10 a.m. in the second floor Commissioners Meeting room. An auction caps a long delinquency, so an owner behind has choices well before then.

Get written payoffs by year, and for a mobile home confirm the decal and permit are settled. The county FAQ charges tax to whoever owns the property on January 1, and the settlement statement is where you and the buyer divide the year. Any earlier balance is then paid by the title company out of your proceeds.

Where can I pay Tattnall County property tax?

At the tax commissioner's office, 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, or through the county's online payment portal. The phone is 912-557-6736 and the office keeps hours of 8 to 5 on weekdays.

What is the homestead cutoff in Tattnall County?

April 1 per the Board of Tax Assessors page. The county FAQ mentions March 1, so file before March to be safe. The assessors' office takes the form.

How much time do I have to appeal in Tattnall County?

Forty-five days from the date of the notice, in writing. Late appeals are invalid.

Does Tattnall County have its own homestead exemptions?

No. The Board of Tax Assessors page says none are offered locally, so owners apply for the statewide exemptions.

Is timber taxed in Tattnall County?

Yes, when it is sold or harvested. The tax uses 100 percent of fair market value, and the FAQ covers lump sum, unit price and owner harvest sales.

What should a seller picture when thinking of Terrell County?

Think of 338 square miles of southwest Georgia farm country around a single city. Dawson holds the courthouse and is the only city, and Bronwood, Parrott and Sasser are the three towns. Wikipedia traces the county to February 16, 1856, with its name taken from William Terrell.

Ichawaynochaway Creek drains the western and southern two thirds, and the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee system takes the northeast. U.S. 82 is the main route, joined by State Routes 32, 41, 45, 49, 50, 55, 118 and 520. Webster, Sumter, Lee, Dougherty, Calhoun and Randolph counties form the borders.

Numbers are heading down. A 2020 census count of 9,185 became a July 2025 estimate of 8,656, a 5.7% slide from the Bureau's base. At roughly 27 residents per square mile, a parcel might be a farmhouse with acreage or a modest house on a Dawson street.

Who handles property tax paperwork in Terrell County?

The tax commissioner sits at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson. Letters go to P.O. Box 484, Dawson, GA 39842, and the tax website shows (229) 995-5151 with counter service from 8:00 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays.

What is Terrell County's due date, November 15 or December 20?

Two county pages give different answers, so rely on the notice that reaches your mailbox. The general information page names December 20, while the FAQ states that bills for land, buildings and business equipment have come due November 15 since 2018. They agree on April 1 for mobile homes.

Late steps for land and buildings, as listed on the general information page:

  • A FIFA lien is filed with the Clerk of Courts after 30 days have passed from the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5% penalty hits at 120 days and again every 120 days, stopping at 20%.
  • A file still open is handed to a collection firm, which tacks on administrative and levy charges that can reach $240.00 plus.

Those charges cover certified mail and a title search that readies the parcel for auction, and the property runs in the Herald Journal for four weeks first. By mail, a United States Postal Service postmark counts as on time, though a postage-meter stamp does not.

How are Terrell County mobile homes taxed?

Georgia classes a mobile or modular home as personal property. When one is in the county on January 1, the owner owes tax by April 1 and picks up a location permit at the same visit. Statements usually go out on January 2.

Missing April 1 draws a 10% penalty, and the county can send the owner to Magistrate Court or sell the home. On an overdue account, interest accrues on the 16th of each month, the penalty is applied April 2, and a FIFA is filed 30 days after the delinquent notice goes out. A decal must stay visible, and the assessors take questions at (229) 995-5210.

If a manufactured home is sold mid-year, find out which owner paid the permit tax before you set the closing.

What exemptions and appeal routes exist in Terrell County?

Terrell's assessors take homestead filings, and the home must be both owned and lived in on January 1. A form can come in at any time, yet it must land by April 1 to cover that year. After approval it continues until you move.

The tax website says Terrell County has local exemptions, and a local figure replaces the state one whenever it is larger. Ask the assessors for current amounts. Owners 62 and older may qualify for more relief. A deferral program lets those owners with gross household income of $15,000 or less delay payment until ownership changes or deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Farm land can be assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and Conservation Use values land on its actual use. Both ask for a covenant of ten years or more.

An appeal must start no later than 45 days after the notice, citing taxability, value or uniformity. Unresolved cases go on to the equalization board or an arbitrator, then Superior Court. For an owner on armed forces duty, a friend or relative can file within 90 days.

Do Terrell County business owners file returns too?

Yes. Personal property returns on form PT-50p go to the Board of Assessors every year, no matter whether value or use has changed. The tax site warns that an owner who no longer has a listed item must say so or stay on the roll for it, and that skipping a required real estate return costs 10% of the value left off.

Business equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent of market value. Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption for raw goods, goods in process, or finished goods held for shipment out of state, filing between the first of January and April 1.

What should I do about taxes before selling in Terrell County?

Phone (229) 995-5151 and request a written balance for every year, mobile home accounts included. Find out whether a FIFA sits on record at the superior court clerk's office, because a lien has to be paid off for a deed to record cleanly.

Georgia fixes value on the first day of January, so the commissioner can describe how the year of your sale will be billed. Tell the title company about each open item early. A lien that surfaces at the closing table pushes the date out, and accounts that reached the collection stage cost more, since the added charges sit on top of the balance.

The county pages disagree: general information says December 20 and the FAQ says November 15 beginning in 2018. Follow the date shown on your own statement.

What is the Terrell County homestead deadline?

April 1 of the year you want the exemption. Apply with the assessors, and bring your deed if you recently bought.

How soon must I appeal a Terrell County assessment?

No later than 45 days after the notice. Valid grounds are taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint about the amount of tax is not one of them.

What if I skip a Terrell County tax payment?

Interest starts the 2nd of the following month, a FIFA lien follows 30 days after the delinquent notice, and a 5% penalty builds every 120 days up to 20%. A long unpaid account is passed to a collection firm and can end in a sale.

What sets Thomas County apart in southwest Georgia?

Thomas County borders Florida and centers on Thomasville, which is both seat and biggest town. Lawmakers carved it out of Decatur and Irwin counties on December 23, 1825, and the later counties of Colquitt, Brooks and Grady each took a slice of its first boundaries, per Wikipedia.

Of its 552 square miles, only 7.6 are water. Rain in the northwest half runs to the Ochlockonee River, the northeastern edge sends water toward the Suwannee, and the southeast drains to the Aucilla, which begins here. The Red Hills region is centered on the county. Across the line to the south lie Jefferson and Leon counties in Florida, and the Georgia neighbors are Colquitt, Brooks, Grady and Mitchell.

Beyond Thomasville the map holds Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs and Pavo as cities and Ochlocknee as a town. Barwick and Pavo spill over into Brooks County, and Meigs reaches into Mitchell. Public education is split between Thomasville City Schools within the city limits and Thomas County Schools for the rest. A house on one side of that boundary draws a different set of school-minded buyers than one a few blocks over.

How do Thomas County home prices compare with its neighbors?

Homeowners hold a solid majority here, and prices run higher than in the other three counties covered in this set of guides. QuickFacts reports 63.8% owner-occupancy for 2020-2024.

Thomas County snapshot from Census QuickFacts (housing units and permits for 2025, other rows for 2020-2024)

The 2020 count was 45,798 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 46,368, which is growth of 1.3% on the estimates base. The county has 18,684 households, and 21.0% of residents are past their 65th birthday. Builders pulled just 203 permits in 2025, so an older Thomasville bungalow faces little new-construction competition.

Which offices bill and value property in Thomas County?

The work is split between two offices. The tax commissioner sends bills and takes payment. The board of tax assessors places a value on each parcel and receives exemption applications.

You can reach the county's tax commissioner at 225 N. Broad Street, Thomasville 31792, or by mail at P.O. Box 2175, Thomasville 31799. The number is (229) 225-4136. The counter is staffed on weekdays, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at 5, and a holiday closing list is posted on the site.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, delinquent balances, payoff amounts before a tax sale
  • Tax assessor: values, returns, homestead filings, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens
  • Seven city tax departments: Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville bill their own residents

The county page explains who sets what. County commissioners pick the county rate, the school board picks the school rate, and the state sets its own by law. Someone living in Thomasville may see a city bill on top of the county one, so ask both offices what is owed.

When is Thomas County property tax due?

Payment falls due each November 15, and the county takes anything stamped by the post office on or before that day. Its information page warns that a bill lost in the mail does not cancel what you owe.

Delinquent totals reset on the sixteenth of every month, so a payoff quote goes stale quickly. Mobile homes pick up penalties each April 2. Skipping a required return carries its own charge, stated on the county page as 10% of whatever value went unreported, with interest on top.

  • Regular property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home penalties: added April 2
  • Past-due totals: change on the 16th
  • Unfiled return: 10% of unreported value plus interest

Tax sales happen at the commissioner's discretion, one or two times annually, and the office wants a phone call for the precise payoff before any sale date. A figure printed on last year's bill will not match.

How does a Thomas County sale handle tax still owed?

The January 1 owner is on the hook for that year's bill. Georgia's revenue department confirms there is no partial-year refund, which means a deed signed the next day still leaves the whole year with the seller.

Most often the closing attorney asks the commissioner for the balance and deducts it from what the seller nets, or the contract spreads the year across both parties. Request the figure in writing, and ask whether a city bill is also open. Unpaid tax can become a lien filed with the superior court clerk, and a buyer's title company will insist that it be cleared before funds move.

If back tax and deferred repairs pile up on one house, an as-is buyer can absorb both and clear the balance at the closing table. That saves listing prep. It does not erase the debt, because the county is paid either way.

What is the route for contesting a Thomas County value?

Put the challenge on paper and deliver it to the assessors. You get 45 days, starting from the mailing date printed on the assessment notice. The Georgia Department of Revenue publishes that limit, and the county page cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 as the source of the right.

State guidance allows four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The form must say how you want to proceed, from three choices: an equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. If the assessors and the owner cannot agree, the county page says the appeal moves along to the Board of Equalization on its own. Objections to the tax rate are not part of a value appeal.

  • Deadline: 45 days from the notice mailing
  • Where to file: the assessors' office
  • If unresolved: Board of Equalization, then court

Assessed value is set at 40% of market value, measured on the January 1 valuation date. The county page defines market value broadly enough to include a short sale, bank sale or auction sale, and a distressed sale of your own home can therefore serve as evidence.

Which Thomas County exemption should you confirm before listing?

Homestead leads the list, and the form goes to the assessor's office. April 1 is the county cutoff, and anything arriving afterward takes effect the next year.

Forms are accepted all year long, though April 1 is the line for that year's bill. The county says it grants local homestead relief that beats the state version, and the assessor can quote the current amounts. Ask for them directly instead of guessing.

Before you list, confirm the exemption sits on the parcel. A lender and a closing attorney will read the bill, and a missing exemption makes the number look larger than it should. The next owner has to apply for themselves, since a sale partway through the year does not carry your filing forward.

More questions about Thomas County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which phone reaches the Thomas County tax commissioner?

Dial (229) 225-4136. The office sits at 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville and takes calls on weekdays between 8 in the morning and 5 in the evening Ask for the assessor's office if your question concerns value or an exemption.

What is the Thomas County property tax deadline?

November 15 each year, with mail postmarked by that day accepted. Overdue amounts change on the 16th of every month, and mobile home penalties begin April 2.

Will selling erase this year's tax in Thomas County?

No. Georgia returns nothing for a partial year, so the January 1 owner carries that bill. At closing the attorney typically settles it out of the seller's proceeds, or the contract shares it.

How many days does an assessment appeal allow in Thomas County?

Forty-five days from the date the notice went out in the mail. Write to the assessors, and mark your preferred hearing path on the state form.

Does Thomasville bill its own tax separately?

Yes. The county tax commissioner's page says Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city taxes. Contact that city's tax department for the city portion.

What makes Tift County, Georgia a farm-and-rail county?

Tift County is the small, dense county around Tifton in south central Georgia. It was created on August 17, 1905, and Tifton serves as seat and largest city, according to Wikipedia.

Tifton grew out of a sawmill settlement that Henry Harding Tift founded in 1872 in the Wiregrass region. His timber land became farms for cotton, corn, pecans and sweet potatoes, and the railroad junction of 1888 tied the town to Atlanta. Tift also donated land for an agricultural experiment station, which is the root of Abraham Baldwin Agricultural College and the Coastal Plain Experiment Station in Tifton.

The county covers 269 square miles. Interstate 75 runs through it, along with U.S. 41, U.S. 82, U.S. 319 and State Route 125. Cities are Tifton, Omega and Ty Ty, and Phillipsburg and Unionville are census-designated places. Chula and Brookfield are unincorporated. Irwin, Berrien, Cook, Colquitt, Worth and Turner counties border it. A single school system, the Tift County School District, runs the public schools countywide.

How do Tift County housing figures look?

Tift County packs in more people per square mile than the other three counties in this group, 158.5 in 2020. Owners occupy 61.0% of housing units for 2020-2024.

Tift County figures from Census QuickFacts (counts are July 2025 estimates; value, rent and income span 2020-2024)
ItemTift County
Residents42,254
Housing units18,311
Middle home value, owners$165,200
Middle monthly rent$777
Middle household income$53,255
Building permits in 2025177

Headcount is up 2.2% since April 2020. Hispanic or Latino residents make up 14.3% of the county, and 12.5% of people age 5 and up use another language at home. Wikipedia's 2020 census tally shows 15,921 households and 41.6% of occupied homes rented, with 5.9% of rentals vacant. With renters that common, a Tifton house with a tenant already in it can attract a landlord-minded buyer. Mention the lease at the start and let the buyer judge.

Which Tift County offices bill and which one values?

The commissioner collects the money and then sends it on to the state, the county, the city and the school board. Values come from the assessors. Two separate offices, two separate phone lines.

The tax commissioner takes mail at P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793, answers at (229) 386-7820, and stays open on weekdays from half past eight until five. The tax assessors take mail at P.O. Box 134, Tifton, GA 31793, and answer at (229) 386-7840 from eight to five, Monday through Friday.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, online payments, delinquent accounts, tax sales
  • Tax assessors: real and personal property values, mobile home decal reviews, exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and executions

That same tax commissioner's office also collects city taxes, so one office can answer for a Tifton address and an unincorporated one.

When is Tift County property tax due?

The commissioner's FAQ puts the regular bill at November 15 and the mobile home bill at April 1.

Installments are welcome online for property tax. No minimum opens a payment plan, since the office names an amount once arrangements are made so the balance clears on schedule. Mobile home owners can pay in pieces too, with the decal withheld until nothing is left owing.

  • Property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home tax: April 1
  • Partial payments: accepted online for property tax
  • Decal: issued only after a mobile home balance is paid in full

Anyone who falls behind should know that clearing a delinquent bill does not hand over the property. The FAQ spells this out, which settles any rumor to the contrary.

How is a Tift County tax bill figured?

The bill starts with the assessor's market value as of January 1, then takes 40% of it as the assessed value. The state revenue department's worked formula subtracts any homestead exemption from that assessed value, including the state's standard $2,000 exemption, and multiplies the remainder by the millage rate.

One mill is a dollar of tax per thousand dollars of assessed value. Tift County officials set their own part of the rate, the school board sets its part, and the state adds a small levy of its own. Cities that levy a tax add a further rate on top, which is why two houses with the same value can receive different bills.

  • Step one: market value on January 1
  • Step two: 40% of that value, less exemptions
  • Step three: multiply by the combined millage rate

The county site links to an online parcel search, so you can look up your own value, owner of record and acreage before talking to either office. Check the acreage and the building description for errors, because a wrong square footage carries straight into the bill.

What does an assessor visit mean when you are about to sell?

It usually means an appraiser is checking on a change. The assessors' page lists homes that traded hands during the previous 12 months among those that get a field review, and it cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 as the notice rule.

Further triggers: a permit for a remodel, pool or outbuilding, a reported fire or storm loss, a parcel split or merger, and an application for a covenant or exemption. Field work clusters between December and May. Staff arrive in a marked county vehicle with identification, and an owner who prefers a set time can book one at (229) 386-7840.

If you just finished permitted work, expect the next notice to show a higher value. Hold on to the permit and photos of the house before the work, which help if you contest the new figure.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tift County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens if Tift County taxes go unpaid until an auction?

The levying office notifies the delinquent taxpayer in writing, and 30 days later an execution, called a fi. fa., can follow on the General Execution Docket kept by the superior court clerk. The county notes that the lien on property attaches every January 1, even before any execution exists.

That officer acts as ex-officio sheriff and may advertise and auction the parcel. County notes label these buyer-beware sales, opening at the taxes, penalties and costs owed. The winner gets a sheriff's tax deed, which is not a fee simple deed, and state law bars possession for 12 months while redemption rights remain.

A seller gains nothing from reaching that stage. Ring (229) 386-7820 and get a payoff figure in hand before you list or take an offer. A house that is behind on tax and in rough shape can also go to a cash buyer who buys as-is and accounts for the tax.

What is the Tift County appeal route?

Submit the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Forty-five days run from the day the notice was mailed, according to the state revenue department, which also lists the permitted grounds: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Your first filing has to pick a forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. State staff cannot override local boards on one parcel, per that FAQ. The assessors' page confirms assessment at 40% of fair market value, so compare the market value on the notice with recent sales of similar homes near you.

More questions about Tift County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I reach the Tift County tax commissioner?

Call (229) 386-7820 or write to P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793. Weekday hours begin at 8:30 in the morning and end at 5 in the afternoon.

Are installments allowed for Tift County property tax?

Yes, the county takes partial payments online. No fixed amount starts the plan, and the office sets one after you make arrangements. Mobile home owners can split payments as well but get the decal only once they have paid everything.

Does clearing a delinquent bill give me the property in Tift County?

No. The commissioner's FAQ says paying delinquent tax does not transfer ownership. Auction buyers get a sheriff's tax deed and, under state law, wait 12 months after the sale before taking possession.

Who collects city tax inside Tifton?

The Tift County tax commissioner does. Its FAQ says the office collects city taxes and distributes funds to the state, the county and the school board as well.

What is the cutoff for contesting a Tift County value?

The cutoff is 45 days after the assessment notice was mailed. Send your appeal to the Tift County assessors, phone (229) 386-7840 with questions, and pick your path on the form.

Where is Toombs County, and which towns are in it?

Toombs County is in southeast Georgia, with Lyons holding the courthouse and Vidalia ranking as the biggest city. State lawmakers established it on August 18, 1905, as Georgia's 144th county and it organized that October, per Wikipedia.

Land came from Tattnall and Montgomery counties, and a sliver of Emanuel County joined in 1907 to complete the county's present outline. Total area is 371 square miles. Streams south of Vidalia reach the Altamaha, while those in the Lyons half of the county run to the Ohoopee.

The cities are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, with Ohoopee counted by the Census Bureau as a place of its own. Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson have no municipal government. Emanuel, Candler, Tattnall, Appling, Jeff Davis, Montgomery and Treutlen counties touch its borders. The county sits within the Vidalia micropolitan area, and the Toombs County School District runs its public schools.

How affordable are Toombs County homes?

Of the four counties covered together here, Toombs has the least expensive houses. The 2020-2024 median is $137,000, and owners occupy 60.5% of units.

Toombs County housing and income figures from Census QuickFacts (units and permits are 2025 data; the rest cover 2020-2024)

The county recorded just 35 building permits for 2025, so nearly every sale involves an existing house. The 2020 census tallied 10,505 households among 12,027 housing units, 12.7% of them empty, with 9.5% of rentals vacant. Population is estimated at 27,545 for mid-2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base. Poverty stands at 22.8%, the highest of the four, and 16.3% of those under 65 lack health insurance.

Which office mails the bill, and which sets the value?

The commissioner handles billing and collection from 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, GA 30436. The phone is (912) 526-8575. Weekday service runs from half past eight to half past four.

The county tax site's FAQ gives (912) 526-6291 for the assessors, who determine value and take returns and exemption forms. For a copy of your warranty deed, go to the clerk of superior court's deed room in the courthouse.

  • Tax commissioner: statements, payments, decals for mobile homes, delinquent sales
  • Assessors: valuation, returns, homestead filings, first-level appeals
  • Equalization board: named by the Grand Jury to hear disputes
  • County commissioners and school board: adopt the millage rates

The commissioner does not decide value or rates, the county site stresses. Anyone upset about how large the bill is should talk to the elected boards that levy it.

What is the Toombs County due date, and what happens after it?

The county's pages contradict each other. The information page has statements leaving the office by October 20 and payment owed on December 20. The FAQ has been naming November 15 for real estate and business personal property since 2018.

Rely on the date on your own statement and call (912) 526-8575 if it looks off. The FAQ adds interest of 1% monthly after the deadline and a 10% penalty on tax unpaid 90 days out. Past 30 days, a fi. fa., which is a recorded lien, may be filed. Those records are open to the public, so credit bureaus can see them.

  • Interest on real estate: 1% each month
  • Penalty once 90 days pass: 10%
  • Lien: allowed once 30 days pass unpaid
  • Mobile homes: April 1, then 10% plus 1% a month

An auction on the courthouse steps was announced for December 2, 2025, at 10 a.m. That date has gone by. The list for any sale can be seen at the office, where staff can tell you the next one.

What should a Toombs County seller do about unpaid tax?

Before you sign a contract, have the commissioner state the parcel's balance in writing. Georgia's revenue department says no refund exists for a part year, which leaves the January 1 owner holding the whole amount.

Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia are cities, and a home inside one may owe city tax along with county tax. Ask whether both apply. If you have fallen behind, check the clerk's records for a recorded lien too, since a title company will want it released. When the roof, wiring or plumbing needs money you lack, an as-is cash buyer removes the repair bill, and any tax owed comes out of the price at closing.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed are the two papers that move a closing fastest.

Must a Toombs County owner file a property return?

Anything taxable that you own on January 1 is supposed to be returned to the assessors during the first three months of the year, ending April 1, according to the county information page. An owner who files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value and real estate exemptions.

An owner who thinks the value is too high may file a return giving their own opinion of market value, and the information page says that filing establishes appeal rights if the assessors change the figure again. The FAQ lists real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber among the taxes the commissioner bills.

  • Window: opens January 1, closes April 1
  • Silence: last year's value and exemptions repeat
  • Own-value return: sets up an appeal if the assessors disagree

Household goods are not normally taxable, per the same FAQ, so a seller does not owe tax on furniture left in the house.

Which homestead amounts appear on the Toombs County site?

The county's information page prints the regular exemption for owners who live in the house before January 1. As printed, the amounts are $20,000 off assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax and $2,000 off the state share. A city house gets a further $10,000 off city and city school tax.

Further categories carry labels: S3 for age 62 and up with an income test, S4 and SC for age 65 and up, S5 for disabled veterans, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local school-tax exemption at 70 and over. The 62-and-over school exemption uses a $10,000 earned-income limit for the prior year. Because details vary by category, ask the assessors which one fits your situation.

Applications are received between January 1 and April 1, and the page notes that state law allows no extension. Once approved, the exemption repeats yearly until eligibility changes. Moving to a new address means filing again.

How do you challenge a Toombs County assessment?

Mail a letter to the Toombs County assessors. The 45 days are counted from the date on the notice, and the county site says notices tend to arrive in spring.

Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. Three tracks are open: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. A dispute can then move on to Superior Court. Mobile homes keep a separate clock. A different value may be declared inside 45 days of the bill mailing, the county says, and a change notice opens a 21-day window to go to the equalization board.
