What is the best way to reach the Toombs County tax commissioner?

Phone (912) 526-8575 or visit 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons, any weekday between half past eight and half past four.

Does Toombs County tax come due in November or December?

The county's pages disagree, with December 20 on one and November 15 on the FAQ. Use the date on your bill, and double-check with the commissioner.

What does paying Toombs County tax late cost?

One percent interest accrues monthly after the deadline, and tax still open 90 days later takes a 10% penalty. A lien may be filed after 30 days.

When are Toombs County mobile home taxes due?

They fall due each April 1. Later payments draw a 10% filing penalty plus 1% per month, and a location permit and decal come only after full payment.

How much time does an owner get to dispute a Toombs County value?

Forty-five days, starting at the date on the assessment notice. Write to the assessors and say which route you want: equalization board, hearing officer or arbitrator.

What is Towns County, Georgia, like for homeowners?

Towns County lies in the north Georgia mountains against the North Carolina border. Hiawassee is the seat and Young Harris the biggest city. The state formed the county in 1856 and honored George W. Towns, a lawyer and politician, according to Wikipedia.

The county's 172 square miles are Blue Ridge terrain, and slices of the Chattahoochee National Forest and the Appalachian Trail cross it. Brasstown Bald, the tallest peak in Georgia, rises at the southwest edge on the Union County line, and Lake Chatuge, formed when the Tennessee Valley Authority finished its dam in 1942, fills the northeast as the state's highest major lake. Tate City is the only place besides the two cities that the Census Bureau names separately.

Students in the Towns County School District go to elementary, middle and high schools that share a single campus east of Hiawassee. Young Harris College, founded in 1886, sits in the county too. Wikipedia credits outdoor recreation with roughly a quarter of local employment, which shapes who buys homes here.

How do Towns County housing numbers differ from neighboring counties?

Residents skew old, values run high, and almost everyone owns. For 2020-2024, QuickFacts reports 82.3% owner occupancy and a typical home value of $316,100.

Towns County housing and population per Census QuickFacts (July 2025 for units and residents, 2020-2024 for the remaining rows)
MeasureResult
Middle home value, owner-held$316,100
Owner cost per month, mortgaged$1,431
Owner cost per month, mortgage-free$470
Middle monthly rent$808
Residents past 6541.2%
Housing units9,120
Residents13,285

Headcount is up 6.4% over the 2020 base, the fastest of the four counties covered here, and households average 2.03 people. Median age was 57.2 in the 2020 count. That count found 8,600 housing units with 36.4% vacant and 15.9% of rentals empty. Some of those empty units may be seasonal or second homes, though the figures do not say. A person who inherits a mountain cabin from afar should make sure the tax statement is forwarded to a current address.

Which Towns County office handles which question?

Statements and payments go through the tax commissioner in the courthouse annex, 48 River Street, Suite H, Hiawassee, GA 30546, phone (706) 896-2267. Weekday service runs from 8:30 until 4:30, with a lunch closure between noon and 1.

The assessor is down the hall in Suite G, reachable at (706) 896-3984 on the same weekday schedule. Parcel records appear on qPublic, which the county calls free. Online payment is available through the county tax site.

  • Commissioner: statements, payments, levies, mobile home tax
  • Assessor: valuations, returns, homestead and conservation forms, mobile home registration
  • Superior court clerk: deeds, with copies handled in the deed room

Rates come from the county Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education, and the commissioner's office has no input.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Towns County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why does Towns County collect property tax in January?

January 10 is the real estate due date here, which falls later than the usual Georgia schedule. The information page and the FAQ agree on it. For a check in the mail, a post office postmark counts, and a postage-meter mark does not.

After the date passes, a monthly interest charge posts on the 10th, calculated as the prime rate plus 3 points spread over 12 months. A 5% penalty follows at 120 days, repeating each 120 days until the total reaches 20%. Mobile home bills generally go out about January 2, payable by April 1, with 10% added on April 2.

  • Real estate: due January 10
  • Interest: posted on the 10th of each month
  • Penalty: 5% every 120 days until it reaches 20%
  • Mobile homes: April 1 deadline, 10% penalty the next day

Twelve months of nonpayment sends an account to a collection agency, with administration and levy fees of up to $215 and more, followed by four weeks of newspaper notices ahead of any sale. Settle the balance or arrange terms long before that.

Who has to file a return in Towns County, and when?

An owner files an initial return for taxable real and personal property held on January 1, and real estate returns for changed or newly acquired property are due at the assessor's office from January 1 through April 1. After the first real estate return, the law renews it automatically at the prior year's value unless the owner adds land, builds, or otherwise changes the property.

Personal property differs: the county says returns on form PT-50p are filed every year, whatever happened to value or use. An owner who no longer holds the listed items needs to tell the assessor, or the tax keeps coming. Skipping a required return carries a 10% penalty on the unreported value, plus interest and possibly more penalties.

  • New or changed real estate: file by April 1
  • Personal property: file every year
  • Missed return: 10% of the unreported value, plus interest

An owner unhappy with the current value can file a new return stating a different one. If the assessors reject it, that filing starts the appeal described below.

What should a Towns County seller know about deferral and conservation use?

Two programs can follow a parcel into a sale. Tax deferral is open to owners age 62 or older whose gross household income is $15,000 or less. It postpones the bill rather than wiping it out, and the county says the deferred amount generally comes due at a change of ownership or once it reaches 85% of fair market value.

Conservation use is the other. Farm or timber land that qualifies is valued by its current use, and in return the owner signs a 10-year covenant with the assessors. According to the assessor's page, a purchaser who continues the same use and signs the covenant owes no penalty, while a change of use triggers one. Acreage in the hills may already be under a covenant, so check before listing.

Call the assessor at (706) 896-3984, ask whether either program applies to your parcel, and request the terms in writing. A cash buyer taking the home in its present condition will ask for the same figures before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Towns County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How do Towns County homestead exemptions work?

According to the county tax site, the place to file a homestead application is the Towns County Tax Assessor's Office, and first-time homeowners should bring a copy of the warranty deed. Anything received after April 1 counts toward the next year.

Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. An approved exemption renews itself, though a move, a transfer of title or a switch to another type means applying again. The county adds that local exemptions replace the state amounts when the local figure is bigger, so get the current amounts from the assessor rather than an old chart.

Nothing carries over to a buyer. The next bill, now in the buyer's name, can run higher until the new owner files.

How does a Towns County appeal work?

Take the appeal to the assessors in writing, counting 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. The county site names three grounds: taxability, value, and uniformity with similar properties. Disagreement over the amount of tax levied does not qualify.

When the assessors leave the value alone, the case moves to the equalization board, and Superior Court is the next stop. Arbitration can stand in for the equalization hearing. For an owner away on military duty, a relative or friend may file inside 90 days of the notice.

Mobile homes use a separate track, with 45 days to file with the assessors and 21 days after a change notice to reach the equalization board.

More questions about Towns County, GA Property Tax Guide

When must Towns County real estate tax be paid?

January 10 every year, with mobile home tax due April 1. A mailed check needs a post office postmark, because a postage-meter mark is not accepted.

How do I contact the Towns County tax commissioner?

Ring (706) 896-2267 or visit 48 River Street, Suite H, Hiawassee. Staff are in Monday to Friday, 8:30 until 4:30, and step out for lunch at noon for an hour.

What does late payment cost in Towns County?

Monthly interest posts on the 10th using the prime rate plus 3 points. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns every 120 days until it hits 20%. Mobile homes pick up a 10% penalty on April 2.

How long can I take to contest a Towns County value?

The window is 45 days counted from the notice's mailing date. Send it to the assessors, (706) 896-3984, and an unsettled appeal moves on to the equalization board.

Will the buyer inherit my Towns County homestead exemption?

No. It renews each year for the same owner, and a change of ownership calls for a fresh application. The buyer files with the assessor's office by April 1.

Where is Troup County and what shapes its housing?

Troup County sits on Georgia's western edge against the Alabama line. LaGrange serves as seat of government and is the largest city. Of 446 square miles, 414 are land, and the Piedmont terrain runs through all of it. Interstate 85 and Interstate 185 cross the county, with U.S. 27 and several state routes, so Atlanta commuters and Columbus-area workers both choose to live here. Heard, Coweta, Meriwether and Harris counties adjoin it, and so do Chambers and Randolph counties in Alabama.

The General Assembly drew the county lines on June 9, 1826, once Creek land cessions opened the area, per Wikipedia's county entry. Cotton mills built around LaGrange in the late 1800s anchored local work for generations. Textile jobs eventually moved overseas, and auto parts suppliers serving the nearby Kia plant took up some of the slack. West Point Lake and Callaway Gardens bring in visitors.

Incorporated places are LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point. Long Cane, Mountville, Harrisonville and Abbottsford are unincorporated communities. A bungalow in LaGrange, a lakeside lot near West Point and a farm tract outside Hogansville attract quite different buyers, and each can come with its own tax history. Troup County School District runs the public schools, and a commission with a countywide chairman plus four district members governs.

How many people and homes does Troup County have?

Census estimates for mid-2025 put Troup County at 72,844 people, which is 4.9% above the April 2020 base. Roughly 61 of every 100 housing units are lived in by their owners, and QuickFacts lists the middle owner-occupied value at $217,200.

Troup County snapshot, QuickFacts, Census Bureau

Decennial counts climbed from 50,003 in 1980 to 58,779 in 2000 and 67,044 in 2010. In 2020 the county tallied 28,721 housing units, 8.4% of them empty, and about four in ten occupied units were rentals. Seniors account for 17.8% of residents, so inherited houses and estate sales appear regularly.

Which Troup County office does what?

Your tax passes through two separate desks. One collects money. The other, a citizens board served by the Property Appraisal Department, decides what the parcel is worth.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 883-1620, open on weekdays from 8 to 5, for bills, mobile home and timber tax, and tag renewals.
  • Property Appraisal: (706) 883-1625, at 100 Ridley Avenue, Suite 2100, LaGrange, for values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Superior Court clerk: where deeds and tax liens are recorded.

The county's appraisal FAQ describes the assessors as a part-time citizens board, so a call may land on voicemail and be returned later. That board picks the Chief Appraiser, answers to state law and the Georgia Constitution, and gets its budget from the county commission. Card and online payments run through a county portal with a Property Taxes choice, and the tax office also takes payment by phone.

When are Troup County property taxes due?

Troup's property tax page names November 15 as the official deadline, with penalties and interest piling up after it. State revenue officials let counties move the statewide default, so read the date printed on the bill you actually receive.

Georgia freezes market value as of January 1 and then taxes 40% of it. Millage comes from the school board, the county governing authority and any other body that covers your parcel. A sample calculation on the appraisal FAQ uses .030260 as the rate and takes off exemptions first. Mobile homes and timber reach the same collector on their own timetables.

  • The state ratio is 40%, applied to market value.
  • One mill means a dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value.
  • A higher value or a dropped exemption can lift a bill while the rate stays flat.

What is the route for disputing a Troup County value?

Appeals grow out of the yearly assessment notice, and you get 45 days after the notice date shown on its face. Once that passes, you lose the chance to challenge that year's number.

The appraisers say they want sales records, photos of similar houses that changed hands lately, and whatever else supports your figure. A Board of Equalization hearing usually follows. Grand jurors name its members, who are neighbors and fellow owners, and filing is free. Arbitration is the other lane: each party hires one arbitrator and splits a third. Going on to Superior Court adds a $25.00 filing fee, per the county FAQ.

After a board or court rules, the assessors cannot move that value for two years without walking the parcel themselves.

Do LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point send separate bills?

Possibly. State revenue officials explain that a city levies its own ad valorem tax and that its clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to one combined statement. Troup's county pages do not say which arrangement applies to each of its three cities, so ask the tax commissioner at (706) 883-1620 and the clerk of your city before you assume one payoff covers everything.

The same state page gives taxpayers at least 60 days from the postmark of a bill before interest starts. A parcel inside city limits can therefore owe two separate payoffs at closing, one to the county and one to City Hall, and each may carry its own due date. Collect both figures in writing.

Which Troup County exemptions are worth a look?

Homestead filings are taken from the first of January through April 1. Miss the window and you forfeit the benefit for that year. Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 hands out the forms and quotes the amounts.

Other special exemptions are kept in the same office. The state's county facts page adds two quirks: skipping a return means you are deemed to have returned the same property at last year's final value, and freeport relief for inventory needs a local vote. A move means filing again for the new address.

  • Own the house and live in it on January 1.
  • A refund claim for a tax wrongly assessed has a three-year limit from payment.
  • Mobile homes sit on a separate location permit and return cycle.

How should a Troup County seller handle the tax bill?

Ask the collector for a payoff amount ahead of scheduling the closing, and let the attorney or title agent pay it from what you receive. Each year's bill goes to whoever held title on January 1, so an October sale can still leave a statement in your mailbox unless the settlement sheet divides the tax.

The tax commissioner's news page posts a courtesy tax sale list and a note that excess funds after such a sale go only to the record owner at that time or to other lienholders. A home that spent years as a rental, an estate asset or an empty shell may owe for several years, so request every year's status in writing.

A cash buyer can still close while a balance is open, because the payoff is deducted at the table. Set the closing statement next to the payoff letter and compare each line.

How do I phone the Troup County tax office?

The number is (706) 883-1620. Questions about value or exemptions go to Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625.

Is November 15 the Troup County payment deadline?

Yes. The county tax page calls November 15 the official deadline and says penalties and interest follow it. Confirm against your own statement.

How long can I challenge a Troup County assessment?

Forty-five days after the notice date. A late filing forfeits the right for that year, and appeals cannot be filed without a notice.

When does Troup County take homestead applications?

From New Year's Day through April 1. Anything filed later waits for the next year.

Who owes the tax if I sell in October?

The person who owned it on January 1 is billed. Pay it at closing, after getting the payoff letter from the tax commissioner.

What makes Twiggs County different from its neighbors?

Twiggs County calls itself the geographic center of Georgia, and the claim has a marker behind it. State geologists and the U.S. Geological Survey placed the center in a swampy spot where Turvin and Savage creeks meet, near the old first county seat of Marion. The legislature passed the bill creating the county on December 14, 1809, carving it from Wilkinson County and naming it for a Revolutionary War major general.

The county covers about 360 square miles. Its north end rolls like the Piedmont, while the south has the flat pine woods of south Georgia. It lies along the Fall Line, which brought kaolin; that clay industry, with forestry and farming, carried the economy through the 1900s. Interstate 16 runs through the middle, linking Macon and Savannah, and two industrial parks of 150 and 500 acres sit where I-16 meets Highway 96.

Jeffersonville is the present county seat. Its courthouse dates to 1902 and 1903 and was renovated in 1979, then expanded in the 1990s and early 2000s, according to the county's own site.

How does Twiggs County look in Census data?

Nearly nine in ten Twiggs homes, 88.2%, house their owners, and the middle value is $111,300. People are leaving more than arriving: the 2025 estimate of 7,597 sits 5.4% under the 2020 base of 8,028.

Builders pulled just 13 permits in 2025, and 96.1% of residents had not moved in the prior year. The county averages 22.3 people per square mile, so many parcels are acreage, timber or family land handed down. A seller with that kind of property often values a quick as-is closing over weeks of showings.

Who buys houses in a county with so few employers?

Twiggs counted only 80 employer establishments and about 1,987 jobs in 2023, with employment up 6.9% from 2022. Only 45.0% of people 16 and older are in the labor force, and workers who commute spend an average of 27.9 minutes getting to work, so a typical trip to work is a long one for a county this small.

Those figures matter to a seller. With a poverty rate of 20.1% and a median household income of $56,324, many owners have little cash set aside for repairs or back taxes. A seller in that position can ask the tax commissioner early what payoff will come out of the proceeds and weigh an as-is sale against fixing the house first.

Which Twiggs County office handles which question?

The courthouse at 425 Railroad Street in Jeffersonville holds the offices you need, and each has its own job.

  • Tax commissioner, (478) 945-3359, mail to P.O. Box 187: property and motor vehicle tax, tags and titles.
  • Assessors and Chief Appraiser, Room 102, (478) 945-3663, mail to P.O. Box 111: values, returns, homestead, current-use and forest land programs, and appeals.
  • County commissioners: adopt the budget and help set the county millage.

The assessors' board gathers on the first Thursday of every month in Room 102, starting at nine in the morning, and the office accepts walk-in filings during the nine-to-five business day. A field appraiser with photo identification in a marked county vehicle may stop by a parcel to check data tied to an appeal, return, permit or sale. The county posted its 2026 tax digest and five-year levy history notice on August 21, 2026.

When is the Twiggs County bill due, and what if I am late?

Go by the date on your own statement. The Georgia default is December 20, but state revenue officials say a county can choose December 1 or November 15 or bill in installments, which makes the Twiggs tax commissioner the final word on yours.

Interest cannot start until 60 days after the bill's postmark, per the state, and unpaid balances may add penalties on top. Phone (478) 945-3359 for the exact date, the current interest rate and a payoff on any past-due year. Mobile home owners should ask separately, since the permit and return follow their own early-year cycle.

  • A refund claim for tax wrongly assessed must start within three years after you paid.
  • In some counties the city clerk bills municipal tax, so confirm whether a Jeffersonville or other city bill applies to your parcel.

How do I fight a Twiggs County value?

Notices of assessment are mailed in late May or early June, and the deadline is 45 days after the printed date. A plain letter works as well as the form if it lists the parcel ID, address, daytime phone, your chosen route and your evidence. Hand-delivered or postmarked papers count. Late filings are not processed, and the office refuses email and fax.

You pick one of three routes when you file:

  • Board of Equalization: free, with three local property owners who each completed at least 40 hours of training. Either party has 30 days to carry the result to Superior Court.
  • Nonbinding arbitration: you provide a certified appraisal dated no more than nine months before January 1, plus a $214 check to the Clerk of Superior Court. If the county accepts your appraisal, the fee comes back.
  • Hearing officer: for value or uniformity disputes over non-homestead property or wireless personal property above $500,000, at no filing cost.

Timing differs by route. On the hearing officer path, the assessors have up to 90 days to review and answer, you then have 30 days to say you are unhappy, and the assessors have another 30 days to send the file to the appeal administrator. If no hearing officer is found, the appeal moves to the Board of Equalization. Either side may ask for the other's witness list and documents at least 10 days before a hearing, and the answer is due at least seven days ahead, or the evidence can be excluded.

How do I claim a Twiggs County homestead exemption?

File in Room 102 with the assessors before April 1 of the first year you want relief. The home must be your primary residence, and a missed deadline counts as a waiver for that year.

The assessors also administer the Conservation Use Valuation Assessment and Forest Land Protection Act programs, which matter in a county where farms and timber dominate. These programs carry covenants, so ask for the commitment length before you enroll land you plan to sell soon. For current exemption amounts, call (478) 945-3663.

What should a Twiggs County seller do about taxes?

Obtain a payoff in writing from the tax commissioner and compare it to the settlement statement. Because Georgia bills the January 1 title holder, a sale late in the year needs the tax divided clearly on paper.

If you inherited land, ask for the history of every year you or the estate held it, since acreage in a shrinking county sometimes sits unpaid longer than a house in town. A bill unpaid more than 90 days after its due date can become a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court. Settling past years at closing clears the title for a buyer, whether that buyer finances or pays cash.

How do I reach the Twiggs County tax commissioner?

Call (478) 945-3359 or visit the Court House Square at 425 Railroad Street in Jeffersonville. Mail goes to P.O. Box 187.

How long can I appeal a Twiggs County value?

Forty-five days after the notice date. Papers must be hand-delivered or postmarked by then, and neither email nor fax appeals are accepted.

Does Twiggs County offer arbitration for appeals?

Yes. Nonbinding arbitration needs a certified appraisal and a $214 filing fee, and either side can later appeal the arbitrator's decision to Superior Court.

What is the homestead cutoff in Twiggs County?

April 1 of the first year you want it. Apply at the assessors' Room 102 in the courthouse.

Why does Twiggs County have so few building permits?

Census QuickFacts lists 13 permits for 2025 in a county of about 7,600 people. The county is rural, and population has fallen since 2020.

Why is Union County called the Top of Georgia?

Brasstown Bald, the highest mountain in Georgia, rises in the southeast corner of Union County and straddles the Towns County line. That is why locals call the county the Top of Georgia. The county measures 329.02 square miles, with 322.55 of them land, and Blairsville is the seat.

Union was carved from Cherokee County territory in the Georgia Land Lottery of 1832, after gold found in the 1820s made land long held by Native Americans more attractive to settlers. The county history page says the name probably traces to the Union Party, not to the Civil War, which came nearly thirty years later. Residents live in Blairsville, in the community of Suches, or out in the countryside among pastures and creeks.

Sellers here hold very different properties: a mountain cabin, a lot in Blairsville, or acreage out in the county. Each calls for its own pricing and access plan, and each needs a settled tax record before the deed changes hands.

What is daily life like in Union County?

The county describes itself as an easy drive of about 90 miles from Atlanta, with rolling pastures, mountain views, clear creeks and waterfalls. Its pages note that Blairsville was named among the Top Ten Places for Retirement in a 1994 Wall Street Journal article and in a 2008 Retire in Georgia feature, and they point to a local hospital and public school system as selling points.

The county's own summary cites about 54 people per square mile from the 2020 count of 24,632. Acreage, mountain parcels and in-town lots are all assessed under the same 40% rule, so the bill depends mostly on land size, exemptions and any current-use covenant that comes with the parcel. Check which of those apply before you price.

What do the numbers show for Union County homes?

Mid-2025 estimates give Union County 27,859 people, a 13.1% jump from the 24,632 counted in 2020. Owners live in 84.4% of housing units, and the middle owner-occupied value stands at $307,400.

Which Union County office do I call?

Billing and valuing sit in different offices. The tax commissioner's site says its mission is to bill, collect and disburse taxes, while the assessors alone determine value.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 439-6017, at the courthouse, 65 Courthouse Street in Blairsville, for bills, payments and tag and title work.
  • Tax assessors: (706) 439-6011, open weekdays until half past four, for values, returns, homestead filings and exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, including a copy of your warranty deed.

The county's ad valorem page adds an unusual detail: Union's tax assessors, not the tax commissioner, have been delegated to receive tax returns and homestead applications. The assessors' page lists seven staff who keep the parcel records: five real-property appraisers, one personal property appraiser and a clerk. A posted public notice says the county hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions and Services to help revalue residential, commercial, industrial and farm parcels. Field crews drive vehicles with a Union County seal and stay outside homes and buildings.

Rate-setting is shared as well. The county commissioner sets the county levy, the Board of Education recommends the school rate, and Blairsville's governing body handles the city. A state revenue commissioner oversees the whole process, so a high bill is rarely about one office alone. Start with the assessors if you question the value and with the tax commissioner if you question the amount owed.

What is the Union County property tax due date, and what do late bills cost?

The tax commissioner's FAQ puts the real estate and business personal property deadline at December 20 annually. Mobile and modular home tax comes due on April 1, vehicle tax tracks the owner's birthday, and boats join the December 20 group once May notices have gone out.

Once the deadline slips by, interest of 1% builds each month on the balance. Past 90 days, the office can record a tax lien, called a FIFA, at the Clerk of Superior Court, and it warns that credit bureaus can read those public records. Tax sale proceedings may start at the same 90-day mark.

  • The county allows at least 60 days to pay the annual bill.
  • Not getting a bill is no defense against owing it.
  • Blairsville issues and collects its own city property tax.

Owners with wooded land should know that uncut timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, and is then taxed on its full market value. On a single lump-sum timber sale, the purchaser sends the tax with form PT-283T to the tax commissioner inside five business days.

How does a Union County appeal work?

Notices of value go out in May, and the challenge period runs 45 days after the notice date. The first filing goes to the Board of Assessors. If no agreement follows, the file is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, which the Grand Jury appoints, and a further written notice to the assessors takes the case to Superior Court.

Arbitration or a certified hearing officer can replace the board for some owners, and that choice is made at filing. Mobile and modular home owners can contest twice, once at the return stage and again within 45 days after the bill goes out, which the county says is usually mid February.

Skipping a required return can draw a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest. Real estate returns are expected from January 1 to April 1 for property that changed hands or changed in value.

How does homestead relief work in Union County?

Bring a copy of your warranty deed to the assessors and file ahead of April 1. The house must be yours and be where you live on January 1. Once approved, relief continues until you move, and a late application starts the following year.

The tax commissioner's site says Union's local homestead exemptions beat the state's, while the state revenue department's county page lists none, so ask the assessors for current figures before relying on either. Freeport covers business inventory, and current-use programs for farm and forest land demand a commitment to stay undeveloped, with stiff penalties for breaking it.

What should I do about the tax bill when I sell in Union County?

The county mails each year's bill to the person who owned the parcel at the start of January, so a buyer closing in March or September will not receive that year's statement. Arrange for the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds and request a written payoff from the tax office.

The tax commissioner confirms that a new owner gets no bill for the purchase year, so check any prorated payment on the settlement statement closely. For a mountain rental or a cabin left by a relative, ask about each year it was held. A cash sale can finish the payoff and the deed recording in a single courthouse visit.

By December 20 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

What does a late Union County payment cost?

The tax site states 1% interest a month. A lien can follow once 90 days pass.

How long can I appeal a Union County value?

Forty-five days counted from the notice date. The assessors see it first, then the equalization board.

Can I file a Union County homestead application late?

A late filing does not help the current year, but the assessors activate it for the next one.

Who collects Blairsville city property tax?

Blairsville bills its own portion. The county tax commissioner handles county and school bills.

Where does Upson County sit between Atlanta, Macon and Columbus?

About one resident in five (20.8%) has passed 65, and 92.8% did not move in the prior year. The assessors' page says the office manages more than 15,000 real property parcels and around 1,400 personal property accounts.

Which Upson County office answers which question?

You will find both at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Money owed goes to one door, and questions about value go to the other.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mailing to P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the payoff figure for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mailing to P.O. Box 508, open weekdays through the working day: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an elected office that stands apart from both the assessors and the county commissioners. Statements are addressed to the homeowner and never to the lender, although the office sends mortgage companies a data file. After a change of lender, pass the bill along yourself.

How is an Upson County tax bill calculated?

Fair market value, the whole 100% figure, the assessors arrive at, and Upson's FAQ defines assessed value as 40% of that. Exemptions come off the 40%, which leaves the net assessed, or taxable, value. Multiply it by the millage rate to get the bill, with each mill worth one dollar on every $1,000.

Owners may also propose their own value by filing a return during the early-year window that ends April 1. If the assessors disagree, a notice goes out with their figure and the appeal clock starts. A copy of your warranty deed is available from the Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street, Thomaston.

Where do Upson County tax dollars go?

The tax commissioner's FAQ lists the uses in plain terms. Property tax pays for the administration of county government and the public school system, for public buildings, bridges and county roads, and for the courts, the jail and law enforcement. It also funds fire protection and public health and sanitation. The FAQ calls this an abbreviated list and refers readers to the Georgia Code for the rest.

The county reports 592 miles of roads across 326 square miles of land. If your bill rose from one year to the next, the county's 2026 notice of increase states the change in mills, so compare it with the rate on your statement.

When do Upson County bills arrive and when are they due?

Real and personal property bills are mailed no later than September 15, and the county FAQ places the due date around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements go out by January 30, and that tax comes due on April 1.

A 2026 notice of property tax increase carried a tentative county rate of 8.244 mills, up 0.391, and listed hearings on August 26 and September 8, 2026. Without the increase the rate would have been no more than 7.853 mills. Your own bill shows the final rate, since the school board and the city set separate ones.

  • The assessed share is 40% of fair market value.
  • Upson's rate is built from separate levies by the Board of Education, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston.
  • The post office's own date stamp proves a timely payment, and a postage meter stamp does not.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Upson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What does a late Upson County bill cost in penalties?

Unpaid balances accrue monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% joins it at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20%.

Hardship can justify partial payments, but only if you phone before the due date to arrange them, and interest and penalties keep running on the rest. The office sends a notice of intent with 30 days to pay before it files a FIFA lien on the General Execution Docket. Tax still unpaid 90 days past the due date is open to a lien, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Full payment, fees included, cancels the lien. Buying liens at the counter is not offered.

How do I dispute an Upson County assessment?

Six weeks and three days after the notice date is the cutoff. Four grounds qualify: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. Address the written appeal to the Board of Assessors and say which route you prefer.

The assessors also post a field review notice letting identified representatives walk onto a property in business hours to check its value. The county takes homestead applications from the first of the year through March 31, and they must reach the office by April 1. You must hold the house and live in it on January 1, and a stable owner needs no yearly renewal unless the deed or address changes. Ask at (706) 647-8176 which exemption amounts fit your parcel.

What does an Upson County seller need to do about the bill?

Have the tax commissioner write out a payoff before closing, and see that the closing agent pays it from what the buyer sends. Because the bill carries the name of whoever owned on New Year's Day, an autumn seller should check the settlement sheet to see who covers the current year.

Heirs and landlords should ask about every year they held the house, including any FIFA on file. A lien goes away only when it is paid in full, which is why the buyer's title agent will want the account clear. A cash purchase can settle old balances at closing and hand you the rest, which helps when a house carries back taxes, repairs or tenants.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

More questions about Upson County, GA Property Tax Guide

How do I contact the Upson County tax commissioner?

The number is (706) 647-8931, and the counter is in Suite D-120 at 305 South Hightower Street, Thomaston.

When is Upson County property tax due?

Around November 15 in a typical year, per the county FAQ. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1.

What does late payment cost in Upson County?

Monthly interest equals prime plus 3%. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns at each 120-day mark, stopping at 20%.

What is the Upson County appeal deadline?

Forty-five days from the notice. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors and name the appeal method.

Does Upson County mail my bill to my lender?

No. Statements go to the homeowner. Lenders get a data file, and passing the bill along is your job when needed.

What kind of place is Walker County for a home seller?

Walker County fills Georgia's northwest corner, right against the Tennessee line, and its northern end belongs to the Chattanooga commuting zone. State lawmakers formed it on December 18, 1833, out of former Cherokee territory, and the seat is LaFayette, per Wikipedia.

At 447 square miles, it holds ridges, caves and coves rather than flat farmland: Lookout Mountain, Pigeon Mountain, McLemore Cove and a slice of the Chattahoochee National Forest. A listing can therefore be a lot in town, a mountainside tract or acreage in a valley. Five incorporated cities sit inside it (Chickamauga, LaFayette, Lookout Mountain, Rossville and a small piece of Fort Oglethorpe), and Rock Spring, Fairview, Lakeview and Chattanooga Valley are census-designated places.

The Walker County School District covers most of the county, while Chickamauga has its own city system. Four of five county commission seats are tied to districts called Rossville, Chickamauga, LaFayette and Lookout Mountain, which gives a rough picture of where residents live. The Chattooga and Chickamauga Railway is among the county's current rail lines.

The Chickamauga Campaign of August 21 to September 20, 1863 played out here, including the Battle of Davis's Cross Roads on September 10 and 11, the Battle of Chickamauga on September 19 and 20, and a skirmish at LaFayette in June 1864 during the Atlanta Campaign. Ellison's Cave, ranked among the deepest caves in the United States, and Rocktown and Lula Lake Land Trust also draw visitors.

Population has swung in long waves. Census takers found 6,572 residents in 1840, 38,198 in 1950, 61,053 in 2000 and 68,756 in 2010. Counties touching Walker include Catoosa, Whitfield, Gordon, Floyd, Chattooga and Dade, plus Hamilton County, Tennessee, and DeKalb County, Alabama.

What do the Census numbers say about Walker County homes?

Walker County leans heavily toward homeowners, and prices run under the national figure. The numbers below come from the Census Bureau.

Walker County QuickFacts snapshot, 2020-2024 estimates except where dated
IndicatorWalkerU.S.
Typical owner-occupied home value$197,100$332,700
Share of homes lived in by owners77.2%65.2%
Typical monthly gross rent$940$1,413

Housing units on July 1, 202530,599148,260,882
Permits issued in 20252991,431,616

Residents numbered 67,654 on census day in 2020, slightly below the 68,756 of 2010, and the July 2025 estimate is 70,250. The 2020 count showed 28.2% of occupied homes rented, 10.1% of all units empty and a median age of 41.6. About 51% of residents lived in rural areas, which fits the mix of hillside and valley parcels. The same census tallied 29,137 housing units and 26,206 households, and about a quarter of households were one person living alone. Veterans number 3,468 in the 2020-2024 estimates, some of whom may qualify for the disabled veteran exemption described below.

Which offices handle Walker County property tax?

Billing sits with the Tax Commissioner and valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors. The commissioner's site says its office neither determines property value nor sets the tax rate.

  • Rock Spring: 122 Highway 95, mail to P O Box 510, Rock Spring, GA 30739, phone 706-638-2929, weekdays 8:00 A.M. until 4:30 P.M., with a drop box beside the front entrance.
  • Rossville: 2012 McFarland Gap Road in the Fairview community, same phone and hours.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 706-638-4823, the number the commissioner lists for preferential assessment questions.
  • Search and pay online at walkercountytax.com.

Both counters take payments and questions, so use whichever is closer. Ask either one to walk you through the county and school levy lines on the bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Walker County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

When does Walker County property tax come due?

Notices carry a 60-day window, and the commissioner says that works out to December 20 in most years. If your printed bill shows another day, follow the bill.

A mailed check needs a USPS postmark, not a meter stamp. The state revenue department says interest waits until 60 days past the bill's postmark.

  • Manufactured homes located in the county on January 1 are due April 1 each year and carry a 10% penalty plus 1% monthly interest when late, with a possible State Court citation.
  • The value date is January 1, so anyone who closes on a purchase after that date should confirm that the bill reaches them.

What is the appeal route for a Walker County value?

Written appeals must reach the assessors within 45 days after the notice date. Grounds are limited to taxability, value and uniformity; the size of the bill is not a ground.

After the assessors' own review, you may take it to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and Superior Court sits beyond that. An owner who disagrees with the carried-forward value can also file a new return between January 1 and April 1. Taxable assessed value is 40% of market value under O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.

Which exemptions and credits does Walker County list?

The commissioner's site lists state and local homestead exemptions, and the local amount wins whenever it is larger than the state one. Bring the warranty deed if this is your first application.

  • Standard homestead: printed as $2,000 for state, school and county purposes.
  • Local senior exemptions begin at age 70: county tax with a $15,000 adjusted gross income limit, and county school tax with $50,000 off taxable value. A county school exemption at age 75 carries the same $15,000 limit.
  • Disabled veteran and armed forces surviving spouse exemptions: the page prints $81,080.
  • Tax deferral: ages 62 and up with gross household income of $15,000 or less, until a change of ownership or until deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of market value.
  • 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant: the page says it lowers assessed value by $18,000 for credit purposes and shows on the 2026 bill if a homestead exemption was on file by April 1, 2026. Rentals and investment property do not receive it.

Applications arriving after April 1 take effect the following year, and an approved exemption renews itself until ownership or residence changes.

How does a Walker County sale handle unpaid tax?

Obtain a written balance from the commissioner and have your closing agent remit it from the proceeds. Property with unpaid tax can be levied and sold, as the commissioner's site puts it, so do not leave a balance for the next owner.

Check any manufactured home on the land separately, since its tax follows the April 1 schedule instead of the autumn one. Inherited houses and rentals can have more than one tax year open, so request the status of each. With 28.2% of occupied homes rented in 2020 and a stock that stretches from hillside cabins to town lots, buyers who take houses as they stand are a natural audience, and a cash sale can pay the county first without a repair list.

When must Walker County real estate tax be paid?

Two months after the notices are mailed, usually December 20. If your bill shows another date, follow the bill.

Who answers questions about a Walker County tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner's staff at 706-638-2929, in either the Rock Spring or the Rossville office. Value questions go to the assessors at 706-638-4823.

What is the deadline to contest a Walker County valuation?

The 45th day after the notice's mailing date. The assessors look first, and a Board of Equalization hearing follows if you stay in dispute.

Where do I file for homestead exemption in Walker County?

At the Tax Commissioner's counter, with April 1 as the cutoff for a new filing. First-time owners take their warranty deed along.

Does a lingering tax balance block a Walker County sale?

No. The balance is paid at closing from your proceeds. Get the amount in writing, and ask about earlier years if a tenant lived in the house or an heir inherited it.

Why does Walton County keep getting bigger?

Walton County lies in the Piedmont, roughly 30 miles from downtown Atlanta, and its census counts show the spread of metro Atlanta in numbers: 38,586 residents in 1990, 60,687 in 2000, 83,768 in 2010 and 96,673 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate from QuickFacts is 112,696.

The General Assembly formed the county in 1818 and named it for George Walton, a Georgia signer of the Declaration of Independence. Monroe holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, with Loganville the other major one, and Social Circle, Between and Good Hope also sit within the borders, according to Wikipedia. The county spans 330 square miles. Its neighbors are Barrow, Oconee, Morgan, Newton, Rockdale and Gwinnett.

Interstate 20, U.S. 78 and U.S. 278 are among its major highways. The Walton County School District serves everything except Social Circle, which runs its own city district. Public high schools are Loganville, Monroe Area and Walnut Grove, and private options include George Walton Academy and Monroe Country Day School.

Elementary schools named in the county's listing include Loganville, Bay Creek, Sharon, Walker Park, Youth and Monroe, and the middle schools are Loganville, Carver and Youth. The county and the school system each levy their own share, so the district matters when you read a bill. Social Circle properties sit in the city district, and everything else is in the county district.

A six-member commission elected by district, plus a chairman chosen countywide, sets the county's share of the levy.

What does QuickFacts show for Walton County housing?

Homeownership here is high and values sit just above the U.S. median. For 2020-2024 the owner-occupied home median is $339,500, compared with $332,700 for the country.

  • 79.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, against 65.2% across the U.S.
  • Monthly gross rent has a median of $1,175.
  • Median household income is $84,945 across 35,755 households.
  • The county had 39,911 housing units on July 1, 2025, and issued 569 building permits during 2025.
  • Veterans number 5,740.

The 2020 census recorded 35,473 housing units, with 4.4% vacant, and 75.2% of occupied units owner-occupied. Households totaled 33,924, and 36.8% of them had children under 18. The median age was 39.7, and 58.1% of residents lived in rural areas, so a listing may be a lot in Monroe or acreage out in the rural parts.

The county's 2025 estimate is 16.6% above the 2020 count. With so much new building going up, an older house with deferred repairs or a tax balance is easier to sell to a buyer who accepts it as it stands.

Where do Walton County owners send questions and payments?

The Tax Commissioner issues one statement per parcel. For Monroe owners it also carries the city's share, because Monroe stopped mailing its own bills in 2016 and now relies on the county statement and its date. Delinquent city bills from 2015 and earlier are still paid at Monroe City Hall.

  • Main counter: 303 S. Hammond Drive, Suite 100, Monroe, GA 30655; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Property tax line (770) 266-1736, email WCTC@co.walton.ga.us.
  • Tax Assessors, same building: (770) 267-1352.
  • Search and pay: tax.waltoncountypay.com.

Tag renewals have their own window in the courthouse at 303 South Hammond Drive, (770) 267-1335, and the commissioner reminds mortgage holders that the mailed copy goes only to the homeowner, so lenders often pull the bill from a third-party service.

The county mails the bill to the owner on record for January 1 only, so a lender or a newly arrived owner should obtain a copy rather than wait. Churches, nonprofit hospitals and public property can be exempt once the assessors approve, with the request due April 1.

What does Walton County charge after the November 15 deadline?

Bills are mailed in late August, and November 15 is the due date. The commissioner's page lays out each later step, summarized here.

Walton County delinquency steps, from the Tax Commissioner's website
WhenCharge or action
After November 15Interest on the unpaid portion, added monthly
At 90 days lateFi.Fa. lien fee: $20.50 under $100, $30.50 over $100
Every 120 days5% penalty on what remains, capped at 20%
Before a lien30-day notice of intent

A Fi.Fa. goes on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court and lasts seven years, and it may show up on credit reports. The office takes partial payments, but charges continue on the leftover amount. A tax sale, when one is scheduled, is an auction outside the Walton County Government Building on a first Tuesday, advertised in the Walton Tribune for four straight Wednesdays.

How do returns, appeals and exemptions work in Walton County?

Real property returns and homestead applications are due January 1 through April 1 at the Tax Assessors' Office. A required return that is never filed draws a 10% penalty on the value left off, and personal property returns are due every year with the same penalty for late filing.

You can contest the assessment within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The assessors respond first, and the county says the file then goes to the Board of Equalization automatically. Mobile and modular homes get two chances to contest, during the return period and within 45 days of a bill that usually arrives in January.

  • Owners 65 and older are exempt from Walton County School District tax on the house and one acre.
  • Owners 70 and older receive up to $30,000 off on land beyond one acre.
  • A filed PT-61 transfer form can serve as a return if the property was not changed.
  • A refund claim for tax paid in error goes in writing to the board of commissioners within three years, and it must rest on an error, not a value disagreement.

Ask the Tax Assessors' Office to confirm an exemption is on file before you list, since the county says failing to apply by the deadline costs the exemption for that year.

What should a Walton County seller do about the bill at closing?

Email the settlement statement to WCTC@co.walton.ga.us or fax it to (770) 267-1416 right after closing. The office says it can mail a duplicate bill to the buyer when the purchase happened before November 15 of that tax year.

Before you close, get a payoff figure dated for the closing day, because monthly interest keeps changing it. If a Fi.Fa. is already recorded, paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. The commissioner says it does not sell liens in bulk to outside investors.

An inherited house, a rental or a place with several years behind can close without repair demands when the buyer purchases as-is and the title company settles the county first.

Anyone who sold after January 1 should keep the closing statement handy for the commissioner's records, as the January 1 owner still receives the first bill.

November 15. The county mails statements in late August, and balances left after the due date begin accruing interest.

Which Walton County office handles exemptions?

The Tax Assessors' Office at 303 S. Hammond Drive, phone (770) 267-1352. April 1 is the usual cutoff, or the last day to contest the assessment notice.

Does Monroe mail a separate city tax bill?

No. Since 2016 Walton County sends a single consolidated statement that includes Monroe city tax, and it is due on the county's date.

What happens 90 days after the Walton County due date?

A Fi.Fa. lien fee applies, $20.50 on bills under $100 and $30.50 on larger bills, after a 30-day notice. A 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%.

Can a house with a Walton County Fi.Fa. be sold?

Yes. Paying the tax with its fees, penalties and interest cancels the lien, and the closing agent can do that from your proceeds using a current written payoff.

Why is Ware County unlike the rest of south Georgia?

Ware County covers 908 square miles, more than any other county in Georgia, and a large block of that is wetland inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its federal refuge. Lawmakers carved it from Appling County on December 15, 1824, numbered it the state's 60th county and named it for Nicholas Ware, per Wikipedia.

Waycross is the county seat and its only incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, so outside the city limits an address answers only to county rules. Neighbors are Bacon, Pierce, Brantley, Charlton, Clinch, Atkinson and Coffee counties, and Baker County, Florida touches the south.

Water runs three ways here. The Suwannee, St. Marys and Satilla river basins all drain parts of the county. Laura S. Walker State Park honors a local author and conservationist who promoted forest parks; the land was bought during the 1930s and deeded to Georgia in 1941.

Ware was once much bigger. Bacon, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee and Pierce counties were each formed partly from its territory. South Georgia State College and Coastal Pines Technical College both have Waycross campuses, and the elementary schools include Wacona, Center, Williams Heights, Memorial Drive, Ruskin and Waresboro. Public schooling runs through a single district: a preschool, six elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school, enrolling upward of 6,370 students. Discovery Montessori School and Lighthouse Christian Academy are private choices.

The city's name comes from its position at railroad junctions, with track leaving in six directions, and CSX still runs the Rice Yard sorting yard and shops there. The settlement dates from about 1820, was renamed Tebeauville in 1857, won the courthouse in 1873 and incorporated as Way Cross on March 3, 1874. In 2020 the city held 13,942 people and 6,775 housing units, with 18.7% of them empty. Four federal highways cross in town (1, 23, 82 and 84), and two historic districts carry National Register listings. Memorial Satilla Health treats most local patients, and a county-and-city airport sits northwest of downtown. NOAA figures show close to 50 inches of rain a year, heaviest from June to August, and with the Okefenokee so near, a buyer may ask how a given lot drains.

One local footnote ties the city to its tax rolls: in 1917 the Waycross city council opened municipal primaries to white women, the first town in Georgia to do so, because some of the largest property owners in town were women who wanted a say in how their tax dollars were spent. The Obediah Barber Homestead, seven miles south of the city, is another National Register property.

What are Ware County homes worth, and who lives in them?

The middle owner-occupied home here is valued at $109,500 for 2020-2024, close to a third of the $332,700 national figure, according to QuickFacts.

The county had 36,312 residents in 2010, 36,251 in 2020 and an estimate of 36,906 for 2025, and it holds 12,957 households. Population history is a long climb and a plateau: 8,811 in 1890, 22,957 in 1910, 37,180 in 1980 and just under 37,000 now. Census day in 2020 turned up 15,858 housing units, 13.9% of them vacant. Renters held 37.8% of the occupied ones, residents had a median age of 39.8, and 67.9% lived in urban areas. Vacancy near one in seven is high, and a balance left unpaid for several years can turn into a recorded lien.

Which Ware County offices send and collect the bill?

The tax commissioner bills and collects. The assessors set values, and the county commission and school board each choose a millage rate.

  • Commissioner's counter: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. The site header lists (912) 490-4305, and the office keeps weekday hours from half past eight to five.
  • Assessors: (912) 287-4383 according to the FAQ page, with written appeals directed to 305 Oak St., Suite 154.
  • Online parcel search and payment: warecountytax.com. Anyone whose lender escrows the tax should call the lender before paying, so the bill is not paid twice.
  • Recorded deeds: the Clerk of Superior Court, 800 Church Street.

Ask the commissioner whether a City of Waycross charge appears on your statement. The exemption list refers to city, county and school freezes, so city tax can matter for houses inside Waycross.

What does a late Ware County bill cost?

The tax commissioner expects to mail statements by September 15, and the due date is November 15. Manufactured homes follow a calendar of their own: January bills, April 1 payment, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid.

The FAQ spells out what happens after the due date for bills dated July 1, 2016 or later.

  • Interest accrues at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • Each 120 days adds a 5% penalty, stopping at 20% of unpaid principal.
  • A homesteaded parcel with tax under $500 owes interest but no penalty.
  • Past 90 days, a FIFA lien can be recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it.

Where an account stays open, a levy is possible. Sales take place at 305 Oak Street in the Board of Commissioners Room on a first Tuesday, following four weeks of notices in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county does not promise title, and a purchaser waits at least a year before using the land or collecting rent.

What homestead and tax relief does Ware County offer?

To qualify for homestead exemption you must own and occupy the house as of January 1, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's office. Its pages print March 1 in one place and April 1 in another as the cutoff, so confirm with the assessors before filing. An approved exemption carries over each year.

  • Freeze exemptions lock the county, school and city operating-tax value at the prior year's level while you stay.
  • An extra local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income of $24,000 or less takes up to $20,000 off the 40% assessed value.
  • A floating exemption for ages 62 and up with household income of $30,000 or less swaps out other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that it may initially raise the bill.
  • Damaged timber: the commissioner's front page points to the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission.

How can I challenge a Ware County valuation?

Appeals must be filed within 45 days after the date on your assessment notice, on grounds of taxability, value or uniformity. The size of the bill is not a ground.

After the assessors reconsider, the next step is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and then Superior Court on written notice. Another route is a return filed from January 1 to April 1 that names a different value.

What is the best way to sell a Ware County house with tax unpaid?

Get a payoff from the commissioner and let the closing agent send it from your proceeds. If a levy has been threatened, check the tax sale list on the county site, since a sale date can set your timeline.

A mobile home has a separate April 1 bill and decal, so keep that account apart from the land. A buyer who takes the property as it stands and accepts the title work can close fast. The commissioner also keeps an excess funds list, worth checking if money may be owed to you from an earlier sale.

More questions about Ware County, GA Property Tax Guide

Which month do Ware County real estate bills fall due?

November. The county aims to mail statements by mid-September, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April.

Can I pay a Ware County bill without going to Waycross?

Yes. Search the parcel and pay on warecountytax.com, or mail a check to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. If your lender escrows the tax, check with the lender first.

Where is an appeal of a Ware County value sent?

To the Board of Tax Assessors at 305 Oak St., Suite 154, Waycross, within 45 days of the notice date.

Is there a penalty if only part of a Ware County bill is late?

Interest runs on the unpaid principal at prime plus 3%, and the 5% penalty steps (every 120 days, up to 20%) apply to what remains unpaid. Homesteaded parcels under $500 skip the penalty.

How do I avoid a Ware County tax sale on my house?

Clear the balance with the commissioner before the first-Tuesday sale. A lien that is satisfied drops off the sale list, and the office can quote a payoff.

The assessors' page carries a notice that appraisal staff may visit a property to refresh their records, citing state code section 48-5-264.1. Visitors arrive in a county vehicle and leave a card at the door when nobody answers.

How does Warren County's housing market look to a seller?

Warren is a quiet rural county where homes are inexpensive and almost nothing new gets built. QuickFacts shows 5,269 people in its July 2025 estimate, compared with 5,834 in the 2010 count and 5,215 in 2020. The county chamber describes Warrenton, Camak and Norwood as the business-friendly towns.

  • Land: 284.36 square miles, which works out to roughly 18 residents for each square mile.
  • Housing stock: 2,687 units, and owners occupy 72.2% of them.
  • What a home is worth to its owner in the 2020 through 2024 survey: $67,100 at the midpoint.
  • Median rent in that survey: $690. Permits issued in 2025: zero.

When a house is worth that little, a few years of unpaid tax plus interest can swallow a large piece of the price. Pay attention to old balances early. The county's own site calls the area the gateway to rural Georgia and leans on farming, history and the outdoors.

More survey detail: 2,097 households of about 2.43 people each, 93.8% of residents in the same home a year earlier, 63.2% with broadband at home, and median household income of $44,289. Buyers who telecommute will want to check connectivity at the specific address.

When does a Warren County tax bill become late?

Georgia's default is December 20, though a county board can pull the date forward to December 1 or November 15 or use installments. The tax commissioner can tell you which schedule your bill follows. State guidance gives every owner 60 days after the postmark before interest starts.

Warren's economic development page explains that the city of Warrenton, Warren County itself, the school system and the state each levy tax as of January 1, and every parcel is assessed at 40% of market value. It prints 30.358 mills for 2017 and an effective rate of 1.21%, which is a historical figure. For a current rate, ask the commissioner about your parcel or read the county finance page, which says the commissioners publish a current digest and a five-year history of levy. That page also says tax hearings are advertised whenever a proposed millage rate exceeds the rollback rate, and it carries the 2026-2027 proposed and tentative budgets and an audit posted July 6, 2026.

  • Returns run January 1 to April 1. If you skip one, last year's value rolls forward.
  • A mobile home owner applies for a location permit within 30 days of placing the unit, then renews each year in the same window.

State guidance lists taxability, value, uniformity and denied exemptions as acceptable reasons. Mail it to the county board rather than the state, which cannot take it.

Form PT-311A makes you choose a path. Most owners choose the equalization board route. A hearing officer only hears non-homestead real estate worth more than $500,000, and arbitration needs a certified appraisal that you supply.

Still unhappy? A written notice for superior court has to reach the county board within a month of the hearing officer's, arbitrator's or Board of Equalization's decision, and taxes must be paid at last year's level before a judge hears the case. If the final value ends at 85% or less of the earlier figure, the owner recovers litigation costs and attorney's fees.

The Development Authority of Warren County tries to change that with incentives its page lists: low-cost land, tax abatement schedules, industrial revenue bond financing, a $4,000 job tax credit per new job for five years, and a 100% freeport exemption on inventory shipped out of state. The page notes that Warren is a Tier 1 community. These programs target businesses, but a seller with commercial or industrial land should ask the authority what applies.

Poverty is 24.6% in the Census estimate, and 12.3% of adults over 25 have finished a bachelor's degree. Those numbers help explain the price level. In a market with few buyers, an owner who arrives with a clear title and paid-up taxes has an easier path to closing.

Does Warren County add its own homestead exemption?

No. The state's revenue department shows no local exemption in Warren, so owners rely on the statewide ones. The form goes in at any point after the home becomes your primary residence, and it needs to arrive by April 1 for the first year you want relief. Missing that date forfeits the exemption for the year.

The commissioner's page says staff handle these applications. Carry proof that you live in the house and ask which age or disability categories you could add. A buyer who will live in the house files a new form of their own, which is worth mentioning when the closing falls late in the year.

How does a sale close out the Warren County tax bill?

The bill follows whoever owned the property on January 1, so sellers and buyers split it on the settlement statement. Ask the commissioner for a written balance that covers each year up to the closing date, then give that paper to the closing attorney. A house inside Warrenton, Camak or Norwood may owe a city levy on top of the county one.

  • Get separate figures for the county, the school district and any city.

Who answers questions about a Warren County tax bill?

The tax commissioner does, at 706-465-2231. The office is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321.

By when must a Warren County value dispute be mailed?

Your envelope needs a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing date. Address it to the county's assessors in writing. State offices do not take these appeals.

Is there a Warren County exemption beyond the state homestead one?

No local exemption is listed for Warren County by the state revenue department. Owners use the statewide homestead exemptions and apply by April 1 for the first year.

What percentage of value does Warren County tax?

Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value, according to the county's economic development page. Exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate applies.

Can I give a card number over the phone to pay Warren County taxes?

Yes. The commissioner's page says staff take card payments by phone, and it links an online option too. Call 706-465-2231 to ask about fees.

Who in Jesup mails the Wayne County tax bill?

The commissioner on East Walnut Street mails it, and the assessors next door decide what the land and buildings are worth. The street address is 341 E Walnut St, Jesup, GA 31546. Letters go to PO Box 287 (ZIP 31598), and the phone is (912) 427-5910, staffed from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon.

A single bill gathers money for five bodies. The commissioner's site lists the State, Odum, Screven, the county government and the school system. Reach the assessor at (912) 427-5920 about value, and the commissioner about payment, penalties or a payoff. The commissioner also serves as the state's tag agent for vehicles. Questions can go by email to taxcommissioner@waynecountyga.us, and the county's online payment site and parcel search sit behind links on the commissioner's home page. Wayne spreads across the Altamaha River country of southeast Georgia. QuickFacts estimates 32,481 residents for July 2025, a rise of 7.8% over April 2020's 30,141, spread over roughly 642 square miles. On its home page the county notes that the river forms the northeast edge of the county with over 60 miles of frontage.

Lake Lindsay Grace is the other landmark the county promotes. Drive about 4.5 miles down Highway 203 from Highway 84 to reach roughly 240 acres of water, two parks and three boat launches. Odum and Screven are the other cities the county lists beside Jesup.

  • Elbow room: 47 residents per square mile in the 2020 count.
  • Homes: 13,180 units, two-thirds lived in by owners.

  • Midpoint rent: $846, with 102 construction permits in 2025.
  • Households: 11,061, and median household income of $53,427.

Total employment in 2023 was 7,669 across 639 employers, an 11.1% rise over the year before. Health care and social assistance brought in $178.6 million during 2022, while retail receipts reached $423.3 million. The average commute is 28.0 minutes each way.

When does Wayne County tax come due, and what follows a missed date?

Bills for real estate and business personal property leave the office by September 15 and fall due November 15. Mobile homes run on a different clock: April 1, plus a 10% penalty after that. Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday.

Interest begins the morning after the deadline and its rate is reset every January. A four-step penalty follows, starting at 5% once 120 days have gone by and rising on the same rhythm to a 20% cap. The commissioner points to state code sections 48-2-40 and 48-2-44.

The board looks again and reports its decision. Next comes a hearing before the county Board of Equalization, and Superior Court sits above that. Arbitration can replace the hearing, and the assessors will walk you through it.

Assessments equal 40% of market value. An owner may declare a figure of their own on a return during the January through April 1 window, and a refusal by the board opens the appeal. Real property returns roll forward at the previous value until the property changes.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Wayne County?

You qualify by living in the home you own on January 1. Wayne adopted local exemptions, and where the local amount beats the state figure it takes over. The assessors take the application, and an approved one renews by itself until you move, sell or switch categories.

One commissioner page sets the filing cutoff at April 1 while another says March 1. Ask the assessor which one governs before you rely on the exemption. A late filing waits for the next year's bill.

Standing timber has its own rule. It carries no tax until sold or cut, and the tax then uses its full value.

Where do White County taxpayers go to pay?

The tax commissioner's lobby is at 506 North Main Street in Cleveland, and the mailing address is P. O. Box 970, Cleveland, GA 30528. Call 706-865-2225. The drive-thru lane opens at 8 am and shuts at 4:30 pm, while the lobby stays open until 4:50 pm, Monday through Friday.

Bills go out each August with a November 15 deadline. You can pay with cash, check or card at the counter, or online, and the county notes that convenience fees apply to cards and web payments. The same office bills timber, real and personal property, mobile homes, utilities and motor vehicles, and it registers vehicles for the state.

Values are a different counter. The assessors work out of Suite 180 in the Mauney Building, and their board sits on the second Wednesday of each month at 9 a.m. to talk through appeals, homestead requests and changes in taxation status.

What do White County's housing numbers look like?

The median owner-occupied home is worth $278,900 for 2020 through 2024, according to QuickFacts. The county covers 240.74 square miles and had 29,802 people in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.4% from April 2020. Cleveland, Helen and Sautee Nacoochee are the communities the county site names.

Nature and travel feed that demand. The county's recreation list includes Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, Hardman Farm State Historic Site, Smithgall Woods State Park and Unicoi State Park and Lodge, and its schools belong to the White County School System.

  • Owner-occupied share: 78.8% of 14,547 housing units.
  • Median rent: $1,032. Construction permits in 2025: 190.
  • Residents 65 and older: 25.4%. Median household income: $70,666.
  • Average drive to work: 30.4 minutes, and 10,729 households average 2.63 people.

On the business side, QuickFacts shows 733 employer businesses and 7,240 jobs in 2023, with a payroll of $286.1 million, 2022 retail sales of $520.5 million and $132.8 million spent in lodging and restaurants. The county also counts 1,862 veterans, and its poverty rate is 10.8%. Among adults 25 and older, 84.8% finished high school and 24.0% hold a bachelor's degree.

How does White County turn a value into a tax bill?

The arithmetic is assessed value, minus exemptions, times the millage rate. Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value unless a rule says otherwise, and each mill means one dollar for every $1,000 of assessed value. The assessors set the value, and the taxing bodies set the rate.

The county commissioners and the Board of Education are the main rate setters. A notice on the county home page for 2026 shows the commissioners planning to cut the county millage rate to 8.555 mills from the 8.842 mills of 2025, a drop of 0.287 mills. That is the county government's piece only, so school and city levies stack on top. Cleveland and Helen are separate cities, so ask the commissioner whether a city levy touches your address.

Owners file a return of real property from January 1 to April 1, and a missing return means the prior year's value stands. The assessors then mail an Annual Notice of Assessment listing last year's value, this year's value, an estimate at last year's millage and the reason for any change. You can look up your record by name or address on the county's property records site, which is also where the homestead application opens.

What is the White County window for contesting a value?

The window lasts 45 days from the date printed on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which usually goes out in early May. Six grounds qualify: value, uniformity, taxability, denial of exemption, breach of covenant and denial of covenant. The bill itself is not appealable in Georgia.

Nobody can extend the deadline. The county says a missed window waives the appeal for that year and the Board of Assessors has no power to make an exception. If you agree with the notice, you do nothing.

Appeals that reach the Board of Equalization go before what the county calls a special jury for property values and denied exemptions. Questions about it go to the Clerk of Court at 706-865-2613.
