How do I claim a homestead exemption in White County?

Use the online application inside the property records site and finish it by April 1 for the current year. The house must be your primary residence, with no homestead claimed elsewhere in Georgia or another state, and a Georgia driver's license or ID showing the street address is required. A late application rolls forward to the following year.

The county says it offers numerous homestead exemptions and sends owners to the assessor for the list. Two other programs share the page. Freeport exemption covers business inventory, and a voter-approved local percentage of 20, 40, 60, 80 or 100 applies; the county notes that over sixty percent of Georgia counties and cities have adopted it at some level. Conservation use assessment covers up to 2,000 acres of farm or timber land under Georgia Code 48-5-7.4, for a single owner who signs a ten-year covenant. Freeport applications go to the Board of Assessors in the same period returns are due, and later ones can earn a partial exemption until June 1.

What happens when White County taxes go unpaid?

After November 15 a balance picks up penalties and moves through four stages. The commissioner still accepts payment on a delinquent bill, though interest keeps running.

  • Penalties and fees start once November 15 passes.
  • A lien, also called a Fi. Fa., goes on record with the Clerk of Court.
  • A levy can seize part of the property.
  • A tax sale auctions the property at the courthouse.

A lien stays on record with the Clerk of Court for seven years and may hurt credit reports and ratings.

A levy seizes part of the property to cover the debt, and personal property may be taken, counted and stored. The county says a sign may go up, extra fees are added, and the owner can stay in the house. A tax sale gets four consecutive weeks of advertising in the White County News and happens on the first Tuesday of a month at the courthouse steps. The sale adds its own advertising and conduct fees. Buyers pay in certified funds and receive a Sheriff's tax deed, issued with a receipt from the commissioner.

The original owner has a year to redeem, and lien and mortgage holders may redeem as well. After that the buyer may foreclose the right of redemption. The county says a lien is removed by paying the delinquent balance with fees and interest, so a seller should request that payoff from the commissioner and hand it to the closing attorney.

What is the due date for White County property tax?

November 15. Bills are sent every August. After that date penalties begin, and interest keeps accruing on a delinquent bill.

Where is the White County Tax Commissioner?

506 North Main Street, Cleveland, with the phone at 706-865-2225. The lobby closes at 4:50 pm and the drive-thru at 4:30 pm on weekdays.

When must a White County value dispute be filed?

Within 45 days of the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in early May. The Board of Assessors cannot extend that deadline.

By what date does a White County homestead application have to arrive?

April 1, to count for the current year. Applications are accepted all year, but a late one shifts the benefit forward. The home must be your primary residence.

Will a White County tax lien block a house sale?

What makes Whitfield County different from other north Georgia counties?

Railroads shaped Whitfield County, and Dalton remains its center. The July 2025 QuickFacts estimate is 106,212 residents, living on 290.45 square miles of land, a density of 354.2 per square mile at the 2020 census. Cohutta, Tunnel Hill and Varnell are the other cities, all settled along rail lines.

The county's history page says a Massachusetts group bought Cross Plains in 1846, the Western & Atlantic Railroad reached it in July 1847, and the legislature incorporated the town as Dalton that year. The county was cut from Murray County in 1851. Norfolk Southern and CSX lines still converge in Dalton, though no passenger trains run. An 1850 tunnel through Chetoogeta Mountain at Tunnel Hill is 1,477 feet long, and the county's history page says the first major battle of the Atlanta Campaign was fought here on February 25, 1864, with more fighting around Rocky Face Ridge that May.

  • Housing units: 40,987, of which 67.0% are owner-occupied.
  • What owners say their homes are worth, at the midpoint: $218,000.
  • Median rent: $971. Permits issued during 2025: 409.
  • Households: 36,834, averaging 2.78 people. Median household income: $67,070.
  • Commute: 21.8 minutes on average. In the labor force: 63.0% of residents 16 and older.

Employers numbered 2,373 and held 55,064 jobs at the 2023 count, paying $2.86 billion in wages. In 2022, transportation and warehousing took in $408.6 million, health care and social assistance $732.1 million, lodging and restaurants $274.6 million and retail $2.03 billion.

Does Whitfield County history affect a property sale?

Only if the parcel sits inside a site the county has designated. A ten-member Historic Preservation Commission oversees protection of battlefields, earthworks, bridges, the railroad tunnel and farm and industrial buildings, and the county posts design review guidelines for designated historic sites.

Two designations stand out. Rocky Face Ridge has a site designation report with an addendum for acreage added in 2020. Prater's Mill, a water-powered flour mill built in 1855, joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 and became an official county historic site in 2019, with an 80-acre property that includes a 65-acre nature preserve.

Before listing land near either place, ask the county planning office whether the lot lies inside a designated area. The same page recounts that the Cherokee lived on this land until Georgia claimed authority over it in 1828.

Who sends the Whitfield County tax bill and when?

Visit 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, GA 30721, or phone (706) 275-7510 any weekday from 8:00 to 4:55. Online payment has its own county tax site. The Board of Assessors, which sets valuation, keeps a separate tax help site that the county's home page links.

Real property bills typically go out in October and rest on the market value as of each January 1. The FAQ names December 20 for the usual real estate due date, but your own bill is what counts. A mobile home is billed in January with April 1 as the deadline.

One line in that FAQ matters for anyone inside the city. The FAQ says the county assesses at 40% of market value and Dalton does so at 100%. A house inside Dalton therefore carries a different base than one in the unincorporated county, and the commissioner can tell you which levies reach your address.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Whitfield County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does a late Whitfield County bill cost?

Each month's interest is the prime rate plus 3 points, taken on January 1 and divided by 12. The commissioner's worked example uses 2025, when prime stood at 7.50%, giving 0.875% a month; other years use their own January 1 figure. An older FAQ entry on the same site mentions 1% a month and a 10% penalty after 90 days, so ask the office which schedule applies before you rely on either.

A penalty of 5% is added each 120 days of delinquency up to a ceiling of 20%. At 120 days the commissioner files a lien against the property and the owner with the Clerk of Court and on the General Execution Docket, adding fees of $12 and $10. The FAQ cautions that these liens are public, so credit bureaus may read them.

Whitfield late-tax and mobile home rules
SubjectRule on the commissioner's site
InterestPrime rate on January 1 plus 3%, divided by 12, each month
Penalty5% per 120 days, ending at 20%
LienRecorded after 120 days; $12 and $10 fees
Mobile home billMailed in January, due April 1
Missing decalFine of $100 to $300, state code 48-5-493

Source: the commissioner's property page.

Can I challenge my Whitfield County value?

Yes, in a written appeal that must be filed within 45 days of the date printed on the notice. Value, uniformity, taxability and a denied exemption count as grounds, while the size of the bill does not. Address it to the Board of Tax Assessors, and say which of the state's methods you want.

Three tracks exist under state rules: the county equalization board, a hearing officer for non-homestead real estate over $500,000, and arbitration supported by a certified appraisal. Taking the result to superior court requires written notice within 30 days of the decision. The state revenue department says it cannot overrule a county board on one parcel.

Returns are accepted from January 1 to April 1, and silence means last year's final value carries over. The assessors mail business and personal property return forms each January. For a mobile home, the tax bill itself serves as the assessment notice and its 45 days run from the mailing date.

Which homestead exemptions can a Whitfield County owner claim?

The commissioner's site lists five codes. Qualifying means owning and living in the home on January 1. The Tax Assessor takes the form, and one that arrives after April 1 is credited to the following year. An approved exemption renews itself unless you move or request another type.

  • S1: regular homestead, with no extra conditions.
  • S1-V: regular homestead plus a City of Varnell exemption, for age 65 and income over $40,000.
  • S3: senior homestead at 65 with spousal income under $40,000.
  • S4-7: senior homestead at age 70.
  • S5: disabled veteran exemption, requiring a DD-214 and a 100% disability rating.

Owners who turn 62 may apply for an additional exemption, according to the FAQ. Special assessment programs cover conservation use, residential transitional property, agriculture, rehabilitated historic buildings, qualified timber and the Forest Land Protection Act. Each requires an application and a commitment to keep the property in that use for a set number of years.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Whitfield County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How should I handle the Whitfield County bill when I sell?

The statement is addressed to the January 1 owner. Per the commissioner, the office does not decide who owes what once a house sells; buyers and sellers typically work that out at closing. Where the office learns of a sale within 90 days of the due date and verifies the transfer, a bill goes to the new owner.

The owner on the record changes after a deed is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. Mortgage companies never get a copy of the bill, so a seller with an escrow account should alert the servicer. Request a balance covering earlier years and ask whether city levies for Dalton or Varnell apply.

More questions about Whitfield County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where do I find the Whitfield County Tax Commissioner?

The main office is at 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, Georgia 30721. Call (706) 275-7510 on a weekday between eight and 4:55.

How soon must I contest a Whitfield County value?

Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors, naming the method you choose. The tax amount itself cannot be appealed.

Does the City of Dalton assess differently from the county?

Yes. According to the commissioner's FAQ, the county uses 40% of market value and the City of Dalton uses 100%. Ask which one reaches your address.

What is the cutoff for a Whitfield County homestead form?

It must be received before April 1 of the tax year to count for that year. Later forms apply to the following year, and you need to own and occupy the home on January 1.

Who pays if I sell partway through the year?

The January 1 owner receives the statement, and buyer and seller typically settle it at closing. Notice of the sale within 90 days of the due date lets the office bill the new owner. Lenders are not mailed a copy.

What should a Wilkinson County owner know about property tax before selling?

Wilkinson County splits the job between two desks in Irwinton. Assessors put a number on the property. The tax commissioner mails the statement and takes payment. The state revenue department's FAQ is blunt on timing: the person on title each January 1 owes the year, and a spring closing earns no rebate.

The county spreads across 452 square miles near the fall line, where the upper coastal plain starts to roll. Irwinton is the seat, Gordon is the biggest town, and Allentown, Danville, Ivey, McIntyre and Toomsboro complete the list of municipalities. The county dates to May 11, 1803.

The population has drifted down from 10,368 in 1980 to 8,877 in 2020, and an estimate for July 2025 puts it at 8,650. All of the residents counted in 2020 lived in rural areas, at roughly 20 people per square mile. A buyer pool this small makes a clean tax record more valuable.

Gather these before talking to any buyer:

  • last year's bill and the newest assessment notice
  • a note of whether the parcel has a homestead exemption on file
  • the location permit and tax receipt for any manufactured home on the land
  • any letter from the commissioner about overdue balances

Which Wilkinson County office handles which task?

Match the question to the desk and the visit goes quickly.

  • Tax Commissioner at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136, open 8:00 a.m. until 4:45 p.m. Phone (478) 946-2232, fax (478) 946-1429, postal box P.O. Box 182. Online payments add a convenience fee.
  • Board of Assessors and Chief Appraiser, P.O. Box 189, phone (478) 946-2076. This office keeps the tax maps, the ownership transfers, and the records for mobile homes without a homestead. It meets the first Wednesday of the month at 9:30 in the courthouse.
  • Board of Equalization, whose members the grand jury appoints. Each member completes 40 hours of training in the first year and eight hours yearly after that. The Clerk of Superior Court supplies clerical help only.
  • Commissioners and school board, the two bodies that set the rates.

The county website, wilkinsoncounty.net, links to a property record search and posts the current digest with a five-year levy history.

What millage rates apply in Wilkinson County?

Your rate depends on the jurisdiction, since municipal levies sit on top of the county, state and school pieces. The assessors post these 2025 combined totals.

Combined 2025 millage in Wilkinson County, county and city levels, from the assessors' posted list

A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value. Assessed value is 40% of fair market value, as the commissioner's site spells out.

The county government's own share changed for 2024. A notice from the Board of Commissioners said it would cut its levy from 14.344 to 13.786 mills, which stayed above the 13.227 rollback figure. Staying above rollback required three public hearings, scheduled for January 21 and January 30, 2025 at the courthouse on Bacon Street.

When do Wilkinson County property taxes come due?

The commissioner's page says December 20 is the usual deadline. Your own bill carries the controlling date. The Revenue Department notes that a county may substitute December 1, November 15, or several installments.

No interest accrues for the first 60 days after the postmark on your bill. Penalties may follow later, so get the office's current charges in writing with your payoff.

  • Returns come in between New Year's Day and April 1.
  • A real property return renews itself at the previous value each year, so new filings are needed only when you add structures or buy more land.
  • Ignored bills can lead to a levy against the parcel and a forced sale.

How can I challenge a Wilkinson County valuation?

An appeal goes to the assessors in writing, and the postmark has to land inside a 45-day span that opens when the notice is sent. Disputes can cover what the property is worth, how it compares with neighbors, whether it is taxable, or an exemption you were refused.

On the state form you name your forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. Revenue department staff have no power to overturn any of those rulings on one house.

A second entry point is the annual return. Declaring a different value on a return filed by April 1 opens an appeal if the assessors reject your figure. Bring recent sales of similar houses nearby, photographs of defects, and contractor estimates. With homes valued at a median $86,300 here, a few thousand dollars of correction can matter, so documented condition problems are worth the effort.

How does the homestead exemption work here?

The exemption trims the assessed value of the house you occupy as your main residence. The state default is $2,000, and a county may offer more through local legislation. For Wilkinson County, the assessors' page says the Chief Appraiser takes homestead applications.

File whenever you like. A form arriving after April 1 waits for next year. An owner who never files is treated as having waived it.

A buyer needs a fresh application of their own. If you moved out and rented the house, ask the Chief Appraiser how the parcel is classified.

What if back taxes or a lien show up before the sale?

Your title company asks the commissioner for a payoff figure and deducts it from your proceeds. If a FiFa lien was filed, it appears on the Clerk of Superior Court's execution docket until the tax, fees and interest clear.

Write the proration into the contract, since the county bills one owner of record and never divides a year.

Manufactured homes have extra steps. Revenue department guidance gives the owner 30 days after placement to obtain a location permit, then a yearly renewal each winter, plus a return due April 1. Check that all three are current before you advertise.

What do local housing numbers look like in Wilkinson County?

QuickFacts lists a $86,300 median home value for the 2020 to 2024 period, and owners occupy 80.5% of houses. The decennial count in 2020 found 3,588 households and 4,288 housing units, with 16.3% of units vacant. Rent runs a median $825 a month. Owners with a mortgage report $1,037 in monthly costs, against $446 for owners who are debt-free.

Median household income is $45,465 and per capita income is $25,403. Residents had a median age of 44.9 in 2020, and 20.4% had reached 65. A bachelor's degree is held by 12.3% of adults, and 78.5% of households subscribe to broadband.

The county counted 143 employer establishments with 2,543 jobs in 2023, and 18 building permits in 2025. Workers spend an average of 26.9 minutes getting to their jobs. Wilkinson County School District is the sole public district. The county's neighbors are Baldwin, Bleckley, Washington, Johnson, Laurens, Twiggs and Jones.

More questions about Wilkinson County, GA Property Tax Guide

Who mails the property tax statement in Wilkinson County?

The tax commissioner does. The office is on Bacon Street in Irwinton and answers at (478) 946-2232. Value disputes belong to the assessors at (478) 946-2076.

Is December 20 the due date for Wilkinson County taxes?

Usually, as the commissioner's website puts it. Follow the date on your own bill, because a county can pick an earlier deadline.

What is the window for contesting a Wilkinson County value?

The count of 45 days starts when the notice is sent. Address the written appeal to the assessors at P.O. Box 189.

Does a mid-year sale shift the tax to the buyer?

Not automatically. The owner on New Year's Day is on the hook for twelve months, so sellers and buyers usually divide the bill inside the contract.

Where is the homestead exemption filed in Wilkinson County?

At the assessors' office, where the Chief Appraiser takes applications.

Who bills and who values property in Worth County?

Worth County runs billing and valuation through different offices. The assessors alone set what a parcel is worth, and the elected tax commissioner, who answers to neither the assessors nor the county commissioners, mails the statements. Sellers need the payoff from one and the value history from the other.

Worth County was carved out of Dooly and Irwin counties in December 1853 and became Georgia's 106th county. Sylvester serves as seat and as biggest city. Parts of Worth were later used to form Tift and Turner counties in 1905. Wikipedia credits cotton, peanuts and poultry as the economic base, and places Worth inside the Albany metropolitan area. The county spans 575 square miles, with Poulan, Warwick and the town of Sumner alongside Sylvester, and Acree, Bridgeboro and Oakfield as unincorporated communities.

On sales, the state rule is short: the January 1 owner owes the year, and a March or June closing returns nothing. Build the closing statement with that in mind.

Which Worth County office should I call?

Call the tax commissioner for bills and payoffs, and call the assessors for values, returns and exemptions.

Worth County property tax contacts and what each one answers
OfficeQuestions it handlesContact
Tax CommissionerBilling, payments, payoff figures, liens, tags201 N. Main St., Room 15, Sylvester, GA 31791; (229) 776-8204; Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30
Board of Tax AssessorsProperty values, returns, appeals, homestead(229) 776-8203
Board of CommissionersMillage, solid waste fee waivers(229) 776-8200, extension 1
Clerk of CourtsCopies of your warranty deedFirst floor of the county courthouse

Payment options on the tax site include paying online, mailing a check to the Room 15 address, calling in a payment, and using the drop box in the alley between the courthouse and the jail.

When is the Worth County property tax bill due?

On the tax office's FAQ, land, buildings and business property are paid in two parts, one due October 15 and the other November 15. Manufactured homes follow an April 1 date instead. Weekend deadlines roll to Monday.

Because schedules can move with the digest, treat the date on your own statement as final, and phone the office if a closing lands near a deadline.

Statewide, the revenue department's default is December 20 unless a local government moves it, with interest held off until 60 days past the bill's postmark. Request the exact late charges along with your payoff.

  • Only a USPS-dated postmark proves a payment was on time. A meter stamp is rejected.
  • The office takes installments of any size, yet charges keep growing on the unpaid remainder.
  • Statements are mailed to the homeowner and never to the lender. Mortgage companies receive a data file, so forward your bill if escrow pays it.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Worth County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What is the solid waste fee on a Worth County tax bill?

Any residential or business structure outside the cities carries an annual $264.00 solid waste fee, added to the same bill. The Board of Commissioners adopted this by resolution beginning in 2019.

Two relief paths exist. If a structure is dilapidated or vacant for the entire year, the owner can file a waiver request for the Board of Commissioners to approve. Owners over 65 whose total household income is $15,200 or less can qualify for an elderly exemption by completing an affidavit at the commissioners' office, reachable at (229) 776-8200, extension 1.

This matters in a sale because an inherited or empty rural house may carry the fee even when nobody has lived there. Ask whether a waiver was ever filed, and include any unpaid fee in the payoff figure.

What is the process to contest a Worth County value?

Your written appeal must reach the assessors within 45 days of the date printed on the notice. State the grounds (taxability, value, uniformity, or a refused exemption) and name the route you want.

Before April 1 each year, owners may file a return stating a preferred value. The assessors review it and, if they disagree, mail a notice carrying their figure, which starts the clock. Questions about the form go to (229) 776-8203.

The three routes are the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue staff oversee the process but cannot reverse a single parcel's outcome. Any refund from a final value is processed automatically.

How do homestead and other exemptions work in Worth County?

Homestead status requires owning and occupying the house on New Year's Day, and the assessors' office approves each application. Forms can arrive in any month, though April 1 is the last day that helps the current bill.

Approval rolls forward each year while you stay put. A move or a deed change restarts the process, so a buyer files fresh after closing.

Other programs the county tax site mentions:

  • The freeport exemption for business personal property, handled by the assessors.
  • Special assessment programs, which the assessors can describe by phone.
  • The elderly exemption from the solid waste fee described above.

What if taxes are late or a lien is recorded in Worth County?

A 30-day warning letter goes out before any lien is filed. The lien, a FiFa, lands on the court's General Execution Docket, held by the superior court clerk, once a balance passes 90 days late, and because the entry is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

Full payment of tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are not sold over the counter here. Once a levy and tax sale advertisement begin, the office urges walking the payment in.

Manufactured and modular homes count as personal property, and the location permit is withheld until the current mobile home tax is paid in full. A seller with one on the lot should settle that account first.

Which Worth County housing figures matter to a seller?

The Census Bureau counted 20,784 people in 2020 and estimates 20,059 for July 2025. Its 2020 to 2024 table lists a $104,900 median home value, owners in 73.7% of houses, and 7,739 households. Rent averages a median $864, and the median household earns $58,694. Builders took out 61 permits in 2025.

That census recorded 9,244 housing units, 11.5% of them vacant, and found 29.6% of people in urban areas. Workers travel an average of 28.4 minutes to their jobs. The county borders Dougherty, Lee, Crisp, Turner, Tift, Colquitt and Mitchell counties.

The population peaked at 23,863 in the 1920 census and has fallen to the 2020 count. Broadband reaches 74.5% of households, a bachelor's degree is held by 11.7% of adults, and the poverty rate is 26.4%. Retail sales were $8,567 per resident in 2022, and employers numbered 288 in 2023, with 2,375 jobs. The county lists 1,186 veterans. The number that controls your sale is still the payoff the tax commissioner gives you, together with the value on your assessment notice.

More questions about Worth County, GA Property Tax Guide

Where is the Worth County tax office?

At 201 N. Main St., Room 15 in Sylvester, or by phone at (229) 776-8204, online, through the mail, or at the drop box in the alley beside the jail.

What are the Worth County tax due dates?

October 15 and November 15 for land and buildings, and April 1 for mobile homes, per the tax FAQ. Your bill has the final word.

What is the cutoff to dispute a Worth County value?

Forty-five days, counting from the notice. Call the assessors at (229) 776-8203 for the form.

Does the solid waste fee apply to a vacant house?

It can, though a structure dilapidated or empty all year may earn a waiver. The commissioners' office at (229) 776-8200, extension 1 decides.

Will a late payment hurt my credit?

Only if a lien is recorded, which can follow a balance more than 90 days late. The tax office itself reports nothing to credit bureaus.
